    1| //! 3D Wave Function Collapse over a 6-connected voxel-module lattice.
    2| //!
    3| //! Every cell starts in superposition of all modules. Each iteration picks
    4| //! the uncollapsed cell with minimal weighted Shannon entropy, collapses it
    5| //! to one module by weighted draw, and propagates the six-axis adjacency
    6| //! constraints until the wave is quiet. A cell emptied of candidates is a
    7| //! contradiction, reported with its position rather than papered over.
    8| //!
    9| //! Module sets are capped at 64 so a superposition is one `u64` bitmask:
   10| //! support unions and constraint intersections are single bitwise ops.
   11| 
   12| use rand::rngs::StdRng;
   13| use rand::{RngExt, SeedableRng};
   14| 
   15| /// The six lattice directions, ordered so `opposite()` is a bit flip.
   16| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   17| pub enum Axis6 {
   18|     PosX = 0,
   19|     NegX = 1,
   20|     PosY = 2,
   21|     NegY = 3,
   22|     PosZ = 4,
   23|     NegZ = 5,
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl Axis6 {
   27|     pub const ALL: [Axis6; 6] = [
   28|         Axis6::PosX,
   29|         Axis6::NegX,
   30|         Axis6::PosY,
   31|         Axis6::NegY,
   32|         Axis6::PosZ,
   33|         Axis6::NegZ,
   34|     ];
   35| 
   36|     pub fn opposite(self) -> Axis6 {
   37|         Axis6::ALL[self as usize ^ 1]
   38|     }
   39| 
   40|     fn offset(self) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
   41|         match self {
   42|             Axis6::PosX => (1, 0, 0),
   43|             Axis6::NegX => (-1, 0, 0),
   44|             Axis6::PosY => (0, 1, 0),
   45|             Axis6::NegY => (0, -1, 0),
   46|             Axis6::PosZ => (0, 0, 1),
   47|             Axis6::NegZ => (0, 0, -1),
   48|         }
   49|     }
   50| }
   51| 
   52| /// A weighted module catalog plus its directional adjacency rules.
   53| pub struct WfcModuleSet {
   54|     weights: Vec<f32>,
   55|     /// `allowed[dir][module]`: bitmask of modules permitted as the neighbor
   56|     /// of `module` in direction `dir`.
   57|     allowed: [Vec<u64>; 6],
   58| }
   59| 
   60| impl WfcModuleSet {
   61|     /// `weights[m]` biases how often module `m` is drawn on collapse.
   62|     pub fn new(weights: Vec<f32>) -> Self {
   63|         assert!(
   64|             weights.len() <= 64,
   65|             "a superposition is one u64: at most 64 modules"
   66|         );
   67|         assert!(weights.iter().all(|&w| w > 0.0), "weights must be positive");
   68|         let empty = vec![0u64; weights.len()];
   69|         Self {
   70|             weights,
   71|             allowed: std::array::from_fn(|_| empty.clone()),
   72|         }
   73|     }
   74| 
   75|     pub fn module_count(&self) -> usize {
   76|         self.weights.len()
   77|     }
   78| 
   79|     /// Declares "`b` may sit in direction `dir` of `a`" and its mirror rule,
   80|     /// so adjacency stays symmetric by construction.
   81|     pub fn allow(&mut self, a: usize, dir: Axis6, b: usize) {
   82|         self.allowed[dir as usize][a] |= 1 << b;
   83|         self.allowed[dir.opposite() as usize][b] |= 1 << a;
   84|     }
   85| 
   86|     /// Union of what every candidate in `mask` tolerates in `dir`.
   87|     fn support(&self, mask: u64, dir: Axis6) -> u64 {
   88|         let mut union = 0;
   89|         let mut rest = mask;
   90|         while rest != 0 {
   91|             let module = rest.trailing_zeros() as usize;
   92|             union |= self.allowed[dir as usize][module];
   93|             rest &= rest - 1;
   94|         }
   95|         union
   96|     }
   97| 
   98|     fn full_mask(&self) -> u64 {
   99|         if self.module_count() == 64 {
  100|             u64::MAX
  101|         } else {
  102|             (1 << self.module_count()) - 1
  103|         }
  104|     }
  105| }
  106| 
  107| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  108| pub struct WfcContradiction {
  109|     pub position: (usize, usize, usize),
  110| }
  111| 
  112| /// A solved lattice: `modules[index_of(x, y, z)]` is the collapsed module.
  113| pub struct WfcSolution {
  114|     pub dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  115|     pub modules: Vec<u8>,
  116| }
  117| 
  118| impl WfcSolution {
  119|     pub fn module_at(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
  120|         self.modules[index_of(self.dims, x, y, z)]
  121|     }
  122| }
  123| 
  124| fn index_of(dims: (usize, usize, usize), x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> usize {
  125|     (y * dims.2 + z) * dims.0 + x
  126| }
  127| 
  128| /// Runs the collapse to completion. Deterministic per (set, dims, seed).
  129| pub fn solve_wfc(
  130|     set: &WfcModuleSet,
  131|     dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  132|     seed: u64,
  133| ) -> Result<WfcSolution, WfcContradiction> {
  134|     let (w, h, d) = dims;
  135|     let mut cells = vec![set.full_mask(); w * h * d];
  136|     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
  137| 
  138|     // Settle the initial wave first: a catalog whose full superposition
  139|     // already lacks support somewhere must surface as a contradiction even
  140|     // if no collapse would ever visit that cell.
  141|     let every_cell: Vec<usize> = (0..cells.len()).collect();
  142|     propagate(set, dims, &mut cells, every_cell)?;
  143| 
  144|     while let Some(cell) = lowest_entropy_cell(set, &cells) {
  145|         collapse(set, &mut cells[cell], &mut rng);
  146|         propagate(set, dims, &mut cells, vec![cell])?;
  147|     }
  148| 
  149|     Ok(WfcSolution {
  150|         dims,
  151|         modules: cells
  152|             .iter()
  153|             .map(|mask| mask.trailing_zeros() as u8)
  154|             .collect(),
  155|     })
  156| }
  157| 
  158| /// The uncollapsed cell with minimal weighted Shannon entropy
  159| /// `H = ln W - (Σ w·ln w)/W`; first occurrence wins ties for determinism.
  160| fn lowest_entropy_cell(set: &WfcModuleSet, cells: &[u64]) -> Option<usize> {
  161|     let mut best: Option<(f32, usize)> = None;
  162|     for (index, &mask) in cells.iter().enumerate() {
  163|         if mask.count_ones() <= 1 {
  164|             continue;
  165|         }
  166|         let (mut total, mut weighted_log) = (0.0f32, 0.0f32);
  167|         let mut rest = mask;
  168|         while rest != 0 {
  169|             let weight = set.weights[rest.trailing_zeros() as usize];
  170|             total += weight;
  171|             weighted_log += weight * weight.ln();
  172|             rest &= rest - 1;
  173|         }
  174|         let entropy = total.ln() - weighted_log / total;
  175|         if best.is_none_or(|(lowest, _)| entropy < lowest) {
  176|             best = Some((entropy, index));
  177|         }
  178|     }
  179|     best.map(|(_, index)| index)
  180| }
  181| 
  182| /// Collapses one superposition to a single module by weighted draw.
  183| fn collapse(set: &WfcModuleSet, mask: &mut u64, rng: &mut StdRng) {
  184|     let total: f32 = candidates(*mask).map(|m| set.weights[m]).sum();
  185|     let mut roll = rng.random::<f32>() * total;
  186|     for module in candidates(*mask) {
  187|         roll -= set.weights[module];
  188|         if roll <= 0.0 {
  189|             *mask = 1 << module;
  190|             return;
  191|         }
  192|     }
  193|     // Float round-off fell past the last candidate: take it.
  194|     let last = 63 - mask.leading_zeros();
  195|     *mask = 1 << last;
  196| }
  197| 
  198| fn candidates(mask: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> {
  199|     (0..64).filter(move |m| mask & (1 << m) != 0)
  200| }
  201| 
  202| /// Worklist constraint propagation: each changed cell re-restricts its six
  203| /// neighbors until the wave settles or a cell runs out of candidates.
  204| fn propagate(
  205|     set: &WfcModuleSet,
  206|     dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  207|     cells: &mut [u64],
  208|     mut work: Vec<usize>,
  209| ) -> Result<(), WfcContradiction> {
  210|     let (w, h, d) = dims;
  211|     while let Some(cell) = work.pop() {
  212|         let x = cell % w;
  213|         let z = (cell / w) % d;
  214|         let y = cell / (w * d);
  215|         for dir in Axis6::ALL {
  216|             let (dx, dy, dz) = dir.offset();
  217|             let (nx, ny, nz) = (x as i64 + dx, y as i64 + dy, z as i64 + dz);
  218|             if nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nz < 0 || nx >= w as i64 || ny >= h as i64 || nz >= d as i64 {
  219|                 continue;
  220|             }
  221|             let neighbor = index_of(dims, nx as usize, ny as usize, nz as usize);
  222|             let restricted = cells[neighbor] & set.support(cells[cell], dir);
  223|             if restricted == cells[neighbor] {
  224|                 continue;
  225|             }
  226|             if restricted == 0 {
  227|                 return Err(WfcContradiction {
  228|                     position: (nx as usize, ny as usize, nz as usize),
  229|                 });
  230|             }
  231|             cells[neighbor] = restricted;
  232|             work.push(neighbor);
  233|         }
  234|     }
  235|     Ok(())
  236| }
  237|

WFC3D analysis:
- `solve_wfc`: O(N) cells. Each iteration: `lowest_entropy_cell` scans ALL N cells → O(N) per iteration. Total iterations ~N (each collapse collapses one cell, but propagate can also collapse cells via restriction... actually each iteration collapses one cell, and there are up to N collapses). So `lowest_entropy_cell` is O(N) per collapse → total O(N^2) where N = w*h*d. This is the classic WFC issue — should use a priority queue / bucket by entropy. Note the scan is O(N) with bitmask entropy computed per cell: entropy computation is O(popcount) per cell, so O(N * popcount). Total O(N^2 * popcount) time.
- `propagate`: worklist; each cell can be re-queued multiple times (each time its mask changes). In the worst case a cell's mask changes O(64) times (each restriction removes at least one bit), so propagate is O(N * 64 * 6) = O(N) per call amortized... Actually per collapse, propagate can push each neighbor at most... a cell's mask can only shrink, so over the entire solve each cell can be restricted at most 63 times → total propagate work across the whole solve is O(N * 64 * 6 * 64)? Let me think: each time a cell is popped from work, we do 6 neighbor checks each with `support()` which is O(popcount of mask) ≤ 64. Each pop happens only when the cell's mask changes, and the mask can change at most 63 times (bit count 64→1). So per cell: O(63 * 6 * 64) = O(24k) ops → total O(N * 63 * 6 * 64) = O(384 * 63 * N)... roughly O(N * 24,192) ≈ O(N) with constant ~24k. Fine.
- `lowest_entropy_cell` is the O(N^2) hotspot: for each of N collapses, scan all N cells → O(N^2). With N = 64^3 = 262k (or smaller), N^2 = 6.9e10 — that's too slow for 64^3. Actually the collapse count equals number of cells that were collapsed by `collapse` calls, not restricted ones... every cell ends collapsed; `lowest_entropy_cell` returns a cell only when popcount > 1. Each loop iteration collapses exactly one cell (via `collapse`), and cells get restricted by propagate too. Number of while-loop iterations ≤ N. So O(N^2) worst. This is a genuine High finding.
- `candidates(mask)` uses `(0..64).filter(...)` — fine.
- Space: O(N) for cells + O(N) work vec allocations per collapse iteration — `vec![cell]` allocates per iteration: N small allocations. Minor.
- `propagate` initial call: `every_cell` vec of N usize — O(N) space, fine.

Also in `collapse`: `candidates(*mask)` iterates 0..64 each time — fine.

Note `support()` is called with `cells[cell]` (the popped cell's mask) — that's correct.

   60|     /// Shared implementation kept generic over the pruning policy so tests can

   62|     fn execute_internal<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
   63|         &self,

   65|         depth: u32,
   66|         world_size: f32,
   67|     ) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
   68|         let mut nodes = Vec::new();
   69| 
   70|         let root_node =
   71|             self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(grid, &mut nodes, OctreeRegion::root(depth));
   72| 
   73|         // Push the root node to the end of the nodes array
   74|         let root_idx = nodes.len();
   75|         nodes.push(root_node);
   76| 
   77|         SparseVoxelOctree {
   78|             root: root_idx,
   79|             nodes,
   80|             depth,
   81|             world_size,
   82|         }
   83|     }
   84| 
   85|     fn build_recursive<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
   86|         &self,
   87|         grid: &VoxelGrid,
   88|         nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
   89|         region: OctreeRegion,
   90|     ) -> SvoNode {
   91|         // Every coordinate sampled outside the dense grid is canonical air.
   92|         // Recursive cubes only extend in the positive direction, so when the
   93|         // cube's minimum lies past any grid dimension the former exhaustive
   94|         // traversal could only collapse back to this same leaf. It also could
   95|         // not append arena nodes, which makes this short-circuit byte-for-byte
   96|         // equivalent while avoiding all descendant calls.
   97|         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE && self.region_is_outside_grid(grid, region.origin) {
   98|             return AIR_LEAF;
   99|         }
  100| 
  101|         if region.depth == 0 {
  102|             let [x, y, z] = region.origin;
  103|             let (v_type, color, ll, fo) = self.get_voxel_attrs(grid, x, y, z);
  104|             return SvoNode::Leaf {
  105|                 voxel_type: v_type,
  106|                 color,
  107|                 light_rgb: ll,
  108|                 face_occlusion: fo,
  109|             };
  110|         }
  111| 
  112|         let mut children = [AIR_LEAF; 8];
  113| 
  114|         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
  115|             children[octant_idx as usize] =
  116|                 self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(grid, nodes, region.child(octant_idx));
  117|         }
  118| 
  119|         // Check if all 8 children are uniform leaves
  120|         let mut uniform = true;
  121|         let mut first_val = None;
  122|         for child in &children {
  123|             match child {
  124|                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
  125|                     uniform = false;
  126|                     break;
  127|                 }
  128|                 SvoNode::Leaf {
  129|                     voxel_type,
  130|                     color,
  131|                     light_rgb,
  132|                     face_occlusion,
  133|                 } => {
  134|                     if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
  135|                         if vt != *voxel_type
  136|                             || col != *color
  137|                             || ll != *light_rgb
  138|                             || fo != *face_occlusion
  139|                         {
  140|                             uniform = false;
  141|                             break;
  142|                         }
  143|                     } else {
  144|                         first_val = Some((*voxel_type, *color, *light_rgb, *face_occlusion));
  145|                     }
  146|                 }
  147|             }
  148|         }
  149| 
  150|         if uniform && let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
  151|             return SvoNode::Leaf {
  152|                 voxel_type: vt,
  153|                 color: col,
  154|                 light_rgb: ll,
  155|                 face_occlusion: fo,
  156|             };
  157|         }
  158| 
  159|         // Push 8 children contiguously to arena
  160|         let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
  161|         let mut child_mask = 0;
  162| 
  163|         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
  164|             let child = children[octant_idx as usize];
  165|             match child {
  166|                 SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
  167|                     if voxel_type != 0 {
  168|                         child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
  169|                     }
  170|                 }
  171|                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
  172|                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
  173|                 }
  174|             }
  175|             nodes.push(child);
  176|         }
  177| 
  178|         SvoNode::Internal {
  179|             child_base_index,
  180|             child_mask,
  181|         }
  182|     }
  183| 
  184|     fn region_is_outside_grid(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, origin: [u32; 3]) -> bool {
  185|         origin[0] as usize >= grid.width()
  186|             || origin[1] as usize >= grid.height()
  187|             || origin[2] as usize >= grid.depth()
  188|     }
  189| 
  190|     fn get_voxel_attrs(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
  191|         if x >= grid.width() as u32 || y >= grid.height() as u32 || z >= grid.depth() as u32 {
  192|             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0); // Out of bounds is air
  193|         }
  194| 
  195|         let v_id = grid.get(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  196|         if v_id == VOXEL_AIR {
  197|             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
  198|         }
  199| 
  200|         let ll = grid.get_light_rgb(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  201|         let fo = grid.get_face_occlusion(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  202|         let base_color = self.palette.color(v_id);
  203| 
  204|         (v_id, base_color, ll, fo)
  205|     }
  206| }

  225|     fn traversal_call_count<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
  226|         dimensions: [u32; 3],
  227|         origin: [u32; 3],
  228|         depth: u32,
  229|     ) -> usize {
  230|         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE
  231|             && (origin[0] >= dimensions[0]
  232|                 || origin[1] >= dimensions[1]
  233|                 || origin[2] >= dimensions[2])
  234|         {
  235|             return 1;
  236|         }
  237|         if depth == 0 {
  238|             return 1;
  239|         }
  240| 
  241|         let child_size = 1 << (depth - 1);
  242|         let mut calls = 1;
  243|         for octant in 0..8u32 {
  244|             calls += traversal_call_count::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(
  245|                 dimensions,
  246|                 [
  247|                     origin[0] + (octant & 1) * child_size,
  248|                     origin[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) * child_size,
  249|                     origin[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) * child_size,
  250|                 ],
  251|                 depth - 1,
  252|             );
  253|         }
  254|         calls
  255|     }

build_octree.rs:
- Recursive build, visits 8^depth leaves in worst case, but with PRUNE_OUTSIDE it short-circuits outside the grid. The recursion visits every node of the octree over the grid's bounding cube → O(8^depth) worst case = O(N) where N = number of grid voxels (grid dims). Actually for a grid of dims W×H×D with depth chosen so 2^depth ≥ max dim, the traversal is O(8^depth) = O(max^3) = O(N_voxels * 8^{depth - log2 max})... Let me be careful: octree over a cube of side S = 2^depth. If the grid is W×H×D ≤ S, then the recursion covers all 8^depth leaf regions = S^3 voxels worth of regions, but PRUNE_OUTSIDE short-circuits regions whose origin ≥ grid dims. Number of octree nodes in the bounding cube of the grid: the recursion covers the octree down to depth 0 for all regions within the grid bounds — that's O(W*H*D) leaves in the worst case (all distinct) = O(N) where N = W*H*D voxels, plus internal nodes O(N/7)... In the worst case (checkerboard), the number of nodes is about 8/7 * N ≈ 1.14N. So O(N) time and space. Each leaf does a grid.get — O(1). Fine. But recursion depth = depth (max ~ 10-20) — fine.
- One subtle issue: the recursion visits nodes for empty regions too — can't prune regions that are fully empty without a "max" query, but PRUNE_OUTSIDE handles outside. For a sparse grid, the octree still visits all 8^depth... wait, does it? No — the recursion always descends into all 8 children at every level, so total visited nodes = full octree nodes over the cube (minus pruned outside). It does NOT skip empty internal regions (no occupancy summary). So for a 512³ grid with a single voxel, it would visit ~8^9 ≈ 134M nodes? No wait — PRUNE_OUTSIDE: grid dims 512³, depth 9, cube 512³. All regions are within bounds, so no pruning. Every region is visited → full 8^9 = 134M leaf visits. That's O(S³) where S is the octree cube side, NOT O(N) where N is the number of *solid* voxels. Hmm. For a typical chunk grid 32³, depth 5, visits = 8^5 = 32768 leaves + internals ≈ 37k — fine. But for large grids, the cost is O(cube volume) regardless of content. The docstring claims "Converts a dense voxel grid into a collapsed sparse octree" — dense input, so O(volume) is expected for dense grids. But the early-uniform-collapse check happens post-recursion (children computed first), so uniform regions don't save work — full descent always. That's inherent to this approach; still worth noting: worst case O(V) where V = 8^depth (cube volume), and it always fully descends even into empty regions. For VoxelGrid 512³ = 134M — the PRUNE_OUTSIDE only helps non-power-of-two. Actually the grid is typically 32³ per chunk. But infinite_level may build bigger grids. This is a Medium/Low finding: could add an occupancy/air-skip using the grid's own data (e.g., check sub-cube emptiness via a prefix-sum or by scanning region bounds, or build from a hash set of solid voxels). Also note nodes vec grows unbounded relative to content — but bounded by volume. Fine.

Also `get_voxel_attrs` calls `self.palette.color(v_id)` per leaf — for 134M leaves × palette lookup (probably a Vec index) — fine.

Now build_octree_direct.rs.
    1| //! Direct-to-SVO emission: build the octree straight from a sampling
    2| //! function, with no dense intermediate 3D array.
    3| //!
    4| //! The classic pipeline allocates a dense grid (megabytes per chunk), fills
    5| //! it, then compresses to an SVO. On low-memory targets that intermediate is
    6| //! pure waste when the source can already answer "what is at (x, y, z)?" —
    7| //! and better, "is this whole cube uniform?". A sampler that can prove
    8| //! uniformity for a region lets the builder emit one leaf and never descend,
    9| //! so cost tracks the *surface* of the geometry, not its volume.
   10| //!
   11| //! The arena layout (children contiguous per block, root pushed last,
   12| //! uniform blocks collapsed to a leaf) matches [`BuildOctreeUseCase`]
   13| //! byte-for-byte, so the two paths are interchangeable and comparable with
   14| //! plain equality in tests.
   15| 
   16| use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
   17| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
   18| use crate::use_cases::ports::MaterialPalette;

   20| /// The attributes of one voxel as the octree stores them.
   21| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   22| pub struct SvoLeaf {
   23|     pub voxel_type: u8,
   24|     pub color: u32,
   25|     pub light_rgb: [u8; 3],
   26|     pub face_occlusion: u8,
   27| }
   28| 
   29| impl SvoLeaf {
   30|     pub const AIR: Self = Self {
   31|         voxel_type: VOXEL_AIR,
   32|         color: 0,
   33|         light_rgb: [0; 3],
   34|         face_occlusion: 0,
   35|     };
   36| 
   37|     fn to_node(self) -> SvoNode {
   38|         SvoNode::Leaf {
   39|             voxel_type: self.voxel_type,
   40|             color: self.color,
   41|             light_rgb: self.light_rgb,
   42|             face_occlusion: self.face_occlusion,
   43|         }
   44|     }
   45| }

   47| /// A volume the builder can sample point-wise, plus an optional proof that a
   48| /// whole cube is uniform (the pruning that makes direct emission cheap).
   49| pub trait VoxelSampler {
   50|     fn sample(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> SvoLeaf;
   51| 
   52|     /// `Some(leaf)` when every voxel in the cube at `origin` with edge
   53|     /// `size` provably has these attributes. Returning `None` just means
   54|     /// "descend"; it must never be wrong, only conservative.
   55|     fn uniform_hint(&self, _origin: [u32; 3], _size: u32) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
   56|         None
   57|     }
   58| }
   59| 
   60| /// Adapts a dense grid (plus presentation palette) to the sampler port.
   61| /// Out-of-grid coordinates are canonical air, and any cube lying entirely
   62| /// past the grid proves itself uniform — the same pruning the dense builder
   63| /// applies.
   64| pub struct GridSampler<'a> {
   65|     pub grid: &'a VoxelGrid,
   66|     pub palette: &'a dyn MaterialPalette,
   67| }
   68| 
   69| impl VoxelSampler for GridSampler<'_> {
   70|     fn sample(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> SvoLeaf {
   71|         let (x, y, z) = (x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
   72|         if x >= self.grid.width() || y >= self.grid.height() || z >= self.grid.depth() {
   73|             return SvoLeaf::AIR;
   74|         }
   75|         let voxel_type = self.grid.get(x, y, z);
   76|         if voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
   77|             return SvoLeaf::AIR;
   78|         }
   79|         SvoLeaf {
   80|             voxel_type,
   81|             color: self.palette.color(voxel_type),
   82|             light_rgb: self.grid.get_light_rgb(x, y, z),
   83|             face_occlusion: self.grid.get_face_occlusion(x, y, z),
   84|         }
   85|     }
   86| 
   87|     fn uniform_hint(&self, origin: [u32; 3], _size: u32) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
   88|         let outside = origin[0] as usize >= self.grid.width()
   89|             || origin[1] as usize >= self.grid.height()
   90|             || origin[2] as usize >= self.grid.depth();
   91|         outside.then_some(SvoLeaf::AIR)
   92|     }
   93| }
   94| 
   95| /// Builds an SVO of `depth` levels by recursive sampling, emitting leaves
   96| /// for provably uniform cubes without descending into them.
   97| pub fn build_octree_direct(
   98|     sampler: &dyn VoxelSampler,
   99|     depth: u32,
  100|     world_size: f32,
  101| ) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
  102|     let mut nodes = Vec::new();
  103|     let root_node = emit_cube(sampler, &mut nodes, [0; 3], 1 << depth, depth);
  104|     let root = nodes.len();
  105|     nodes.push(root_node);
  106|     SparseVoxelOctree {
  107|         root,
  108|         nodes,
  109|         depth,
  110|         world_size,
  111|     }
  112| }
  113| 
  114| fn emit_cube(
  115|     sampler: &dyn VoxelSampler,
  116|     nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
  117|     origin: [u32; 3],
  118|     size: u32,
  119|     depth: u32,
  120| ) -> SvoNode {
  121|     if let Some(leaf) = sampler.uniform_hint(origin, size) {
  122|         return leaf.to_node();
  123|     }
  124|     if depth == 0 {
  125|         return sampler.sample(origin[0], origin[1], origin[2]).to_node();
  126|     }
  127| 
  128|     let half = size / 2;
  129|     let mut children = [SvoLeaf::AIR.to_node(); 8];
  130|     for (octant, child) in children.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  131|         let octant = octant as u32;
  132|         let child_origin = [
  133|             origin[0] + (octant & 1) * half,
  134|             origin[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) * half,
  135|             origin[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) * half,
  136|         ];
  137|         *child = emit_cube(sampler, nodes, child_origin, half, depth - 1);
  138|     }
  139| 
  140|     if let Some(leaf) = uniform_leaf(&children) {
  141|         return leaf.to_node();
  142|     }
  143| 
  144|     let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
  145|     let mut child_mask = 0u8;
  146|     for (octant, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
  147|         let occupied = match child {
  148|             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => *voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR,
  149|             SvoNode::Internal { .. } => true,
  150|         };
  151|         if occupied {
  152|             child_mask |= 1 << octant;
  153|         }
  154|         nodes.push(*child);
  155|     }
  156|     SvoNode::Internal {
  157|         child_base_index,
  158|         child_mask,
  159|     }
  160| }
  161| 
  162| /// `Some` when all eight children are leaves with identical attributes.
  163| fn uniform_leaf(children: &[SvoNode; 8]) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
  164|     let mut first: Option<SvoLeaf> = None;
  165|     for child in children {
  166|         let leaf = match *child {
  167|             SvoNode::Internal { .. } => return None,
  168|             SvoNode::Leaf {
  169|                 voxel_type,
  170|                 color,
  171|                 light_rgb,
  172|                 face_occlusion,
  173|             } => SvoLeaf {
  174|                 voxel_type,
  175|                 color,
  176|                 light_rgb,
  177|                 face_occlusion,
  178|             },
  179|         };
  180|         match first {
  181|             None => first = Some(leaf),
  182|             Some(seen) if seen != leaf => return None,
  183|             Some(_) => {}
  184|         }
  185|     }
  186|     first
  187| }

    1| //! Sparse Voxel DAG compression: bottom-up merging of identical subtrees.
    2| //!
    3| //! The SVO arena stores every internal node's eight children as one
    4| //! contiguous block, so the unit of sharing is that block: two internal
    5| //! nodes whose child blocks are structurally identical can point at a single
    6| //! canonical copy. Repetitive architecture (identical ceiling tiles, wall
    7| //! runs, column bays) then costs one subtree instead of hundreds.
    8| //!
    9| //! The result is still a [`SparseVoxelOctree`]: traversal only ever follows
   10| //! `child_base_index`, so lookups and the GPU serializer are agnostic to
   11| //! whether the arena is a tree or a DAG. The one consumer that must NOT
   12| //! receive a DAG is any walk that visits every arena node expecting each to
   13| //! appear once per world position (e.g. collision extraction) — compress
   14| //! after those walks, immediately before upload.
   15| 
   16| use std::collections::HashMap;
   17| 
   18| use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
   19| 
   20| /// Arena sizes before and after deduplication, for telemetry.
   21| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   22| pub struct SvdagStats {
   23|     pub nodes_before: usize,
   24|     pub nodes_after: usize,
   25| }
   26| 
   27| /// A node in canonical form: internals are identified by the id of their
   28| /// interned child block rather than an arena offset, which is what makes
   29| /// structural equality (and therefore hashing) meaningful.
   30| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
   31| enum CanonNode {
   32|     Leaf {
   33|         voxel_type: u8,
   34|         color: u32,
   35|         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
   36|         face_occlusion: u8,
   37|     },
   38|     Internal {
   39|         child_base_index: u32,
   40|         child_mask: u8,
   41|     },
   42| }
   43| 
   44| impl CanonNode {
   45|     fn to_svo(self) -> SvoNode {
   46|         match self {
   47|             CanonNode::Leaf {
   48|                 voxel_type,
   49|                 color,
   50|                 light_rgb,
   51|                 face_occlusion,
   52|             } => SvoNode::Leaf {
   53|                 voxel_type,
   54|                 color,
   55|                 light_rgb,
   56|                 face_occlusion,
   57|             },
   58|             CanonNode::Internal {
   59|                 child_base_index,
   60|                 child_mask,
   61|             } => SvoNode::Internal {
   62|                 child_base_index,
   63|                 child_mask,
   64|             },
   65|         }
   66|     }
   67| }
   68| 
   69| struct BlockInterner {
   70|     /// Canonical child block -> its base index in the output arena.
   71|     blocks: HashMap<[CanonNode; 8], u32>,
   72|     nodes: Vec<SvoNode>,
   73| }
   74| 
   75| impl BlockInterner {
   76|     /// Returns the output-arena base of this block, materializing it only
   77|     /// the first time the block's structure is seen.
   78|     fn intern(&mut self, block: [CanonNode; 8]) -> u32 {
   79|         if let Some(&base) = self.blocks.get(&block) {
   80|             return base;
   81|         }
   82|         let base = self.nodes.len() as u32;
   83|         self.nodes.extend(block.iter().map(|canon| canon.to_svo()));
   84|         self.blocks.insert(block, base);
   85|         base
   86|     }
   87| 
   88|     /// Rebuilds the subtree rooted at `index` bottom-up, sharing every child
   89|     /// block already interned.
   90|     fn canonicalize(&mut self, source: &SparseVoxelOctree, index: usize) -> CanonNode {
   91|         match source.nodes[index] {
   92|             SvoNode::Leaf {
   93|                 voxel_type,
   94|                 color,
   95|                 light_rgb,
   96|                 face_occlusion,
   97|             } => CanonNode::Leaf {
   98|                 voxel_type,
   99|                 color,
  100|                 light_rgb,
  101|                 face_occlusion,
  102|             },
  103|             SvoNode::Internal {
  104|                 child_base_index,
  105|                 child_mask,
  106|             } => {
  107|                 let mut block = [CanonNode::Leaf {
  108|                     voxel_type: 0,
  109|                     color: 0,
  110|                     light_rgb: [0; 3],
  111|                     face_occlusion: 0,
  112|                 }; 8];
  113|                 for (octant, slot) in block.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  114|                     *slot = self.canonicalize(source, child_base_index as usize + octant);
  115|                 }
  116|                 CanonNode::Internal {
  117|                     child_base_index: self.intern(block),
  118|                     child_mask,
  119|                 }
  120|             }
  121|         }
  122|     }
  123| }
  124| 
  125| /// Deduplicates identical subtrees, returning a lookup-equivalent octree
  126| /// whose arena shares one copy of every repeated child block.
  127| pub fn compress_svdag(source: &SparseVoxelOctree) -> (SparseVoxelOctree, SvdagStats) {
  128|     let mut interner = BlockInterner {
  129|         blocks: HashMap::new(),
  130|         nodes: Vec::new(),
  131|     };
  132|     let root_canon = interner.canonicalize(source, source.root);
  133| 
  134|     // Root last, matching the tree builder's arena convention.
  135|     let root = interner.nodes.len();
  136|     interner.nodes.push(root_canon.to_svo());
  137| 
  138|     let stats = SvdagStats {
  139|         nodes_before: source.nodes.len(),
  140|         nodes_after: interner.nodes.len(),
  141|     };
  142|     (
  143|         SparseVoxelOctree {
  144|             root,
  145|             nodes: interner.nodes,
  146|             depth: source.depth,
  147|             world_size: source.world_size,
  148|         },
  149|         stats,
  150|     )
  151| }

--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/compress_svdag.rs: 255 lines, showed 1-255 ---

compress_svdag.rs:
- canonicalize is recursive over the SVO tree; each internal node's block gets interned into a HashMap<[CanonNode;8], u32>. `[CanonNode; 8]` — size: Leaf has u8 + u32 + [u8;3] + u8 = 12 bytes; Internal: u32+u8 = 8 bytes. Enum with 2 variants → size ~16 bytes. [CanonNode;8] = 128 bytes key. Hashing 128 bytes per internal node: O(nodes × 128). Total time O(V) where V = number of SVO nodes (each internal node visited once, plus its 8 children in the block). Note the recursion visits leaves too (canonicalize on every node). Each visit is O(1) plus hash of the block. So O(V) time, O(V × 128) space for the HashMap keys (each unique block stored as a full copy of 8 CanonNodes = 128 bytes). Since most blocks are unique in the worst case, memory = 128 × V_internal bytes. Could be a memory concern but acceptable. Recursion depth = octree depth (~6-10) — fine.
- One important subtlety: it walks the entire tree — O(V). Fine, no quadratic behavior.

   10| /// Deepest octree currently supported by every renderer and serializer.
   11| ///
   12| /// A depth-eight tree has a 256-voxel padded axis. Raising this is an
   13| /// architectural change: generation cost, payload size, shader traversal
   14| /// bounds, and GPU texture limits all need to be reviewed together.
   15| pub const MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH: u32 = 8;

  213|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotFinite);
  214|         }
  215|         if voxel_size <= 0.0 {
  216|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotPositive);
  217|         }
  218| 
  219|         let ratio = f64::from(self.chunk_size) / f64::from(voxel_size);
  220|         let axis_voxels = ratio.round();
  221|         let reconstructed_chunk = axis_voxels * f64::from(voxel_size);
  222|         let seam_tolerance = f64::from(self.chunk_size).abs().mul_add(1.0e-6, 1.0e-6);
  223|         if axis_voxels < 1.0
  224|             || !ratio.is_finite()
  225|             || (reconstructed_chunk - f64::from(self.chunk_size)).abs() > seam_tolerance
  226|         {
  227|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileChunk {
  228|                 chunk_size: self.chunk_size,
  229|                 voxel_size,
  230|             });
  231|         }
  232| 
  233|         let axis_voxels = axis_voxels as u32;
  234|         if axis_voxels % PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR != 0 {
  235|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
  236|                 fine_axis_voxels: axis_voxels,
  237|                 divisor: PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR,
  238|             });
  239|         }
  240|         let required_depth = axis_voxels
  241|             .checked_next_power_of_two()
  242|             .map(u32::trailing_zeros)
  243|             .unwrap_or(u32::BITS);
  244|         if required_depth > MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH {
  245|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
  246|                 required: required_depth,
  247|                 maximum: MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH,
  248|             });
  249|         }
  250| 
  251|         // LocalChunkSource generates one lateral cell on each side for seam
  252|         // visibility and boundary light-volume samples. Validate the real
  253|         // dense allocation rather than only the cropped payload.
  254|         let allocated_axis = u64::from(axis_voxels) + 2;
  255|         let required_columns = allocated_axis * allocated_axis;
  256|         if required_columns > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS {
  257|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
  258|                 required_columns,
  259|                 maximum_columns: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS,
  260|             });
  261|         }
  262| 
  263|         let height_voxels =
  264|             (MAX_GENERATED_HEIGHT_WORLD_UNITS / f64::from(voxel_size)).ceil() as u64 + 2;
  265|         let required_voxels = required_columns
  266|             .checked_mul(height_voxels)
  267|             .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
  268|         if required_voxels > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS {
  269|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
  270|                 required_voxels,
  271|                 maximum_voxels: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS,
  272|             });
  273|         }
  274| 
  275|         self.voxel_scale = voxel_size;
  276|         Ok(self)
  277|     }
  278| 
  279|     /// The same chunk at a coarser level of detail: voxels double per LOD
  280|     /// step, so lod 1 costs ~1/8 of lod 0 to generate, light, and serialize.
  281|     /// `svo_world_size()` is invariant across LODs (half the voxels at twice
  282|     /// the scale), so payloads of any LOD are interchangeable to the renderer.
  283|     pub fn at_lod(mut self, lod: u8) -> Self {
  284|         self.voxel_scale *= (1u32 << lod.min(4)) as f32;
  285|         self
  286|     }
  287| 
  288|     pub fn svo_depth(&self) -> u32 {
  289|         let voxels = (self.chunk_size / self.voxel_scale).round().max(1.0) as u32;
  290|         voxels.next_power_of_two().trailing_zeros()
  291|     }
  292| 
  293|     pub fn svo_world_size(&self) -> f32 {
  294|         let size = 1 << self.svo_depth();
  295|         size as f32 * self.voxel_scale
  296|     }
  297| }

  299| pub struct GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
  300|     noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/generate_chunk.rs: 989 lines, showed 1-300 ---

  300|     noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
  301|     telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
  302| }
  303| 
  304| impl<'a> GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
  305|     /// Constructs the use case with silent telemetry (tests, wasm default).
  306|     pub fn new(noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider) -> Self {
  307|         Self {
  308|             noise_provider,
  309|             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
  310|         }
  311|     }
  312| 
  313|     /// Constructs the use case with an injected telemetry sink (native server,
  314|     /// browser console, ...). Keeps the Dependency Rule intact: the use case
  315|     /// only knows the TelemetryPort trait.
  316|     pub fn with_telemetry(
  317|         noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
  318|         telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
  319|     ) -> Self {
  320|         Self {
  321|             noise_provider,
  322|             telemetry,
  323|         }
  324|     }
  325| 
  326|     pub fn execute(
  327|         &self,
  328|         chunk_pos: Position,
  329|         seed: u32,
  330|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  331|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
  332|         self.execute_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, &RealitySnapshot::default())
  333|     }
  334| 
  335|     /// Generates a chunk against an immutable encounter-state snapshot.
  336|     /// The snapshot is part of the request identity in the browser pipeline;
  337|     /// generation itself remains pure and replayable.
  338|     pub fn execute_with_reality(
  339|         &self,
  340|         chunk_pos: Position,
  341|         seed: u32,
  342|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  343|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  344|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
  345|         self.execute_from_plans(chunk_pos, seed, config, reality, None)
  346|     }
  347| 
  348|     /// [`execute_with_reality`](Self::execute_with_reality), voxelizing from
  349|     /// region plans that have already been made instead of deriving them for
  350|     /// this chunk alone.
  351|     ///
  352|     /// This is the bulk-loading seam. A [`WorldBlock`] plans a 1280 u square
  353|     /// once and every chunk inside it is cut from those plans, which is both
  354|     /// far cheaper than re-deriving per chunk and the only way a decision
  355|     /// spanning more than one chunk can exist at all.
  356|     ///
  357|     /// Passing `None` derives per chunk exactly as before — that arm is the
  358|     /// original streaming path, untouched. Plans are honoured only by level
  359|     /// 0, the one level that has them; every other level ignores the argument
  360|     /// because there is nothing it could mean.
  361|     ///
  362|     /// [`WorldBlock`]: crate::use_cases::world_block::WorldBlock
  363|     pub fn execute_from_plans(
  364|         &self,
  365|         chunk_pos: Position,
  366|         seed: u32,
  367|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  368|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  369|         plans: Option<&InfiniteRegionWindow>,
  370|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
  371|         // Pluggable levels: everything except the legacy office blueprint
  372|         // (level 90, kept inline below) goes through the LevelGenerator port.
  373|         // Level 0 is the architecturally *planned* Backrooms: region plans
  374|         // (circulation -> assemblies -> corruption) drive the voxelization.
  375|         if config.level == 0 || config.level == 1 || config.level == 34 {
  376|             use crate::use_cases::grassland_level::GrasslandLevel;
  377|             use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
  378|             use crate::use_cases::level_one::HabitableLevel;
  379|             use crate::use_cases::level_zero::BackroomsLevel;
  380| 
  381|             let start_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros();
  382|             let generator: &dyn LevelGenerator = match config.level {
  383|                 0 => &BackroomsLevel,
  384|                 1 => &HabitableLevel,
  385|                 _ => &GrasslandLevel,
  386|             };
  387|             let mut grid = match (config.level, plans) {
  388|                 (0, Some(plans)) => BackroomsLevel::generate_from_plans(
  389|                     chunk_pos,
  390|                     seed,
  391|                     config,
  392|                     self.noise_provider,
  393|                     reality,
  394|                     Some(plans),
  395|                 ),
  396|                 _ => generator.generate_with_reality(
  397|                     chunk_pos,
  398|                     seed,
  399|                     config,
  400|                     self.noise_provider,
  401|                     reality,
  402|                 ),
  403|             };
  404|             let lighting =
  405|                 crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
  406|                     config.voxel_scale,
  407|                 )
  408|                 .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
  409|             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
  410| 
  411|             let elapsed_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros().saturating_sub(start_micros);
  412|             self.telemetry.log(&format!(
  413|                 "[TELEMETRY] level {} chunk generated. Duration={}us, Grid={}x{}x{}",
  414|                 config.level,
  415|                 elapsed_micros,
  416|                 grid.width(),
  417|                 grid.height(),
  418|                 grid.depth()
  419|             ));
  420|             return grid;
  421|         }
  422| 
  423|         GeneratedChunk::new(legacy_blueprint::generate_legacy_blueprint(
  424|             self.noise_provider,
  425|             self.telemetry,
  426|             chunk_pos,
  427|             seed,
  428|             config,
  429|         ))
  430|     }
  431| }

  559|     #[test]
  560|     fn coarse_chunk_generates_the_same_layout_smaller() {
  561|         let noise = MockNoiseProvider { value: 0.0 };
  562|         let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
  563|         let fine = generator.execute(
  564|             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
  565|             42,
  566|             GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
  567|                 .with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES),
  568|         );
  569|         let coarse = generator.execute(
  570|             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
  571|             42,
  572|             GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
  573|                 .with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES)
  574|                 .at_lod(1),
  575|         );
  576|         assert_eq!(coarse.width() * 2, fine.width());
  577|         assert_eq!(coarse.depth() * 2, fine.depth());
  578|         // Same maze at half resolution. Cell sizes truncate differently per
  579|         // scale (5.0/0.4 = 12 voxels vs 25 at fine), so wall planes may land
  580|         // one fine voxel off; an LOD proxy only needs walls to line up to
  581|         // within that tolerance.
  582|         let wall = crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
  583|         let mut wall_match = 0usize;
  584|         let mut wall_total = 0usize;
  585|         for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
  586|             for x in 0..coarse.width() {
  587|                 if coarse.get(x, 1, z) != wall {
  588|                     continue;
  589|                 }
  590|                 wall_total += 1;
  591|                 let (fx, fz) = (x * 2, z * 2);
  592|                 let mut near = false;
  593|                 for dz in -1i32..=2 {
  594|                     for dx in -1i32..=2 {
  595|                         let (sx, sz) = (fx as i32 + dx, fz as i32 + dz);
  596|                         if sx >= 0
  597|                             && sz >= 0
  598|                             && (sx as usize) < fine.width()
  599|                             && (sz as usize) < fine.depth()
  600|                             && fine.get(sx as usize, 1, sz as usize) == wall
  601|                         {
  602|                             near = true;
  603|                         }
  604|                     }
  605|                 }
  606|                 if near {
  607|                     wall_match += 1;
  608|                 }
  609|             }
  610|         }
  611|         assert!(wall_total > 0, "coarse chunk must still contain walls");
  612|         assert!(
  613|             wall_match * 10 >= wall_total * 9,
  614|             "coarse walls should lie within one fine voxel of fine walls: {wall_match}/{wall_total}"
  615|         );
  616|     }

  670|         use rand::SeedableRng;

  679|

  688|         let mut open_high = 0;

  694|                 }
  695|                 if let Some(cell) = grid_high.get(x, z) {

generate_chunk.rs is mostly a facade + validation + tests. The real logic is in level generators. Note the pipeline: `execute_from_plans` → level generator → `bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting)`. Lighting bake runs on every chunk generation. That's the pipeline end-to-end.

Now the region planning core:
    1| //! Region-scale architectural planning for Backrooms Level 0.
    2| //!
    3| //! The world is tiled by fixed 80 u square regions on a world-space lattice.
    4| //! [`generate_region_plan`] is a *pure* function of `(seed, region)`: it
    5| //! derives the region's designers ([`ArchitectGenome`]), routes a dominant
    6| //! circulation spine first (between edge portals shared with the neighboring
    7| //! regions), attaches incomplete program masses ([`AssemblyInstance`]) beside
    8| //! that circulation,
    9| //! gives them structure / ceilings / fixtures, and finally applies a
   10| //! Backrooms corruption pass (duplicated suites, abandoned expansions,
   11| //! renovation overlays).
   12| //!
   13| //! Cross-region continuity: a corridor leaves a region only at a *portal* on
   14| //! a shared edge, and the portal position is derived from the *edge's*
   15| //! lattice coordinate — both neighbors compute the identical portal, so
   16| //! corridors chain across regions forever (a main corridor that never ends
   17| //! is the first and cheapest corruption).
   18| //!
   19| //! Dimensions and split planes use a 0.4 u lattice. Hosted wall centerlines
   20| //! may use its 0.2 u half-step, which aligns them with coarse voxel centers
   21| //! without changing the physical plan at different LODs.
   22| 
   23| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
   24| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   25| use crate::use_cases::anomaly_plan::plan_anomalies_for_region;
   26| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   27| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   28| 
   29| /// Side of a region, world units. A multiple of both chunk sizes (10/20).
   30| pub const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
   31| /// Plan wall thickness: an institutional double-wythe partition (two CAD
   32| /// interior walls back to back). The value must also stay >= one coarse
   33| /// voxel (0.4) or walls vanish at the LOD-1 proxy resolution.
   34| pub const PLAN_WALL_T: f32 = 2.0 * crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_WALL_THICKNESS;
   35| /// Doorways are cased rough openings around the referencable CAD single
   36| /// door: finished width plus 0.15 u of jamb clearance per side, so the
   37| /// coarsest supported voxel scale (0.4 u) still quantizes the opening
   38| /// wider than the player capsule.
   39| pub const DOOR_JAMB_CLEARANCE: f32 = 0.15;
   40| pub const DOOR_WIDTH: f32 =
   41|     crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_DOOR_WIDTH + 2.0 * DOOR_JAMB_CLEARANCE;
   42| /// Lintels sit at the standard CAD door-frame height.
   43| pub const DOOR_HEIGHT: f32 = crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_DOOR_HEIGHT;
   44| /// Snap lattice for all plan geometry (= coarsest voxel size).
   45| const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
   46| /// Keep-out margin from region edges for assembly footprints.
   47| const EDGE_MARGIN: f32 = 3.2;
   48| 
   49| /// Region lattice index of a world coordinate.
   50| pub fn region_index(w: f32) -> i64 {
   51|     (w / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64
   52| }
   53| 
   54| fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
   55|     (v / SNAP).round() * SNAP
   56| }
   57| 
   58| /// Corridor widths snap to 0.8 so *half*-widths stay on the 0.4 lattice and
   59| /// suite front walls land flush against corridor edges.
   60| fn snap_width(v: f32) -> f32 {
   61|     ((v / (2.0 * SNAP)).round() * 2.0 * SNAP).max(2.0 * SNAP)
   62| }
   63| 
   64| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   65| // Deterministic hashing and edge portals.
   66| //
   67| // All "randomness" flows through `world_topology::hash01`, and the portal a
   68| // corridor uses to cross a region border is the macro graph's portal — one
   69| // derivation shared by both neighbors of the edge and by the topology layer.
   70| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   71| 
   72| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::{hash01, primary_portal_z as v_edge_portal_z};
   73| 
   74| fn pick_index(h: f32, len: usize) -> usize {
   75|     ((h * len as f32) as usize).min(len - 1)
   76| }
   77| 
   78| /// World spawn: a point *on the main corridor centerline* of region (0, 0),
   79| /// a few units east of its west portal. The first thing the player sees is
   80| /// therefore the region's dominant circulation route — walls running away in
   81| /// both directions — rather than unplanned fabric. Both the generator core
   82| /// and the browser composition root derive spawn from this single function,
   83| /// so the player and the voxelizer can never disagree about where "here" is.
   84| pub fn spawn_point(seed: u32) -> Position {
   85|     // The main spine's west leg always runs from (0, west_z) to at least
   86|     // x = 0.35 * REGION_SIZE, so a few units in we are guaranteed to stand
   87|     // on a straight, readable stretch of corridor.
   88|     Position::new(6.0, v_edge_portal_z(seed, 0, 0))
   89| }

   91| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   92| // The planning stages, one intent per module.
   93| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   94| 
   95| mod circulation;
   96| mod corruption;
   97| mod debug;
   98| mod genome;
   99| mod suites;
  100| // Phase 2 steps 2-3: free-space decomposition and scored greedy placement.
  101| // These drive `generate_region_plan` -- see the placement pass below.
  102| mod layout;
  103| mod territories;
  104| #[cfg(test)]
  105| mod tests;
  106| 
  107| pub use debug::debug_region_ascii;
  108| pub use genome::derive_genome;

  113| /// Pure, deterministic plan for the region whose lower-left corner is
  114| /// `region_origin` (must lie on the region lattice).
  115| pub fn generate_region_plan(
  116|     seed: u32,
  117|     region_origin: Position,
  118|     region_size: f32,
  119|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  120|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  121| ) -> RegionPlan {
  122|     let rx = region_index(region_origin.x + 0.1);
  123|     let rz = region_index(region_origin.z + 0.1);
  124|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xA0 + k, rx, rz]);
  125| 
  126|     let dominant = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 0, noise);
  127|     let renovator = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 1, noise);
  128|     let mut architects = vec![dominant.clone(), renovator];
  129|     // A third designer intrudes where the style-blend field runs high: the
  130|     // macro fields decide *where* cultures leak into each other; the hash
  131|     // only decides whether this particular region exposes the seam.
  132|     let fields = crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields(
  133|         noise,
  134|         seed,
  135|         (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
  136|         (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
  137|     );
  138|     if h(0) < 0.10 + 0.55 * fields.style_blend {
  139|         architects.push(derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 2, noise));
  140|     }
  141| 
  142|     let corridors = build_corridors(seed, rx, rz, &dominant, region_origin, region_size);
  143| 
  144|     // --- incomplete masses beside circulation -------------------------------
  145|     // Scored greedy placement over the region's free space: decompose what
  146|     // circulation leaves, then let each program in the budget simulate every
  147|     // seat on every leg and commit the best. Every spine offers legs, not
  148|     // only the dominant one -- a secondary hall with nothing on it is a
  149|     // corridor to nowhere, which reads as liminal only when authored.
  150|     let mut assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
  151|     let mut taken: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = Vec::new();
  152|     let mut id = 0u32;
  153|     let placement_legs = layout::legs_of(&corridors, 14.0);
  154|     let territories = territories::free_territories(
  155|         region_origin.x,
  156|         region_origin.z,
  157|         region_size,
  158|         &corridors,
  159|         &taken,
  160|         EDGE_MARGIN,
  161|         PLAN_WALL_T,
  162|     );
  163|     assemblies.extend(layout::lay_out_suites(
  164|         &|k| hash01(seed, &[k, rx, rz]),
  165|         &dominant,
  166|         &placement_legs,
  167|         &territories,
  168|         region_origin,
  169|         region_size,
  170|         PLAN_WALL_T,
  171|         &corridors,
  172|         &mut taken,
  173|         &mut id,
  174|     ));
  175| 
  176|     // The stair placer wants raw leg spans, not placement candidates.
  177|     let legs: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = placement_legs
  178|         .iter()
  179|         .map(|l| (l.x0, l.x1, l.z, l.half_width * 2.0))
  180|         .collect();
  181| 
  182|     // --- corruption pass ----------------------------------------------------
  183|     corrupt(
  184|         seed,
  185|         rx,
  186|         rz,
  187|         &dominant,
  188|         config,
  189|         noise,
  190|         &mut assemblies,
  191|         &mut taken,
  192|         &corridors,
  193|     );
  194| 
  195|     // --- vertical circulation ------------------------------------------------
  196|     // The macro graph may have reserved a stairwell here. Upward links are
  197|     // realized as a Stair assembly beside the main spine; downward links
  198|     // stay graph reservations until the engine streams below elevation 0.
  199|     // Placed after corruption so no pass can duplicate, abandon, or redden
  200|     // a stair core.
  201|     if let Some(link) =
  202|         crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, rx, rz)
  203|         && crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry(&link)
  204|         && let Some(stair) = crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::place_stairwell(
  205|             id + 2000,
  206|             &link,
  207|             &legs,
  208|             region_origin,
  209|             region_size,
  210|             EDGE_MARGIN,
  211|             PLAN_WALL_T,
  212|             &taken,
  213|             |cx, cz, clearance| {
  214|                 corridors
  215|                     .iter()
  216|                     .all(|s| s.distance(cx, cz) >= s.width * 0.5 + clearance)
  217|             },
  218|         )
  219|     {
  220|         taken.push(stair.footprint.bounds());
  221|         assemblies.push(stair);
  222|     }
  223| 
  224|     // Macro anomalies are derived after ordinary architecture so compact red
  225|     // rooms can promote a real assembly, while region-spanning families keep
  226|     // stable world-lattice identities independent of this region query.
  227|     let anomalies = plan_anomalies_for_region(
  228|         seed,
  229|         region_origin,
  230|         region_size,
  231|         &assemblies,
  232|         spawn_point(seed),
  233|         config,
  234|         noise,
  235|     );
  236| 
  237|     RegionPlan {
  238|         origin_world: region_origin,
  239|         size_world: region_size,
  240|         architects,
  241|         assemblies,
  242|         corridors,
  243|         anomalies,
  244|     }

    1| //! Scored greedy room placement.
    2| //!
    3| //! The floor-plan literature's step 2 is: simulate placing each room at
    4| //! every free position, score the placements, commit the best, repeat, in
    5| //! order of program importance. This is that solver.
    6| //!
    7| //! What it replaces was a cursor walk: slide along the dominant corridor
    8| //! leg, roll a hash, and place a suite if the roll passed and the spot
    9| //! happened to be clear. Three consequences, all visible in a plan view --
   10| //! a failed spot was skipped rather than improved on, only the dominant leg
   11| //! was ever considered, and nothing compared two candidate spots against
   12| //! each other. An 80 u region resolved to two rooms and 90% unplanned
   13| //! fabric.
   14| //!
   15| //! Scoring, not solving: this is greedy best-first, not an optimizer. The
   16| //! literature is explicit that greedy placement with good scoring functions
   17| //! reproduces designer judgement well enough, and it stays fast and
   18| //! debuggable, which an annealer would not.
   19| 
   20| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
   21|     ArchitectGenome, AssemblyInstance, CirculationSpine, SpaceProgram,
   22| };
   23| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   24| 
   25| use super::suites::{entrance_faces_route, place_suite};
   26| use super::territories::Territory;
   27| 
   28| /// Programs in descending importance, with how many of each a region wants
   29| /// at most. Importance order is load-bearing: the literature places the
   30| /// large public rooms first because they are the ones a bad leftover shape
   31| /// ruins, and lets small service rooms take what is left.
   32| /// Interleaved rather than grouped: importance still decides who chooses
   33| /// first, but taking all five open offices before any other program lets
   34| /// the first entry eat the floor and returns a region of nothing but open
   35| /// offices. One pass per round, largest programs earliest in the round.
   36| const PROGRAM_BUDGET: [(SpaceProgram, usize); 11] = [
   37|     // Public and large first: these are the rooms a bad leftover shape
   38|     // ruins, and the ones that give a floor its character.
   39|     (SpaceProgram::Atrium, 1),
   40|     (SpaceProgram::OpenOffice, 3),
   41|     (SpaceProgram::Reception, 1),
   42|     (SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom, 2),
   43|     (SpaceProgram::WaitingArea, 1),
   44|     (SpaceProgram::BreakRoom, 1),
   45|     (SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice, 3),
   46|     // Service last: small, tolerant of awkward remainders, and plausible
   47|     // wherever they end up. A floor plan that never shows its plumbing or
   48|     // its plant reads as a set rather than a building.
   49|     (SpaceProgram::RestroomCore, 2),
   50|     (SpaceProgram::Storage, 2),
   51|     (SpaceProgram::ServerRoom, 1),
   52|     (SpaceProgram::Mechanical, 1),
   53| ];
   54| 
   55| /// Rounds the solver makes over the budget. Each round places at most one
   56| /// of each program, so a floor gets a mix before it gets a repeat.
   57| /// Two, not three. The corruption pass that runs after this one needs
   58| /// somewhere to put duplicated suites, abandoned expansions and red rooms;
   59| /// a solver that takes every good seat leaves it nothing, and a Backrooms
   60| /// region without corruption is just an office. Density is traded against
   61| /// that headroom deliberately.
   62| const ROUNDS: usize = 2;
   63| 
   64| /// Candidate anchors are tried at this pitch along a leg. Finer than a
   65| /// room is wide, so no viable seat falls between two samples.
   66| const ANCHOR_PITCH: f32 = 2.0;
   67| 
   68| /// How much of a leg's ends stay clear of rooms, so corners and junctions
   69| /// remain legible as circulation.
   70| const LEG_END_MARGIN: f32 = 4.0;
   71| 
   72| /// Clear distance required between two placed rooms.
   73| ///
   74| /// The suite builder only rejects overlap by 0.8 u, which was ample when a
   75| /// region held two rooms far apart. Packed against each other, neighbours
   76| /// interfere: a doorway samples through the strip between two shells, and a
   77| /// ceiling fixture lands inside the next room's wall. Rooms in a real plan
   78| /// either share a wall or stand clear of one another, and sharing is the
   79| /// connectivity graph's job, not the packer's.
   80| pub(super) const ROOM_SEPARATION: f32 = 3.2;
   81| 
   82| /// A horizontal run of corridor that rooms can hang off.
   83| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
   84| pub(super) struct Leg {
   85|     pub x0: f32,
   86|     pub x1: f32,
   87|     pub z: f32,
   88|     pub half_width: f32,
   89| }
   90| 
   91| /// Extracts the corridor runs rooms may attach to.
   92| ///
   93| /// Every spine contributes, not only the dominant one: a secondary hall
   94| /// with nothing on it is a corridor to nowhere, which is a liminal
   95| /// *feature* only when it is authored as one rather than left over.
   96| pub(super) fn legs_of(spines: &[CirculationSpine], min_length: f32) -> Vec<Leg> {
   97|     let mut legs = Vec::new();
   98|     for spine in spines {
   99|         for segment in spine.path.windows(2) {
  100|             // Horizontal runs only. Vertical legs need the suite builder to
  101|             // work on the other axis, which it does not yet -- see the
  102|             // module note in `mod.rs`.
  103|             if (segment[0].z - segment[1].z).abs() > 1e-4 {
  104|                 continue;
  105|             }
  106|             let (x0, x1) = (
  107|                 segment[0].x.min(segment[1].x),
  108|                 segment[0].x.max(segment[1].x),
  109|             );
  110|             if x1 - x0 < min_length {
  111|                 continue;
  112|             }
  113|             legs.push(Leg {
  114|                 x0,
  115|                 x1,
  116|                 z: segment[0].z,
  117|                 half_width: spine.width * 0.5,
  118|             });
  119|         }
  120|     }
  121|     legs
  122| }
  123| 
  124| /// Places rooms by scored greedy selection, returning them in commit order.
  125| ///
  126| /// `taken` is extended with every committed footprint, so callers that run
  127| /// later passes (corruption, stairs) see the same occupancy this did.
  128| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  129| pub(super) fn lay_out_suites(
  130|     seed_hash: &dyn Fn(i64) -> f32,
  131|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  132|     legs: &[Leg],
  133|     territories: &[Territory],
  134|     origin: Position,
  135|     region_size: f32,
  136|     wall_thickness: f32,
  137|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  138|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
  139|     next_id: &mut u32,
  140| ) -> Vec<AssemblyInstance> {
  141|     let mut placed: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
  142|     if legs.is_empty() {
  143|         return placed;
  144|     }
  145| 
  146|     let mut used = [0usize; PROGRAM_BUDGET.len()];
  147|     for round in 0..ROUNDS {
  148|         for (slot, (program, budget)) in PROGRAM_BUDGET.iter().enumerate() {
  149|             if used[slot] >= *budget {
  150|                 continue;
  151|             }
  152|             let salt = (slot * 64 + round) as i64;
  153|             let aseed = seed_hash(0x5EA0 + salt);
  154|             let threshold_seed = seed_hash(0x7A110 + salt);
  155| 
  156|             // Simulate every anchor on every leg, both sides, and keep the
  157|             // best-scoring one that the builder actually accepts.
  158|             let mut best: Option<(f32, AssemblyInstance)> = None;
  159|             for leg in legs {
  160|                 let mut x = leg.x0 + LEG_END_MARGIN;
  161|                 let mut anchor = 0u32;
  162|                 while x <= leg.x1 - LEG_END_MARGIN {
  163|                     // Size is part of the placement, not a per-program
  164|                     // constant. Drawing one width for the whole round meant
  165|                     // every candidate for a program was the same room in a
  166|                     // different spot: a region whose legs are all short then
  167|                     // rejected that program everywhere (one region in 81 came
  168|                     // out with no assemblies at all), and the scorer's area
  169|                     // term could never prefer anything, because there was
  170|                     // nothing to prefer between. Advancing the draw per
  171|                     // anchor by the golden-ratio conjugate spreads sizes
  172|                     // low-discrepancy across the leg at no extra cost -- the
  173|                     // same number of candidates, now spanning the program's
  174|                     // size range.
  175|                     let aseed = (aseed + 0.618_034 * anchor as f32).fract();
  176|                     anchor += 1;
  177|                     for side in [1.0f32, -1.0] {
  178|                         let Some(candidate) = place_suite(
  179|                             *next_id,
  180|                             *program,
  181|                             genome,
  182|                             aseed,
  183|                             threshold_seed,
  184|                             x,
  185|                             leg.z,
  186|                             leg.half_width + wall_thickness * 0.5,
  187|                             side,
  188|                             origin,
  189|                             region_size,
  190|                             taken,
  191|                             spines,
  192|                         ) else {
  193|                             continue;
  194|                         };
  195|                         // The whole front wall must face corridor, not just
  196|                         // the anchor. A room hung off the last few units of
  197|                         // a leg overhangs its end, and the part that
  198|                         // overhangs faces fabric -- so its entrance opens
  199|                         // into solid wall.
  200|                         //
  201|                         // Against the leg's own span, not the anchor margin.
  202|                         // The margin keeps rooms from *starting* on a
  203|                         // junction; demanding the far wall clear it too
  204|                         // costs a room 8 u of leg it does not need, and a
  205|                         // genome whose rooms run wide then fits nowhere at
  206|                         // all -- one region in 81 came out empty that way,
  207|                         // every candidate rejected here rather than for any
  208|                         // architectural reason. A room flush to the end of a
  209|                         // leg still faces corridor along its whole front,
  210|                         // which is the only thing this guards.
  211|                         let b = candidate.footprint.bounds();
  212|                         if b.0 < leg.x0 || b.2 > leg.x1 {
  213|                             continue;
  214|                         }
  215|                         // Every entrance must read as a door onto a route.
  216|                         if !candidate.entrances().all(|e| {
  217|                             entrance_faces_route(spines, e.center.x, e.center.z, wall_thickness)
  218|                         }) {
  219|                             continue;
  220|                         }
  221|                         if taken.iter().any(|t| {
  222|                             b.0 < t.2 + ROOM_SEPARATION
  223|                                 && t.0 < b.2 + ROOM_SEPARATION
  224|                                 && b.1 < t.3 + ROOM_SEPARATION
  225|                                 && t.1 < b.3 + ROOM_SEPARATION
  226|                         }) {
  227|                             continue;
  228|                         }
  229|                         let score = score_placement(
  230|                             candidate.footprint.bounds(),
  231|                             *program,
  232|                             territories,
  233|                             &placed,
  234|                         );
  235|                         if best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(b, _)| score > *b) {
  236|                             best = Some((score, candidate));
  237|                         }
  238|                     }
  239|                     x += ANCHOR_PITCH;
  240|                 }
  241|             }
  242| 
  243|             let Some((_, chosen)) = best else {
  244|                 // Nothing viable for this program in this round. Smaller
  245|                 // programs later in the round may still fit, so move on
  246|                 // rather than abandoning the pass.
  247|                 continue;
  248|             };
  249|             taken.push(chosen.footprint.bounds());
  250|             placed.push(chosen);
  251|             used[slot] += 1;
  252|             *next_id += 1;
  253|         }
  254|     }
  255| 
  256|     placed
  257| }
  258| 
  259| /// How good a seat is for a room, higher is better.
  260| ///
  261| /// The terms are the ones the office-planning study derived from real
  262| /// layouts: usable area, a habitable proportion, and separation from rooms
  263| /// of the same kind. Corridor adjacency needs no term -- every candidate is
  264| /// corridor-hosted by construction, which is what keeps the plan reachable.
  265| fn score_placement(
  266|     bounds: (f32, f32, f32, f32),
  267|     program: SpaceProgram,
  268|     territories: &[Territory],
  269|     placed: &[AssemblyInstance],
  270| ) -> f32 {
  271|     let (width, depth) = (bounds.2 - bounds.0, bounds.3 - bounds.1);
  272|     let center = ((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
  273| 
  274|     // Area, against what this program wants. Both too small and too large
  275|     // are penalized: a 400 m^2 private office is as wrong as a 6 m^2 one.
  276|     let area = width * depth;
  277|     let ideal = ideal_area(program);
  278|     let area_score = 1.0 - ((area - ideal) / ideal).abs().min(1.0);
  279| 
  280|     // Proportion. Rooms read as rooms between about 1:1 and 1:1.8; beyond
  281|     // that they read as corridors that failed to become corridors.
  282|     let aspect = width.max(depth) / width.min(depth).max(0.01);
  283|     let aspect_score = 1.0 - ((aspect - 1.4) / 1.4).abs().min(1.0);
  284| 
  285|     // Space used well: a seat inside a large free territory leaves that
  286|     // territory still usable, while one that half-covers a small territory
  287|     // strands the remainder as a sliver.
  288|     let host = territories
  289|         .iter()
  290|         .filter(|t| {
  291|             let (cx, cz) = t.center();
  292|             (cx - center.0).abs() < t.width() * 0.5 + width * 0.5
  293|                 && (cz - center.1).abs() < t.depth() * 0.5 + depth * 0.5
  294|         })
  295|         .map(|t| t.area())
  296|         .fold(0.0f32, f32::max);
  297|     let fit_score = if host > 0.0 {
  298|         (area / host).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
  299|     } else {
  300|         0.35
  301|     };
  302| 
  303|     // Separation from the same program: five open offices in a row is a
  304|     // tiled floorplan, which is the failure mode this whole pass exists to
  305|     // avoid. Distance to the nearest same-program room, saturating at 24 u.
  306|     let separation = placed
  307|         .iter()
  308|         .filter(|other| other.program == program)
  309|         .map(|other| {
  310|             let b = other.footprint.bounds();
  311|             let c = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
  312|             (c.0 - center.0).hypot(c.1 - center.1)
  313|         })
  314|         .fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
  315|     let separation_score = if separation.is_finite() {
  316|         (separation / 24.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
  317|     } else {
  318|         1.0
  319|     };
  320| 
  321|     0.30 * area_score + 0.25 * aspect_score + 0.20 * fit_score + 0.25 * separation_score
  322| }
  323| 
  324| /// Floor area each program is planned around, m^2. Drawn from ordinary
  325| /// commercial space standards rather than tuned: the point of the term is
  326| /// to stop a server room from taking the biggest bay on the floor.
  327| fn ideal_area(program: SpaceProgram) -> f32 {
  328|     match program {
  329|         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 220.0,
  330|         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 90.0,
  331|         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 70.0,
  332|         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 80.0,
  333|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 45.0,
  334|         SpaceProgram::Storage => 55.0,
  335|         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 60.0,
  336|         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 300.0,
  337|         SpaceProgram::Reception => 110.0,
  338|         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 40.0,
  339|         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 50.0,
  340|         _ => 100.0,
  341|     }
  342| }
