--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/region_plan/layout.rs: 398 lines, showed 1-398 ---

layout.rs analysis:
- `lay_out_suites`: for each round (2) × program (11) × legs (L) × anchors (leg length/2u ≈ 35) × 2 sides → candidates C ≈ 2×11×L×~35×2. Each candidate calls `place_suite` (need to check cost in suites.rs) and then:
  - `taken.iter().any(...)` → O(|taken|) — taken grows up to ~20. 
  - `score_placement` → `territories.iter().filter(...)` O(|T|) + `placed.iter().filter(...)` O(|placed|).
  - `entrance_faces_route(spines, ...)` — check suites.rs.
  So per-candidate cost is O(|taken| + |territories| + |placed| + spines). Total: C × (T + P). With C ~ thousands, T ~ tens, P ~ tens — that's fine (no blowup). This is not quadratic in any large variable; region planning is bounded. It's a greedy solver, documented as such. Overall region plan is constant-ish per region (bounded region size). OK.

The `taken` Vec linear scan: with ~20-30 taken entries and ~1500 candidates, it's ~30k ops per program... total maybe a few hundred thousand — fine for a one-time per-region plan. Low severity at most. Actually wait — candidates: legs up to maybe 6, anchors per leg ~ (80-8)/2 = 36, ×2 sides = ~432 per program per round; 11 programs × 2 rounds = 22 → ~9500 candidates × (taken scan ~20 + score ~50) ≈ 665k ops per region. Fine.

But `place_suite` is called per candidate and may do its own overlap checks. Let me read suites.rs — the biggest region_plan file (34k).
    1| //! Program masses beside the dominant route: suite placement, structure,
    2| //! ceilings, fixtures, and sparse interior partitioning.
    3| 
    4| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
    5| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;

    7| use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, PLAN_WALL_T, snap};

    9| fn ceiling_height_for(program: SpaceProgram, aseed: f32) -> f32 {
   10|     match program {
   11|         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 4.8 + 0.6 * aseed,
   12|         // Compression is a deliberate contrast, never the default ceiling.
   13|         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom | SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 2.6 + 0.2 * aseed,
   14|         SpaceProgram::Storage | SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 3.0 + 0.3 * aseed,
   15|         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 3.5 + 0.7 * aseed,
   16|         _ => 3.2 + 0.5 * aseed,
   17|     }
   18| }
   19| 
   20| /// Splits a room's flat ceiling into authored bands.
   21| ///
   22| /// One height across a whole room is a specification, not a design. Level 0
   23| /// is described by its *contrast* -- compression against expanse -- and the
   24| /// canon reads that way at room scale too: carpet runs deep under arches and
   25| /// shallow between pillars, ceilings drop and lift as you cross a space.
   26| ///
   27| /// The band is a deliberate violation of the room's own baseline, which is
   28| /// what makes it read as authored rather than noisy: the room states a
   29| /// height, then contradicts it once, across a strip you walk through. Two
   30| /// contradictions in one room would just be a bumpy ceiling.
   31| ///
   32| /// Which contradiction depends on the designer. A mechanical-heavy hand
   33| /// (`ExposedSoffit`) drops a soffit; anyone else lifts the band instead,
   34| /// because a raised centre is what an architect does with a room they are
   35| /// proud of. Rooms too small to carry a band keep their single zone -- a
   36| /// strip needs room on both sides or it is just a lower ceiling.
   37| fn ceiling_bands_for(
   38|     footprint: &Polygon2,
   39|     base: CeilingZone,
   40|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
   41|     aseed: f32,
   42| ) -> CeilingPlan {
   43|     /// Fraction of rooms that get a band at all. Most ceilings stay flat,
   44|     /// so the ones that do not are events.
   45|     const BAND_SHARE: f32 = 0.45;
   46|     /// Shortest room side that can carry a band across it.
   47|     const MIN_SIDE: f32 = 8.0;
   48| 
   49|     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
   50|     let (width, depth) = (x1 - x0, z1 - z0);
   51|     if width.min(depth) < MIN_SIDE || keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA4D) > BAND_SHARE {
   52|         return CeilingPlan::flat(base);
   53|     }
   54| 
   55|     // The band crosses the room's *long* axis, so it is something you pass
   56|     // under rather than a lower corner you never visit.
   57|     let long_x = width >= depth;
   58|     let span = if long_x { width } else { depth };
   59|     let band_width = snap((span * (0.22 + 0.16 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA5E))).clamp(2.4, 9.6));
   60|     // Kept off the room's ends, so the band never merges with a wall.
   61|     let free = span - band_width - 2.0 * PLAN_WALL_T;
   62|     if free <= 0.0 {
   63|         return CeilingPlan::flat(base);
   64|     }
   65|     let offset = snap(PLAN_WALL_T + free * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA60));
   66| 
   67|     let (band_area, drop) = if long_x {
   68|         (Polygon2::rect(x0 + offset, z0, band_width, depth), true)
   69|     } else {
   70|         (Polygon2::rect(x0, z0 + offset, width, band_width), true)
   71|     };
   72|     let _ = drop;
   73| 
   74|     let compress = genome.ceiling_language == CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit;
   75|     let height = if compress {
   76|         // Never below head height plus a margin; a soffit you cannot walk
   77|         // under is a wall.
   78|         (base.height_units - 0.8 - 0.4 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA61)).max(2.4)
   79|     } else {
   80|         base.height_units + 0.6 + 0.8 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA61)
   81|     };
   82| 
   83|     CeilingPlan::banded(
   84|         base,
   85|         vec![CeilingZone {
   86|             area: band_area,
   87|             language: if compress {
   88|                 CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit
   89|             } else {
   90|                 CeilingLanguage::Coffered
   91|             },
   92|             height_units: height,
   93|         }],
   94|     )
   95| }
   96| 
   97| fn structure_for(genome: &ArchitectGenome, aseed: f32) -> StructuralSystemInstance {
   98|     let bay = snap(4.4 + 1.6 * aseed);
   99|     let (bay_x, bay_z) = match genome.structural_system {
  100|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => (bay * 1.5, bay),
  101|         _ => (bay, bay),
  102|     };
  103|     // A designer with no tolerance for asymmetry (1) centers the column
  104|     // grid on the footprint instead of letting it fall wherever an offset
  105|     // phase lands; one with none of that tolerance (0) keeps today's
  106|     // freely offset grid.
  107|     let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  108|     let phase = (
  109|         snap(aseed * 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
  110|         snap(aseed * 8.0 % 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
  111|     );
  112|     StructuralSystemInstance {
  113|         system: genome.structural_system,
  114|         bay_x,
  115|         bay_z,
  116|         phase,
  117|         column_side: 0.4,
  118|     }
  119| }
  120| 
  121| /// Fixtures for a rectangular footprint in the genome's lighting language.
  122| fn fixtures_for(
  123|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  124|     footprint: &Polygon2,
  125|     lit: bool,
  126|     aseed: f32,
  127| ) -> Vec<Fixture> {
  128|     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
  129|     let mut out = Vec::new();
  130|     match genome.lighting_language {
  131|         LightingLanguage::GridPanels => {
  132|             let step = 2.4;
  133|             let mut z = z0 + 1.2;
  134|             while z < z1 - 0.8 {
  135|                 let mut x = x0 + 1.2;
  136|                 while x < x1 - 0.8 {
  137|                     out.push(Fixture {
  138|                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(z)),
  139|                         half_x: 0.4,
  140|                         half_z: 0.4,
  141|                         lit,
  142|                     });
  143|                     x += step;
  144|                 }
  145|                 z += step;
  146|             }
  147|         }
  148|         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation => {
  149|             // Strips run down the room's long axis.
  150|             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
  151|             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
  152|             let step = 3.2;
  153|             if long_x {
  154|                 let mut x = x0 + 1.6;
  155|                 while x < x1 - 1.2 {
  156|                     out.push(Fixture {
  157|                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(cz)),
  158|                         half_x: 1.0,
  159|                         half_z: 0.25,
  160|                         lit,
  161|                     });
  162|                     x += step;
  163|                 }
  164|             } else {
  165|                 let mut z = z0 + 1.6;
  166|                 while z < z1 - 1.2 {
  167|                     out.push(Fixture {
  168|                         at: Position::new(snap(cx), snap(z)),
  169|                         half_x: 0.25,
  170|                         half_z: 1.0,
  171|                         lit,
  172|                     });
  173|                     z += step;
  174|                 }
  175|             }
  176|         }
  177|         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants => {
  178|             let n = 1 + (aseed * 2.0) as i32;
  179|             // A designer with high tolerance for symmetry mirrors and
  180|             // centers pendants along the room's long axis instead of
  181|             // scattering them by golden-ratio jitter; `tol` blends between
  182|             // the two rather than switching sharply between them.
  183|             let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  184|             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
  185|             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
  186|             for k in 0..n {
  187|                 let jx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.618 + aseed) % 1.0));
  188|                 let jz = z0 + (z1 - z0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.382 + aseed * 2.0) % 1.0));
  189|                 let centered = if n > 1 {
  190|                     k as f32 / (n - 1) as f32 - 0.5
  191|                 } else {
  192|                     0.0
  193|                 };
  194|                 let (sx, sz) = if long_x {
  195|                     (cx + centered * (x1 - x0) * 0.6, cz)
  196|                 } else {
  197|                     (cx, cz + centered * (z1 - z0) * 0.6)
  198|                 };
  199|                 let fx = jx + (sx - jx) * tol;
  200|                 let fz = jz + (sz - jz) * tol;
  201|                 out.push(Fixture {
  202|                     at: Position::new(snap(fx), snap(fz)),
  203|                     half_x: 0.3,
  204|                     half_z: 0.3,
  205|                     lit,
  206|                 });
  207|             }
  208|         }
  209|     }
  210|     out
  211| }
  212| 
  213| /// Recursively divide a program envelope along its dominant axis. This is a
  214| /// small shape grammar, not a random room packer: every child remains inside
  215| /// its parent, split planes snap to the plan lattice, and stable path keys
  216| /// make the result independent of traversal, chunks, and voxel resolution.
  217| #[derive(Default)]
  218| struct SpaceLayout {
  219|     spaces: Vec<Space>,
  220|     partitions: Vec<(Position, Position)>,
  221| }
  222| 
  223| #[cfg(test)]
  224| fn spaces_for(
  225|     program: SpaceProgram,
  226|     footprint: &Polygon2,
  227|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  228|     aseed: f32,
  229| ) -> Vec<Space> {
  230|     space_layout_for(program, footprint, genome, aseed).spaces
  231| }
  232| 
  233| fn space_layout_for(
  234|     program: SpaceProgram,
  235|     footprint: &Polygon2,
  236|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  237|     aseed: f32,
  238| ) -> SpaceLayout {
  239|     if !matches!(
  240|         program,
  241|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice | SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom
  242|     ) {
  243|         return SpaceLayout::default();
  244|     }
  245|     let split_threshold = (1.0 - genome.partition_density).clamp(0.05, 0.95);
  246|     if aseed <= split_threshold {
  247|         return SpaceLayout::default();
  248|     }
  249| 
  250|     let rule = SubdivisionRule {
  251|         target_side: (genome.room_proportions.min_side * 0.42).clamp(4.0, 7.2),
  252|         max_depth: 1 + (genome.partition_density.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.5) as u8,
  253|         seed: aseed,
  254|     };
  255|     let mut leaves = Vec::new();
  256|     let mut partitions = Vec::new();
  257|     subdivide_space(
  258|         footprint.bounds(),
  259|         0,
  260|         1,
  261|         &rule,
  262|         &mut leaves,
  263|         &mut partitions,
  264|     );
  265|     if leaves.len() <= 1 {
  266|         return SpaceLayout::default();
  267|     }
  268|     SpaceLayout {
  269|         spaces: leaves
  270|             .into_iter()
  271|             .map(|(x0, z0, x1, z1)| Space {
  272|                 program,
  273|                 footprint: Polygon2::rect(x0, z0, x1 - x0, z1 - z0),
  274|             })
  275|             .collect(),
  276|         partitions,
  277|     }
  278| }
  279| 
  280| struct SubdivisionRule {
  281|     target_side: f32,
  282|     max_depth: u8,
  283|     seed: f32,
  284| }
  285| 
  286| fn subdivide_space(
  287|     bounds: (f32, f32, f32, f32),
  288|     depth: u8,
  289|     path: u32,
  290|     rule: &SubdivisionRule,
  291|     leaves: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
  292|     partitions: &mut Vec<(Position, Position)>,
  293| ) {
  294|     let width = bounds.2 - bounds.0;
  295|     let depth_units = bounds.3 - bounds.1;
  296|     let split_x = width >= depth_units;
  297|     let span = if split_x { width } else { depth_units };
  298|     if depth >= rule.max_depth || span < rule.target_side * 2.05 {
  299|         leaves.push(bounds);
  300|         return;
  301|     }
  302| 
  303|     let jitter = keyed_unit(rule.seed, path) - 0.5;
  304|     let split = (span * (0.5 + jitter * 0.16) / 0.4).round() * 0.4;
  305|     if split < rule.target_side || span - split < rule.target_side {
  306|         leaves.push(bounds);
  307|         return;
  308|     }
  309|     let (a, b) = if split_x {
  310|         let plane = bounds.0 + split;
  311|         partitions.push((
  312|             Position::new(plane, bounds.1),
  313|             Position::new(plane, bounds.3),
  314|         ));
  315|         (
  316|             (bounds.0, bounds.1, plane, bounds.3),
  317|             (plane, bounds.1, bounds.2, bounds.3),
  318|         )
  319|     } else {
  320|         let plane = bounds.1 + split;
  321|         partitions.push((
  322|             Position::new(bounds.0, plane),
  323|             Position::new(bounds.2, plane),
  324|         ));
  325|         (
  326|             (bounds.0, bounds.1, bounds.2, plane),
  327|             (bounds.0, plane, bounds.2, bounds.3),
  328|         )
  329|     };
  330|     subdivide_space(a, depth + 1, path << 1, rule, leaves, partitions);
  331|     subdivide_space(b, depth + 1, path << 1 | 1, rule, leaves, partitions);
  332| }
  333| 
  334| fn keyed_unit(seed: f32, key: u32) -> f32 {
  335|     let mut value = seed.to_bits() ^ key.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9);
  336|     value ^= value >> 16;
  337|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
  338|     value ^= value >> 13;
  339|     (value >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
  340| }
  341| 
  342| /// Whether an interior partition would run into an opening and seal it.
  343| ///
  344| /// Subdivision and the openings are derived independently, so nothing stops
  345| /// a partition plane from landing on a doorway: the opening is cut
  346| /// correctly and then a wall is built across it, perpendicular, from the
  347| /// inside. The room reads as walled shut and the plan's whole reachability
  348| /// argument fails at its first step. Observed as soon as rooms are placed
  349| /// densely: entrance on HostId(0) at x=11.20 with a Partition at x=11.20
  350| /// running through it.
  351| fn blocks_opening(start: Position, end: Position, opening: &Opening) -> bool {
  352|     let partition_is_horizontal = (start.z - end.z).abs() <= 1e-4;
  353|     // `through_x_wall` means you walk through it along Z, so the opening
  354|     // sits on a wall parallel to X and its clear span runs along X. A
  355|     // partition threatens it only when it runs the other way.
  356|     if partition_is_horizontal == opening.through_x_wall {
  357|         return false;
  358|     }
  359|     let (plane, along) = if partition_is_horizontal {
  360|         (start.z, opening.center.z)
  361|     } else {
  362|         (start.x, opening.center.x)
  363|     };
  364|     if (plane - along).abs() >= opening.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T {
  365|         return false;
  366|     }
  367|     // The plane alone is not enough: the partition must actually reach the
  368|     // opening's wall to seal it. One on the far side of the room merely
  369|     // sharing a coordinate with the doorway is not in its way.
  370|     let (near, far, wall) = if partition_is_horizontal {
  371|         (start.x.min(end.x), start.x.max(end.x), opening.center.x)
  372|     } else {
  373|         (start.z.min(end.z), start.z.max(end.z), opening.center.z)
  374|     };
  375|     near - PLAN_WALL_T <= wall && wall <= far + PLAN_WALL_T
  376| }
  377| 
  378| /// Lower a suite's room subdivision into explicit wall hosts and hosted
  379| /// openings. The recursive/automata layer can rewrite these elements later;
  380| /// voxel sampling no longer has to rediscover partitions from rectangles.
  381| fn hosts_and_openings_for(
  382|     footprint: &Polygon2,
  383|     partition_segments: &[(Position, Position)],
  384|     ceiling_units: f32,
  385|     entrance: Opening,
  386|     partition_density: f32,
  387|     grammar_seed: f32,
  388| ) -> (Vec<HostSegment>, Vec<Opening>) {
  389|     let mut hosts = HostSegment::rectangular_shell(footprint, PLAN_WALL_T, ceiling_units);
  390|     let mut openings = vec![entrance];
  391| 
  392|     // A short totalistic cellular automaton acts as a renovation/demolition
  393|     // pass over the partition graph. It can merge neighboring program cells,
  394|     // but never touches the shell and never creates an unpierced retained
  395|     // partition, so topology stays legible and walkable.
  396|     let retained = evolve_partitions(partition_segments, partition_density, grammar_seed);
  397|     for (&(start, end), retain) in partition_segments.iter().zip(retained) {
  398|         // Checked against every opening accepted so far, not just the
  399|         // entrance: two partitions can collide with each other's doorways
  400|         // exactly as one can collide with the shell's.
  401|         if retain && !openings.iter().any(|o| blocks_opening(start, end, o)) {
  402|             let host_id = HostId(hosts.len() as u32);
  403|             let horizontal = (start.z - end.z).abs() <= 1e-4;
  404|             let center = Position::new((start.x + end.x) * 0.5, (start.z + end.z) * 0.5);
  405|             hosts.push(HostSegment {
  406|                 id: host_id,
  407|                 start,
  408|                 end,
  409|                 thickness: PLAN_WALL_T,
  410|                 base_units: 0.0,
  411|                 top_units: ceiling_units,
  412|                 role: HostRole::Partition,
  413|             });
  414|             openings.push(Opening {
  415|                 id: OpeningId(openings.len() as u32),
  416|                 host: host_id,
  417|                 role: OpeningRole::Interior,
  418|                 center,
  419|                 width: super::DOOR_WIDTH,
  420|                 through_x_wall: horizontal,
--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/region_plan/suites.rs: 891 lines, showed 1-420 ---

  420|                 through_x_wall: horizontal,
  421|                 lintel_units: Some(super::DOOR_HEIGHT),
  422|             });
  423|         }
  424|     }
  425|     (hosts, openings)
  426| }
  427| 
  428| fn point_on_segment(point: Position, segment: (Position, Position)) -> bool {
  429|     const EPSILON: f32 = 1e-4;
  430|     if (segment.0.z - segment.1.z).abs() <= EPSILON {
  431|         (point.z - segment.0.z).abs() <= EPSILON
  432|             && point.x >= segment.0.x.min(segment.1.x) - EPSILON
  433|             && point.x <= segment.0.x.max(segment.1.x) + EPSILON
  434|     } else {
  435|         (point.x - segment.0.x).abs() <= EPSILON
  436|             && point.z >= segment.0.z.min(segment.1.z) - EPSILON
  437|             && point.z <= segment.0.z.max(segment.1.z) + EPSILON
  438|     }
  439| }
  440| 
  441| fn segments_touch(a: (Position, Position), b: (Position, Position)) -> bool {
  442|     point_on_segment(a.0, b)
  443|         || point_on_segment(a.1, b)
  444|         || point_on_segment(b.0, a)
  445|         || point_on_segment(b.1, a)
  446| }
  447| 
  448| fn evolve_partitions(segments: &[(Position, Position)], density: f32, seed: f32) -> Vec<bool> {
  449|     if segments.is_empty() {
  450|         return Vec::new();
  451|     }
  452|     let survival = (0.25 + density.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 0.75).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  453|     let mut state: Vec<bool> = segments
  454|         .iter()
  455|         .enumerate()
  456|         .map(|(index, _)| keyed_unit(seed, index as u32 ^ 0xA170) < survival)
  457|         .collect();
  458|     for _ in 0..2 {
  459|         state = segments
  460|             .iter()
  461|             .enumerate()
  462|             .map(|(index, segment)| {
  463|                 let neighbours = segments
  464|                     .iter()
  465|                     .enumerate()
  466|                     .filter(|(other_index, other)| {
  467|                         *other_index != index && segments_touch(*segment, **other)
  468|                     })
  469|                     .filter(|(other_index, _)| state[*other_index])
  470|                     .count();
  471|                 if state[index] {
  472|                     neighbours <= 3
  473|                 } else {
  474|                     neighbours == 2
  475|                 }
  476|             })
  477|             .collect();
  478|     }
  479|     if !state.iter().any(|retained| *retained) {
  480|         let fallback = (keyed_unit(seed, 0xFA11) * segments.len() as f32) as usize;
  481|         state[fallback.min(segments.len() - 1)] = true;
  482|     }
  483|     state
  484| }
  485| 
  486| pub(super) fn aabb_overlap(a: (f32, f32, f32, f32), b: (f32, f32, f32, f32), gap: f32) -> bool {
  487|     a.0 < b.2 + gap && b.0 < a.2 + gap && a.1 < b.3 + gap && b.1 < a.3 + gap
  488| }
  489| 
  490| /// Does an opening at `(x, z)` read as a door onto a route?
  491| ///
  492| /// Two conditions, and the second is the one that is easy to miss: the
  493| /// opening must sit in *some* corridor's wall band -- outside the clear
  494| /// width, inside the band beyond it -- and inside *no* corridor's clear
  495| /// width. Corridors cross, so an entrance correctly banded against the run
  496| /// its room hangs off can still sit squarely inside a perpendicular one.
  497| /// There, `compose_column` takes the circulation branch before it ever
  498| /// reaches the assembly: the column is carved full height and the doorway
  499| /// loses the lintel that makes it read as a door rather than a gap.
  500| ///
  501| /// Checking only "is banded against some corridor" is what let that
  502| /// through; both callers that place doors need the same answer, so they
  503| /// share this one.
  504| pub(super) fn entrance_faces_route(
  505|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  506|     x: f32,
  507|     z: f32,
  508|     wall_thickness: f32,
  509| ) -> bool {
  510|     let mut banded = false;
  511|     for spine in spines {
  512|         let d = spine.distance(x, z);
  513|         let half = spine.width * 0.5;
  514|         // Matches `compose_column`'s own test for "this column belongs to
  515|         // circulation", so the two can never disagree about a threshold.
  516|         if d <= half {
  517|             return false;
  518|         }
  519|         if d <= half + wall_thickness + 0.05 {
  520|             banded = true;
  521|         }
  522|     }
  523|     banded
  524| }
  525| 
  526| /// Places one suite beside a horizontal corridor segment. Returns `None` if
  527| /// the footprint would leave the region, collide with a prior assembly, or
  528| /// cross another corridor.
  529| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  530| pub(super) fn place_suite(
  531|     id: u32,
  532|     program: SpaceProgram,
  533|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  534|     aseed: f32,
  535|     threshold_seed: f32,
  536|     cursor_x: f32,
  537|     corridor_z: f32,
  538|     corridor_half: f32,
  539|     side: f32, // +1 = suite on +Z side of corridor, -1 = -Z side
  540|     origin: Position,
  541|     size: f32,
  542|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
  543|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  544| ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
  545|     let p = &genome.room_proportions;
  546|     let w = snap((p.min_side + (p.max_side - p.min_side) * aseed).clamp(12.0, 24.0));
  547|     let d = snap((w * (0.72 - 0.28 * p.elongation)).clamp(8.0, 18.0));
  548| 
  549|     let x0 = snap(cursor_x);
  550|     // Wall centerlines may occupy the half-step of the 0.4-unit plan lattice:
  551|     // coarse voxel centers live there too. Snapping this midpoint back to a
  552|     // full step can move the shell outside the corridor wall it is hosting.
  553|     let z_front = if side > 0.0 {
  554|         corridor_z + corridor_half
  555|     } else {
  556|         corridor_z - corridor_half - d
  557|     };
  558|     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, w, d);
  559|     let b = footprint.bounds();
  560| 
  561|     // Stay inside the region with margin.
  562|     if b.0 < origin.x + EDGE_MARGIN
  563|         || b.1 < origin.z + EDGE_MARGIN
  564|         || b.2 > origin.x + size - EDGE_MARGIN
  565|         || b.3 > origin.z + size - EDGE_MARGIN
  566|     {
  567|         return None;
  568|     }
  569|     if taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.8)) {
  570|         return None;
  571|     }
  572|     // Don't let a suite swallow a *different* corridor (its front corridor
  573|     // touching the footprint edge is fine and expected).
  574|     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
  575|     for s in spines {
  576|         if s.distance(center.0, center.1) < s.width * 0.5 + d.min(w) * 0.25 {
  577|             return None;
  578|         }
  579|     }
  580| 
  581|     // Entrance on the corridor-facing wall. The genome biases the language,
  582|     // but a narrow framed door is only about 8--14% of thresholds globally.
  583|     // Most fronts dissolve into a room through an unframed or broad portal.
  584|     let threshold = match genome.threshold_language {
  585|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.14 => {
  586|             ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel
  587|         }
  588|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.08 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
  589|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
  590|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.62 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
  591|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
  592|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
  593|         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
  594|     };
  595|     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
  596|     let (width, lintel) = match threshold {
  597|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel => (super::DOOR_WIDTH, Some(super::DOOR_HEIGHT)),
  598|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal => (4.8, None),
  599|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal => (3.6, Some(3.0)),
  600|     };
  601|     let edge = width * 0.5 + 0.8;
  602|     let door_x = snap((b.0 + w * (0.25 + 0.5 * threshold_seed)).clamp(b.0 + edge, b.2 - edge));
  603|     let ceiling = CeilingZone {
  604|         area: footprint.clone(),
  605|         language: genome.ceiling_language,
  606|         height_units: ceiling_height_for(program, aseed),
  607|     };
  608|     let layout = space_layout_for(program, &footprint, genome, aseed);
  609|     let entrance = Opening {
  610|         id: OpeningId(0),
  611|         host: if side > 0.0 { HostId(0) } else { HostId(2) },
  612|         role: OpeningRole::Entrance,
  613|         center: Position::new(door_x, front_z),
  614|         width,
  615|         through_x_wall: true,
  616|         lintel_units: lintel,
  617|     };
  618|     let door_leaves = if threshold == ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel {
  619|         vec![DoorLeaf {
  620|             opening: entrance.id,
  621|         }]
  622|     } else {
  623|         Vec::new()
  624|     };
  625|     let (hosts, openings) = hosts_and_openings_for(
  626|         &footprint,
  627|         &layout.partitions,
  628|         ceiling.height_units,
  629|         entrance,
  630|         genome.partition_density,
  631|         aseed,
  632|     );
  633|     Some(AssemblyInstance {
  634|         id,
  635|         program,
  636|         spaces: layout.spaces,
  637|         structure: structure_for(genome, aseed),
  638|         ceiling: ceiling_bands_for(&footprint, ceiling, genome, aseed),
  639|         fixtures: fixtures_for(genome, &footprint, true, aseed),
  640|         service_voids: Vec::new(),
  641|         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
  642|         hosts,
  643|         openings,
  644|         door_leaves,
  645|         footprint,
  646|     })
  647| }

  652| 
  653|     fn genome_with(partition_density: f32, tolerance_for_symmetry: f32) -> ArchitectGenome {
  654|         ArchitectGenome {
  655|             circulation: CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
  656|             structural_system: StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,

    1| //! The Backrooms corruption pass: the plan was sane; the building is not.
    2| //!
    3| //! Duplicated suites, abandoned expansions, renovation overlays, and the
    4| //! realization of macro-graph red-room events on eligible assemblies.
    5| 
    6| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
    7| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
    8| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
    9| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   10| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;

   12| 
   13| use super::suites::{aabb_overlap, entrance_faces_route, place_suite};

   15| 
   16| /// Backrooms corruption: the plan was sane; the building is not. Pure
   17| /// sequencing over four independent rules, each its own named function so
   18| /// any one of them is testable without the other three — previously all
   19| /// four were inlined together sharing one hash-key closure, which made it
   20| /// impossible to exercise, say, just the abandonment rule in isolation.
   21| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   22| pub(super) fn corrupt(
   23|     seed: u32,
   24|     rx: i64,
   25|     rz: i64,
   26|     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
   27|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
   28|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   29|     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
   30|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
   31|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
   32| ) {
   33|     if assemblies.is_empty() {
   34|         return;
   35|     }
   36|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0DE + k, rx, rz]);
   37| 
   38|     if h(1) < 0.6 {
   39|         let src = pick_index(h(2), assemblies.len());
   40|         let shift = snap(12.0 + 12.0 * h(3));
   41|         let dup = duplication_skews(&assemblies[src], spines)
   42|             .into_iter()
   43|             .find_map(|skew| {
   44|                 duplication_offsets(shift).into_iter().find_map(|offset| {
   45|                     duplicate_suite_candidate(
   46|                         assemblies,
   47|                         taken,
   48|                         spines,
   49|                         rx,
   50|                         rz,
   51|                         src,
   52|                         snap(offset),
   53|                         skew,
   54|                     )
   55|                 })
   56|             });
   57|         if let Some(dup) = dup {
   58|             taken.push(dup.footprint.bounds());
   59|             assemblies.push(dup);
   60|         }
   61|     }
   62| 
   63|     if h(6) < 0.6 {
   64|         let k = pick_index(h(7), assemblies.len());
   65|         abandon_assembly(&mut assemblies[k]);
   66|     }
   67| 
   68|     apply_renovation_history(dominant.renovation_history, assemblies, h(8), h(9));
   69| 
   70|     // Applied last so it respects whatever the earlier passes decided (an
   71|     // abandoned shell stays dark).
   72|     let sp = spawn_point(seed);
   73|     let forced_in_spawn_region = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom)
   74|         && rx == region_index(sp.x)
   75|         && rz == region_index(sp.z);
   76|     let red_room_realized = forced_in_spawn_region
   77|         && force_red_room_in_spawn_region(dominant, rx, rz, assemblies, taken, spines);
   78|     if !red_room_realized {
   79|         let red_room_scale = config.anomalies.frequency * config.anomalies.red_rooms;
   80|         realize_red_room_event(seed, noise, rx, rz, red_room_scale, assemblies);
   81|     }
   82| }
   83| 
   84| /// Longitudinal offsets a duplicate is tried at, in preference order.
   85| ///
   86| /// The authored distance first, then further down the corridor, then closer
   87| /// than authored. A fixed ladder of six offsets was enough when a region
   88| /// held two suites and the floor was mostly empty; against a floor the
   89| /// placement solver has actually laid out, every one of them lands on a
   90| /// neighbour, and duplication -- the most recognizably Backrooms corruption
   91| /// there is -- silently stopped happening in all 36 test regions. Sweeping
   92| /// finds whatever gap the solver left instead of guessing where one might
   93| /// be, and keeping the authored distance first means the seed still decides
   94| /// where the copy *wants* to sit; the sweep only decides where it can.
   95| fn duplication_offsets(shift: f32) -> Vec<f32> {
   96|     let authored = shift.abs().max(DUPLICATE_STEP);
   97|     let mut out = Vec::new();
   98|     let mut d = authored;
   99|     while d <= DUPLICATE_MAX_OFFSET {
  100|         out.push(d);
  101|         out.push(-d);
  102|         d += DUPLICATE_STEP;
  103|     }
  104|     let mut d = authored - DUPLICATE_STEP;
  105|     while d >= DUPLICATE_STEP {
  106|         out.push(d);
  107|         out.push(-d);
  108|         d -= DUPLICATE_STEP;
  109|     }
  110|     out
  111| }
  112| 
  113| /// Sweep pitch for duplicate offsets. Matches the placement solver's anchor
  114| /// pitch, so a gap the solver could seat a room in is one this can find.
  115| const DUPLICATE_STEP: f32 = 2.0;
  116| 
  117| /// Perpendicular offsets a duplicate is tried at: its own corridor first,
  118| /// then every other parallel run in the region.
  119| ///
  120| /// Staying on the source's own corridor run is the cleanest repetition, but
  121| /// it is also where there is least space -- the placement solver has
  122| /// already seated rooms along that leg, and a copy needs as much clearance
  123| /// as any other room. The free space is on the *other* runs. Moving the
  124| /// copy by the centerline distance between two parallel corridors lands it
  125| /// at the same offset from its new corridor as it had from its old, so the
  126| /// entrance stays in a wall band and faces a route; `duplicate_suite_candidate`
  127| /// re-checks that rather than trusting it.
  128| fn duplication_skews(source: &AssemblyInstance, spines: &[CirculationSpine]) -> Vec<f32> {
  129|     let mut out = vec![0.0];
  130|     let Some(entrance) = source.primary_entrance() else {
  131|         return out;
  132|     };
  133|     // The centerline the source's entrance actually sits against.
  134|     let Some(host_z) = spines
  135|         .iter()
  136|         .flat_map(|s| s.path.windows(2))
  137|         .filter(|seg| (seg[0].z - seg[1].z).abs() <= 1e-4)
  138|         .map(|seg| seg[0].z)
  139|         .min_by(|a, b| {
  140|             (a - entrance.center.z)
  141|                 .abs()
  142|                 .total_cmp(&(b - entrance.center.z).abs())
  143|         })
  144|     else {
  145|         return out;
  146|     };
  147|     let mut targets: Vec<f32> = spines
  148|         .iter()
  149|         .flat_map(|s| s.path.windows(2))
  150|         .filter(|seg| (seg[0].z - seg[1].z).abs() <= 1e-4)
  151|         .map(|seg| seg[0].z - host_z)
  152|         .filter(|skew| skew.abs() > 1e-4)
  153|         .collect();
  154|     // Nearest parallel run first, and deterministic: two queries of this
  155|     // region must order the candidates identically.
  156|     targets.sort_by(|a, b| a.abs().total_cmp(&b.abs()));
  157|     targets.dedup_by(|a, b| (*a - *b).abs() < 1e-4);
  158|     out.extend(targets);
  159|     out
  160| }
  161| 
  162| /// How far down the corridor a copy may sit from its source. Beyond a
  163| /// region there is no shared corridor to repeat along.
  164| const DUPLICATE_MAX_OFFSET: f32 = REGION_SIZE;
  165| 
  166| /// Rule 1: a suite repeats itself further down the corridor, slightly wrong.
  167| /// Pure — reads the existing plan, returns the candidate duplicate (already
  168| /// translated, with its misalignment recorded) or `None` if it would fall
  169| /// outside the region, overlap something already placed, or seal itself
  170| /// away from every corridor. The caller decides whether to keep it.
  171| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  172| fn duplicate_suite_candidate(
  173|     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
  174|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
  175|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  176|     rx: i64,
  177|     rz: i64,
  178|     src: usize,
  179|     shift: f32,
  180|     skew: f32,
  181| ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
  182|     // `skew` moves the copy between parallel corridor runs, never off a
  183|     // corridor: the repetition is wrong in its position, not sealed away
  184|     // behind an accidental strip of wall. The `reachable` check below is
  185|     // what actually enforces that.
  186|     let mut dup = assemblies[src].clone();
  187|     dup.translate(shift, skew);
  188|     dup.id = assemblies.len() as u32 + 1000;
  189|     dup.corruption.misalignment = (shift, skew);
  190| 
  191|     let b = dup.footprint.bounds();
  192|     let inside = b.0 > rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
  193|         && b.2 < (rx + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN
  194|         && b.1 > rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
  195|         && b.3 < (rz + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN;
  196|     // The moved entrance must still read as a door onto a route, or the
  197|     // copy would be a sealed pocket.
  198|     let reachable = dup
  199|         .entrances()
  200|         .any(|e| entrance_faces_route(spines, e.center.x, e.center.z, PLAN_WALL_T));
  201|     // The same clearance the placement solver keeps between rooms, not a
  202|     // looser one. A copy squeezed into a 0.4 u gap is close enough that a
  203|     // neighbour's ceiling fixture samples inside this shell -- which reads
  204|     // as an abandoned expansion that is somehow still lit. Rooms in a real
  205|     // plan either share a wall or stand clear; a duplicate is no exception.
  206|     let clear = !taken
  207|         .iter()
  208|         .any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, super::layout::ROOM_SEPARATION));
  209|     (inside && reachable && clear).then_some(dup)
  210| }
  211| 
  212| /// Rule 2: one assembly was built and then never occupied — an empty shell,
  213| /// nothing lit.
  214| fn abandon_assembly(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
  215|     assembly.program = SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion;
  216|     assembly.corruption.abandoned = true;
  217|     assembly.spaces.clear();
  218|     assembly
  219|         .hosts
  220|         .retain(|host| host.role != HostRole::Partition);
  221|     assembly.openings.retain(|opening| {
  222|         opening.role != OpeningRole::Interior
  223|             && assembly.hosts.iter().any(|host| host.id == opening.host)
  224|     });
  225|     for f in &mut assembly.fixtures {
  226|         f.lit = false;
  227|     }
  228| }
  229| 
  230| /// Rule 3: renovation history overlays the original structural grid. A
  231| /// partial refit contradicts one assembly; a fuller history of layered
  232| /// refits leaves a second, distinct assembly contradicted too — otherwise
  233| /// the two `RenovationStyle` variants would be indistinguishable once
  234| /// generated, despite the type's own doc comment promising more.
  235| fn apply_renovation_history(
  236|     history: RenovationStyle,
  237|     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
  238|     pick1: f32,
  239|     pick2: f32,
  240| ) {
  241|     match history {
  242|         RenovationStyle::Untouched => {}
  243|         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit => {
  244|             let k = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
  245|             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k]);
  246|         }
  247|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => {
  248|             let k1 = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
  249|             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k1]);
  250|             if assemblies.len() > 1 {
  251|                 // Offset from k1 rather than re-rolling, so the second pick
  252|                 // is guaranteed distinct instead of merely likely to be.
  253|                 let k2 = (k1 + 1 + pick_index(pick2, assemblies.len() - 1)) % assemblies.len();
  254|                 overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k2]);
  255|             }
  256|         }
  257|     }
  258| }

  260| /// A renovation overlays the original structural grid on one assembly.
  261| fn overlay_renovation(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
  262|     assembly.corruption.renovation_overlay = true;
  263| }

  265| /// Rule 4a: the debug/authored path. `?force_anomaly=redroom` targets the
  266| /// region the player actually spawns in, so this must succeed there even
  267| /// when nothing qualifies yet — mark an existing occupied assembly if one
  268| /// exists, otherwise place a brand new one against the main corridor.
  269| /// Returns whether a red room was realized.
  270| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  271| fn force_red_room_in_spawn_region(
  272|     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
  273|     rx: i64,
  274|     rz: i64,
  275|     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
  276|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
  277|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  278| ) -> bool {
  279|     if let Some(a) = assemblies
  280|         .iter_mut()
  281|         .find(|a| a.primary_entrance().is_some() && !a.corruption.abandoned)
  282|     {
  283|         a.corruption.red_room = true;
  284|         return true;
  285|     }
  286|     let Some(spine) = spines
  287|         .iter()
  288|         .find(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
  289|     else {
  290|         return false;
  291|     };
  292|     let Some(seg) = spine.path.windows(2).find(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z) else {
  293|         return false;
  294|     };
  295|     let lx0 = seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x);
  296|     let lz = seg[0].z;
  297|     let origin = Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE);
  298|     let Some(mut a) = place_suite(
  299|         9999,
  300|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
  301|         dominant,
  302|         0.5,
  303|         0.5,
  304|         lx0 + 12.0,
  305|         lz,
  306|         spine.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5,
  307|         1.0,
  308|         origin,
  309|         REGION_SIZE,
  310|         taken,
  311|         spines,
  312|     ) else {
  313|         return false;
  314|     };
  315|     a.corruption.red_room = true;
  316|     taken.push(a.footprint.bounds());
  317|     assemblies.push(a);
  318|     true
  319| }
  320| 
  321| /// Rule 4b: the ordinary path. Where a red room happens is a *graph event*,
  322| /// not a per-region coin flip — the macro topology plans separated events on
  323| /// its lattice (`world_topology::red_room_event_for_region`), and this rule
  324| /// merely realizes an event that targets this region on one eligible
  325| /// assembly, rotating from a stable start so the choice replays identically
  326| /// for every query of this region. If no assembly qualifies the event stays
  327| /// unrealized — a planned encounter never overwrites navigable circulation.
  328| fn realize_red_room_event(
  329|     seed: u32,
  330|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  331|     rx: i64,
  332|     rz: i64,
  333|     red_room_scale: f32,
  334|     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
  335| ) {
  336|     let Some(event) = crate::use_cases::world_topology::red_room_event_for_region(
  337|         seed,
  338|         noise,
  339|         rx,
  340|         rz,
  341|         red_room_scale.clamp(0.0, 4.0),
  342|     ) else {
  343|         return;
  344|     };
  345|     let count = assemblies.len();
  346|     let start = (event.id % count as u64) as usize;
  347|     for offset in 0..count {
  348|         let a = &mut assemblies[(start + offset) % count];
  349|         if !a.corruption.abandoned && a.primary_entrance().is_some() {
  350|             a.corruption.red_room = true;
  351|             break;
  352|         }
  353|     }
  354| }

    1| //! Architect genomes: the designers a region inherits.
    2| //!
    3| //! `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator, 2 = intruder. The circulation style
    4| //! comes from low-frequency noise so neighboring regions tend to share a
    5| //! culture; every other property is hash-derived, but *not independently*:
    6| //! a real designer's decisions form a chain, not a set of parallel dice
    7| //! rolls. `structural_system` and `renovation_history` are decided first;
    8| //! everything downstream of them (room proportions, ceiling language,
    9| //! threshold language, furnishing density, tolerance for symmetry) biases
   10| //! toward what that earlier choice implies, with its own hash key still
   11| //! supplying the roll *within* the biased range. A `CoreAndShell` designer
   12| //! who chose that system to achieve big clear-span rooms should get big
   13| //! rooms and a ceiling that doesn't pretend to hide beams it doesn't have;
   14| //! a `DeepSpansWithBeams` designer's ceiling should show the beams that
   15| //! justify the system's name.
   16| 
   17| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
   18| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   19| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   20| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
   21| 
   22| use super::{REGION_SIZE, pick_index};
   23| 
   24| /// Derive one designer for a region. `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator,
   25| /// 2 = intruder. The circulation style comes from low-frequency noise so
   26| /// neighboring regions tend to share a culture; everything else hashes.
   27| pub fn derive_genome(
   28|     seed: u32,
   29|     rx: i64,
   30|     rz: i64,
   31|     salt: i64,
   32|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   33| ) -> ArchitectGenome {
   34|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0x6E0 + salt, rx, rz, k]);
   35|     // ~130 u wavelength: cultures span a few regions.
   36|     let culture = noise.evaluate_2d(
   37|         seed ^ 0xA11C_0DE ^ (salt as u32),
   38|         Position::new(
   39|             (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
   40|             (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
   41|         ),
   42|     );
   43|     let circulation = match ((culture * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999) * 4.0) as u32 {
   44|         0 => CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
   45|         1 => CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine,
   46|         2 => CirculationStyle::PairedBranches,
   47|         _ => CirculationStyle::TreeWithCulDeSacs,
   48|     };
   49|     // ---- site strategy: decided first, everything else answers to it ----
   50|     let structural_system = *[
   51|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
   52|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams,
   53|         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid,
   54|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
   55|     ]
   56|     .get(pick_index(h(1), 4))
   57|     .unwrap();
   58|     let renovation_history = *[
   59|         RenovationStyle::Untouched,
   60|         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit,
   61|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits,
   62|     ]
   63|     .get(pick_index(h(5), 3))
   64|     .unwrap();
   65| 
   66|     // ---- consequences of the structural system --------------------------
   67|     // CoreAndShell and DeepSpansWithBeams are chosen specifically to permit
   68|     // large clear-span rooms (see `suites::on_column`, which gives
   69|     // CoreAndShell zero interior columns); RegularGrid/OffsetGrid bound
   70|     // their rooms to a small structural module instead. Room size is a
   71|     // consequence of that choice, not a second independent roll.
   72|     let spans_wide = matches!(
   73|         structural_system,
   74|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell | StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams
   75|     );
   76|     let (min_lo, min_span, max_lo, max_span) = if spans_wide {
   77|         (16.0, 6.0, 24.0, 10.0)
   78|     } else {
   79|         (12.0, 4.0, 18.0, 6.0)
   80|     };
   81| 
   82|     // A coffered or exposed-soffit ceiling is a description of what a deep
   83|     // beam grid looks like from underneath, not an unrelated stylistic
   84|     // choice — so it should follow from having beams to show. CoreAndShell
   85|     // has no beam grid to express at all; flat tiles are the honest default
   86|     // for it. RegularGrid/OffsetGrid are unbiased: either reads as fine for
   87|     // an ordinary column grid.
   88|     let ceiling_language = match structural_system {
   89|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => match h(3) {
   90|             v if v < 0.55 => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
   91|             v if v < 0.85 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
   92|             _ => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
   93|         },
   94|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => match h(3) {
   95|             v if v < 0.70 => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
   96|             v if v < 0.90 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
   97|             _ => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
   98|         },
   99|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => *[
  100|             CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
  101|             CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
  102|             CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
  103|         ]
  104|         .get(pick_index(h(3), 3))
  105|         .unwrap(),
  106|     };
  107| 
  108|     // A grid that never breaks its own module (Regular, CoreAndShell) reads
  109|     // as more deliberately symmetric than one that already contradicts
  110|     // itself every other row (OffsetGrid).
  111|     let symmetry_bias = match structural_system {
  112|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => 0.25,
  113|         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => -0.20,
  114|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => 0.0,
  115|     };
  116| 
  117|     // ---- consequences of the renovation history --------------------------
  118|     // A framed office door is now an anomaly. The chosen language is only a

  126|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => 0.25,
  127|     };

  129|         v if v < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
  130|         v if v < 0.55 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
  131|         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,

    1| //! Free-space decomposition: what is left of a region once circulation and
    2| //! already-committed masses are removed.
    3| //!
    4| //! Room placement needs somewhere to place rooms. The old cursor walk did
    5| //! without this by sliding along a corridor leg and trying one spot at a
    6| //! time, which is why a region ended up with two suites and 90% unplanned
    7| //! fabric: a spot that failed was simply skipped, and space away from the
    8| //! dominant leg was never considered at all.
    9| //!
   10| //! This produces the candidate set the placement solver scores over:
   11| //! maximal free rectangles, biggest first, each carved out of the free area
   12| //! before the next is found. Rectangles rather than arbitrary polygons
   13| //! because rooms in this building are rectangular, and a candidate that
   14| //! cannot host a room is not a useful candidate.
   15| 
   16| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::CirculationSpine;
   17| 
   18| /// Free-space lattice pitch. Two coarse voxels: fine enough that a wall
   19| /// band cannot hide between samples, coarse enough that a region is a
   20| /// 100x100 grid rather than a 200x200 one.
   21| const CELL: f32 = 0.8;
   22| 
   23| /// Smallest side a territory may have and still be offered as a candidate.
   24| /// Below a corridor's width there is nothing a room could occupy.
   25| const MIN_SIDE: f32 = 3.2;
   26| 
   27| /// An axis-aligned patch of unoccupied region floor, in world units.
   28| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
   29| pub struct Territory {
   30|     pub min_x: f32,
   31|     pub min_z: f32,
   32|     pub max_x: f32,
   33|     pub max_z: f32,
   34| }
   35| 
   36| impl Territory {
   37|     pub fn width(&self) -> f32 {
   38|         self.max_x - self.min_x
   39|     }
   40| 
   41|     pub fn depth(&self) -> f32 {
   42|         self.max_z - self.min_z
   43|     }
   44| 
   45|     pub fn area(&self) -> f32 {
   46|         self.width() * self.depth()
   47|     }
   48| 
   49|     pub fn center(&self) -> (f32, f32) {
   50|         (
   51|             (self.min_x + self.max_x) * 0.5,
   52|             (self.min_z + self.max_z) * 0.5,
   53|         )
   54|     }
   55| 
   56|     /// Only the overlap assertions need a territory as a raw tuple; the
   57|     /// solver scores territories through `center`/`width`/`depth`.
   58|     #[cfg(test)]
   59|     pub fn bounds(&self) -> (f32, f32, f32, f32) {
   60|         (self.min_x, self.min_z, self.max_x, self.max_z)
   61|     }
   62| 
   63|     fn overlaps(&self, other: &(f32, f32, f32, f32)) -> bool {
   64|         self.min_x < other.2 && other.0 < self.max_x && self.min_z < other.3 && other.1 < self.max_z
   65|     }
   66| }
   67| 
   68| /// Decomposes the region's unoccupied floor into candidate territories,
   69| /// largest first.
   70| ///
   71| /// Pure in its inputs, so two chunks asking about the same region get the
   72| /// same answer without coordinating -- the same discipline the rest of the
   73| /// planner keeps.
   74| pub fn free_territories(
   75|     origin_x: f32,
   76|     origin_z: f32,
   77|     region_size: f32,
   78|     corridors: &[CirculationSpine],
   79|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
   80|     edge_margin: f32,
   81|     wall_thickness: f32,
   82| ) -> Vec<Territory> {
   83|     let usable = region_size - 2.0 * edge_margin;
   84|     if usable <= MIN_SIDE {
   85|         return Vec::new();
   86|     }
   87|     let n = (usable / CELL).floor() as usize;
   88|     if n == 0 {
   89|         return Vec::new();
   90|     }
   91|     let base_x = origin_x + edge_margin;
   92|     let base_z = origin_z + edge_margin;
   93| 
   94|     // A cell is free when its centre clears every corridor by half a width
   95|     // plus a wall, and falls in no committed footprint. Corridors are kept
   96|     // clear rather than merely un-overlapped: a room flush against a
   97|     // corridor edge has no wall between it and the route.
   98|     let mut free = vec![true; n * n];
   99|     for iz in 0..n {
  100|         for ix in 0..n {
  101|             let x = base_x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * CELL;
  102|             let z = base_z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * CELL;
  103|             let blocked = corridors
  104|                 .iter()
  105|                 .any(|s| s.distance(x, z) < s.width * 0.5 + wall_thickness)
  106|                 || taken
  107|                     .iter()
  108|                     .any(|b| x >= b.0 && x <= b.2 && z >= b.1 && z <= b.3);
  109|             free[iz * n + ix] = !blocked;
  110|         }
  111|     }
  112| 
  113|     let min_cells = (MIN_SIDE / CELL).ceil() as usize;
  114|     let mut out = Vec::new();
  115|     // Repeatedly take the largest all-free rectangle and remove it. Greedy
  116|     // maximal-rectangle carving, not an exact partition: the aim is a good
  117|     // candidate set for scoring, and the scorer is free to use only part of
  118|     // whatever it is offered.
  119|     while let Some(rect) = largest_free_rectangle(&free, n, min_cells) {
  120|         let (ix0, iz0, ix1, iz1) = rect;
  121|         for iz in iz0..=iz1 {
  122|             for ix in ix0..=ix1 {
  123|                 free[iz * n + ix] = false;
  124|             }
  125|         }
  126|         let territory = Territory {
  127|             min_x: base_x + ix0 as f32 * CELL,
  128|             min_z: base_z + iz0 as f32 * CELL,
  129|             max_x: base_x + (ix1 + 1) as f32 * CELL,
  130|             max_z: base_z + (iz1 + 1) as f32 * CELL,
  131|         };
  132|         if taken.iter().any(|b| territory.overlaps(b)) {
  133|             continue;
  134|         }
  135|         out.push(territory);
  136|         if out.len() >= 64 {
  137|             break;
  138|         }
  139|     }
  140|     out
  141| }
  142| 
  143| /// Largest all-free axis-aligned rectangle in the mask, as inclusive cell
  144| /// indices. Classic largest-rectangle-in-histogram swept down the rows:
  145| /// O(n^2) for the whole grid rather than the O(n^4) of testing every
  146| /// rectangle.
  147| fn largest_free_rectangle(
  148|     free: &[bool],
  149|     n: usize,
  150|     min_cells: usize,
  151| ) -> Option<(usize, usize, usize, usize)> {
  152|     let mut heights = vec![0usize; n];
  153|     let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, usize, usize, usize)> = None; // + area
  154| 
  155|     for iz in 0..n {
  156|         for ix in 0..n {
  157|             heights[ix] = if free[iz * n + ix] {
  158|                 heights[ix] + 1
  159|             } else {
  160|                 0
  161|             };
  162|         }
  163|         // Monotonic stack over this row's histogram.
  164|         let mut stack: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // (start index, height)
  165|         for ix in 0..=n {
  166|             let height = if ix == n { 0 } else { heights[ix] };
  167|             let mut start = ix;
  168|             while let Some(&(top_start, top_height)) = stack.last() {
  169|                 if top_height <= height {
  170|                     break;
  171|                 }
  172|                 stack.pop();
  173|                 let width = ix - top_start;
  174|                 let area = width * top_height;
  175|                 if width >= min_cells
  176|                     && top_height >= min_cells
  177|                     && best.is_none_or(|(_, _, _, _, b)| area > b)
  178|                 {
  179|                     best = Some((top_start, iz + 1 - top_height, ix - 1, iz, area));
  180|                 }
  181|                 start = top_start;
  182|             }
  183|             if ix < n {
  184|                 stack.push((start, height));
  185|             }
  186|         }
  187|     }
  188| 
  189|     best.map(|(x0, z0, x1, z1, _)| (x0, z0, x1, z1))
  190| }

--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/region_plan/territories.rs: 289 lines, showed 1-289 ---

territories.rs analysis — this is a real hotspot:
- `free_territories`: n = 73.6/0.8 ≈ 92 cells per side → free grid 92×92 = 8464 cells. Initial fill: for each cell, scan corridors (C small) and taken (T small) → O(n²·(C+T)). Fine.
- Loop: `while let Some(rect) = largest_free_rectangle(...)` — each iteration is O(n²) (histogram sweep), and it clears the rectangle. In the worst case (e.g., alternating pattern), the number of rectangles carved can be O(n²) → total O(n⁴)! In practice, with corridors, each carve removes a large chunk. Worst case: a checkerboard free/blocked pattern yields rectangles of size min_cells... but the loop caps out at 64 territories (line 136). So bounded by 64 iterations × O(n²) = O(64 n²) = ~5.4M ops worst. Actually largest_free_rectangle is O(n²) per call: n rows × (n pushes/pops) — yes O(n²) = 8464 per call; ×64 = 541k. Fine, bounded. But note: the loop doesn't stop when no rectangle remains... it does stop when None. Each carve clears cells so eventually None. Worst-case iterations bounded by 64 cap. So total is O(64·n²) — acceptable, but worth noting worst-case O(n² · #rectangles) if cap removed.
- Note that free_territories is called per chunk generation?! Let me check: `generate_region_plan` is called from... where? infinite_level / world_block — need to check. If per-chunk, then the whole region plan could be recomputed for every chunk in the region — a cache-miss / recomputation issue. The docstring in generate_chunk.rs says "A WorldBlock plans a 1280 u square once and every chunk inside it is cut from those plans". So plans are computed once per WorldBlock. Need to verify in world_block.rs.

genome.rs: O(1). Fine.

    1| //! Circulation routing: one dominant cross-region spine plus rare branches.
    2| //!
    3| //! The main spine always runs west portal -> east portal, so circulation
    4| //! chains across regions forever; branches are optional and never form a
    5| //! competing street grid.
    6| 
    7| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
    8| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
    9| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
   10| 
   11| use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap, snap_width, v_edge_portal_z};
   12| 
   13| /// Z coordinate of the main spine where it passes world x (assumes the spine
   14| /// is a west-to-east Manhattan path).
   15| fn spine_z_at(path: &[Position], x: f32) -> f32 {
   16|     for seg in path.windows(2) {
   17|         let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
   18|         if a.z == b.z && (x >= a.x.min(b.x)) && (x <= a.x.max(b.x)) {
   19|             return a.z;
   20|         }
   21|     }
   22|     path[0].z
   23| }
   24| 
   25| pub(super) fn build_corridors(
   26|     seed: u32,
   27|     rx: i64,
   28|     rz: i64,
   29|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
   30|     origin: Position,
   31|     size: f32,
   32| ) -> Vec<CirculationSpine> {
   33|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0 + k, rx, rz]);
   34|     let (x0, x1) = (origin.x, origin.x + size);
   35|     let (z0, z1) = (origin.z, origin.z + size);
   36|     let west_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx, rz);
   37|     let east_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx + 1, rz);
   38|     // The primary route is deliberately too broad for an ordinary office
   39|     // corridor. It carries the infinite cross-region continuity; anything
   40|     // else is an optional branch, never a competing street grid.
   41|     let main_w = snap_width(4.8 + 2.4 * h(1));
   42|     let sec_w = snap_width(3.6 + 1.4 * hash01(seed, &[0xC1, rx, rz]));
   43| 
   44|     let mut spines = Vec::new();
   45|     let mut id = 0u32;
   46|     let mut push = |kind: SpaceProgram, path: Vec<Position>, width: f32, id: &mut u32| {
   47|         spines_push(&mut spines, kind, path, width, id);
   48|     };
   49| 
   50|     // Main spine: west portal -> east portal, always. Its Manhattan bend
   51|     // position is the designer's one free choice.
   52|     let bend_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.35 + 0.30 * h(2)));
   53|     let main_path: Vec<Position> = match genome.circulation {
   54|         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine => {
   55|             let mid_z = snap(z0 + size * (0.30 + 0.40 * h(3)));
   56|             let bend2_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.60 + 0.25 * h(4)));
   57|             vec![
   58|                 Position::new(x0, west_z),
   59|                 Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
   60|                 Position::new(bend_x, mid_z),
   61|                 Position::new(bend2_x, mid_z),
   62|                 Position::new(bend2_x, east_z),
   63|                 Position::new(x1, east_z),
   64|             ]
   65|         }
   66|         _ => vec![
   67|             Position::new(x0, west_z),
   68|             Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
   69|             Position::new(bend_x, east_z),
   70|             Position::new(x1, east_z),
   71|         ],
   72|     };
   73|     let main_z_at = main_path.clone();
   74|     push(SpaceProgram::MainCorridor, main_path, main_w, &mut id);
   75| 
   76|     // Secondary routes are branches, not a second regional grid: roughly a
   77|     // quarter of regions have none, most have one, and a few have two. The
   78|     // former ring and north/south through-route are intentionally absent.
   79|     let branch_count = match genome.circulation {
   80|         CirculationStyle::StraightSpine if h(11) < 0.45 => 0,
   81|         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine if h(11) < 0.20 => 0,
   82|         _ if h(11) < 0.28 => 0,
   83|         _ if h(11) < 0.82 => 1,
   84|         _ => 2,
   85|     };
   86|     for k in 0..branch_count {
   87|         let sx = snap(x0 + size * (0.18 + 0.64 * h(12 + k)));
   88|         let sz = spine_z_at(&main_z_at, sx);
   89|         let len = snap(12.0 + 14.0 * h(22 + k));
   90|         let dir = if h(32 + k) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
   91|         let end = (sz + dir * len).clamp(z0 + EDGE_MARGIN, z1 - EDGE_MARGIN);
   92|         if (end - sz).abs() >= 8.0 {
   93|             push(
   94|                 SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall,
   95|                 vec![Position::new(sx, sz), Position::new(sx, snap(end))],
   96|                 sec_w,
   97|                 &mut id,
   98|             );
   99|         }
  100|     }
  101|     spines
  102| }
  103| 
  104| fn spines_push(
  105|     spines: &mut Vec<CirculationSpine>,
  106|     kind: SpaceProgram,
  107|     path: Vec<Position>,
  108|     width: f32,
  109|     id: &mut u32,
  110| ) {
  111|     spines.push(CirculationSpine {
  112|         id: *id,
  113|         spine_kind: kind,
  114|         path,
  115|         width,
  116|     });
  117|     *id += 1;
  118| }

    1| //! User-facing controls for Level 0 anomaly planning and mutation.
    2| 
    3| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
    4| 
    5| /// Anomaly controls are separate from ordinary office-fabric tuning: changing
    6| /// wall or light density must never silently change encounter frequency.
    7| /// Multipliers are centered on `1.0`; distances are world units.
    8| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
    9| pub struct AnomalyTuning {
   10|     /// Overall organic candidate frequency. Debug forcing remains independent.
   11|     pub frequency: f32,
   12|     /// Macro-footprint scale for region-spanning instances.
   13|     pub size: f32,
   14|     pub pillar_expanses: f32,
   15|     pub blackouts: f32,
   16|     pub red_rooms: f32,
   17|     pub pit_lattices: f32,
   18|     /// Strength/probability of epoch-dependent mutable infill.
   19|     pub remap_intensity: f32,
   20|     /// Minimum distance behind a crossed threshold before infill may differ.
   21|     pub remap_distance: f32,
   22|     /// Radius around the player protected from any resident transition.
   23|     pub safe_radius: f32,
   24|     /// Width of the deterministic single Red Room escape. Zero keeps the loop
   25|     /// sealed; one opens the widest authored breach.

    1| //! Shared deterministic primitives for anomaly planners.
    2| //!
    3| //! These helpers are intentionally integer-first. A candidate's identity must
    4| //! depend on the world seed and its stable lattice anchor, never on which
    5| //! region or voxel chunk happened to request it.
    6| 
    7| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
    8| 
    9| pub(crate) const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
   10| 
   11| pub(crate) fn snap(value: f32) -> f32 {
   12|     (value / SNAP).round() * SNAP
   13| }
   14| 
   15| pub(crate) fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
   16|     value ^= value >> 30;
   17|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
   18|     value ^= value >> 27;
   19|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
   20|     value ^ (value >> 31)
   21| }
   22| 
   23| pub(crate) fn hash(seed: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> u64 {
   24|     mix64(
   25|         seed as u64
   26|             ^ salt
   27|             ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
   28|             ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(31),
   29|     )
   30| }
   31| 
   32| pub(crate) fn unit(hash: u64) -> f32 {
   33|     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
   34| }
   35| 
   36| pub(crate) fn stable_id(seed: u32, kind: AnomalyKind, anchor_x: i64, anchor_z: i64) -> u64 {
   37|     hash(
   38|         seed,
   39|         0xA110_4A1E_0000_0000 | kind as u64,
   40|         anchor_x,
   41|         anchor_z,
   42|     )
   43| }

    2| //!
    3| //! This module composes two independent sources of immutable plans:

   19| /// Returns every immutable anomaly instance whose footprint overlaps a region.
   20| ///
   21| /// Identity is independent of the query partition: callers may ask through
   22| /// adjacent regions or different voxel sizes and receive the same instance.
   23| /// The noise port feeds the macro `anomaly_pressure` field, which clusters
   24| /// candidates without ever placing one itself.
   25| pub fn plan_anomalies_for_region(
   26|     seed: u32,
   27|     region_origin: Position,
   28|     region_size: f32,
   29|     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
   30|     protected_point: Position,
   31|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
   32|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   33| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
   34|     let query = WorldBounds::new(
   35|         region_origin.x,
   36|         region_origin.z,
   37|         region_origin.x + region_size,
   38|         region_origin.z + region_size,
   39|     );
   40|     let mut instances =
   41|         macro_planner::plan_macro_anomalies(seed, query, protected_point, config, noise);
   42|     instances.extend(plan_red_rooms(seed, region_origin, assemblies, config));
   43|     instances.sort_by_key(|instance| instance.id);
   44|     instances.dedup_by_key(|instance| instance.id);
   45|     instances
   46| }
