    1| //! World-lattice planner for region-spanning Level 0 anomalies.
    2| //!
    3| //! Macro candidates live on a 160-unit lattice. Regions merely query that
    4| //! lattice, so overlapping region and chunk requests recover identical
    5| //! instance IDs, footprints, internal phases, and traversal gates.
    6| 
    7| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
    8|     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, ArchBehavior, ArchLayout, ArchProfile, Axis2, AxisDirection,
    9|     OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, PillarLattice, PitLattice, QuarterTurn, TraversalGate,
   10|     TraversalGateKind, WorldBounds,
   11| };
   12| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   14| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   15| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields;
   16| 
   17| use super::determinism::{hash, mix64, snap, stable_id, unit};
   18| 
   19| /// The anomaly lattice *is* the world-graph lattice, so anomaly anchors and
   20| /// macro-cell fields stay phase-aligned by construction.
   21| const MACRO_CELL: f32 = crate::domain::entities::world_topology::MACRO_CELL_SIZE;
   22| const MAX_QUERY_MARGIN: f32 = 400.0;
   23| 
   24| fn weighted_family(config: &GeneratorConfig, sample: f32) -> Option<AnomalyKind> {
   25|     let tuning = config.anomalies;
   26|     let weights = [
   27|         (AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse, tuning.pillar_expanses.max(0.0)),
   28|         (AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse, tuning.blackouts.max(0.0)),
   29|         (AnomalyKind::PitLattice, tuning.pit_lattices.max(0.0)),
   30|         (AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom, tuning.archways.max(0.0)),
   31|     ];
   32|     let total: f32 = weights.iter().map(|(_, weight)| weight).sum();
   33|     if total <= 0.0 {
   34|         return None;
   35|     }
   36| 
   37|     let mut cursor = sample * total;
   38|     for (kind, weight) in weights {
   39|         if cursor < weight {
   40|             return Some(kind);
   41|         }
   42|         cursor -= weight;
   43|     }
   44|     Some(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse)
   45| }
   46| 
   47| fn remap_gates(instance: &AnomalyInstance) -> Vec<TraversalGate> {
   48|     let (step, first, last) = match instance.kind {
   49|         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => {
   50|             let bay = instance.pillar_lattice.map_or(4.0, |lattice| lattice.bay_x);
   51|             (
   52|                 bay * 4.0,
   53|                 -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
   54|                 instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
   55|             )
   56|         }
   57|         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
   58|             22.0,
   59|             -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
   60|             instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
   61|         ),
   62|         _ => return Vec::new(),
   63|     };
   64| 
   65|     let mut gates = Vec::new();
   66|     let mut local_x = snap((first / step).ceil() * step);
   67|     let world_bounds = instance.footprint.bounds();
   68|     let axis = instance.basis.local_axis_in_world(Axis2::X);
   69|     while local_x <= last {
   70|         let at = instance.world_coords(local_x, 0.0);
   71|         let (plane, span_min, span_max) = match axis {
   72|             Axis2::X => (at.x, world_bounds.min_z, world_bounds.max_z),
   73|             Axis2::Z => (at.z, world_bounds.min_x, world_bounds.max_x),
   74|         };
   75|         let gate_index = (local_x / step).round() as i64;
   76|         gates.push(TraversalGate {
   77|             id: mix64(instance.id ^ (gate_index as u64).rotate_left(23) ^ 0x6A7E),
   78|             instance_id: instance.id,
   79|             anomaly_kind: instance.kind,
   80|             kind: TraversalGateKind::Remap,
   81|             axis,
   82|             plane,
   83|             span_min,
   84|             span_max,
   85|             forward: AxisDirection::Positive,
   86|             affected_bounds: world_bounds,
   87|         });
   88|         local_x += step;
   89|     }
   90|     gates
   91| }
   92| 
   93| fn macro_instance(
   94|     seed: u32,
   95|     anchor_x: i64,
   96|     anchor_z: i64,
   97|     kind: AnomalyKind,
   98|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
   99| ) -> AnomalyInstance {
  100|     let id = stable_id(seed, kind, anchor_x, anchor_z);
  101|     let h = |salt| hash(seed, salt, anchor_x, anchor_z);
  102|     let size_scale = config.anomalies.size.clamp(0.5, 2.0);
  103|     let center_x = snap((anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC1)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
  104|     let center_z = snap((anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC2)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
  105|     let basis = OrthoBasis {
  106|         turn: if h(0xC3) & 1 == 0 {
  107|             QuarterTurn::Zero
  108|         } else {
  109|             QuarterTurn::Clockwise
  110|         },
  111|     };
  112|     let (half_x, half_z, entry_band, skeleton_half_width) = match kind {
  113|         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => (
  114|             snap((75.0 + 85.0 * unit(h(0xD1))) * size_scale),
  115|             snap((55.0 + 65.0 * unit(h(0xD2))) * size_scale),
  116|             16.0,
  117|             2.0,
  118|         ),
  119|         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
  120|             snap((65.0 + 70.0 * unit(h(0xD3))) * size_scale),
  121|             snap((50.0 + 55.0 * unit(h(0xD4))) * size_scale),
  122|             12.0,
  123|             2.0,
  124|         ),
  125|         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => (
  126|             snap((32.0 + 30.0 * unit(h(0xD5))) * size_scale),
  127|             snap((28.0 + 25.0 * unit(h(0xD6))) * size_scale),
  128|             6.0,
  129|             1.8,
  130|         ),
  131|         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => (
  132|             snap(4.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD7))),
  133|             snap(5.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD8))),
  134|             0.0,
  135|             0.0,
  136|         ),
  137|         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms are planned from assemblies"),
  138|     };
  139|     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
  140|         center: Position::new(center_x, center_z),
  141|         half_x,
  142|         half_z,
  143|         basis,
  144|     };
  145|     // "Occasionally, one will come across massive pillar rooms -- they can
  146|     // sometimes stretch for miles and will always appear in a lattice or
  147|     // grid pattern." The grid is the canon part and stays. The rest was
  148|     // not massive: a 1.2--1.6 u pillar every 3.6--4.8 u left barely two
  149|     // units of clearance, so the room played as a thicket you push through
  150|     // rather than a hall you are lost in -- and with only two possible
  151|     // sizes, every pillar in it was one of two objects.
  152|     //
  153|     // A bay you can see down, and pillars with the mass to block what is
  154|     // behind them. Each room draws its own bay and its own range of sizes,
  155|     // so one is a forest of squat piers and the next a colonnade of slabs.
  156|     let pillar_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse).then(|| {
  157|         let min_side = snap(1.2 + 0.8 * unit(h(0xE5)));
  158|         PillarLattice {
  159|             bay_x: snap(7.2 + 3.6 * unit(h(0xE1))),
  160|             bay_z: snap(7.2 + 3.6 * unit(h(0xE2))),
  161|             phase_x: snap((unit(h(0xE3)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
  162|             phase_z: snap((unit(h(0xE4)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
  163|             min_side,
  164|             max_side: snap(min_side + 1.2 + 1.6 * unit(h(0xE6))),
  165|             variation_seed: id ^ 0xA111_AA55_u64,
  166|         }
  167|     });
  168|     let pit_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PitLattice).then(|| PitLattice {
  169|         spacing_x: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF1))),
  170|         spacing_z: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF2))),
  171|         phase_x: snap(unit(h(0xF3)) * 1.2),
  172|         phase_z: snap(unit(h(0xF4)) * 1.2),
  173|         side: snap(0.8 + 0.2 * unit(h(0xF5))),
  174|         depth: 2.4,
  175|     });
  176|     let arch = (kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom).then(|| {
  177|         // Most arch rooms are walk-through connectors; the sheltered dead
  178|         // end is the rarer find. Both stay immutable anchors.
  179|         let layout = if unit(h(0xA0)) < 0.7 {
  180|             ArchLayout::Transition
  181|         } else {
  182|             ArchLayout::DeadEnd
  183|         };
  184|         // Transition rooms are graph connectors: most stay plain anchors,
  185|         // but some are seams into another culture or scale. A dead end
  186|         // connects nothing, so it never claims a seam behavior.
  187|         let behavior = if layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
  188|             ArchBehavior::Anchor
  189|         } else {
  190|             match unit(h(0xA4)) {
  191|                 v if v < 0.40 => ArchBehavior::Anchor,
  192|                 v if v < 0.75 => ArchBehavior::CultureSeam,
  193|                 _ => ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach,
  194|             }
  195|         };
  196|         // Every instance is its own arcade: rhythm, clear width, springing
  197|         // height, and blind cadence all vary, so no two arch rooms present
  198|         // the same silhouette — yet every non-blind opening stays walkable
  199|         // (the opening is capped so piers survive, and the head springs at
  200|         // standing height before rising toward the center).
  201|         let bay = snap(2.4 + 2.0 * unit(h(0xA1)));
  202|         ArchProfile {
  203|             layout,
  204|             behavior,
  205|             bay,
  206|             opening: snap((1.4 + 1.4 * unit(h(0xA2))).min(bay - 0.8)),
  207|             blind_every: 3 + (h(0xA3) % 4) as u8,
  208|             spring_units: ((2.0 + 0.8 * unit(h(0xA5))) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
  209|         }
  210|     });
  211|     let mut instance = AnomalyInstance {
  212|         id,
  213|         kind,
  214|         footprint,
  215|         basis,
  216|         macro_anchor: (anchor_x, anchor_z),
  217|         pillar_lattice,
  218|         pit_lattice,
  219|         arch,
  220|         gates: Vec::new(),
  221|         skeleton_half_width,
  222|         entry_band,
  223|     };
  224|     instance.gates = remap_gates(&instance);
  225|     instance
  226| }
  227| 
  228| fn forced_instance(
  229|     seed: u32,
  230|     query: WorldBounds,
  231|     protected_point: Position,
  232|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  233| ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
  234|     let kind = config.anomalies.forced_kind?;
  235|     if kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom {
  236|         return None;
  237|     }
  238| 
  239|     if kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom {
  240|         // A forced anchor is moved next to the protected point so it is both
  241|         // resident and visible; organic anchors keep their macro-cell center.
  242|         let center = Position::new(snap(protected_point.x + 10.0), snap(protected_point.z));
  243|         let anchor_x = (center.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  244|         let anchor_z = (center.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  245|         let mut instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
  246|         instance.footprint.center = center;
  247|         return instance
  248|             .footprint
  249|             .bounds()
  250|             .intersects(query)
  251|             .then_some(instance);
  252|     }
  253| 
  254|     let anchor_x = (protected_point.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  255|     let anchor_z = (protected_point.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  256|     let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
  257|     instance
  258|         .footprint
  259|         .bounds()
  260|         .intersects(query)
  261|         .then_some(instance)
  262| }

  264| pub(crate) fn plan_macro_anomalies(
  265|     seed: u32,
  266|     query: WorldBounds,
  267|     protected_point: Position,
  268|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  269|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  270| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
  271|     let mut instances: Vec<_> = forced_instance(seed, query, protected_point, config)
  272|         .into_iter()
  273|         .collect();
  274|     if config.anomalies.frequency <= 0.0 {
  275|         return instances;
  276|     }
  277| 
  278|     let expanded = query.expanded(MAX_QUERY_MARGIN);
  279|     let anchor_x_min = (expanded.min_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  280|     let anchor_x_max = (expanded.max_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  281|     let anchor_z_min = (expanded.min_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  282|     let anchor_z_max = (expanded.max_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
  283|     let base_chance = (0.20 * config.anomalies.frequency.clamp(0.0, 4.0)).min(0.75);
  284| 
  285|     for anchor_z in anchor_z_min..=anchor_z_max {
  286|         for anchor_x in anchor_x_min..=anchor_x_max {
  287|             // The macro anomaly-pressure field clusters candidates: quiet
  288|             // territory thins toward 0.4× the base chance and pressured
  289|             // territory rises toward 1.6×, so anomalies arrive in loose
  290|             // constellations instead of a uniform sprinkle. The field is a
  291|             // pure world function, so every query that can see this anchor
  292|             // computes the identical decision.
  293|             let pressure = sample_fields(
  294|                 noise,
  295|                 seed,
  296|                 (anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
  297|                 (anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
  298|             )
  299|             .anomaly_pressure;
  300|             let chance = base_chance * (0.40 + 1.20 * pressure);
  301|             let candidate = hash(seed, 0xCAAD_1DA7, anchor_x, anchor_z);
  302|             if unit(candidate) >= chance {
  303|                 continue;
  304|             }
  305|             let Some(kind) = weighted_family(config, unit(candidate.rotate_left(21))) else {
  306|                 continue;
  307|             };
  308|             let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
  309|             if !instance.footprint.bounds().intersects(query) {
  310|                 continue;
  311|             }
  312|             // Organic candidates honor the opening-region keep-out. Forced
  313|             // candidates intentionally bypass it for developer inspection.
  314|             if instance
  315|                 .footprint
  316|                 .bounds()
  317|                 .expanded(48.0)
  318|                 .contains(protected_point.x, protected_point.z)
  319|             {
  320|                 continue;
  321|             }
  322|             instances.push(instance);
  323|         }
  324|     }
  325|     instances
  326| }

macro_planner.rs: the query area is (80+800)²/160² ≈ 30 anchors per axis → 900-1000 anchors per region query. Each anchor: sample_fields (noise eval — O(1)) + macro_instance (O(1) except remap_gates which loops over footprint span/step ≈ 160/16 = 10 gates). So O(anchors) ≈ O((region+margin)²/MACRO_CELL²) per region query — constant-ish ~1000 instances created, most discarded. This is recomputed per region plan — but region plans are cached per WorldBlock? Need to check. Each chunk generation would re-plan macro anomalies if plans are per-region... Let me check world_block.rs / infinite_level.rs to see caching.
    1| //! Loading a place instead of streaming a frontier.
    2| //!
    3| //! The level used to plan chunk-locally: every architectural decision had to
    4| //! be answerable from one coordinate with no cross-chunk reads, because a
    5| //! chunk arriving in front of the player had nobody to ask. That constraint
    6| //! bought infinite streaming and cost the architecture nearly everything
    7| //! that needs to see more than one room — connectivity you can *verify*
    8| //! rather than assume, integration over a circulation graph, composition
    9| //! staged across an area, a motif established before it is broken.
   10| //!
   11| //! A [`WorldBlock`] is the trade taken deliberately: behind one loading
   12| //! screen, plan a very large area at once. Only the *plans* are bulk-built —
   13| //! a region is a few kilobytes of assemblies, corridors and genomes, so a
   14| //! whole block is a few hundred kilobytes. Voxels keep streaming from those
   15| //! plans exactly as before, which is what keeps frame time flat on a small
   16| //! machine. Bulk-generating voxels instead would be hundreds of megabytes
   17| //! and would buy nothing: voxel sampling was never the part that was
   18| //! starved for context.
   19| //!
   20| //! Crossing a block is not a level transition. The player walks out of one
   21| //! and into the next with no seam and no pause, because the next was
   22| //! planned in the background the moment they crossed the [`PRELOAD_MARGIN`]
   23| //! — the loading screen is paid once, at the start, and never again.
   24| 
   25| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
   26| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
   27| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   28| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   29| use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
   30| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   31| use crate::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
   32| 
   33| /// Regions along one edge of a block.
   34| ///
   35| /// Sixteen 80 u regions is a 1280 u square — 1.6 km² of floor. Crossing it
   36| /// in a straight line takes minutes; nobody crosses a labyrinth in a
   37| /// straight line, and finding your way through one is hours. That is the
   38| /// unit the loading screen is buying.
   39| pub const REGIONS_PER_BLOCK: i64 = 16;
   40| 
   41| /// Side of a block, world units.
   42| pub const BLOCK_SIZE: f32 = REGIONS_PER_BLOCK as f32 * REGION_SIZE;
   43| 
   44| /// How close to the edge a player must come before the next block starts
   45| /// planning, world units.
   46| ///
   47| /// Three regions. Wide enough that even a sprint across the margin finishes
   48| /// planning before the player arrives, narrow enough that a wanderer who
   49| /// merely brushes a boundary and turns back does not trigger work for a
   50| /// place they never visit.
   51| pub const PRELOAD_MARGIN: f32 = 3.0 * REGION_SIZE;
   52| 
   53| /// Address of a block on the block lattice.
   54| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
   55| pub struct BlockCoord {
   56|     pub x: i64,
   57|     pub z: i64,
   58| }
   59| 
   60| impl BlockCoord {

   62|     pub fn of(world: Position) -> Self {
   63|         Self {
   64|             x: (world.x / BLOCK_SIZE).floor() as i64,
   65|             z: (world.z / BLOCK_SIZE).floor() as i64,
   66|         }
   67|     }

   69|     pub fn origin(self) -> Position {
   70|         Position::new(self.x as f32 * BLOCK_SIZE, self.z as f32 * BLOCK_SIZE)
   71|     }

   73|     pub fn bounds(self) -> WorldBounds {
   74|         let origin = self.origin();
   75|         WorldBounds::new(
   76|             origin.x,
   77|             origin.z,
   78|             origin.x + BLOCK_SIZE,
   79|             origin.z + BLOCK_SIZE,
   80|         )
   81|     }
   82| }

   84| /// A large, fully planned, walkable area.
   85| pub struct WorldBlock {
   86|     coord: BlockCoord,
   87|     window: InfiniteRegionWindow,
   88| }
   89| 
   90| impl WorldBlock {
   91|     /// Plans an entire block, reporting progress so a loading screen has
   92|     /// something honest to show.
   93|     ///
   94|     /// `progress` receives `(regions_done, regions_total)`. It is called per
   95|     /// region rather than per chunk because a region is the unit of work
   96|     /// that actually takes time, and a progress bar that advances in units
   97|     /// nobody is waiting on is a lie.
   98|     pub fn load(
   99|         seed: u32,
  100|         coord: BlockCoord,
  101|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
  102|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  103|         progress: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize),
  104|     ) -> Self {
  105|         // One halo region beyond the block, so a chunk sampled at the very
  106|         // edge still finds the plan of the region across the boundary and
  107|         // the two blocks agree about what is built there.
  108|         //
  109|         // The halo is why the reported total is larger than
  110|         // `REGIONS_PER_BLOCK^2`: the window really does plan the surrounding
  111|         // ring, and a bar that hid that work would stall at 100% while it
  112|         // finished.
  113|         let window = InfiniteRegionWindow::covering_with_progress(
  114|             coord.bounds(),
  115|             REGION_SIZE,
  116|             seed,
  117|             config,
  118|             noise,
  119|             progress,
  120|         );
  121|         Self { coord, window }
  122|     }
  123| 
  124|     /// The planned regions, for feeding straight into chunk generation.
  125|     ///
  126|     /// Handing the window over rather than copying plans out is the whole
  127|     /// economy of the block: one derivation serves every chunk inside it,
  128|     /// and any block-scale pass run over these plans is automatically seen
  129|     /// by all of them.
  130|     pub fn plans(&self) -> &InfiniteRegionWindow {
  131|         &self.window
  132|     }
  133| 
  134|     pub fn coord(&self) -> BlockCoord {
  135|         self.coord
  136|     }
  137| 
  138|     pub fn bounds(&self) -> WorldBounds {
  139|         self.coord.bounds()
  140|     }
  141| 
  142|     /// The plan for a world point, if this block covers it.
  143|     pub fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
  144|         self.window.plan_at(world)
  145|     }
  146| 
  147|     /// Is this position inside the block proper (not merely its halo)?
  148|     pub fn contains(&self, world: Position) -> bool {
  149|         self.bounds().contains(world.x, world.z)
  150|     }
  151| 
  152|     /// Blocks that should start planning now, given where the player is.
  153|     ///
  154|     /// Returns the neighbours whose edge the player has come within
  155|     /// [`PRELOAD_MARGIN`] of — up to three at a corner. Empty in the
  156|     /// interior, which is almost always, so the caller does no work for most
  157|     /// of a session.
  158|     ///
  159|     /// Deliberately returns *what to load* rather than loading it: this
  160|     /// module plans, and only the caller knows whether it has a thread to
  161|     /// plan on.
  162|     pub fn preload_targets(&self, world: Position) -> Vec<BlockCoord> {
  163|         let b = self.bounds();
  164|         let mut out = Vec::new();
  165|         let near_west = world.x - b.min_x < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
  166|         let near_east = b.max_x - world.x < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
  167|         let near_north = world.z - b.min_z < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
  168|         let near_south = b.max_z - world.z < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
  169| 
  170|         let mut push = |dx: i64, dz: i64| {
  171|             out.push(BlockCoord {
  172|                 x: self.coord.x + dx,
  173|                 z: self.coord.z + dz,
  174|             })
  175|         };
  176|         if near_west {
  177|             push(-1, 0);
  178|         }
  179|         if near_east {
  180|             push(1, 0);
  181|         }
  182|         if near_north {
  183|             push(0, -1);
  184|         }
  185|         if near_south {
  186|             push(0, 1);
  187|         }
  188|         // The diagonal too: a player heading for a corner arrives in the
  189|         // diagonal block without ever entering either edge neighbour, and
  190|         // finding it unplanned is exactly the stall this exists to avoid.
  191|         if near_west && near_north {
  192|             push(-1, -1);
  193|         }
  194|         if near_east && near_north {
  195|             push(1, -1);
  196|         }
  197|         if near_west && near_south {
  198|             push(-1, 1);
  199|         }
  200|         if near_east && near_south {
  201|             push(1, 1);
  202|         }
  203|         out
  204|     }
  205| }

    1| //! Deterministic access to the finite window of an infinite planned level.
    2| //!
    3| //! Chunk generation is local, but Level 0 architecture is not: a chunk may
    4| //! sample corridors, assemblies, or anomaly footprints planned by any region
    5| //! that overlaps its voxel halo.  This module makes that query explicit.  The
    6| //! window owns a stable, row-major set of region plans and is otherwise just a
    7| //! world-point-to-plan lookup; callers do not need to reproduce region-range
    8| //! arithmetic or fall back to an unrelated plan when a lookup misses.
    9| 
   10| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
   11| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
   12| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   14| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   15| use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan, region_index};
   16| 
   17| /// The region plans needed to sample one bounded area of an infinite level.
   18| ///
   19| /// Plans are stored in `(z, x)` row-major order.  That order is deliberately
   20| /// independent of hash maps and request timing, so planning the same area is
   21| /// replayable on the main thread, in a worker, or during a test.
   22| #[derive(Debug)]
   23| pub struct InfiniteRegionWindow {
   24|     min_region_x: i64,
   25|     min_region_z: i64,
   26|     max_region_x: i64,
   27|     max_region_z: i64,
   28|     plans: Vec<RegionPlan>,
   29| }
   30| 
   31| impl InfiniteRegionWindow {
   32|     /// Plans every region touched by `area` after expanding it by `halo` world
   33|     /// units.  Boundary-touching regions are included intentionally: a voxel
   34|     /// sampler may ask about the exact far edge while constructing skirts,
   35|     /// meshes, or collision data.
   36|     pub fn covering(
   37|         area: WorldBounds,
   38|         halo: f32,
   39|         seed: u32,
   40|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
   41|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   42|     ) -> Self {
   43|         Self::covering_with_progress(area, halo, seed, config, noise, &mut |_, _| {})
   44|     }
   45| 
   46|     /// [`covering`](Self::covering), reporting `(regions_done, regions_total)`
   47|     /// after each region is planned.
   48|     ///
   49|     /// A window over one chunk is a handful of regions and nobody waits for
   50|     /// it; a window over a whole block is hundreds and somebody is watching a
   51|     /// loading screen. The callback is what lets that screen advance in the
   52|     /// unit the time is actually spent in, rather than jumping from 0 to 100
   53|     /// around a silent second.
   54|     pub fn covering_with_progress(
   55|         area: WorldBounds,
   56|         halo: f32,
   57|         seed: u32,
   58|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
   59|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   60|         progress: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize),
   61|     ) -> Self {
   62|         assert!(
   63|             halo.is_finite() && halo >= 0.0,
   64|             "region-window halo must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
   65|         );
   66|         let area = area.expanded(halo);
   67|         assert!(
   68|             [area.min_x, area.min_z, area.max_x, area.max_z]
   69|                 .into_iter()
   70|                 .all(f32::is_finite),
   71|             "an infinite-region window requires finite world bounds"
   72|         );
   73| 
   74|         let min_region_x = region_index(area.min_x);
   75|         let min_region_z = region_index(area.min_z);
   76|         let max_region_x = region_index(area.max_x);
   77|         let max_region_z = region_index(area.max_z);
   78|         let width = region_count(min_region_x, max_region_x);
   79|         let height = region_count(min_region_z, max_region_z);
   80|         let capacity = width
   81|             .checked_mul(height)
   82|             .expect("requested region window is too large to address");
   83|         let mut plans = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
   84| 
   85|         progress(0, capacity);
   86|         for region_z in min_region_z..=max_region_z {
   87|             for region_x in min_region_x..=max_region_x {
   88|                 plans.push(generate_region_plan(
   89|                     seed,
   90|                     region_origin(region_x, region_z),
   91|                     REGION_SIZE,
   92|                     config,
   93|                     noise,
   94|                 ));
   95|                 progress(plans.len(), capacity);
   96|             }
   97|         }
   98| 
   99|         Self {
  100|             min_region_x,
  101|             min_region_z,
  102|             max_region_x,
  103|             max_region_z,
  104|             plans,
  105|         }
  106|     }
  107| 
  108|     /// Convenience constructor for the common chunk-plus-voxel-halo query.
  109|     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
  110|         chunk_origin: Position,
  111|         chunk_size: f32,
  112|         halo: f32,
  113|         seed: u32,
  114|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
  115|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  116|     ) -> Self {
  117|         assert!(
  118|             chunk_size.is_finite() && chunk_size >= 0.0,
  119|             "chunk size must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
  120|         );
  121|         Self::covering(
  122|             WorldBounds::new(
  123|                 chunk_origin.x,
  124|                 chunk_origin.z,
  125|                 chunk_origin.x + chunk_size,
  126|                 chunk_origin.z + chunk_size,
  127|             ),
  128|             halo,
  129|             seed,
  130|             config,
  131|             noise,
  132|         )
  133|     }
  134| 
  135|     /// Returns the authoritative plan for a world point, or `None` when the
  136|     /// caller sampled beyond the area/halo declared at construction time.
  137|     pub fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
  138|         self.plan_for_region(region_index(world.x), region_index(world.z))
  139|     }
  140| 
  141|     pub fn plan_for_region(&self, region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
  142|         if region_x < self.min_region_x
  143|             || region_x > self.max_region_x
  144|             || region_z < self.min_region_z
  145|             || region_z > self.max_region_z
  146|         {
  147|             return None;
  148|         }
  149| 
  150|         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
  151|         let local_x = usize::try_from(region_x - self.min_region_x).ok()?;
  152|         let local_z = usize::try_from(region_z - self.min_region_z).ok()?;
  153|         self.plans
  154|             .get(local_z.saturating_mul(width).saturating_add(local_x))
  155|     }
  156| 
  157|     #[cfg(test)]
  158|     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
  159|         self.plans.len()
  160|     }
  161| 
  162|     #[cfg(test)]
  163|     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  164|         self.plans.is_empty()
  165|     }
  166| 
  167|     /// Stable row-major iteration for semantic export and deterministic tests.
  168|     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
  169|         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
  170|         self.plans.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, plan)| {
  171|             let local_z = index / width;
  172|             let local_x = index % width;
  173|             (
  174|                 (
  175|                     self.min_region_x + local_x as i64,
  176|                     self.min_region_z + local_z as i64,
  177|                 ),
  178|                 plan,
  179|             )
  180|         })
  181|     }
  182| }
  183| 
  184| fn region_count(first: i64, last: i64) -> usize {
  185|     let count = last
  186|         .checked_sub(first)
  187|         .and_then(|distance| distance.checked_add(1))
  188|         .expect("requested region window exceeds integer address space");
  189|     usize::try_from(count).expect("requested region window exceeds platform address space")
  190| }
  191| 
  192| fn region_origin(region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Position {
  193|     Position::new(region_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE, region_z as f32 * REGION_SIZE)
  194| }

    1| //! The pure macro-scale world planner: an infinite graph, one cell at a time.
    2| //!
    3| //! [`plan_macro_cell`] is a pure function of `(seed, cell id, red-room
    4| //! scale)` — the top of the planning hierarchy documented in
    5| //! [`crate::domain::entities::world_topology`]. It owns three jobs:
    6| //!
    7| //! 1. **Parameter fields.** [`sample_fields`] turns the noise port into
    8| //!    multi-octave `[0, 1]` fields (openness, vertical pressure, anomaly
    9| //!    pressure, ...). This is the *only* legitimate role of fractal math in
   10| //!    the world: it chooses where the building's rules change; it never
   11| //!    substitutes for an architectural decision.
   12| //! 2. **Graph events.** Red rooms are planned here as separated events on
   13| //!    the macro lattice (a deterministic tournament gives every event a
   14| //!    cooldown radius), and vertical links reserve stairwell footprints
   15| //!    where vertical pressure is high.
   16| //! 3. **Continuity contracts.** Primary-route portals are derived from the
   17| //!    *edge's* lattice coordinate, so both neighbors of an edge compute the
   18| //!    identical crossing — the invariant that lets circulation chain across
   19| //!    regions forever.
   20| //!
   21| //! Everything downstream (region planner, anomaly planner, voxelizer)
   22| //! consumes these obligations; nothing here writes a voxel or knows a chunk
   23| //! size. Determinism is testable: see the 5×5 snapshot test at the bottom.
   24| 
   25| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   26| use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{
   27|     MACRO_CELL_SIZE, MacroCell, MacroCellId, MacroFields, PlaceKind, Portal,
   28|     REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL, RedRoomEvent, VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind, WorldNode,
   29| };
   30| use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
   31| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
   32| 
   33| /// Side of a region, world units. Kept in lockstep with
   34| /// `region_plan::REGION_SIZE` by a compile-time-adjacent test below.
   35| const REGION_SIZE: f32 = MACRO_CELL_SIZE / REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL as f32;
   36| 
   37| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   38| // Shared 32-bit deterministic hashing.
   39| //
   40| // All architectural "randomness" in region planning flows through these two
   41| // functions. They live here — at the top of the planning hierarchy — and
   42| // `region_plan` imports them, so the macro graph and the regional plans can
   43| // never disagree about a shared derivation (portals, most importantly).
   44| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   45| 
   46| pub(crate) fn mix(mut h: u32) -> u32 {
   47|     h ^= h >> 16;
   48|     h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
   49|     h ^= h >> 13;
   50|     h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2_AE35);
   51|     h ^= h >> 16;
   52|     h
   53| }
   54| 
   55| /// Hash of a seed plus any number of integer keys, uniform in [0, 1).
   56| pub(crate) fn hash01(seed: u32, keys: &[i64]) -> f32 {
   57|     let mut h = mix(seed ^ 0x9E37_79B9);
   58|     for &k in keys {
   59|         h = mix(h ^ (k as u32)).wrapping_add(mix((k >> 32) as u32));
   60|     }
   61|     (mix(h) >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
   62| }
   63| 
   64| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   65| // Portals: the cross-region continuity contract.
   66| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   67| 
   68| /// World Z of the primary-route portal on the vertical edge
   69| /// `x = edge_x * REGION_SIZE` of region row `row_z`. Both regions sharing the
   70| /// edge derive the same value — this function is the single source of truth
   71| /// (the region planner routes its main spine between two of these).
   72| pub fn primary_portal_z(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> f32 {
   73|     let f = 0.30 + 0.40 * hash01(seed, &[0x0E1, edge_x, row_z]);
   74|     snap((row_z as f32 + f) * REGION_SIZE)
   75| }
   76| 
   77| /// Snap to the 0.4 u plan lattice (one coarse voxel).
   78| fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
   79|     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
   80| }
   81| 
   82| fn portal(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> Portal {
   83|     Portal {
   84|         id: hash(seed, 0x7047_A100, edge_x, row_z),
   85|         edge_x,
   86|         row_z,
   87|         at: Position::new(
   88|             edge_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
   89|             primary_portal_z(seed, edge_x, row_z),
   90|         ),
   91|     }
   92| }
   93| 
   94| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   95| // Parameter fields.
   96| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   97| 
   98| /// One multi-octave field in [0, 1]:
   99| /// `F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ · N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`, rescaled and clamped. The provider's
  100| /// base wavelength is ~20 u, so `20 / wavelength` stretches each octave.
  101| fn field(
  102|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  103|     seed: u32,
  104|     salt: u32,
  105|     wx: f32,
  106|     wz: f32,
  107|     wavelengths: [f32; 3],
  108|     weights: [f32; 3],
  109| ) -> f32 {
  110|     let mut sum = 0.0;
  111|     let mut norm = 0.0;
  112|     for (octave, (&wavelength, &weight)) in wavelengths.iter().zip(weights.iter()).enumerate() {
  113|         let s = 20.0 / wavelength;
  114|         sum += weight
  115|             * noise.evaluate_2d(
  116|                 seed ^ salt.wrapping_add((octave as u32).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9)),
  117|                 Position::new(wx * s, wz * s),
  118|             );
  119|         norm += weight;
  120|     }
  121|     // Octave sums cluster toward zero; stretch before biasing to [0, 1] so
  122|     // thresholds see a usable spread instead of everything at 0.5.
  123|     ((sum / norm) * 0.8 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
  124| }
  125| 
  126| /// The institution-age field alone — how long this stretch of the building
  127| /// has been rotting. Split out of [`sample_fields`] (and used by it, so the
  128| /// two can never disagree) because per-column callers need one field, not
  129| /// six: old territory keeps fewer of its fluorescents alive.
  130| pub fn institution_age_at(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
  131|     field(
  132|         noise,
  133|         seed,
  134|         0xF1E1_0003,
  135|         wx,
  136|         wz,
  137|         [260.0, 90.0, 30.0],
  138|         [1.0, 0.5, 0.25],
  139|     )
  140| }
  141| 
  142| /// Sample every macro parameter field at one world point. Pure and
  143| /// world-space: two callers asking about the same point always agree,
  144| /// regardless of which cell, region, or chunk asked.
  145| pub fn sample_fields(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> MacroFields {
  146|     MacroFields {
  147|         openness: field(
  148|             noise,
  149|             seed,
  150|             0xF1E1_0001,
  151|             wx,
  152|             wz,
  153|             [350.0, 130.0, 45.0],
  154|             [1.0, 0.5, 0.2],
  155|         ),
  156|         vertical_pressure: field(
  157|             noise,
  158|             seed,
  159|             0xF1E1_0002,
  160|             wx,
  161|             wz,
  162|             [520.0, 170.0, 60.0],
  163|             [1.0, 0.4, 0.15],
  164|         ),
  165|         institution_age: institution_age_at(noise, seed, wx, wz),
  166|         anomaly_pressure: field(
  167|             noise,
  168|             seed,
  169|             0xF1E1_0004,
  170|             wx,
  171|             wz,
  172|             [620.0, 210.0, 70.0],
  173|             [1.0, 0.35, 0.1],
  174|         ),
  175|         redroom_pressure: field(
  176|             noise,
  177|             seed,
  178|             0xF1E1_0005,
  179|             wx,
  180|             wz,
  181|             [700.0, 230.0, 80.0],
  182|             [1.0, 0.3, 0.1],
  183|         ),
  184|         style_blend: field(
  185|             noise,
  186|             seed,
  187|             0xF1E1_0006,
  188|             wx,
  189|             wz,
  190|             [420.0, 140.0, 50.0],
  191|             [1.0, 0.45, 0.2],
  192|         ),
  193|     }
  194| }
  195| 
  196| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  197| // Red rooms as separated graph events.
  198| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  199| 
  200| /// Cooldown radius in macro cells (Chebyshev). Two committed events are
  201| /// always at least one full macro cell (160 u) apart, so red rooms read as
  202| /// rare landmarks instead of a recurring biome.
  203| const RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS: i64 = 1;
  204| 
  205| /// Base per-cell candidate chance at `red_room_scale == 1.0`.
  206| const RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE: f32 = 0.32;
  207| 
  208| /// The candidate score of one macro cell: `Some(score)` if the cell wants a
  209| /// red room this epoch, lower score = higher priority in the tournament.
  210| fn red_room_candidate(
  211|     seed: u32,
  212|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  213|     cell: MacroCellId,
  214|     red_room_scale: f32,
  215| ) -> Option<f32> {
  216|     if red_room_scale <= 0.0 {
  217|         return None;
  218|     }
  219|     let center = cell.center();
  220|     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z).redroom_pressure;
  221|     let score = unit(hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0011, cell.x, cell.z));
  222|     // Pressure clusters events without ever making them uniform or certain.
  223|     let chance = (RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE * red_room_scale).min(0.85) * (0.35 + 0.65 * pressure);
  224|     (score < chance).then_some(score)
  225| }
  226| 
  227| /// The red-room event a macro cell *wins*, if any. A candidate cell fires
  228| /// only when no candidate within the separation radius beats its score
  229| /// (ties broken by lattice coordinate), so any two firing cells are more
  230| /// than the separation radius apart — a deterministic Matérn-style
  231| /// exclusion, computed locally without global state.
  232| pub fn red_room_event_for_cell(
  233|     seed: u32,
  234|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  235|     cell: MacroCellId,
  236|     red_room_scale: f32,
  237| ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
  238|     let mine = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale)?;
  239|     for dz in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
  240|         for dx in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
  241|             if dx == 0 && dz == 0 {
  242|                 continue;
  243|             }
  244|             let rival_cell = MacroCellId::new(cell.x + dx, cell.z + dz);
  245|             if let Some(rival) = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, rival_cell, red_room_scale) {
  246|                 let rival_wins = (rival, rival_cell.x, rival_cell.z) < (mine, cell.x, cell.z);
  247|                 if rival_wins {
  248|                     return None;
  249|                 }
  250|             }
  251|         }
  252|     }
  253|     // The event targets exactly one of the cell's 2×2 regions.
  254|     let pick = hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0022, cell.x, cell.z);
  255|     let region = (
  256|         cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + (pick & 1) as i64,
  257|         cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + ((pick >> 1) & 1) as i64,
  258|     );
  259|     Some(RedRoomEvent {
  260|         id: hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0033, cell.x, cell.z),
  261|         region,
  262|         score: mine,
  263|     })
  264| }
  265| 
  266| /// Does a red-room event target this specific region? This is the query the
  267| /// region planner asks; the answer is independent of which chunk, region, or
  268| /// LOD triggered the plan.
  269| pub fn red_room_event_for_region(
  270|     seed: u32,
  271|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  272|     region_x: i64,
  273|     region_z: i64,
  274|     red_room_scale: f32,
  275| ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
  276|     red_room_event_for_cell(
  277|         seed,
  278|         noise,
  279|         MacroCellId::of_region(region_x, region_z),
  280|         red_room_scale,
  281|     )
  282|     .filter(|event| event.region == (region_x, region_z))
  283| }
  284| 
  285| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  286| // Vertical links.
  287| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  288| 
  289| /// The vertical link reserved inside one region, if any. Stairwells are
  290| /// planned per region so the region planner can honor the reservation while
  291| /// laying out its assemblies; the *kind* mix leans ordinary, with the
  292| /// endless variants appearing only under high vertical pressure.
  293| pub fn vertical_link_for_region(
  294|     seed: u32,
  295|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  296|     region_x: i64,
  297|     region_z: i64,
  298| ) -> Option<VerticalLink> {
  299|     let center_x = (region_x as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
  300|     let center_z = (region_z as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
  301|     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z).vertical_pressure;
  302|     let gate = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0001, region_x, region_z));
  303|     if gate >= 0.06 + 0.30 * pressure * pressure {
  304|         return None;
  305|     }
  306| 
  307|     let kind_roll = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0002, region_x, region_z));
  308|     let (kind, to_elevation) = if kind_roll < 0.55 {
  309|         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
  310|     } else if kind_roll < 0.75 && pressure > 0.55 {
  311|         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, 1)
  312|     } else if kind_roll < 0.90 && pressure > 0.55 {
  313|         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessDescent, -1)
  314|     } else if kind_roll < 0.97 {
  315|         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
  316|     } else {
  317|         (VerticalLinkKind::ServiceShaft, -1)
  318|     };
  319| 
  320|     // Anchor well inside the region so the stair mass never has to fight the
  321|     // edge margin. The region planner snaps the actual footprint to its
  322|     // corridor network; the anchor only says "near here".
  323|     let ax = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0003, region_x, region_z));
  324|     let az = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0004, region_x, region_z));
  325|     Some(VerticalLink {
  326|         id: hash(seed, 0x57A1_0005, region_x, region_z),
  327|         kind,
  328|         region: (region_x, region_z),
  329|         anchor: Position::new(
  330|             snap((region_x as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * ax) * REGION_SIZE),
  331|             snap((region_z as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * az) * REGION_SIZE),
  332|         ),
  333|         from_elevation: 0,
  334|         to_elevation,
  335|     })
  336| }

  342| fn classify_region(
  343|     seed: u32,
  344|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  345|     region: (i64, i64),
  346|     red_room_event: Option<&RedRoomEvent>,
  347|     vertical: Option<&VerticalLink>,
  348| ) -> PlaceKind {
  349|     if red_room_event.is_some_and(|event| event.region == region) {
  350|         return PlaceKind::RedRoomEncounter;
  351|     }
  352|     if vertical.is_some() {
  353|         return PlaceKind::Stairwell;
  354|     }
  355|     let center_x = (region.0 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
  356|     let center_z = (region.1 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
  357|     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z);
  358|     if fields.openness > 0.66 {
  359|         if fields.vertical_pressure > 0.60 {
  360|             PlaceKind::Atrium
  361|         } else {
  362|             PlaceKind::OpenPlate
  363|         }
  364|     } else {
  365|         PlaceKind::Warren
  366|     }
  367| }

  369| /// Plan one macro cell of the infinite world graph.
  370| ///
  371| /// Pure: the same `(seed, cell, red_room_scale)` always yields the same
  372| /// graph, and shared contracts (portals, red-room tournaments) agree with
  373| /// every neighboring cell's own computation. `red_room_scale` is the
  374| /// world-wide `anomalies.frequency * anomalies.red_rooms` product; passing
  375| /// different scales for different cells of one world is a caller bug.

  395|             nodes.push(WorldNode {
  396|                 id: hash(seed, 0x40DE_0001, region.0, region.1),
  397|                 region,
  398|                 kind: classify_region(
  399|                     seed,
  400|                     noise,

  518|     fn digest(text: &str) -> u64 {
  519|         let mut h = 0xCBF2_9CE4_8422_2325u64;
  520|         for byte in text.bytes() {
  521|             h = mix64(h ^ byte as u64);
  522|         }
  523|         h
  524|     }
  525|

world_topology.rs analysis:
- `plan_macro_cell`: O(REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL²) nodes × each does `vertical_link_for_region` (3 noise evals) + `classify_region` (sample_fields = 6×3=18 noise evals). `red_room_event_for_cell` calls `red_room_candidate` 9 times, each sampling fields (18 noise evals) — so ~180 noise evaluations per macro cell plan. O(1) per cell — fine, but note `red_room_event_for_cell` is called from `red_room_event_for_region` per region plan → each region plan recomputes the 3×3 tournament + field sampling. With plans computed once per WorldBlock, this is bounded.

Key redundancy: `red_room_event_for_region` → `red_room_event_for_cell` recomputes sample_fields at cell centers, and region plan also calls `sample_fields` at region centers + `vertical_link_for_region` + `derive_genome` (noise) — all per region, pure hash/noise, no caching. Since plans are derived once per block (18×18=324 regions), the total is fine. But each chunk generation samples... let me check level_zero (out of scope) — the chunk-level voxelizer is in level_zero, which is NOT in my scope. My scope includes world_topology (the use_case), and I should note recomputation across calls: fields are recomputed per region per block (each block re-plans its own region set + halo — adjacent blocks overlap in the halo; region plans on the halo are computed twice by two blocks — acceptable, deterministic).

Also note `red_room_event_for_cell` is O(9) candidates with each candidate doing sample_fields → 9×~18 noise evals + tournament — constant.

    2| //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
    3| //!
    4| //! Contract for implementors:
    5| //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
    6| //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
    7| //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
    8| //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
    9| //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
   10| //!   ~1 world unit wide.
   11| //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
   12| //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
   13| //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the

   31| impl GrasslandLevel {
   32|     /// Uniform per-cell hash in [0, 1): samples the value noise exactly on
   33|     /// its lattice (provider frequency 0.05 → inputs that are multiples of
   34|     /// 20 hit lattice points, where the noise is a raw uniform hash).
   35|     fn hash(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, salt: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64) -> f32 {
   36|         let v = noise.evaluate_2d(
   37|             seed ^ salt,
   38|             Position::new(cx as f32 * 20.0, cz as f32 * 20.0),
   39|         );
   40|         (v * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999)
   41|     }
   42| }
   43| 
   44| impl LevelGenerator for GrasslandLevel {
   45|     fn generate_with_reality(
   46|         &self,
   47|         chunk_pos: Position,
   48|         seed: u32,
   49|         config: GeneratorConfig,
   50|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   51|         _reality: &crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot,
   52|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
   53|         let s = config.voxel_scale;
   54|         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
   55|         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
   56|         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
   57|         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
   58|         let sky_y = height - 1;
   59| 
   60|         for z in 0..depth {
   61|             for x in 0..width {
   62|                 let wx = chunk_pos.x + (x as f32 + 0.5) * s;
   63|                 let wz = chunk_pos.z + (z as f32 + 0.5) * s;
   64| 
   65|                 // Lakes: smooth blobs of the world-space noise field.
   66|                 let lake = noise.evaluate_2d(seed ^ 0x1A5E, Position::new(wx * 0.7, wz * 0.7));
   67|                 let ground = if lake > 0.62 {
   68|                     VOXEL_WATER
   69|                 } else {
   70|                     VOXEL_GRASS
   71|                 };
   72|                 grid.set(x, 0, z, ground);
   73| 
   74|                 // Sky glow: an unbroken luminous layer overhead.
   75|                 grid.set(x, sky_y, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
   76| 
   77|                 // Ground glow grid keeps the turf bright at eye level (the
   78|                 // BFS light from the sky layer alone fades before the floor).
   79|                 let gx = wx.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
   80|                 let gz = wz.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
   81|                 if ground == VOXEL_GRASS && gx < s && gz < s {
   82|                     grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
   83|                 }
   84| 
   85|                 // Trees: hashed world cells, never in water.
   86|                 let cell_x = (wx / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
   87|                 let cell_z = (wz / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
   88|                 if Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE5, cell_x, cell_z) > 0.6 && ground == VOXEL_GRASS {
   89|                     // Trunk position jittered inside the cell.
   90|                     let jx =
   91|                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE6, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
   92|                     let jz =
   93|                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE7, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
   94|                     let tx = cell_x as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jx;
   95|                     let tz = cell_z as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jz;
   96|                     let dx = wx - tx;
   97|                     let dz = wz - tz;
   98|                     let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
   99| 
  100|                     let trunk_top = (2.2 / s) as usize;
  101|                     let canopy_top = (3.6 / s) as usize;
  102|                     if d2 < (0.25f32).powi(2) {
  103|                         for y in 1..trunk_top.min(height - 2) {
  104|                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_TREE);
  105|                         }
  106|                     }
  107|                     if d2 < (1.6f32).powi(2) {
  108|                         for y in trunk_top..canopy_top.min(height - 2) {
  109|                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_GRASS);
  110|                         }
  111|                     }
  112|                 }
  113|             }
  114|         }
  115| 
  116|         GeneratedChunk::new(grid)
  117|     }
  118| }

    1| //! Red Room presentation layered over an authored Level 0 assembly.
    2| //!
    3| //! This sampler knows nothing about chunks or voxel indices.  It receives one
    4| //! world column and returns one architectural decision, leaving recursive
    5| //! world addressing and voxelization to their own stages.
    6| 
    7| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyInstance, Axis2, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase};
    8| use crate::domain::entities::environment::EnvironmentProfile;
    9| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
   10| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   11| use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
   12| use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
   13| 
   14| /// Applies avoidable warning cues and the committed encounter topology.
   15| pub(crate) fn sample_red_room(
   16|     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
   17|     mut column: ColumnPlan,
   18|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
   19|     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
   20|     world_x: f32,
   21|     world_z: f32,
   22| ) -> ColumnPlan {
   23|     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
   24|     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
   25|     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
   26|     let loop_width = 2.0f32.min(half_x * 0.35).min(half_z * 0.35).max(1.2);
   27|     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
   28| 
   29|     // Warning cues intensify toward the shell but never replace masonry with
   30|     // a special red wall.  The anomaly is read through carpet, compression,
   31|     // and light; collision remains ordinary Level 0 architecture.
   32|     let contamination = (1.0 - boundary / (loop_width * 2.0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
   33|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::red_room(contamination);
   34|     if boundary > PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
   35|         if contamination > 0.15 {
   36|             column.floor_material = profile.floor_voxel();
   37|         }
   38|         if contamination > 0.33 {
   39|             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.2).max(2.6);
   40|         }
   41|         if contamination > 0.66 {
   42|             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.4).max(2.4);
   43|         }
   44|     }
   45|     column.fixture = Some(crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureSample {
   46|         id: (instance.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
   47|         kind: crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
   48|         state: crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureState::Lit,
   49|         center_x: 0.0,
   50|         center_z: 0.0,
   51|         half_x: 0.3,
   52|         half_z: 0.3,
   53|         ceiling_units: column.ceiling_units,
   54|         red_room: true,
   55|     });
   56| 
   57|     let Some(state) = instance.state(reality) else {
   58|         return column;
   59|     };
   60|     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::Outside {
   61|         return column;
   62|     }
   63| 
   64|     // Commitment closes the remembered entrance and reduces the authored
   65|     // room to one walkable perimeter loop around an opaque core.
   66|     let in_core = local_x.abs() < half_x - loop_width && local_z.abs() < half_z - loop_width;
   67|     column.solid = boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T || in_core;
   68|     column.lintel_from_units = None;
   69|     column.floor_material = VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
   70|     column.ceiling_units = column.ceiling_units.min(2.8);
   71|     if column.solid {
   72|         column.fixture = None;
   73|     }
   74| 
   75|     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::EscapeOpen {
   76|         open_single_escape(
   77|             instance,
   78|             state.epoch,
   79|             config.anomalies.red_escape_bias,
   80|             local_x,
   81|             local_z,
   82|             &mut column,
   83|         );
   84|     }
   85|     column
   86| }
   87| 
   88| /// Opens one deterministic side of the loop.  The bias is an authored width
   89| /// control: zero keeps the encounter sealed; positive values widen a single
   90| /// breach without turning both symmetric walls into exits.
   91| fn open_single_escape(
   92|     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
   93|     epoch: u32,
   94|     bias: f32,
   95|     local_x: f32,
   96|     local_z: f32,
   97|     column: &mut ColumnPlan,
   98| ) {
   99|     let width = bias.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.4;
  100|     if width <= 0.0 {
  101|         return;
  102|     }
  103|     let Some(threshold) = instance.gates.first() else {
  104|         return;
  105|     };
  106|     let side_sign = if stable_bit(instance.id, epoch) {
  107|         1.0
  108|     } else {
  109|         -1.0
  110|     };
  111|     let (side_coordinate, side_extent, along) = match threshold.axis {
  112|         Axis2::Z => (local_x, instance.footprint.half_x, local_z),
  113|         Axis2::X => (local_z, instance.footprint.half_z, local_x),
  114|     };
  115|     let on_selected_wall = (side_coordinate - side_sign * side_extent).abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
  116|     if on_selected_wall && along.abs() < width {
  117|         column.solid = false;
  118|     }
  119| }
  120| 
  121| fn stable_bit(instance_id: u64, epoch: u32) -> bool {
  122|     let mut value = instance_id ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(29) ^ 0xE5CA_9E5C_A9E5_CA9E;
  123|     value ^= value >> 30;
  124|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  125|     value ^= value >> 27;
  126|     value & 1 == 1
  127| }

    1| //! Assembly-derived Red Room encounter planning.
    2| //!
    3| //! A Red Room is not a macro-lattice shape. It inherits a real assembly's
    4| //! footprint and entrance, then adds stable semantic crossing planes.
    5| 
    6| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
    7|     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, AxisDirection, OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, QuarterTurn,
    8|     TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
    9| };
   10| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::AssemblyInstance;
   11| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   12| use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{SNAP, mix64, stable_id};
   13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
   14| 
   15| const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
   16| const THRESHOLD_DEPTH: f32 = 2.8;
   17| const LOOP_GATE_DEPTH: f32 = 6.0;
   18| 
   19| fn clamp_inward(desired: f32, far_inner_plane: f32, direction: AxisDirection) -> f32 {
   20|     match direction {
   21|         AxisDirection::Positive => desired.min(far_inner_plane),
   22|         AxisDirection::Negative => desired.max(far_inner_plane),
   23|     }
   24| }
   25| 
   26| fn red_room_instance(
   27|     seed: u32,
   28|     region_origin: Position,
   29|     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
   30| ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
   31|     let entrance = *assembly.primary_entrance()?;
   32|     let bounds = assembly.footprint.bounds();
   33|     let center = Position::new((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
   34|     let region_x = (region_origin.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
   35|     let region_z = (region_origin.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
   36|     let id = mix64(
   37|         stable_id(seed, AnomalyKind::RedRoom, region_x, region_z)
   38|             ^ (assembly.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
   39|     );
   40|     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
   41|         center,
   42|         half_x: (bounds.2 - bounds.0) * 0.5,
   43|         half_z: (bounds.3 - bounds.1) * 0.5,
   44|         basis: OrthoBasis {
   45|             turn: QuarterTurn::Zero,
   46|         },
   47|     };
   48|     let axis = if entrance.through_x_wall {
   49|         Axis2::Z
   50|     } else {
   51|         Axis2::X
   52|     };
   53|     let (edge_coordinate, center_coordinate, half_depth) = match axis {
   54|         Axis2::X => (entrance.center.x, center.x, footprint.half_x),
   55|         Axis2::Z => (entrance.center.z, center.z, footprint.half_z),
   56|     };
   57|     let forward = if center_coordinate >= edge_coordinate {
   58|         AxisDirection::Positive
   59|     } else {
   60|         AxisDirection::Negative
   61|     };
   62| 
   63|     // Commitment happens inside the room, beyond the externally readable
   64|     // doorway. Entrance placement guarantees enough depth for this vestibule.
   65|     let threshold_plane = edge_coordinate + forward.sign() * THRESHOLD_DEPTH;
   66|     let (span_min, span_max) = if axis == Axis2::Z {
   67|         (
   68|             entrance.center.x - entrance.width * 0.5,
   69|             entrance.center.x + entrance.width * 0.5,
   70|         )
   71|     } else {
   72|         (
   73|             entrance.center.z - entrance.width * 0.5,
   74|             entrance.center.z + entrance.width * 0.5,
   75|         )
   76|     };
   77|     let affected_bounds = footprint.bounds();
   78|     let threshold_gate = TraversalGate {
   79|         id: mix64(id ^ 0x6A7E_0ED0),
   80|         instance_id: id,
   81|         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
   82|         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
   83|         axis,
   84|         plane: threshold_plane,
   85|         span_min,
   86|         span_max,
   87|         forward,
   88|         affected_bounds,
   89|     };
   90| 
   91|     // The loop checkpoint is six units beyond commitment when the room has
   92|     // that depth. Shallow rooms clamp it one plan voxel inside the far wall,
   93|     // keeping the semantic crossing on geometry owned by this encounter.
   94|     let far_inner_plane = center_coordinate + forward.sign() * (half_depth - SNAP).max(0.0);
   95|     let loop_plane = clamp_inward(
   96|         threshold_plane + forward.sign() * LOOP_GATE_DEPTH,
   97|         far_inner_plane,
   98|         forward,
   99|     );
  100|     let loop_gate = TraversalGate {
  101|         id: mix64(id ^ 0x9B4C_1A2F),
  102|         instance_id: id,
  103|         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
  104|         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
  105|         axis,
  106|         plane: loop_plane,
  107|         span_min,
  108|         span_max,
  109|         // `forward` records the authored inward direction. Runtime state owns
  110|         // the separate policy for which traversal directions advance a loop.
  111|         forward,
  112|         affected_bounds,
  113|     };
  114| 
  115|     Some(AnomalyInstance {
  116|         id,
  117|         kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
  118|         footprint,
  119|         basis: footprint.basis,
  120|         macro_anchor: (region_x, region_z),
  121|         pillar_lattice: None,
  122|         pit_lattice: None,
  123|         arch: None,
  124|         gates: vec![threshold_gate, loop_gate],
  125|         skeleton_half_width: 1.0,
  126|         entry_band: THRESHOLD_DEPTH,
  127|     })
  128| }
  129| 
  130| pub(crate) fn plan_red_rooms(
  131|     seed: u32,
  132|     region_origin: Position,
  133|     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
  134|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  135| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
  136|     let forced = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
  137|     let organic_enabled = config.anomalies.frequency > 0.0 && config.anomalies.red_rooms > 0.0;
  138|     if !forced && !organic_enabled {
  139|         return Vec::new();
  140|     }
  141| 
  142|     assemblies
  143|         .iter()
  144|         .filter(|assembly| assembly.corruption.red_room)
  145|         .filter_map(|assembly| red_room_instance(seed, region_origin, assembly))
  146|         .collect()
  147| }

    1| //! Addressing for the Level 0 world reached through a committed Red Room.
    2| //!
    3| //! A Red Room does not invent a second procedural grammar.  It addresses a
    4| //! distant, deterministic copy of Level 0 and changes its presentation.  The
    5| //! address must therefore be stable across chunk order and worker boundaries,
    6| //! while retaining all 64 bits of anomaly identity until hashing is complete.
    7| //! Converting an `AnomalyId` directly to `f32` loses most of those bits and can
    8| //! make distinct rooms share a world; this module derives integer region
    9| //! coordinates first and converts only the small final translation.
   10|

   12|     AnomalyId, AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, PitHazard, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase, TraversalGate,
   13|     WorldBounds,

   25| // sub-centimetre detail for future fine voxel requests. Branch uniqueness is
   26| // carried by the derived seed, so the translation itself need not be huge.

  105|     /// Project a semantic gate authored in the recursive branch back into
  106|     /// the player's visible coordinate frame.
  107|     pub(crate) fn project_gate(&self, mut gate: TraversalGate) -> TraversalGate {
  108|         let offset = self.address.translation_world();
  109|         match gate.axis {
  110|             Axis2::X => {
  111|                 gate.plane -= offset.x;
  112|                 gate.span_min -= offset.z;
  113|                 gate.span_max -= offset.z;
  114|             }
  115|             Axis2::Z => {
  116|                 gate.plane -= offset.z;
  117|                 gate.span_min -= offset.x;
  118|                 gate.span_max -= offset.x;
  119|             }
  120|         }
  121|         gate.affected_bounds = self.project_bounds(gate.affected_bounds);
  122|         gate
  123|     }

  156| impl RecursiveLevelAddress {
  157|     /// Derives an address using integer avalanche hashes only.  Both halves of
  158|     /// the 64-bit instance id participate in the seed and in each axis.
  159|     pub(crate) fn derive(world_seed: u32, instance_id: AnomalyId) -> Self {
  160|         let root = mix64(
  161|             ADDRESS_DOMAIN ^ instance_id ^ (world_seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15),
  162|         );
  163|         let seed_hash = mix64(root ^ 0x5EED_5EED_A11C_0DE5);
  164|         let derived_seed = (seed_hash as u32) ^ ((seed_hash >> 32) as u32);
  165|         let translation_regions = (
  166|             translation_component(root, 0x5841_5849_5300_0001),
  167|             translation_component(root, 0x5A41_5849_5300_0002),
  168|         );
  169| 
  170|         Self {
  171|             instance_id,
  172|             derived_seed,
  173|             translation_regions,
  174|         }
  175|     }

  195|     /// Exact transform for region keys.  Planning should prefer this form so
  196|     /// large-world floating-point precision never participates in identity.
  197|     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_region(self, source_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
  198|         (
  199|             source_region.0.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.0),
  200|             source_region.1.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.1),
  201|         )
  202|     }

  204|     pub(crate) fn to_source_region(self, recursive_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
  205|         (
  206|             recursive_region
  207|                 .0
  208|                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.0),
  209|             recursive_region
  210|                 .1
  211|                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.1),
  212|         )
  213|     }

  215|     /// World-space form used by column sampling.  The translation is an exact
  216|     /// multiple of the 80u region lattice, preserving portals and 0.4u plan
  217|     /// geometry across every chunk and LOD.
  218|     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_world(self, source: Position) -> Position {
  219|         let (region, local) = split_world_position(source);
  220|         let recursive = self.to_recursive_region(region);
  221|         join_world_position(recursive, local)
  222|     }

  224|     pub(crate) fn to_source_world(self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
  225|         let (region, local) = split_world_position(recursive);
  226|         let source = self.to_source_region(region);
  227|         join_world_position(source, local)
  228|     }

  230|     pub(crate) fn translation_world(self) -> Position {
  231|         let translation = self.translation_regions();
  232|         Position::new(
  233|             translation.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
  234|             translation.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
  235|         )
  236|     }

  238|     /// Produces a Level 0 config for the addressed world.  Organic anomaly
  239|     /// tuning is preserved, allowing recursive Level 0 to remain the complete
  240|     /// generator; only the one-shot debug override is cleared so it cannot be
  241|     /// cloned into every recursive address.
  242|     pub(crate) fn recursive_config(self, mut base: GeneratorConfig) -> GeneratorConfig {
  243|         base.level = LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
  244|         base.anomalies.forced_kind = None;
  245|         base
  246|     }

  249| /// Chooses one committed Red Room without depending on snapshot insertion
  250| /// order.  Under the current state machine, only red thresholds can produce a
  251| /// non-`Outside` phase.  Progress is compared explicitly because `epoch` is
  252| /// the best available recency signal; stable identity is the final tie-break.
  253| pub(crate) fn active_red_room(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Option<&AnomalyStateStamp> {
  254|     reality
  255|         .stamps()
  256|         .iter()
  257|         .filter(|state| state.phase != RedRoomPhase::Outside)
  258|         .max_by_key(|state| {
  259|             (
  260|                 state.epoch,
  261|                 state.phase,
  262|                 state.loop_count,
  263|                 state.last_gate_id,
  264|                 state.instance_id,
  265|             )
  266|         })
  267| }
  268| 
  269| fn translation_component(root: u64, axis_domain: u64) -> i64 {
  270|     let hash = mix64(root ^ axis_domain);
  271|     let magnitude = MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS + (hash % TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN) as i64;
  272|     if hash & (1 << 63) == 0 {
  273|         magnitude
  274|     } else {
  275|         -magnitude
  276|     }
  277| }
  278| 
  279| fn split_world_position(position: Position) -> ((i64, i64), (f32, f32)) {
  280|     let region = (
  281|         (position.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
  282|         (position.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
  283|     );
  284|     let local = (
  285|         position.x - region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
  286|         position.z - region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
  287|     );
  288|     (region, local)
  289| }
  290| 
  291| fn join_world_position(region: (i64, i64), local: (f32, f32)) -> Position {
  292|     Position::new(
  293|         region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.0,
  294|         region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.1,
  295|     )
  296| }
  297| 
  298| fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
  299|     value ^= value >> 30;
  300|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  301|     value ^= value >> 27;
  302|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  303|     value ^ (value >> 31)
  304| }

recursive_level.rs: O(stamps) for active_red_room (linear scan — fine, small). No recursion. Note: RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk creates a full InfiniteRegionWindow per chunk request — if the level_zero voxelizer calls this per chunk, each call re-plans the ~9 regions of the window. This is a cache-miss opportunity: the recursive window is rebuilt per chunk with no memoization across chunks. But where is it called from? level_zero (out of scope). Still, worth noting in concurrency/perf notes: repeated planning per chunk. Actually the note at line 39-41: "The finite planning window needed to render one request... remains infinite; this value is only its local query cache". If a caller constructs RecursiveLevelWindow per chunk request without caching, that's O(9 region plans) per chunk. Let me grep who calls around_chunk.

    1| //! Bake finite-range voxel irradiance from the scene's emissive geometry.
    2| //!
    3| //! This use case deliberately separates four physically meaningful stages:
    4| //!
    5| //! 1. erase the previous bake;
    6| //! 2. inject emission through exposed downward faces of ceiling fixtures;
    7| //! 3. find shortest unobstructed paths through air in world-space units;
    8| //! 4. project that air irradiance onto the first solid surface it reaches.
    9| //!
   10| //! Solids are receivers, never propagation nodes. A wall can therefore be lit
   11| //! on its near side without becoming a light source for the room behind it.
   12| //! The working calculation is floating point; quantization happens only when
   13| //! the result is written back to the grid's established RGB 0--15 contract.
   14| //! This field is deliberately an approximate, finite-range diffuse fill. The
   15| //! renderer's analytic area lights remain authoritative for direct lighting;
   16| //! this bake neither invents omnidirectional emitters nor requires unbounded
   17| //! cross-chunk propagation halos.
   18| 
   19| mod clear_previous_bake;
   20| mod exposed_emissive_faces;
   21| mod project_onto_solid_receivers;
   22| mod propagate_through_air;
   23| mod settings;
   24| mod voxel_neighborhood;
   25| mod world_space_attenuation;
   26| mod write_air_irradiance;
   27| 
   28| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
   29| 
   30| pub use settings::{
   31|     DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings, VoxelLightingSettings,
   32| };
   33| 
   34| /// Replaces every prior light sample in `grid` with a deterministic bake.
   35| ///
   36| /// Once light has entered the air below a fixture, approximate diffuse fill
   37| /// attenuates symmetrically along face-connected paths. Its independent
   38| /// variable is shortest unobstructed path length in world units, so changing
   39| /// voxel resolution does not silently change a fixture's physical reach.
   40| pub fn bake_voxel_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, settings: VoxelLightingSettings) {
   41|     clear_previous_bake::clear_previous_bake(grid);
   42| 
   43|     let propagated = propagate_through_air::propagate_through_air(grid, settings);
   44|     write_air_irradiance::write_air_irradiance(grid, &propagated, settings);
   45|     project_onto_solid_receivers::project_onto_solid_receivers(grid, &propagated, settings);
   46| }

   49| mod tests;

   14|     pub(crate) depth: usize,
   15| }

   17| impl GridDimensions {
   18|     pub(crate) fn of(grid: &VoxelGrid) -> Self {
   19|         Self {
   20|             width: grid.width(),
   21|             height: grid.height(),
   22|             depth: grid.depth(),
   23|         }
   24|     }
   25|

   27|         self.width * self.height * self.depth
   28|     }

   30|     /// Matches `VoxelGrid`'s y-major, then z, then x storage order without
   31|     /// exposing the entity's backing vectors to the use case.
   32|     pub(crate) fn index(self, coord: VoxelCoord) -> usize {
   33|         coord.y * (self.width * self.depth) + coord.z * self.width + coord.x
   34|     }
