    1| //! # Frame Quality & Budget Controller Use Case
    2| //!
    3| //! ## Business Intent & Rationale
    4| //! In low-spec rendering environments (WebGL, low-end integrated GPUs, mobile devices),
    5| //! hardware rendering capacity is strictly constrained. Running out of frame budget causes
    6| //! stuttering, thermal throttling, and missed v-sync intervals.
    7| //!
    8| //! The `FrameQualityController` orchestrates runtime quality profiles (`SurfaceQualityProfile`)
    9| //! and enforces hard frame work budgets (maximum visible surface chunks, triangle limits, light limits).
   10| //!
   11| //! ## Design Patterns Used
   12| //! - **Strategy Pattern**: `FrameQualityHysteresisStrategy` decouples performance measurement
   13| //!   and tier transition logic from chunk submission algorithms. Hysteresis ensures the system
   14| //!   degrades rapidly upon detecting performance degradation (1 slow frame triggers downgrade)
   15| //!   while upgrading conservatively (requiring 30 consecutive fast frames to upgrade).
   16| //! - **Observer Pattern / Telemetry**: `SurfaceRenderingTelemetry` records per-frame performance metrics,
   17| //!   ISO 8601 timestamps, input arguments, and return values for observability.
   18| 
   19| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   20| use crate::domain::entities::surface_quality_profile::{SurfaceQualityProfile, SurfaceQualityTier};
   21| use std::time::Duration;
   22| 
   23| /// Telemetry metric payload for observability & performance tracking.
   24| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
   25| pub struct SurfaceRenderingTelemetry {
   26|     /// ISO 8601 formatted timestamp of the frame render event.
   27|     pub timestamp_iso8601: String,
   28|     /// Total candidate chunks evaluated for rendering.
   29|     pub candidate_chunks: usize,
   30|     /// Chunks culled by frustum/distance culling.
   31|     pub distance_culled_chunks: usize,
   32|     /// Chunks culled due to work budget limits.
   33|     pub budget_culled_chunks: usize,
   34|     /// Chunks accepted and submitted for surface rendering.
   35|     pub visible_surface_chunks: usize,
   36|     /// Total surface quads submitted.
   37|     pub submitted_quads: usize,
   38|     /// Total surface triangles submitted (2 per quad).
   39|     pub submitted_triangles: usize,
   40|     /// Total draw call submissions.
   41|     pub draw_calls: usize,
   42|     /// Active dynamic light count.
   43|     pub active_lights: usize,
   44|     /// Active quality tier name.
   45|     pub active_tier: SurfaceQualityTier,
   46|     /// Current render scale.
   47|     pub render_scale: f32,
   48| }
   49| 
   50| impl SurfaceRenderingTelemetry {
   51|     pub fn new(
   52|         timestamp_iso8601: impl Into<String>,
   53|         active_tier: SurfaceQualityTier,
   54|         render_scale: f32,
   55|     ) -> Self {
   56|         Self {
   57|             timestamp_iso8601: timestamp_iso8601.into(),
   58|             candidate_chunks: 0,
   59|             distance_culled_chunks: 0,
   60|             budget_culled_chunks: 0,
   61|             visible_surface_chunks: 0,
   62|             submitted_quads: 0,
   63|             submitted_triangles: 0,
   64|             draw_calls: 0,
   65|             active_lights: 0,
   66|             active_tier,
   67|             render_scale,
   68|         }
   69|     }
   70| }
   71| 
   72| /// A surface chunk candidate with its world origin position and quad count.
   73| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
   74| pub struct ChunkSurfaceCandidate {
   75|     pub chunk_x: i32,
   76|     pub chunk_z: i32,
   77|     pub origin: Position,
   78|     pub quad_count: usize,
   79| }
   80| 
   81| /// Use case controller governing real-time frame quality and budget culling.
   82| #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   83| pub struct FrameQualityController {
   84|     pub profile: SurfaceQualityProfile,
   85|     target_frame_duration: Duration,
   86|     fast_frame_counter: usize,
   87|     upgrade_threshold_frames: usize,
   88| }
   89| 
   90| impl FrameQualityController {
   91|     pub fn new(initial_tier: SurfaceQualityTier) -> Self {
   92|         let profile = match initial_tier {
   93|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => SurfaceQualityProfile::ultra_low(),
   94|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => SurfaceQualityProfile::low(),
   95|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced(),
   96|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => SurfaceQualityProfile::high(),
   97|         };
   98|         Self {
   99|             profile,
  100|             target_frame_duration: Duration::from_millis(16), // ~60 FPS target
  101|             fast_frame_counter: 0,
  102|             upgrade_threshold_frames: 30, // Require 30 consecutive fast frames to upgrade
  103|         }
  104|     }
  105| 
  106|     /// Reports a completed frame's execution time and applies hysteresis rules.
  107|     ///
  108|     /// # Inputs
  109|     /// - `frame_duration`: Execution time of the previous frame.
  110|     ///
  111|     /// # Returns
  112|     /// - `bool`: True if the quality tier was changed.
  113|     pub fn report_frame_time(&mut self, frame_duration: Duration) -> bool {
  114|         let slow_threshold = self
  115|             .target_frame_duration
  116|             .saturating_add(Duration::from_millis(4)); // > 20ms is slow
  117|         let fast_threshold = Duration::from_millis(11); // < 11ms is fast
  118| 
  119|         if frame_duration > slow_threshold {
  120|             // Immediate downgrade on sustained slow frame to protect frame rate stability
  121|             self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
  122|             self.downgrade_tier()
  123|         } else if frame_duration < fast_threshold {
  124|             self.fast_frame_counter += 1;
  125|             if self.fast_frame_counter >= self.upgrade_threshold_frames {
  126|                 self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
  127|                 self.upgrade_tier()
  128|             } else {
  129|                 false
  130|             }
  131|         } else {
  132|             self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
  133|             false
  134|         }
  135|     }
  136| 
  137|     fn downgrade_tier(&mut self) -> bool {
  138|         match self.profile.tier {
  139|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => {
  140|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced();
  141|                 true
  142|             }
  143|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => {
  144|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::low();
  145|                 true
  146|             }
  147|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => {
  148|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::ultra_low();
  149|                 true
  150|             }
  151|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => false,
  152|         }
  153|     }
  154| 
  155|     fn upgrade_tier(&mut self) -> bool {
  156|         match self.profile.tier {
  157|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => {
  158|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::low();
  159|                 true
  160|             }
  161|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => {
  162|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced();
  163|                 true
  164|             }
  165|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => {
  166|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::high();
  167|                 true
  168|             }
  169|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => false,
  170|         }
  171|     }
  172| 
  173|     /// Filters and sorts surface chunk candidates by distance from player, enforcing hard work budgets.
  174|     ///
  175|     /// # Rules
  176|     /// 1. Chunks farther than max distance or max_visible_chunks budget are culled.
  177|     /// 2. Triangle budget (`max_triangles_per_frame`) is strictly enforced.
  178|     /// 3. Closest chunks to player are prioritized deterministically.
  179|     pub fn evaluate_and_cull_chunks(
  180|         &self,
  181|         player_pos: Position,
  182|         candidates: &[ChunkSurfaceCandidate],
  183|         iso8601_timestamp: &str,
  184|     ) -> (Vec<ChunkSurfaceCandidate>, SurfaceRenderingTelemetry) {
  185|         let mut telemetry = SurfaceRenderingTelemetry::new(
  186|             iso8601_timestamp,
  187|             self.profile.tier,
  188|             self.profile.render_scale,
  189|         );
  190|         telemetry.candidate_chunks = candidates.len();
  191| 
  192|         // Distance calculate and sort candidates closest to player first
  193|         let mut scored: Vec<(f32, &ChunkSurfaceCandidate)> = candidates
  194|             .iter()
  195|             .map(|c| {
  196|                 let dx = c.origin.x - player_pos.x;
  197|                 let dz = c.origin.z - player_pos.z;
  198|                 let dist_sq = dx * dx + dz * dz;
  199|                 (dist_sq, c)
  200|             })
  201|             .collect();
  202| 
  203|         scored.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.partial_cmp(&b.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
  204| 
  205|         let mut accepted = Vec::new();
  206|         let mut accumulated_triangles = 0;
  207| 
  208|         for (_dist_sq, candidate) in scored {
  209|             if accepted.len() >= self.profile.max_visible_chunks {
  210|                 telemetry.budget_culled_chunks += 1;
  211|                 continue;
  212|             }
  213| 
  214|             let cand_triangles = candidate.quad_count * 2;
  215|             if accumulated_triangles + cand_triangles > self.profile.max_triangles_per_frame
  216|                 && !accepted.is_empty()
  217|             {
  218|                 telemetry.budget_culled_chunks += 1;
  219|                 continue;
  220|             }
  221| 
  222|             accumulated_triangles += cand_triangles;
  223|             telemetry.submitted_quads += candidate.quad_count;
  224|             accepted.push(candidate.clone());
  225|         }
  226| 
  227|         telemetry.visible_surface_chunks = accepted.len();
  228|         telemetry.submitted_triangles = accumulated_triangles;
  229|         telemetry.draw_calls = accepted.len(); // 1 draw call per chunk baseline
  230|         telemetry.active_lights = self.profile.max_dynamic_lights;
  231| 
  232|         (accepted, telemetry)
  233|     }
  234| }

It re-sorts every frame — could keep a sorted structure or reuse the previous frame's order (players move slowly). This is a per-frame recomputation: O(N log N) sort of all candidate chunks per frame — Medium/Low. Since most chunks remain visible across frames, incremental/sorted insertion could help, but N is small (~100-1000). Also note the clone per accepted candidate (`candidate.clone()`). Fine.

    1| //! Debug hook: ASCII plan view of one region.

    5| 
    6| /// ASCII plan view at `step` world units per character. Corridors `=`, macro
    7| /// anomalies `P/B/H` (pillar/blackout/pits), red loops `R`, assembly interiors
    8| /// by program initial, entrances `+`, empty fabric `.`.
    9| pub fn debug_region_ascii(plan: &RegionPlan, step: f32) -> String {
   10|     let n = (plan.size_world / step) as usize;
   11|     let mut out = String::with_capacity((n + 1) * n);
   12|     for iz in 0..n {
   13|         for ix in 0..n {
   14|             let x = plan.origin_world.x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * step;
   15|             let z = plan.origin_world.z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * step;
   16|             let mut ch = '.';
   17|             for a in &plan.assemblies {
   18|                 if a.footprint.contains(x, z) {
   19|                     ch = match a.program {
   20|                         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 'o',
   21|                         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 'p',
   22|                         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 'c',
   23|                         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 'b',
   24|                         SpaceProgram::Storage => 's',
   25|                         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 'v',
   26|                         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 'w',
   27|                         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => 'x',
   28|                         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 'A',
   29|                         SpaceProgram::Reception => 'R',
   30|                         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 't',
   31|                         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 'm',
   32|                         SpaceProgram::Stair => 'S',
   33|                         _ => 'r',
   34|                     };
   35|                 }
   36|             }
   37|             for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
   38|                 if anomaly.contains(x, z) {
   39|                     ch = match anomaly.kind {
   40|                         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => 'P',
   41|                         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => 'B',
   42|                         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => 'H',
   43|                         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => 'R',
   44|                         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => 'M',
   45|                     };
   46|                 }
   47|             }
   48|             for s in &plan.corridors {
   49|                 if s.distance(x, z) <= s.width * 0.5 {
   50|                     ch = '=';
   51|                 }
   52|             }

   42| /// Sample one immutable macro anomaly or stable archway anchor.
   43| ///
   44| /// Corridors have already won composition priority before this function is
   45| /// called, so every family may assume its protected bearing route is the only
   46| /// remaining cross-cutting circulation concern. Blackout expanses delegate
   47| /// their substrate to the ordinary Level 0 fabric sampler before applying the
   48| /// anomaly profile.
   49| pub(crate) fn sample_anomaly(
   50|     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
   51|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
   52|     seed: u32,
   53|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
   54|     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
   55|     world_x: f32,

   58|     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
   59|     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
   60|     let seam_x = world_x.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
   61|     let seam_z = world_z.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);

   63|         instance,
   64|         noise,
   65|         seed,
   66|         config,
   67|         reality,

   74|         skeleton: local_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width,

   76|             && seam_x < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
   77|             && seam_z > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
   78|             && seam_z < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0,

   84|         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => sample_pit_lattice(&context),
   85|         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => sample_archway_anchor(&context),
   86|         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms have a dedicated geometry sampler"),

   90| /// Dehydration multiplies mutable-infill probability: tier 3 nearly
   91| /// doubles how much anomalous mass a re-dealt space grows.
   92| fn delirium_gain(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> f32 {
   93|     1.0 + 0.3 * reality.delirium() as f32

   95| 
   96| fn anomaly_hash(instance: &AnomalyInstance, epoch: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> f32 {
   97|     let mut hash = instance.id
   98|         ^ salt
   99|         ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(19)
  100|         ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
  101|         ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(37);
  102|     hash ^= hash >> 30;
  103|     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  104|     hash ^= hash >> 27;
  105|     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  106|     hash ^= hash >> 31;
  107|     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
  108| }
  109| 
  110| fn remap_epoch(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
  111|     let state = context.instance.state(context.reality)?;
  112|     (state.epoch > 0
  113|         && context.boundary > context.instance.entry_band
  114|         && state.point_is_in_wake(
  115|             context.world_x,
  116|             context.world_z,
  117|             context.config.anomalies.remap_distance,
  118|         ))
  119|     .then_some(state.epoch)
  120| }

  122| fn sample_pillar_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
  123|     let instance = context.instance;
  124|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
  125|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
  126|     let lattice = instance.pillar_lattice.expect("pillar instance lattice");
  127|     // A pillar stands *on* a lattice line, straddling it, so the column
  128|     // that owns it is the nearest line — `round`, not `floor`. Under
  129|     // `floor` the four quadrants of one pillar fell into four different
  130|     // bays and each looked up its own size, which is why pillars came out
  131|     // as stepped, L-shaped masses that read as two or three blocks fused.
  132|     // That was invisible while every pillar was the same size and became
  133|     // obvious the moment they were not: the bug was always there, the
  134|     // uniformity was hiding it.
  135|     let mut off_x = local_x - lattice.phase_x;
  136|     let off_z = local_z - lattice.phase_z;
  137|     let cell_z = (off_z / lattice.bay_z).round() as i64;
  138| 
  139|     // Distortion grows only after the entry has taught the player a regular
  140|     // grid. The route and entry band therefore remain a reliable baseline.
  141|     // Every decision here is about *this pillar* — drop it, fatten it,
  142|     // shift its row — so each is answered once, against the row's own
  143|     // budget rather than a budget that varies across the pillar's own
  144|     // footprint.
  145|     let row_centre = instance.world_coords(
  146|         lattice.phase_x + off_x,
  147|         lattice.phase_z + cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z,
  148|     );
  149|     let budget = ((instance.boundary_distance(row_centre.x, row_centre.z) - instance.entry_band)
  150|         / (instance.entry_band.max(8.0) * 2.5))
  151|         .clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  152|     let immutable_zone = context.skeleton || budget <= 0.0;
  153|     // A shifted row moves the whole line of pillars half a bay across.
  154|     // Decided before the column index is taken, so the shift moves which
  155|     // pillar this is rather than tearing the one it lands on.
  156|     if !immutable_zone && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D1, cell_z, 0) < 0.30 * budget {
  157|         off_x += lattice.bay_x * 0.5;
  158|     }
  159|     let cell_x = (off_x / lattice.bay_x).round() as i64;
  160|     let mut shape = instance
  161|         .pillar_shape(cell_x, cell_z)
  162|         .unwrap_or(PillarShape {
  163|             half_x: 0.6,
  164|             half_z: 0.6,
  165|             cross: None,
  166|         });
  167| 
  168|     // The protected bearing lane is a route the wanderer can trust, and it
  169|     // is cut before anything is built rather than after: a pillar the lane
  170|     // passes through is not built at all. Clipping it instead left a thin
  171|     // cap of masonry on each side of the route — debris, and precisely the
  172|     // kind of fragment that reads as a mistake rather than as a building.
  173|     let reach_z = shape
  174|         .cross
  175|         .map_or(shape.half_z, |(_, hz)| shape.half_z.max(hz));
  176|     let line_z = lattice.phase_z + cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z;
  177|     let mut dropped = line_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width + reach_z;
  178|     let mut nudge_x = 0.0f32;
  179|     if !immutable_zone {
  180|         dropped |= anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D0, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.10 * budget;
  181|         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D2, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.08 * budget {
  182|             shape = shape.grown(0.2);
  183|         }
  184|     }
  185| 
  186|     // A committed wake may change relationships between bays, but never at a
  187|     // stable content-tile seam where resident reality cohorts meet.
  188|     let wake_epoch = (!immutable_zone && context.away_from_seam)
  189|         .then(|| remap_epoch(context))
  190|         .flatten();
  191|     if let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
  192|         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F4, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.25 {
  193|             shape = shape.grown(0.2);
  194|         }
  195|         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F5, cell_z, cell_x) < 0.35 {
  196|             // Off its line, and off it as one piece: the pillar moves, it
  197|             // does not smear.
  198|             nudge_x = 0.4;
  199|         }
  200|     }
  201| 
  202|     let dx = (off_x - cell_x as f32 * lattice.bay_x - nudge_x).abs();
  203|     let dz = (off_z - cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z).abs();
  204|     let mut solid = context.perimeter || (!dropped && shape.covers(dx, dz));
  205|     if !solid && let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
  206|         let edge_x = dx < PLAN_WALL_T;
  207|         let edge_z = dz < PLAN_WALL_T;
  208|         let threshold =
  209|             (0.12 * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity * delirium_gain(context.reality))
  210|                 .clamp(0.0, 0.48);
  211|         solid = (edge_x && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F1, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold)
  212|             || (edge_z && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F2, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold);
  213|     }
  214|     if context.skeleton {
  215|         solid = false;
  216|     }
  217| 
  218|     let lane_light =
  219|         local_z.abs() < 0.45 && (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
  220|     let field_light = (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
  221|         && (local_z + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
  222|         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11A7, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.62 * tuning.lights;
  223|     let ceiling_units = if !immutable_zone
  224|         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D3, cell_x / 2, cell_z / 2) < 0.35 * budget
  225|     {
  226|         4.0
  227|     } else {
  228|         4.2
  229|     };
  230|     let fixture = (!solid && (lane_light || field_light)).then_some(FixtureSample {
  231|         id: (instance.id as u64) << 32 ^ ((cell_x as u64) << 16) ^ (cell_z as u64 & 0xFFFF),
  232|         kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
  233|         state: FixtureState::Lit,
  234|         center_x: context.world_x,
  235|         center_z: context.world_z,
  236|         half_x: 0.3,
  237|         half_z: 0.3,
  238|         ceiling_units,
  239|         red_room: false,
  240|     });
  241|     ColumnPlan {
  242|         fixture,
  243|         solid,
  244|         ceiling_units,
  245|         floor_material: EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel(),
  246|         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
  247|     }
  248| }

  250| fn sample_blackout_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
  251|     let instance = context.instance;
  252|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
  253|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
  254|     // The blackout substrate is ordinary fabric under the profile — and it
  255|     // drifts under the same Peripheral Shift stamps as ordinary fabric. In
  256|     // here the engine also advances drift *behind the player in real time*
  257|     // (the darkness hides the swap), so a blackout rearranges more cruelly
  258|     // than the level outside it: turning around is never a way back.
  259|     let mut plan = BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
  260|         context.noise,

  268|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::blackout(depth);

  319|             (local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45 && tuning.lights > 0.0).then_some(FixtureSample {
  320|                 id: (instance.id as u64) << 16 ^ 0xCA71_C001,
  321|                 kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentStrip,
  322|                 state: FixtureState::Lit,

  324|                 center_z: context.world_z,

  456| /// Stable pale arch rooms never inspect `RealitySnapshot`, which keeps them a
  457| /// fixed landmark against every mutable anomaly family.
  458| ///
  459| /// A `Transition` room is a *graph connector*: its `ArchBehavior` decides
  460| /// what its far half (local `z > 0`) belongs to. The seam is expressed only
  461| /// through legal architectural vocabulary — ceiling regime, floor finish,
  462| /// lintel height, fixture rhythm — never through impossible collision or a
  463| /// repainted wall, so the crossing is felt before it is understood.
  464| fn sample_archway_anchor(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
  465|     let instance = context.instance;
  466|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
  467|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
  468|     let arch = instance.arch.expect("arch instance profile");
  469|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::archway_room();
  470|     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
  471|     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
  472| 
  473|     // The far half of a seam room disagrees with the near half.
  474|     let far_side = local_z > 0.0;
  475|     let (ceiling_units, floor_material) = match arch.behavior {
  476|         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => {
  477|             (3.0, EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel())
  478|         }
  479|         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => (4.4, profile.floor_voxel()),
  480|         _ => (3.6, profile.floor_voxel()),
  481|     };
  482|     let mut plan = ColumnPlan {
  483|         wall_material: profile.wall_voxel(),
  484|         floor_material,
  485|         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
  486|     };
  487| 
  488|     let bay_index = ((local_x + half_x) / arch.bay).floor() as i64;
  489|     let along = (local_x + half_x).rem_euclid(arch.bay);
  490|     // The far arcade of a scale breach broadens its openings; a culture
  491|     // seam presses its lintels lower. Both stay on the shared bay rhythm so
  492|     // the two walls visibly disagree about the same structure.
  493|     let effective_opening = match arch.behavior {
  494|         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => arch.opening * 1.5,
  495|         _ => arch.opening,
  496|     };
  497|     let head_drop = match arch.behavior {
  498|         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => 0.4,
  499|         _ => 0.0,
  500|     };
  501|     let across_opening = (along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() < effective_opening * 0.5;
  502|     let blind = bay_index.rem_euclid(arch.blind_every as i64) == arch.blind_every as i64 - 1;
  503|     let arch_head = {
  504|         let t = ((along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() / (effective_opening * 0.5)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  505|         (((arch.spring_units - head_drop) + 0.6 * (1.0 - t)) / 0.2).round() * 0.2
  506|     };
  507| 
  508|     if context.perimeter {
  509|         plan.solid = tuning.walls > 0.0;
  510|         let on_long_wall = half_z - local_z.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T;
  511|         match arch.layout {
  512|             ArchLayout::Transition => {
  513|                 if on_long_wall && across_opening && !blind {
  514|                     plan.solid = false;
  515|                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(arch_head);
  516|                 }
  517|             }
  518|             ArchLayout::DeadEnd => {
  519|                 let on_entrance_wall = half_x - local_x.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T && local_x < 0.0;
  520|                 if on_entrance_wall && local_z.abs() < 1.0 {
  521|                     plan.solid = false;
  522|                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(
  523|                         ((arch.spring_units + 0.6 * (1.0 - local_z.abs())) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
  524|                     );
  525|                 }
  526|             }
  527|         }
  528|         return plan;
  529|     }
  530| 
  531|     if arch.layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
  532|         let arcade_plane = half_z - 1.2 - PLAN_WALL_T;
  533|         let in_arcade = (local_z.abs() - arcade_plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5;
  534|         let in_alcove = local_z.abs() > arcade_plane;
  535|         if in_arcade && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
  536|             if across_opening && !blind {
  537|                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(arch_head);
  538|             } else {
  539|                 plan.solid = true;
  540|             }
  541|         } else if in_alcove {
  542|             plan.ceiling_units = 3.0;
  543|             if ((local_x * 2.5).sin() * (local_z * 1.7).cos()).abs() < 0.3 {
  544|                 plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
  545|             }
  546|         }
  547|     }
  548| 
  549|     let has_light = local_z.abs() < 0.45
  550|         && (local_x + half_x - arch.bay * 0.5).rem_euclid(arch.bay * 2.0) < 0.45
  551|         && tuning.lights > 0.0;
  552|     plan.fixture = has_light.then_some(FixtureSample {
  553|         id: (instance.id as u64) ^ 0xA0C1_0000_0000,
  554|         kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
  555|         state: FixtureState::Lit,
  556|         center_x: context.world_x,
  557|         center_z: context.world_z,
  558|         half_x: 0.3,
  559|         half_z: 0.3,
  560|         ceiling_units,
  561|         red_room: false,
  562|     });
  563|     let _ = context.boundary;
  564|     plan
  565| }

Key finding: `level_zero/generate.rs:331` — `RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk(...)` is called **per chunk generation** (inside `generate_from_plans`).  291| impl BackroomsLevel {
 292|     /// Voxelizes one chunk, optionally from plans somebody else already
 293|     /// made. `None` derives them per chunk, exactly as streaming always has.
 294|     pub fn generate_from_plans(
 295|         chunk_pos: Position,
 296|         seed: u32,
 297|         config: GeneratorConfig,
 298|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 299|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 300|         provided_plans: Option<&InfiniteRegionWindow>,
 301|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
 302|         let s = config.voxel_scale;
 303|         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 304|         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 305|         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
 306|         let mut chunk = GeneratedChunk::new(VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth));
 307| 
 308|         // Base plans remain available for the authored threshold and for
 309|         // ordinary reality. A committed Red Room adds a second, explicitly
 310|         // addressed Level 0 window instead of smuggling offsets and seeds
 311|         // through the voxel loop.
 312|         // Plans come from outside when a `WorldBlock` has already planned
 313|         // this area, and are derived per chunk otherwise. Injecting rather
 314|         // than always deriving is what lets a bulk-planned block feed the
 315|         // voxel path: same plans, one derivation, and any block-scale pass
 316|         // run over them is visible to every chunk inside it.
 317|         let derived;
 318|         let plans = match provided_plans {
 319|             Some(plans) => plans,
 320|             None => {
 321|                 derived = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 322|                     chunk_pos,
 323|                     config.chunk_size,
 324|                     seed,
 325|                     &config,
 326|                     noise,
 327|                 );
 328|                 &derived
 329|             }
 330|         };
 331|         let recursive_level = RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk(
 332|             chunk_pos,
 333|             config.chunk_size,
 334|             1.0,
 335|             seed,
 336|             config,
 337|             noise,
 338|             reality,
 339|         );
 340| 
 341|         // Architecture first: plan every region this chunk overlaps.
 342|         let plan_of = |wx: f32, wz: f32| -> &RegionPlan {
 343|             plans
 344|                 .plan_at(Position::new(wx, wz))
 345|                 .expect("region window covers the requested voxel halo")
 346|         };
 347| 
 348|         // Export semantic crossings/hazards/lights from the same immutable
 349|         // plans as voxel geometry, decided before anything is voxelized —
 350|         // see decide_traversal_gates_and_hazards and decide_runtime_lights.
 351|         let chunk_bounds = WorldBounds::new(
 352|             chunk_pos.x,
 353|             chunk_pos.z,
 354|             chunk_pos.x + config.chunk_size,
 355|             chunk_pos.z + config.chunk_size,
 356|         );
 357|         let (gates, hazards) =
 358|             decide_traversal_gates_and_hazards(&plans, recursive_level.as_ref(), chunk_bounds);
 359|         chunk.entities.traversal_gates.extend(gates);

 361|         chunk.entities.runtime_lights.extend(decide_runtime_lights(

 365|             &config,
 366|             seed,
 367|             noise,
 368|             reality,
 369|         ));

 371|         // Plan every column plus a 1-voxel margin: ceiling skirts must seal
 372|         // height steps across chunk borders too.
 373|         let plan_at = |lx: i64, lz: i64| -> ColumnPlan {
 374|             let wx = chunk_pos.x + (lx as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 375|             let wz = chunk_pos.z + (lz as f32 + 0.5) * s;

 377|             if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {

 379|                     .plan_at(Position::new(wx, wz))
 380|                     .expect("recursive region window covers the voxel halo");

This confirms a major finding:
1. **`RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk` at level_zero/generate.rs:331** is constructed on **every chunk generation** (inside `generate_from_plans`, called from `execute_from_plans` → `generate_chunk.rs:388` and `generate_chunk.rs:396`). When a red room is committed, it builds a full `InfiniteRegionWindow` — planning ~9 regions × full `generate_region_plan` (which itself plans corridors, does the greedy layout solver, corruption pass, anomaly planning, etc.). This is a heavy recomputation per chunk with zero caching across chunks. Even the base path (`None` plans → `region_plans_for`) derives ~9 region plans per chunk — the streaming path. The WorldBlock path injects plans, but the recursive window is still rebuilt per chunk. High impact finding: memoize RecursiveLevelWindow per (instance_id, area) across chunk requests.

2. The per-chunk `plans.plan_at(...)` is called per column (width×depth ≈ 40k columns) — plan_at is O(1) (index math + Vec get) — fine.

 759|     /// Nearest point on the centerline: `(distance, along, is_horizontal)`.
 760|     /// `along` is the world coordinate *along* the nearest segment's axis, so
 761|     /// modules (light strips, wall gaps) repeat in world space and stay
 762|     /// continuous across chunk and region borders.
 763|     pub fn nearest(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> (f32, f32, bool) {
 764|         let mut best = (f32::MAX, 0.0, true);
 765|         for seg in self.path.windows(2) {
 766|             let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 767|             let (dx, dz) = (b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z);
 768|             let len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 769|             let t = if len2 > 0.0 {
 770|                 (((x - a.x) * dx + (z - a.z) * dz) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 771|             } else {
 772|                 0.0
 773|             };

 775|             let d2 = (x - px) * (x - px) + (z - pz) * (z - pz);
 776|             if d2 < best.0 {

 778|                 best = (d2, if horizontal { px } else { pz }, horizontal);

    1| //! 3D Wave Function Collapse over a 6-connected voxel-module lattice.
    2| //!
    3| //! Every cell starts in superposition of all modules. Each iteration picks
    4| //! the uncollapsed cell with minimal weighted Shannon entropy, collapses it
    5| //! to one module by weighted draw, and propagates the six-axis adjacency
    6| //! constraints until the wave is quiet. A cell emptied of candidates is a
    7| //! contradiction, reported with its position rather than papered over.
    8| //!
    9| //! Module sets are capped at 64 so a superposition is one `u64` bitmask:
   10| //! support unions and constraint intersections are single bitwise ops.
   11| 
   12| use rand::rngs::StdRng;
   13| use rand::{RngExt, SeedableRng};
   14| 
   15| /// The six lattice directions, ordered so `opposite()` is a bit flip.
   16| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   17| pub enum Axis6 {
   18|     PosX = 0,
   19|     NegX = 1,
   20|     PosY = 2,
   21|     NegY = 3,
   22|     PosZ = 4,
   23|     NegZ = 5,
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl Axis6 {
   27|     pub const ALL: [Axis6; 6] = [
   28|         Axis6::PosX,
   29|         Axis6::NegX,
   30|         Axis6::PosY,
   31|         Axis6::NegY,
   32|         Axis6::PosZ,
   33|         Axis6::NegZ,
   34|     ];
   35| 
   36|     pub fn opposite(self) -> Axis6 {
   37|         Axis6::ALL[self as usize ^ 1]
   38|     }
   39| 
   40|     fn offset(self) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
   41|         match self {
   42|             Axis6::PosX => (1, 0, 0),
   43|             Axis6::NegX => (-1, 0, 0),
   44|             Axis6::PosY => (0, 1, 0),
   45|             Axis6::NegY => (0, -1, 0),
   46|             Axis6::PosZ => (0, 0, 1),
   47|             Axis6::NegZ => (0, 0, -1),
   48|         }
   49|     }
   50| }
   51| 
   52| /// A weighted module catalog plus its directional adjacency rules.
   53| pub struct WfcModuleSet {
   54|     weights: Vec<f32>,
   55|     /// `allowed[dir][module]`: bitmask of modules permitted as the neighbor
   56|     /// of `module` in direction `dir`.
   57|     allowed: [Vec<u64>; 6],
   58| }
   59| 
   60| impl WfcModuleSet {
   61|     /// `weights[m]` biases how often module `m` is drawn on collapse.
   62|     pub fn new(weights: Vec<f32>) -> Self {
   63|         assert!(
   64|             weights.len() <= 64,
   65|             "a superposition is one u64: at most 64 modules"
   66|         );
   67|         assert!(weights.iter().all(|&w| w > 0.0), "weights must be positive");
   68|         let empty = vec![0u64; weights.len()];
   69|         Self {
   70|             weights,
   71|             allowed: std::array::from_fn(|_| empty.clone()),
   72|         }
   73|     }
   74| 
   75|     pub fn module_count(&self) -> usize {
   76|         self.weights.len()
   77|     }
   78| 
   79|     /// Declares "`b` may sit in direction `dir` of `a`" and its mirror rule,
   80|     /// so adjacency stays symmetric by construction.
   81|     pub fn allow(&mut self, a: usize, dir: Axis6, b: usize) {
   82|         self.allowed[dir as usize][a] |= 1 << b;
   83|         self.allowed[dir.opposite() as usize][b] |= 1 << a;
   84|     }
   85| 
   86|     /// Union of what every candidate in `mask` tolerates in `dir`.
   87|     fn support(&self, mask: u64, dir: Axis6) -> u64 {
   88|         let mut union = 0;
   89|         let mut rest = mask;
   90|         while rest != 0 {
   91|             let module = rest.trailing_zeros() as usize;
   92|             union |= self.allowed[dir as usize][module];
   93|             rest &= rest - 1;
   94|         }
   95|         union
   96|     }
   97| 
   98|     fn full_mask(&self) -> u64 {
   99|         if self.module_count() == 64 {
  100|             u64::MAX
  101|         } else {
  102|             (1 << self.module_count()) - 1
  103|         }
  104|     }
  105| }
  106| 
  107| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  108| pub struct WfcContradiction {
  109|     pub position: (usize, usize, usize),
  110| }
  111| 
  112| /// A solved lattice: `modules[index_of(x, y, z)]` is the collapsed module.
  113| pub struct WfcSolution {
  114|     pub dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  115|     pub modules: Vec<u8>,
  116| }
  117| 
  118| impl WfcSolution {
  119|     pub fn module_at(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
  120|         self.modules[index_of(self.dims, x, y, z)]
  121|     }
  122| }
  123| 
  124| fn index_of(dims: (usize, usize, usize), x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> usize {
  125|     (y * dims.2 + z) * dims.0 + x
  126| }
  127| 
  128| /// Runs the collapse to completion. Deterministic per (set, dims, seed).
  129| pub fn solve_wfc(
  130|     set: &WfcModuleSet,
  131|     dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  132|     seed: u64,
  133| ) -> Result<WfcSolution, WfcContradiction> {
  134|     let (w, h, d) = dims;
  135|     let mut cells = vec![set.full_mask(); w * h * d];
  136|     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
  137| 
  138|     // Settle the initial wave first: a catalog whose full superposition
  139|     // already lacks support somewhere must surface as a contradiction even
  140|     // if no collapse would ever visit that cell.
  141|     let every_cell: Vec<usize> = (0..cells.len()).collect();
  142|     propagate(set, dims, &mut cells, every_cell)?;
  143| 
  144|     while let Some(cell) = lowest_entropy_cell(set, &cells) {
  145|         collapse(set, &mut cells[cell], &mut rng);
  146|         propagate(set, dims, &mut cells, vec![cell])?;
  147|     }
  148| 
  149|     Ok(WfcSolution {
  150|         dims,
  151|         modules: cells
  152|             .iter()
  153|             .map(|mask| mask.trailing_zeros() as u8)
  154|             .collect(),
  155|     })
  156| }
  157| 
  158| /// The uncollapsed cell with minimal weighted Shannon entropy
  159| /// `H = ln W - (Σ w·ln w)/W`; first occurrence wins ties for determinism.
  160| fn lowest_entropy_cell(set: &WfcModuleSet, cells: &[u64]) -> Option<usize> {
  161|     let mut best: Option<(f32, usize)> = None;
  162|     for (index, &mask) in cells.iter().enumerate() {
  163|         if mask.count_ones() <= 1 {
  164|             continue;
  165|         }
  166|         let (mut total, mut weighted_log) = (0.0f32, 0.0f32);
  167|         let mut rest = mask;
  168|         while rest != 0 {
  169|             let weight = set.weights[rest.trailing_zeros() as usize];
  170|             total += weight;
  171|             weighted_log += weight * weight.ln();
  172|             rest &= rest - 1;
  173|         }
  174|         let entropy = total.ln() - weighted_log / total;
  175|         if best.is_none_or(|(lowest, _)| entropy < lowest) {
  176|             best = Some((entropy, index));
  177|         }
  178|     }
  179|     best.map(|(_, index)| index)
  180| }
  181| 
  182| /// Collapses one superposition to a single module by weighted draw.
  183| fn collapse(set: &WfcModuleSet, mask: &mut u64, rng: &mut StdRng) {
  184|     let total: f32 = candidates(*mask).map(|m| set.weights[m]).sum();
  185|     let mut roll = rng.random::<f32>() * total;
  186|     for module in candidates(*mask) {
  187|         roll -= set.weights[module];
  188|         if roll <= 0.0 {
  189|             *mask = 1 << module;
  190|             return;
  191|         }
  192|     }
  193|     // Float round-off fell past the last candidate: take it.
  194|     let last = 63 - mask.leading_zeros();
  195|     *mask = 1 << last;
  196| }
  197| 
  198| fn candidates(mask: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> {
  199|     (0..64).filter(move |m| mask & (1 << m) != 0)
  200| }
  201| 
  202| /// Worklist constraint propagation: each changed cell re-restricts its six
  203| /// neighbors until the wave settles or a cell runs out of candidates.
  204| fn propagate(
  205|     set: &WfcModuleSet,
  206|     dims: (usize, usize, usize),
  207|     cells: &mut [u64],
  208|     mut work: Vec<usize>,
  209| ) -> Result<(), WfcContradiction> {
  210|     let (w, h, d) = dims;
  211|     while let Some(cell) = work.pop() {
  212|         let x = cell % w;
  213|         let z = (cell / w) % d;
  214|         let y = cell / (w * d);
  215|         for dir in Axis6::ALL {
  216|             let (dx, dy, dz) = dir.offset();
  217|             let (nx, ny, nz) = (x as i64 + dx, y as i64 + dy, z as i64 + dz);
  218|             if nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nz < 0 || nx >= w as i64 || ny >= h as i64 || nz >= d as i64 {
  219|                 continue;
  220|             }
  221|             let neighbor = index_of(dims, nx as usize, ny as usize, nz as usize);
  222|             let restricted = cells[neighbor] & set.support(cells[cell], dir);
  223|             if restricted == cells[neighbor] {
  224|                 continue;
  225|             }
  226|             if restricted == 0 {
  227|                 return Err(WfcContradiction {
  228|                     position: (nx as usize, ny as usize, nz as usize),
  229|                 });
  230|             }
  231|             cells[neighbor] = restricted;
  232|             work.push(neighbor);
  233|         }
  234|     }
  235|     Ok(())
  236| }
  237|

WFC3D analysis:
- `solve_wfc`: O(N) cells. Each iteration: `lowest_entropy_cell` scans ALL N cells → O(N) per iteration. Total iterations ~N (each collapse collapses one cell, but propagate can also collapse cells via restriction... actually each iteration collapses one cell, and there are up to N collapses). So `lowest_entropy_cell` is O(N) per collapse → total O(N^2) where N = w*h*d. This is the classic WFC issue — should use a priority queue / bucket by entropy. Note the scan is O(N) with bitmask entropy computed per cell: entropy computation is O(popcount) per cell, so O(N * popcount). Total O(N^2 * popcount) time.
- `propagate`: worklist; each cell can be re-queued multiple times (each time its mask changes). In the worst case a cell's mask changes O(64) times (each restriction removes at least one bit), so propagate is O(N * 64 * 6) = O(N) per call amortized... Actually per collapse, propagate can push each neighbor at most... a cell's mask can only shrink, so over the entire solve each cell can be restricted at most 63 times → total propagate work across the whole solve is O(N * 64 * 6 * 64)? Let me think: each time a cell is popped from work, we do 6 neighbor checks each with `support()` which is O(popcount of mask) ≤ 64. Each pop happens only when the cell's mask changes, and the mask can change at most 63 times (bit count 64→1). So per cell: O(63 * 6 * 64) = O(24k) ops → total O(N * 63 * 6 * 64) = O(384 * 63 * N)... roughly O(N * 24,192) ≈ O(N) with constant ~24k. Fine.
- `lowest_entropy_cell` is the O(N^2) hotspot: for each of N collapses, scan all N cells → O(N^2). With N = 64^3 = 262k (or smaller), N^2 = 6.9e10 — that's too slow for 64^3. Actually the collapse count equals number of cells that were collapsed by `collapse` calls, not restricted ones... every cell ends collapsed; `lowest_entropy_cell` returns a cell only when popcount > 1. Each loop iteration collapses exactly one cell (via `collapse`), and cells get restricted by propagate too. Number of while-loop iterations ≤ N. So O(N^2) worst. This is a genuine High finding.
- `candidates(mask)` uses `(0..64).filter(...)` — fine.
- Space: O(N) for cells + O(N) work vec allocations per collapse iteration — `vec![cell]` allocates per iteration: N small allocations. Minor.
- `propagate` initial call: `every_cell` vec of N usize — O(N) space, fine.

Also in `collapse`: `candidates(*mask)` iterates 0..64 each time — fine.

Note `support()` is called with `cells[cell]` (the popped cell's mask) — that's correct.

   60|     /// Shared implementation kept generic over the pruning policy so tests can
   61|     /// compare the optimized traversal with the former exhaustive traversal.
   62|     fn execute_internal<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
   63|         &self,
   64|         grid: &VoxelGrid,
   65|         depth: u32,
   66|         world_size: f32,
   67|     ) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
   68|         let mut nodes = Vec::new();
   69| 
   70|         let root_node =
   71|             self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(grid, &mut nodes, OctreeRegion::root(depth));
   72| 
   73|         // Push the root node to the end of the nodes array
   74|         let root_idx = nodes.len();
   75|         nodes.push(root_node);
   76| 
   77|         SparseVoxelOctree {
   78|             root: root_idx,
   79|             nodes,
   80|             depth,
   81|             world_size,
   82|         }
   83|     }
   84| 
   85|     fn build_recursive<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
   86|         &self,
   87|         grid: &VoxelGrid,
   88|         nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
   89|         region: OctreeRegion,
   90|     ) -> SvoNode {
   91|         // Every coordinate sampled outside the dense grid is canonical air.
   92|         // Recursive cubes only extend in the positive direction, so when the
   93|         // cube's minimum lies past any grid dimension the former exhaustive
   94|         // traversal could only collapse back to this same leaf. It also could
   95|         // not append arena nodes, which makes this short-circuit byte-for-byte
   96|         // equivalent while avoiding all descendant calls.
   97|         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE && self.region_is_outside_grid(grid, region.origin) {
   98|             return AIR_LEAF;
   99|         }
  100| 
  101|         if region.depth == 0 {
  102|             let [x, y, z] = region.origin;
  103|             let (v_type, color, ll, fo) = self.get_voxel_attrs(grid, x, y, z);
  104|             return SvoNode::Leaf {
  105|                 voxel_type: v_type,
  106|                 color,
  107|                 light_rgb: ll,
  108|                 face_occlusion: fo,
  109|             };
  110|         }
  111| 
  112|         let mut children = [AIR_LEAF; 8];
  113| 
  114|         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
  115|             children[octant_idx as usize] =
  116|                 self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(grid, nodes, region.child(octant_idx));
  117|         }
  118| 
  119|         // Check if all 8 children are uniform leaves
  120|         let mut uniform = true;
  121|         let mut first_val = None;
  122|         for child in &children {
  123|             match child {
  124|                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
  125|                     uniform = false;
  126|                     break;
  127|                 }
  128|                 SvoNode::Leaf {
  129|                     voxel_type,
  130|                     color,
  131|                     light_rgb,
  132|                     face_occlusion,
  133|                 } => {
  134|                     if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
  135|                         if vt != *voxel_type
  136|                             || col != *color
  137|                             || ll != *light_rgb
  138|                             || fo != *face_occlusion
  139|                         {
  140|                             uniform = false;
  141|                             break;
  142|                         }
  143|                     } else {
  144|                         first_val = Some((*voxel_type, *color, *light_rgb, *face_occlusion));
  145|                     }
  146|                 }
  147|             }
  148|         }
  149| 
  150|         if uniform && let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
  151|             return SvoNode::Leaf {
  152|                 voxel_type: vt,
  153|                 color: col,
  154|                 light_rgb: ll,
  155|                 face_occlusion: fo,
  156|             };
  157|         }
  158| 
  159|         // Push 8 children contiguously to arena
  160|         let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
  161|         let mut child_mask = 0;
  162| 
  163|         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
  164|             let child = children[octant_idx as usize];
  165|             match child {
  166|                 SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
  167|                     if voxel_type != 0 {
  168|                         child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
  169|                     }
  170|                 }
  171|                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
  172|                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
  173|                 }
  174|             }
  175|             nodes.push(child);
  176|         }
  177| 
  178|         SvoNode::Internal {
  179|             child_base_index,
  180|             child_mask,
  181|         }
  182|     }
  183| 
  184|     fn region_is_outside_grid(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, origin: [u32; 3]) -> bool {
  185|         origin[0] as usize >= grid.width()
  186|             || origin[1] as usize >= grid.height()
  187|             || origin[2] as usize >= grid.depth()
  188|     }
  189| 
  190|     fn get_voxel_attrs(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
  191|         if x >= grid.width() as u32 || y >= grid.height() as u32 || z >= grid.depth() as u32 {
  192|             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0); // Out of bounds is air
  193|         }
  194| 
  195|         let v_id = grid.get(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  196|         if v_id == VOXEL_AIR {
  197|             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
  198|         }
  199| 
  200|         let ll = grid.get_light_rgb(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  201|         let fo = grid.get_face_occlusion(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
  202|         let base_color = self.palette.color(v_id);
  203| 
  204|         (v_id, base_color, ll, fo)
  205|     }
  206| }

  225|     fn traversal_call_count<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
  226|         dimensions: [u32; 3],
  227|         origin: [u32; 3],
  228|         depth: u32,
  229|     ) -> usize {
  230|         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE
  231|             && (origin[0] >= dimensions[0]
  232|                 || origin[1] >= dimensions[1]
  233|                 || origin[2] >= dimensions[2])
  234|         {
  235|             return 1;
  236|         }
  237|         if depth == 0 {
  238|             return 1;
  239|         }
  240| 
  241|         let child_size = 1 << (depth - 1);
  242|         let mut calls = 1;
  243|         for octant in 0..8u32 {
  244|             calls += traversal_call_count::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(
  245|                 dimensions,
  246|                 [
  247|                     origin[0] + (octant & 1) * child_size,
  248|                     origin[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) * child_size,
  249|                     origin[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) * child_size,
  250|                 ],
  251|                 depth - 1,
  252|             );
  253|         }
  254|         calls
  255|     }

build_octree.rs:
- Recursive build, visits 8^depth leaves in worst case, but with PRUNE_OUTSIDE it short-circuits outside the grid. The recursion visits every node of the octree over the grid's bounding cube → O(8^depth) worst case = O(N) where N = number of grid voxels (grid dims). Actually for a grid of dims W×H×D with depth chosen so 2^depth ≥ max dim, the traversal is O(8^depth) = O(max^3) = O(N_voxels * 8^{depth - log2 max})... Let me be careful: octree over a cube of side S = 2^depth. If the grid is W×H×D ≤ S, then the recursion covers all 8^depth leaf regions = S^3 voxels worth of regions, but PRUNE_OUTSIDE short-circuits regions whose origin ≥ grid dims. Number of octree nodes in the bounding cube of the grid: the recursion covers the octree down to depth 0 for all regions within the grid bounds — that's O(W*H*D) leaves in the worst case (all distinct) = O(N) where N = W*H*D voxels, plus internal nodes O(N/7)... In the worst case (checkerboard), the number of nodes is about 8/7 * N ≈ 1.14N. So O(N) time and space. Each leaf does a grid.get — O(1). Fine. But recursion depth = depth (max ~ 10-20) — fine.
- One subtle issue: the recursion visits nodes for empty regions too — can't prune regions that are fully empty without a "max" query, but PRUNE_OUTSIDE handles outside. For a sparse grid, the octree still visits all 8^depth... wait, does it? No — the recursion always descends into all 8 children at every level, so total visited nodes = full octree nodes over the cube (minus pruned outside). It does NOT skip empty internal regions (no occupancy summary). So for a 512³ grid with a single voxel, it would visit ~8^9 ≈ 134M nodes? No wait — PRUNE_OUTSIDE: grid dims 512³, depth 9, cube 512³. All regions are within bounds, so no pruning. Every region is visited → full 8^9 = 134M leaf visits. That's O(S³) where S is the octree cube side, NOT O(N) where N is the number of *solid* voxels. Hmm. For a typical chunk grid 32³, depth 5, visits = 8^5 = 32768 leaves + internals ≈ 37k — fine. But for large grids, the cost is O(cube volume) regardless of content. The docstring claims "Converts a dense voxel grid into a collapsed sparse octree" — dense input, so O(volume) is expected for dense grids. But the early-uniform-collapse check happens post-recursion (children computed first), so uniform regions don't save work — full descent always. That's inherent to this approach; still worth noting: worst case O(V) where V = 8^depth (cube volume), and it always fully descends even into empty regions. For VoxelGrid 512³ = 134M — the PRUNE_OUTSIDE only helps non-power-of-two. Actually the grid is typically 32³ per chunk. But infinite_level may build bigger grids. This is a Medium/Low finding: could add an occupancy/air-skip using the grid's own data (e.g., check sub-cube emptiness via a prefix-sum or by scanning region bounds, or build from a hash set of solid voxels). Also note nodes vec grows unbounded relative to content — but bounded by volume. Fine.

Also `get_voxel_attrs` calls `self.palette.color(v_id)` per leaf — for 134M leaves × palette lookup (probably a Vec index) — fine.

Now build_octree_direct.rs.
    1| //! Direct-to-SVO emission: build the octree straight from a sampling
    2| //! function, with no dense intermediate 3D array.
    3| //!
    4| //! The classic pipeline allocates a dense grid (megabytes per chunk), fills
    5| //! it, then compresses to an SVO. On low-memory targets that intermediate is
    6| //! pure waste when the source can already answer "what is at (x, y, z)?" —
    7| //! and better, "is this whole cube uniform?". A sampler that can prove
    8| //! uniformity for a region lets the builder emit one leaf and never descend,
    9| //! so cost tracks the *surface* of the geometry, not its volume.
   10| //!
   11| //! The arena layout (children contiguous per block, root pushed last,
   12| //! uniform blocks collapsed to a leaf) matches [`BuildOctreeUseCase`]
   13| //! byte-for-byte, so the two paths are interchangeable and comparable with
   14| //! plain equality in tests.
   15| 
   16| use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
   17| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
   18| use crate::use_cases::ports::MaterialPalette;

   20| /// The attributes of one voxel as the octree stores them.
   21| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   22| pub struct SvoLeaf {
   23|     pub voxel_type: u8,
   24|     pub color: u32,
   25|     pub light_rgb: [u8; 3],
   26|     pub face_occlusion: u8,
   27| }
   28| 
   29| impl SvoLeaf {
   30|     pub const AIR: Self = Self {
   31|         voxel_type: VOXEL_AIR,
   32|         color: 0,
   33|         light_rgb: [0; 3],
   34|         face_occlusion: 0,
   35|     };
   36| 
   37|     fn to_node(self) -> SvoNode {
   38|         SvoNode::Leaf {
   39|             voxel_type: self.voxel_type,
   40|             color: self.color,
   41|             light_rgb: self.light_rgb,
   42|             face_occlusion: self.face_occlusion,
   43|         }
   44|     }

   47| /// A volume the builder can sample point-wise, plus an optional proof that a
   48| /// whole cube is uniform (the pruning that makes direct emission cheap).
   49| pub trait VoxelSampler {
   50|     fn sample(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> SvoLeaf;
   51| 
   52|     /// `Some(leaf)` when every voxel in the cube at `origin` with edge
   53|     /// `size` provably has these attributes. Returning `None` just means
   54|     /// "descend"; it must never be wrong, only conservative.
   55|     fn uniform_hint(&self, _origin: [u32; 3], _size: u32) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
   56|         None
   57|     }
   58| }
   59| 
   60| /// Adapts a dense grid (plus presentation palette) to the sampler port.
   61| /// Out-of-grid coordinates are canonical air, and any cube lying entirely
   62| /// past the grid proves itself uniform — the same pruning the dense builder
   63| /// applies.
   64| pub struct GridSampler<'a> {
   65|     pub grid: &'a VoxelGrid,
   66|     pub palette: &'a dyn MaterialPalette,
   67| }
   68| 
   69| impl VoxelSampler for GridSampler<'_> {
   70|     fn sample(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> SvoLeaf {
   71|         let (x, y, z) = (x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
   72|         if x >= self.grid.width() || y >= self.grid.height() || z >= self.grid.depth() {
   73|             return SvoLeaf::AIR;
   74|         }
   75|         let voxel_type = self.grid.get(x, y, z);
   76|         if voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
   77|             return SvoLeaf::AIR;
   78|         }
   79|         SvoLeaf {
   80|             voxel_type,
   81|             color: self.palette.color(voxel_type),
   82|             light_rgb: self.grid.get_light_rgb(x, y, z),
   83|             face_occlusion: self.grid.get_face_occlusion(x, y, z),
   84|         }
   85|     }
   86| 
   87|     fn uniform_hint(&self, origin: [u32; 3], _size: u32) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
   88|         let outside = origin[0] as usize >= self.grid.width()
   89|             || origin[1] as usize >= self.grid.height()
   90|             || origin[2] as usize >= self.grid.depth();
   91|         outside.then_some(SvoLeaf::AIR)
   92|     }
   93| }
   94| 
   95| /// Builds an SVO of `depth` levels by recursive sampling, emitting leaves
   96| /// for provably uniform cubes without descending into them.
   97| pub fn build_octree_direct(
   98|     sampler: &dyn VoxelSampler,
   99|     depth: u32,
  100|     world_size: f32,
  101| ) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
  102|     let mut nodes = Vec::new();
  103|     let root_node = emit_cube(sampler, &mut nodes, [0; 3], 1 << depth, depth);
  104|     let root = nodes.len();
  105|     nodes.push(root_node);
  106|     SparseVoxelOctree {
  107|         root,
  108|         nodes,
  109|         depth,
  110|         world_size,
  111|     }
  112| }
  113| 
  114| fn emit_cube(
  115|     sampler: &dyn VoxelSampler,
  116|     nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
  117|     origin: [u32; 3],
  118|     size: u32,
  119|     depth: u32,
  120| ) -> SvoNode {
  121|     if let Some(leaf) = sampler.uniform_hint(origin, size) {
  122|         return leaf.to_node();
  123|     }
  124|     if depth == 0 {
  125|         return sampler.sample(origin[0], origin[1], origin[2]).to_node();
  126|     }
  127| 
  128|     let half = size / 2;
  129|     let mut children = [SvoLeaf::AIR.to_node(); 8];
  130|     for (octant, child) in children.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  131|         let octant = octant as u32;
  132|         let child_origin = [
  133|             origin[0] + (octant & 1) * half,
  134|             origin[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) * half,
  135|             origin[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) * half,
  136|         ];
  137|         *child = emit_cube(sampler, nodes, child_origin, half, depth - 1);
  138|     }
  139| 
  140|     if let Some(leaf) = uniform_leaf(&children) {
  141|         return leaf.to_node();
  142|     }
  143| 
  144|     let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
  145|     let mut child_mask = 0u8;
  146|     for (octant, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
  147|         let occupied = match child {
  148|             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => *voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR,
  149|             SvoNode::Internal { .. } => true,
  150|         };
  151|         if occupied {
  152|             child_mask |= 1 << octant;
  153|         }
  154|         nodes.push(*child);
  155|     }
  156|     SvoNode::Internal {
  157|         child_base_index,
  158|         child_mask,
  159|     }
  160| }
  161| 
  162| /// `Some` when all eight children are leaves with identical attributes.
  163| fn uniform_leaf(children: &[SvoNode; 8]) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
  164|     let mut first: Option<SvoLeaf> = None;
  165|     for child in children {
  166|         let leaf = match *child {
  167|             SvoNode::Internal { .. } => return None,
  168|             SvoNode::Leaf {
  169|                 voxel_type,
  170|                 color,
  171|                 light_rgb,
  172|                 face_occlusion,
  173|             } => SvoLeaf {
  174|                 voxel_type,
  175|                 color,
  176|                 light_rgb,
  177|                 face_occlusion,
  178|             },
  179|         };
  180|         match first {
  181|             None => first = Some(leaf),
  182|             Some(seen) if seen != leaf => return None,
  183|             Some(_) => {}
  184|         }
  185|     }
  186|     first
  187| }

Now compress_svdag.rs.
    1| //! Sparse Voxel DAG compression: bottom-up merging of identical subtrees.
    2| //!
    3| //! The SVO arena stores every internal node's eight children as one
    4| //! contiguous block, so the unit of sharing is that block: two internal
    5| //! nodes whose child blocks are structurally identical can point at a single
    6| //! canonical copy. Repetitive architecture (identical ceiling tiles, wall
    7| //! runs, column bays) then costs one subtree instead of hundreds.
    8| //!
    9| //! The result is still a [`SparseVoxelOctree`]: traversal only ever follows
   10| //! `child_base_index`, so lookups and the GPU serializer are agnostic to
   11| //! whether the arena is a tree or a DAG. The one consumer that must NOT
   12| //! receive a DAG is any walk that visits every arena node expecting each to
   13| //! appear once per world position (e.g. collision extraction) — compress
   14| //! after those walks, immediately before upload.
   15| 
   16| use std::collections::HashMap;
   17| 
   18| use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
   19| 
   20| /// Arena sizes before and after deduplication, for telemetry.
   21| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   22| pub struct SvdagStats {
   23|     pub nodes_before: usize,
   24|     pub nodes_after: usize,
   25| }
   26| 
   27| /// A node in canonical form: internals are identified by the id of their
   28| /// interned child block rather than an arena offset, which is what makes
   29| /// structural equality (and therefore hashing) meaningful.
   30| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
   31| enum CanonNode {
   32|     Leaf {
   33|         voxel_type: u8,
   34|         color: u32,
   35|         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
   36|         face_occlusion: u8,
   37|     },
   38|     Internal {
   39|         child_base_index: u32,
   40|         child_mask: u8,
   41|     },
   42| }
   43| 
   44| impl CanonNode {
   45|     fn to_svo(self) -> SvoNode {
   46|         match self {
   47|             CanonNode::Leaf {
   48|                 voxel_type,
   49|                 color,
   50|                 light_rgb,
   51|                 face_occlusion,
   52|             } => SvoNode::Leaf {
   53|                 voxel_type,
   54|                 color,
   55|                 light_rgb,
   56|                 face_occlusion,
   57|             },
   58|             CanonNode::Internal {
   59|                 child_base_index,
   60|                 child_mask,
   61|             } => SvoNode::Internal {
   62|                 child_base_index,
   63|                 child_mask,
   64|             },
   65|         }
   66|     }
   67| }
   68| 
   69| struct BlockInterner {
   70|     /// Canonical child block -> its base index in the output arena.
   71|     blocks: HashMap<[CanonNode; 8], u32>,
   72|     nodes: Vec<SvoNode>,
   73| }
   74| 
   75| impl BlockInterner {
   76|     /// Returns the output-arena base of this block, materializing it only
   77|     /// the first time the block's structure is seen.
   78|     fn intern(&mut self, block: [CanonNode; 8]) -> u32 {
   79|         if let Some(&base) = self.blocks.get(&block) {
   80|             return base;
   81|         }
   82|         let base = self.nodes.len() as u32;
   83|         self.nodes.extend(block.iter().map(|canon| canon.to_svo()));
   84|         self.blocks.insert(block, base);
   85|         base
   86|     }
   87| 
   88|     /// Rebuilds the subtree rooted at `index` bottom-up, sharing every child
   89|     /// block already interned.
   90|     fn canonicalize(&mut self, source: &SparseVoxelOctree, index: usize) -> CanonNode {
   91|         match source.nodes[index] {
   92|             SvoNode::Leaf {
   93|                 voxel_type,
   94|                 color,
   95|                 light_rgb,
   96|                 face_occlusion,
   97|             } => CanonNode::Leaf {
   98|                 voxel_type,
   99|                 color,
  100|                 light_rgb,
  101|                 face_occlusion,
  102|             },
  103|             SvoNode::Internal {
  104|                 child_base_index,
  105|                 child_mask,
  106|             } => {
  107|                 let mut block = [CanonNode::Leaf {
  108|                     voxel_type: 0,
  109|                     color: 0,
  110|                     light_rgb: [0; 3],
  111|                     face_occlusion: 0,
  112|                 }; 8];
  113|                 for (octant, slot) in block.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  114|                     *slot = self.canonicalize(source, child_base_index as usize + octant);
  115|                 }
  116|                 CanonNode::Internal {
  117|                     child_base_index: self.intern(block),
  118|                     child_mask,
  119|                 }
  120|             }
  121|         }
  122|     }
  123| }
  124| 
  125| /// Deduplicates identical subtrees, returning a lookup-equivalent octree
  126| /// whose arena shares one copy of every repeated child block.
  127| pub fn compress_svdag(source: &SparseVoxelOctree) -> (SparseVoxelOctree, SvdagStats) {
  128|     let mut interner = BlockInterner {
  129|         blocks: HashMap::new(),
  130|         nodes: Vec::new(),
  131|     };
  132|     let root_canon = interner.canonicalize(source, source.root);
  133| 
  134|     // Root last, matching the tree builder's arena convention.
  135|     let root = interner.nodes.len();
  136|     interner.nodes.push(root_canon.to_svo());
  137| 
  138|     let stats = SvdagStats {
  139|         nodes_before: source.nodes.len(),
  140|         nodes_after: interner.nodes.len(),
  141|     };
  142|     (
  143|         SparseVoxelOctree {
  144|             root,
  145|             nodes: interner.nodes,
  146|             depth: source.depth,
  147|             world_size: source.world_size,
  148|         },
  149|         stats,
  150|     )
  151| }

--- /home/dbslim/vackrooms/src/use_cases/compress_svdag.rs: 255 lines, showed 1-255 ---

compress_svdag.rs:
- canonicalize is recursive over the SVO tree; each internal node's block gets interned into a HashMap<[CanonNode;8], u32>. `[CanonNode; 8]` — size: Leaf has u8 + u32 + [u8;3] + u8 = 12 bytes; Internal: u32+u8 = 8 bytes. Enum with 2 variants → size ~16 bytes. [CanonNode;8] = 128 bytes key. Hashing 128 bytes per internal node: O(nodes × 128). Total time O(V) where V = number of SVO nodes (each internal node visited once, plus its 8 children in the block). Note the recursion visits leaves too (canonicalize on every node). Each visit is O(1) plus hash of the block. So O(V) time, O(V × 128) space for the HashMap keys (each unique block stored as a full copy of 8 CanonNodes = 128 bytes). Since most blocks are unique in the worst case, memory = 128 × V_internal bytes. Could be a memory concern but acceptable. Recursion depth = octree depth (~6-10) — fine.
- One important subtlety: it walks the entire tree — O(V). Fine, no quadratic behavior.
