 209|     /// stay inside the dense pre-compression memory budget. Callers should
 210|     /// keep the original profile when this returns an error.
 211|     pub fn try_with_voxel_size(mut self, voxel_size: f32) -> Result<Self, VoxelSizeError> {
 212|         if !voxel_size.is_finite() {
 213|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotFinite);
 214|         }
 215|         if voxel_size <= 0.0 {
 216|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotPositive);
 217|         }
 218| 
 219|         let ratio = f64::from(self.chunk_size) / f64::from(voxel_size);
 220|         let axis_voxels = ratio.round();
 221|         let reconstructed_chunk = axis_voxels * f64::from(voxel_size);
 222|         let seam_tolerance = f64::from(self.chunk_size).abs().mul_add(1.0e-6, 1.0e-6);
 223|         if axis_voxels < 1.0
 224|             || !ratio.is_finite()
 225|             || (reconstructed_chunk - f64::from(self.chunk_size)).abs() > seam_tolerance
 226|         {
 227|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileChunk {
 228|                 chunk_size: self.chunk_size,
 229|                 voxel_size,
 230|             });
 231|         }
 232| 
 233|         let axis_voxels = axis_voxels as u32;
 234|         if axis_voxels % PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR != 0 {
 235|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
 236|                 fine_axis_voxels: axis_voxels,
 237|                 divisor: PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR,
 238|             });
 239|         }
 240|         let required_depth = axis_voxels
 241|             .checked_next_power_of_two()
 242|             .map(u32::trailing_zeros)
 243|             .unwrap_or(u32::BITS);
 244|         if required_depth > MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH {
 245|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
 246|                 required: required_depth,
 247|                 maximum: MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH,
 248|             });
 249|         }
 250| 
 251|         // LocalChunkSource generates one lateral cell on each side for seam
 252|         // visibility and boundary light-volume samples. Validate the real
 253|         // dense allocation rather than only the cropped payload.
 254|         let allocated_axis = u64::from(axis_voxels) + 2;
 255|         let required_columns = allocated_axis * allocated_axis;
 256|         if required_columns > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS {
 257|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
 258|                 required_columns,
 259|                 maximum_columns: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS,
 260|             });
 261|         }
 262| 
 263|         let height_voxels =
 264|             (MAX_GENERATED_HEIGHT_WORLD_UNITS / f64::from(voxel_size)).ceil() as u64 + 2;
 265|         let required_voxels = required_columns
 266|             .checked_mul(height_voxels)
 267|             .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
 268|         if required_voxels > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS {
 269|             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
 270|                 required_voxels,
 271|                 maximum_voxels: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS,
 272|             });
 273|         }
 274| 
 275|         self.voxel_scale = voxel_size;
 276|         Ok(self)
 277|     }
 278| 
 279|     /// The same chunk at a coarser level of detail: voxels double per LOD
 280|     /// step, so lod 1 costs ~1/8 of lod 0 to generate, light, and serialize.
 281|     /// `svo_world_size()` is invariant across LODs (half the voxels at twice
 282|     /// the scale), so payloads of any LOD are interchangeable to the renderer.
 283|     pub fn at_lod(mut self, lod: u8) -> Self {
 284|         self.voxel_scale *= (1u32 << lod.min(4)) as f32;
 285|         self
 286|     }
 287| 
 288|     pub fn svo_depth(&self) -> u32 {
 289|         let voxels = (self.chunk_size / self.voxel_scale).round().max(1.0) as u32;
 290|         voxels.next_power_of_two().trailing_zeros()
 291|     }
 292| 
 293|     pub fn svo_world_size(&self) -> f32 {
 294|         let size = 1 << self.svo_depth();
 295|         size as f32 * self.voxel_scale
 296|     }
 297| }
 298| 
 299| pub struct GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
 300|     noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 301|     telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
 302| }
 303| 
 304| impl<'a> GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
 305|     /// Constructs the use case with silent telemetry (tests, wasm default).
 306|     pub fn new(noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider) -> Self {
 307|         Self {
 308|             noise_provider,
 309|             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
 310|         }
 311|     }
 312| 
 313|     /// Constructs the use case with an injected telemetry sink (native server,
 314|     /// browser console, ...). Keeps the Dependency Rule intact: the use case
 315|     /// only knows the TelemetryPort trait.
 316|     pub fn with_telemetry(
 317|         noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 318|         telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
 319|     ) -> Self {
 320|         Self {
 321|             noise_provider,
 322|             telemetry,
 323|         }
 324|     }
 325| 
 326|     pub fn execute(
 327|         &self,
 328|         chunk_pos: Position,
 329|         seed: u32,
 330|         config: GeneratorConfig,
 331|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
 332|         self.execute_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, &RealitySnapshot::default())
 333|     }
 334| 
 335|     /// Generates a chunk against an immutable encounter-state snapshot.
 336|     /// The snapshot is part of the request identity in the browser pipeline;
 337|     /// generation itself remains pure and replayable.
 338|     pub fn execute_with_reality(
 339|         &self,
 340|         chunk_pos: Position,
 341|         seed: u32,
 342|         config: GeneratorConfig,
 343|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 344|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
 345|         self.execute_from_plans(chunk_pos, seed, config, reality, None)
 346|     }
 347| 
 348|     /// [`execute_with_reality`](Self::execute_with_reality), voxelizing from
 349|     /// region plans that have already been made instead of deriving them for
 350|     /// this chunk alone.
 351|     ///
 352|     /// This is the bulk-loading seam. A [`WorldBlock`] plans a 1280 u square
 353|     /// once and every chunk inside it is cut from those plans, which is both
 354|     /// far cheaper than re-deriving per chunk and the only way a decision
 355|     /// spanning more than one chunk can exist at all.
 356|     ///
 357|     /// Passing `None` derives per chunk exactly as before — that arm is the
 358|     /// original streaming path, untouched. Plans are honoured only by level
 359|     /// 0, the one level that has them; every other level ignores the argument
 360|     /// because there is nothing it could mean.
 361|     ///
 362|     /// [`WorldBlock`]: crate::use_cases::world_block::WorldBlock
 363|     pub fn execute_from_plans(
 364|         &self,
 365|         chunk_pos: Position,
 366|         seed: u32,
 367|         config: GeneratorConfig,
 368|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 369|         plans: Option<&InfiniteRegionWindow>,
 370|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
 371|         // Pluggable levels: everything except the legacy office blueprint
 372|         // (level 90, kept inline below) goes through the LevelGenerator port.
 373|         // Level 0 is the architecturally *planned* Backrooms: region plans
 374|         // (circulation -> assemblies -> corruption) drive the voxelization.
 375|         if config.level == 0 || config.level == 1 || config.level == 34 {
 376|             use crate::use_cases::grassland_level::GrasslandLevel;
 377|             use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
 378|             use crate::use_cases::level_one::HabitableLevel;
 379|             use crate::use_cases::level_zero::BackroomsLevel;
 380| 
 381|             let start_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros();
 382|             let generator: &dyn LevelGenerator = match config.level {
 383|                 0 => &BackroomsLevel,
 384|                 1 => &HabitableLevel,
 385|                 _ => &GrasslandLevel,
 386|             };
 387|             let mut grid = match (config.level, plans) {
 388|                 (0, Some(plans)) => BackroomsLevel::generate_from_plans(
 389|                     chunk_pos,
 390|                     seed,
 391|                     config,
 392|                     self.noise_provider,
 393|                     reality,
 394|                     Some(plans),
 395|                 ),
 396|                 _ => generator.generate_with_reality(
 397|                     chunk_pos,
 398|                     seed,
 399|                     config,
 400|                     self.noise_provider,
 401|                     reality,
 402|                 ),
 403|             };
 404|             let lighting =
 405|                 crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
 406|                     config.voxel_scale,
 407|                 )
 408|                 .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
 409|             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
 410| 
 411|             let elapsed_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros().saturating_sub(start_micros);
 412|             self.telemetry.log(&format!(
 413|                 "[TELEMETRY] level {} chunk generated. Duration={}us, Grid={}x{}x{}",
 414|                 config.level,
 415|                 elapsed_micros,
 416|                 grid.width(),
 417|                 grid.height(),
 418|                 grid.depth()
 419|             ));
 420|             return grid;
 421|         }
 422| 
 423|         GeneratedChunk::new(legacy_blueprint::generate_legacy_blueprint(
 424|             self.noise_provider,
 425|             self.telemetry,
 426|             chunk_pos,
 427|             seed,
 428|             config,
 429|         ))
 430|     }
 431| }

 559|     #[test]
 560|     fn coarse_chunk_generates_the_same_layout_smaller() {
 561|         let noise = MockNoiseProvider { value: 0.0 };
 562|         let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 563|         let fine = generator.execute(
 564|             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 565|             42,
 566|             GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 567|                 .with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES),
 568|         );
 569|         let coarse = generator.execute(
 570|             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 571|             42,
 572|             GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 573|                 .with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES)
 574|                 .at_lod(1),
 575|         );
 576|         assert_eq!(coarse.width() * 2, fine.width());
 577|         assert_eq!(coarse.depth() * 2, fine.depth());
 578|         // Same maze at half resolution. Cell sizes truncate differently per
 579|         // scale (5.0/0.4 = 12 voxels vs 25 at fine), so wall planes may land
 580|         // one fine voxel off; an LOD proxy only needs walls to line up to
 581|         // within that tolerance.
 582|         let wall = crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
 583|         let mut wall_match = 0usize;
 584|         let mut wall_total = 0usize;
 585|         for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
 586|             for x in 0..coarse.width() {
 587|                 if coarse.get(x, 1, z) != wall {
 588|                     continue;
 589|                 }
 590|                 wall_total += 1;
 591|                 let (fx, fz) = (x * 2, z * 2);
 592|                 let mut near = false;
 593|                 for dz in -1i32..=2 {
 594|                     for dx in -1i32..=2 {
 595|                         let (sx, sz) = (fx as i32 + dx, fz as i32 + dz);
 596|                         if sx >= 0
 597|                             && sz >= 0
 598|                             && (sx as usize) < fine.width()
 599|                             && (sz as usize) < fine.depth()
 600|                             && fine.get(sx as usize, 1, sz as usize) == wall
 601|                         {
 602|                             near = true;
 603|                         }
 604|                     }
 605|                 }
 606|                 if near {
 607|                     wall_match += 1;
 608|                 }
 609|             }
 610|         }
 611|         assert!(wall_total > 0, "coarse chunk must still contain walls");
 612|         assert!(
 613|             wall_match * 10 >= wall_total * 9,
 614|             "coarse walls should lie within one fine voxel of fine walls: {wall_match}/{wall_total}"
 615|         );
 616|     }

 778|                     seed ^ 0x2b8f_a43c,
 779|                     crate::domain::entities::position::Position::new(wx * 0.05, wz * 0.05),
 780|                 );
 781| 
 782|                 let zone = if n < -0.7 {
 783|                     MicrobiomeZone::Blackout
 784|                 } else if n < -0.4 {
 785|                     MicrobiomeZone::Holes
 786|                 } else if n > 0.85 - (config.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1) {
 787|                     MicrobiomeZone::Atrium
 788|                 } else if n > 0.6 {
 789|                     MicrobiomeZone::PillarField
 790|                 } else if n > 0.4 {
 791|                     MicrobiomeZone::Arch
 792|                 } else if n > 0.2 && n < 0.25 {
 793|                     MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom
 794|                 } else {
 795|                     MicrobiomeZone::Standard
 796|                 };
 797| 
 798|                 zones.insert(zone);
 799|                 grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx] = zone;
 800|             }
 801|         }
 802| 
 803|         assert!(zones.len() >= 2, "Expected at least 2 distinct zones");
 804| 
 805|         let mut same_neighbor_count = 0;
 806|         let mut total_neighbors = 0;
 807|         for cz in 1..9 {
 808|             for cx in 1..9 {
 809|                 let z = grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx];
 810|                 total_neighbors += 4;
 811|                 if grid_zones[(cz - 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
 812|                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
 813|                 }
 814|                 if grid_zones[(cz + 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
 815|                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
 816|                 }
 817|                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx - 1] == z {
 818|                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
 819|                 }
 820|                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx + 1] == z {
 821|                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
 822|                 }
 823|             }
 824|         }
 825| 
 826|         assert!(
 827|             same_neighbor_count as f32 / total_neighbors as f32 > 0.6,
 828|             "Expected zones to be highly contiguous"
 829|         );
 830|     }

   1| //! The pluggable level-generator port: each Backrooms "level" (Level 0
   2| //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
   3| //!
   4| //! Contract for implementors:
   5| //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
   6| //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
   7| //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
   8| //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
   9| //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
  10| //!   ~1 world unit wide.
  11| //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
  12| //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
  13| //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the
  14| //!   orchestrating use case runs the exposed-face lighting bake afterwards.
  15| 
  16| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
  17| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  18| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  19| use crate::use_cases::generated_chunk::GeneratedChunk;
  20| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  21| 
  22| /// Well-known level ids (the `GeneratorConfig::level` / noclip targets).
  23| pub const LEVEL_BACKROOMS: u32 = 0;
  24| /// Level 1, the Habitable Zone: concrete warehouse/parking structure.
  25| pub const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
  26| pub const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
  27| /// The pre-canon office blueprint, kept reachable for tests and archaeology.
  28| /// It vacated id 1 when the canonical Level 1 landed.
  29| pub const LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES: u32 = 90;
  30| 
  31| pub trait LevelGenerator {
  32|     /// Fills one chunk under a deterministic encounter-state snapshot.
  33|     /// Implementors must choose explicitly whether that state affects them;
  34|     /// no default is allowed to silently discard it.
  35|     fn generate_with_reality(
  36|         &self,
  37|         chunk_pos: Position,
  38|         seed: u32,
  39|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  40|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  41|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  42|     ) -> GeneratedChunk;
  43| 
  44|     /// Convenience entry point for tools that deliberately request epoch zero.
  45|     /// `chunk_pos` is the chunk origin in world units.
  46|     fn generate(
  47|         &self,
  48|         chunk_pos: Position,
  49|         seed: u32,
  50|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  51|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  52|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
  53|         self.generate_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, noise, &RealitySnapshot::empty())
  54|     }
  55| }

   1| //! Deterministic access to the finite window of an infinite planned level.
   2| //!
   3| //! Chunk generation is local, but Level 0 architecture is not: a chunk may
   4| //! sample corridors, assemblies, or anomaly footprints planned by any region
   5| //! that overlaps its voxel halo.  This module makes that query explicit.  The
   6| //! window owns a stable, row-major set of region plans and is otherwise just a
   7| //! world-point-to-plan lookup; callers do not need to reproduce region-range
   8| //! arithmetic or fall back to an unrelated plan when a lookup misses.
   9| 
  10| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
  11| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
  12| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  14| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  15| use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan, region_index};
  16| 
  17| /// The region plans needed to sample one bounded area of an infinite level.
  18| ///
  19| /// Plans are stored in `(z, x)` row-major order.  That order is deliberately
  20| /// independent of hash maps and request timing, so planning the same area is
  21| /// replayable on the main thread, in a worker, or during a test.
  22| #[derive(Debug)]
  23| pub struct InfiniteRegionWindow {
  24|     min_region_x: i64,
  25|     min_region_z: i64,
  26|     max_region_x: i64,
  27|     max_region_z: i64,
  28|     plans: Vec<RegionPlan>,
  29| }
  30| 
  31| impl InfiniteRegionWindow {
  32|     /// Plans every region touched by `area` after expanding it by `halo` world
  33|     /// units.  Boundary-touching regions are included intentionally: a voxel
  34|     /// sampler may ask about the exact far edge while constructing skirts,
  35|     /// meshes, or collision data.
  36|     pub fn covering(
  37|         area: WorldBounds,
  38|         halo: f32,
  39|         seed: u32,
  40|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
  41|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  42|     ) -> Self {
  43|         Self::covering_with_progress(area, halo, seed, config, noise, &mut |_, _| {})
  44|     }
  45| 
  46|     /// [`covering`](Self::covering), reporting `(regions_done, regions_total)`
  47|     /// after each region is planned.
  48|     ///
  49|     /// A window over one chunk is a handful of regions and nobody waits for
  50|     /// it; a window over a whole block is hundreds and somebody is watching a
  51|     /// loading screen. The callback is what lets that screen advance in the
  52|     /// unit the time is actually spent in, rather than jumping from 0 to 100
  53|     /// around a silent second.
  54|     pub fn covering_with_progress(
  55|         area: WorldBounds,
  56|         halo: f32,
  57|         seed: u32,
  58|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
  59|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  60|         progress: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize),
  61|     ) -> Self {
  62|         assert!(
  63|             halo.is_finite() && halo >= 0.0,
  64|             "region-window halo must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
  65|         );
  66|         let area = area.expanded(halo);
  67|         assert!(
  68|             [area.min_x, area.min_z, area.max_x, area.max_z]
  69|                 .into_iter()
  70|                 .all(f32::is_finite),
  71|             "an infinite-region window requires finite world bounds"
  72|         );
  73| 
  74|         let min_region_x = region_index(area.min_x);
  75|         let min_region_z = region_index(area.min_z);
  76|         let max_region_x = region_index(area.max_x);
  77|         let max_region_z = region_index(area.max_z);
  78|         let width = region_count(min_region_x, max_region_x);
  79|         let height = region_count(min_region_z, max_region_z);
  80|         let capacity = width
  81|             .checked_mul(height)
  82|             .expect("requested region window is too large to address");
  83|         let mut plans = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
  84| 
  85|         progress(0, capacity);
  86|         for region_z in min_region_z..=max_region_z {
  87|             for region_x in min_region_x..=max_region_x {
  88|                 plans.push(generate_region_plan(
  89|                     seed,
  90|                     region_origin(region_x, region_z),
  91|                     REGION_SIZE,
  92|                     config,
  93|                     noise,
  94|                 ));
  95|                 progress(plans.len(), capacity);
  96|             }
  97|         }
  98| 
  99|         Self {
 100|             min_region_x,
 101|             min_region_z,
 102|             max_region_x,
 103|             max_region_z,
 104|             plans,
 105|         }
 106|     }
 107| 
 108|     /// Convenience constructor for the common chunk-plus-voxel-halo query.
 109|     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 110|         chunk_origin: Position,
 111|         chunk_size: f32,
 112|         halo: f32,
 113|         seed: u32,
 114|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 115|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 116|     ) -> Self {
 117|         assert!(
 118|             chunk_size.is_finite() && chunk_size >= 0.0,
 119|             "chunk size must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
 120|         );
 121|         Self::covering(
 122|             WorldBounds::new(
 123|                 chunk_origin.x,
 124|                 chunk_origin.z,
 125|                 chunk_origin.x + chunk_size,
 126|                 chunk_origin.z + chunk_size,
 127|             ),
 128|             halo,
 129|             seed,
 130|             config,
 131|             noise,
 132|         )
 133|     }
 134| 
 135|     /// Returns the authoritative plan for a world point, or `None` when the
 136|     /// caller sampled beyond the area/halo declared at construction time.
 137|     pub fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
 138|         self.plan_for_region(region_index(world.x), region_index(world.z))
 139|     }
 140| 
 141|     pub fn plan_for_region(&self, region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
 142|         if region_x < self.min_region_x
 143|             || region_x > self.max_region_x
 144|             || region_z < self.min_region_z
 145|             || region_z > self.max_region_z
 146|         {
 147|             return None;
 148|         }
 149| 
 150|         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
 151|         let local_x = usize::try_from(region_x - self.min_region_x).ok()?;
 152|         let local_z = usize::try_from(region_z - self.min_region_z).ok()?;
 153|         self.plans
 154|             .get(local_z.saturating_mul(width).saturating_add(local_x))
 155|     }
 156| 
 157|     #[cfg(test)]
 158|     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
 159|         self.plans.len()
 160|     }
 161| 
 162|     #[cfg(test)]
 163|     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 164|         self.plans.is_empty()
 165|     }
 166| 
 167|     /// Stable row-major iteration for semantic export and deterministic tests.
 168|     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
 169|         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
 170|         self.plans.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, plan)| {
 171|             let local_z = index / width;
 172|             let local_x = index % width;
 173|             (
 174|                 (
 175|                     self.min_region_x + local_x as i64,
 176|                     self.min_region_z + local_z as i64,
 177|                 ),
 178|                 plan,
 179|             )
 180|         })
 181|     }
 182| }
 183| 
 184| fn region_count(first: i64, last: i64) -> usize {
 185|     let count = last
 186|         .checked_sub(first)
 187|         .and_then(|distance| distance.checked_add(1))
 188|         .expect("requested region window exceeds integer address space");
 189|     usize::try_from(count).expect("requested region window exceeds platform address space")
 190| }
 191| 
 192| fn region_origin(region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Position {
 193|     Position::new(region_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE, region_z as f32 * REGION_SIZE)
 194| }

total: 694
   1| //! The pure macro-scale world planner: an infinite graph, one cell at a time.
   2| //!
   3| //! [`plan_macro_cell`] is a pure function of `(seed, cell id, red-room
   4| //! scale)` — the top of the planning hierarchy documented in
   5| //! [`crate::domain::entities::world_topology`]. It owns three jobs:
   6| //!
   7| //! 1. **Parameter fields.** [`sample_fields`] turns the noise port into
   8| //!    multi-octave `[0, 1]` fields (openness, vertical pressure, anomaly
   9| //!    pressure, ...). This is the *only* legitimate role of fractal math in
  10| //!    the world: it chooses where the building's rules change; it never
  11| //!    substitutes for an architectural decision.
  12| //! 2. **Graph events.** Red rooms are planned here as separated events on
  13| //!    the macro lattice (a deterministic tournament gives every event a
  14| //!    cooldown radius), and vertical links reserve stairwell footprints
  15| //!    where vertical pressure is high.
  16| //! 3. **Continuity contracts.** Primary-route portals are derived from the
  17| //!    *edge's* lattice coordinate, so both neighbors of an edge compute the
  18| //!    identical crossing — the invariant that lets circulation chain across
  19| //!    regions forever.
  20| //!
  21| //! Everything downstream (region planner, anomaly planner, voxelizer)
  22| //! consumes these obligations; nothing here writes a voxel or knows a chunk
  23| //! size. Determinism is testable: see the 5×5 snapshot test at the bottom.
  24| 
  25| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  26| use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{
  27|     MACRO_CELL_SIZE, MacroCell, MacroCellId, MacroFields, PlaceKind, Portal,
  28|     REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL, RedRoomEvent, VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind, WorldNode,
  29| };
  30| use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
  31| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  32| 
  33| /// Side of a region, world units. Kept in lockstep with
  34| /// `region_plan::REGION_SIZE` by a compile-time-adjacent test below.
  35| const REGION_SIZE: f32 = MACRO_CELL_SIZE / REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL as f32;
  36| 
  37| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  38| // Shared 32-bit deterministic hashing.
  39| //
  40| // All architectural "randomness" in region planning flows through these two
  41| // functions. They live here — at the top of the planning hierarchy — and
  42| // `region_plan` imports them, so the macro graph and the regional plans can
  43| // never disagree about a shared derivation (portals, most importantly).
  44| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  45| 
  46| pub(crate) fn mix(mut h: u32) -> u32 {
  47|     h ^= h >> 16;
  48|     h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
  49|     h ^= h >> 13;
  50|     h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2_AE35);
  51|     h ^= h >> 16;
  52|     h
  53| }
  54| 
  55| /// Hash of a seed plus any number of integer keys, uniform in [0, 1).
  56| pub(crate) fn hash01(seed: u32, keys: &[i64]) -> f32 {
  57|     let mut h = mix(seed ^ 0x9E37_79B9);
  58|     for &k in keys {
  59|         h = mix(h ^ (k as u32)).wrapping_add(mix((k >> 32) as u32));
  60|     }
  61|     (mix(h) >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
  62| }
  63| 
  64| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  65| // Portals: the cross-region continuity contract.
  66| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  67| 
  68| /// World Z of the primary-route portal on the vertical edge
  69| /// `x = edge_x * REGION_SIZE` of region row `row_z`. Both regions sharing the
  70| /// edge derive the same value — this function is the single source of truth
  71| /// (the region planner routes its main spine between two of these).
  72| pub fn primary_portal_z(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> f32 {
  73|     let f = 0.30 + 0.40 * hash01(seed, &[0x0E1, edge_x, row_z]);
  74|     snap((row_z as f32 + f) * REGION_SIZE)
  75| }
  76| 
  77| /// Snap to the 0.4 u plan lattice (one coarse voxel).
  78| fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
  79|     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
  80| }
  81| 
  82| fn portal(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> Portal {
  83|     Portal {
  84|         id: hash(seed, 0x7047_A100, edge_x, row_z),
  85|         edge_x,
  86|         row_z,
  87|         at: Position::new(
  88|             edge_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
  89|             primary_portal_z(seed, edge_x, row_z),
  90|         ),
  91|     }
  92| }
  93| 
  94| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  95| // Parameter fields.
  96| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  97| 
  98| /// One multi-octave field in [0, 1]:
  99| /// `F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ · N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`, rescaled and clamped. The provider's
 100| /// base wavelength is ~20 u, so `20 / wavelength` stretches each octave.
 101| fn field(
 102|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 103|     seed: u32,
 104|     salt: u32,
 105|     wx: f32,
 106|     wz: f32,
 107|     wavelengths: [f32; 3],
 108|     weights: [f32; 3],
 109| ) -> f32 {
 110|     let mut sum = 0.0;
 111|     let mut norm = 0.0;
 112|     for (octave, (&wavelength, &weight)) in wavelengths.iter().zip(weights.iter()).enumerate() {
 113|         let s = 20.0 / wavelength;
 114|         sum += weight
 115|             * noise.evaluate_2d(
 116|                 seed ^ salt.wrapping_add((octave as u32).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9)),
 117|                 Position::new(wx * s, wz * s),
 118|             );
 119|         norm += weight;
 120|     }
 121|     // Octave sums cluster toward zero; stretch before biasing to [0, 1] so
 122|     // thresholds see a usable spread instead of everything at 0.5.
 123|     ((sum / norm) * 0.8 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 124| }
 125| 
 126| /// The institution-age field alone — how long this stretch of the building
 127| /// has been rotting. Split out of [`sample_fields`] (and used by it, so the
 128| /// two can never disagree) because per-column callers need one field, not
 129| /// six: old territory keeps fewer of its fluorescents alive.
 130| pub fn institution_age_at(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
 131|     field(
 132|         noise,
 133|         seed,
 134|         0xF1E1_0003,
 135|         wx,
 136|         wz,
 137|         [260.0, 90.0, 30.0],
 138|         [1.0, 0.5, 0.25],
 139|     )
 140| }

 142| /// Sample every macro parameter field at one world point. Pure and
 143| /// world-space: two callers asking about the same point always agree,
 144| /// regardless of which cell, region, or chunk asked.
 145| pub fn sample_fields(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> MacroFields {
 146|     MacroFields {
 147|         openness: field(
 148|             noise,
 149|             seed,
 150|             0xF1E1_0001,
 151|             wx,
 152|             wz,
 153|             [350.0, 130.0, 45.0],
 154|             [1.0, 0.5, 0.2],
 155|         ),
 156|         vertical_pressure: field(
 157|             noise,
 158|             seed,
 159|             0xF1E1_0002,
 160|             wx,
 161|             wz,
 162|             [520.0, 170.0, 60.0],
 163|             [1.0, 0.4, 0.15],
 164|         ),
 165|         institution_age: institution_age_at(noise, seed, wx, wz),
 166|         anomaly_pressure: field(
 167|             noise,
 168|             seed,
 169|             0xF1E1_0004,
 170|             wx,
 171|             wz,
 172|             [620.0, 210.0, 70.0],
 173|             [1.0, 0.35, 0.1],
 174|         ),
 175|         redroom_pressure: field(
 176|             noise,
 177|             seed,
 178|             0xF1E1_0005,
 179|             wx,
 180|             wz,
 181|             [700.0, 230.0, 80.0],
 182|             [1.0, 0.3, 0.1],
 183|         ),
 184|         style_blend: field(
 185|             noise,
 186|             seed,
 187|             0xF1E1_0006,
 188|             wx,
 189|             wz,
 190|             [420.0, 140.0, 50.0],
 191|             [1.0, 0.45, 0.2],
 192|         ),
 193|     }

 196| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 197| // Red rooms as separated graph events.
 198| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 199| 
 200| /// Cooldown radius in macro cells (Chebyshev). Two committed events are
 201| /// always at least one full macro cell (160 u) apart, so red rooms read as
 202| /// rare landmarks instead of a recurring biome.
 203| const RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS: i64 = 1;
 204| 
 205| /// Base per-cell candidate chance at `red_room_scale == 1.0`.
 206| const RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE: f32 = 0.32;
 207| 
 208| /// The candidate score of one macro cell: `Some(score)` if the cell wants a
 209| /// red room this epoch, lower score = higher priority in the tournament.
 210| fn red_room_candidate(
 211|     seed: u32,
 212|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 213|     cell: MacroCellId,
 214|     red_room_scale: f32,
 215| ) -> Option<f32> {
 216|     if red_room_scale <= 0.0 {
 217|         return None;
 218|     }
 219|     let center = cell.center();
 220|     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z).redroom_pressure;
 221|     let score = unit(hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0011, cell.x, cell.z));
 222|     // Pressure clusters events without ever making them uniform or certain.
 223|     let chance = (RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE * red_room_scale).min(0.85) * (0.35 + 0.65 * pressure);
 224|     (score < chance).then_some(score)
 225| }
 226| 
 227| /// The red-room event a macro cell *wins*, if any. A candidate cell fires
 228| /// only when no candidate within the separation radius beats its score
 229| /// (ties broken by lattice coordinate), so any two firing cells are more
 230| /// than the separation radius apart — a deterministic Matérn-style
 231| /// exclusion, computed locally without global state.
 232| pub fn red_room_event_for_cell(
 233|     seed: u32,
 234|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 235|     cell: MacroCellId,
 236|     red_room_scale: f32,
 237| ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
 238|     let mine = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale)?;
 239|     for dz in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
 240|         for dx in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
 241|             if dx == 0 && dz == 0 {
 242|                 continue;
 243|             }
 244|             let rival_cell = MacroCellId::new(cell.x + dx, cell.z + dz);
 245|             if let Some(rival) = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, rival_cell, red_room_scale) {
 246|                 let rival_wins = (rival, rival_cell.x, rival_cell.z) < (mine, cell.x, cell.z);
 247|                 if rival_wins {
 248|                     return None;
 249|                 }
 250|             }
 251|         }
 252|     }
 253|     // The event targets exactly one of the cell's 2×2 regions.
 254|     let pick = hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0022, cell.x, cell.z);
 255|     let region = (
 256|         cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + (pick & 1) as i64,
 257|         cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + ((pick >> 1) & 1) as i64,
 258|     );
 259|     Some(RedRoomEvent {
 260|         id: hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0033, cell.x, cell.z),
 261|         region,
 262|         score: mine,
 263|     })
 264| }
 265| 
 266| /// Does a red-room event target this specific region? This is the query the
 267| /// region planner asks; the answer is independent of which chunk, region, or
 268| /// LOD triggered the plan.
 269| pub fn red_room_event_for_region(
 270|     seed: u32,
 271|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 272|     region_x: i64,
 273|     region_z: i64,
 274|     red_room_scale: f32,
 275| ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
 276|     red_room_event_for_cell(
 277|         seed,
 278|         noise,
 279|         MacroCellId::of_region(region_x, region_z),
 280|         red_room_scale,
 281|     )
 282|     .filter(|event| event.region == (region_x, region_z))
 283| }
 284| 
 285| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 286| // Vertical links.
 287| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 288| 
 289| /// The vertical link reserved inside one region, if any. Stairwells are
 290| /// planned per region so the region planner can honor the reservation while
 291| /// laying out its assemblies; the *kind* mix leans ordinary, with the
 292| /// endless variants appearing only under high vertical pressure.
 293| pub fn vertical_link_for_region(
 294|     seed: u32,
 295|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 296|     region_x: i64,
 297|     region_z: i64,
 298| ) -> Option<VerticalLink> {
 299|     let center_x = (region_x as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
 300|     let center_z = (region_z as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
 301|     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z).vertical_pressure;
 302|     let gate = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0001, region_x, region_z));
 303|     if gate >= 0.06 + 0.30 * pressure * pressure {
 304|         return None;
 305|     }
 306| 
 307|     let kind_roll = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0002, region_x, region_z));
 308|     let (kind, to_elevation) = if kind_roll < 0.55 {
 309|         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
 310|     } else if kind_roll < 0.75 && pressure > 0.55 {
 311|         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, 1)
 312|     } else if kind_roll < 0.90 && pressure > 0.55 {
 313|         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessDescent, -1)
 314|     } else if kind_roll < 0.97 {
 315|         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
 316|     } else {
 317|         (VerticalLinkKind::ServiceShaft, -1)
 318|     };
 319| 
 320|     // Anchor well inside the region so the stair mass never has to fight the
 321|     // edge margin. The region planner snaps the actual footprint to its
 322|     // corridor network; the anchor only says "near here".
 323|     let ax = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0003, region_x, region_z));
 324|     let az = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0004, region_x, region_z));
 325|     Some(VerticalLink {
 326|         id: hash(seed, 0x57A1_0005, region_x, region_z),
 327|         kind,
 328|         region: (region_x, region_z),
 329|         anchor: Position::new(
 330|             snap((region_x as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * ax) * REGION_SIZE),

 331|             snap((region_z as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * az) * REGION_SIZE),
 332|         ),
 333|         from_elevation: 0,
 334|         to_elevation,
 335|     })
 336| }
 337| 
 338| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 339| // The cell planner.
 340| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 341| 
 342| fn classify_region(
 343|     seed: u32,
 344|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 345|     region: (i64, i64),
 346|     red_room_event: Option<&RedRoomEvent>,
 347|     vertical: Option<&VerticalLink>,
 348| ) -> PlaceKind {
 349|     if red_room_event.is_some_and(|event| event.region == region) {
 350|         return PlaceKind::RedRoomEncounter;
 351|     }
 352|     if vertical.is_some() {
 353|         return PlaceKind::Stairwell;
 354|     }
 355|     let center_x = (region.0 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
 356|     let center_z = (region.1 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
 357|     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z);
 358|     if fields.openness > 0.66 {
 359|         if fields.vertical_pressure > 0.60 {
 360|             PlaceKind::Atrium
 361|         } else {
 362|             PlaceKind::OpenPlate
 363|         }
 364|     } else {
 365|         PlaceKind::Warren
 366|     }
 367| }
 368| 
 369| /// Plan one macro cell of the infinite world graph.
 370| ///
 371| /// Pure: the same `(seed, cell, red_room_scale)` always yields the same
 372| /// graph, and shared contracts (portals, red-room tournaments) agree with
 373| /// every neighboring cell's own computation. `red_room_scale` is the
 374| /// world-wide `anomalies.frequency * anomalies.red_rooms` product; passing
 375| /// different scales for different cells of one world is a caller bug.
 376| pub fn plan_macro_cell(
 377|     seed: u32,
 378|     cell: MacroCellId,
 379|     red_room_scale: f32,
 380|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 381| ) -> MacroCell {
 382|     let center = cell.center();
 383|     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z);
 384|     let red_room_event = red_room_event_for_cell(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale);
 385| 
 386|     let region_x0 = cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
 387|     let region_z0 = cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
 388| 
 389|     let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity((REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL) as usize);
 390|     let mut vertical_links = Vec::new();
 391|     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 392|         for dx in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 393|             let region = (region_x0 + dx, region_z0 + dz);
 394|             let vertical = vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, region.0, region.1);
 395|             nodes.push(WorldNode {
 396|                 id: hash(seed, 0x40DE_0001, region.0, region.1),
 397|                 region,
 398|                 kind: classify_region(
 399|                     seed,
 400|                     noise,
 401|                     region,
 402|                     red_room_event.as_ref(),
 403|                     vertical.as_ref(),
 404|                 ),
 405|                 elevation: 0,
 406|             });
 407|             vertical_links.extend(vertical);
 408|         }
 409|     }
 410| 
 411|     // Every vertical edge the cell's regions touch: interior, west boundary,
 412|     // and east boundary. Boundary portals are recomputed identically by the
 413|     // neighboring cell (asserted by test below).
 414|     let mut portals = Vec::new();
 415|     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 416|         for edge in 0..=REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 417|             portals.push(portal(seed, region_x0 + edge, region_z0 + dz));
 418|         }
 419|     }
 420| 
 421|     MacroCell {
 422|         id: cell,
 423|         fields,
 424|         nodes,
 425|         portals,
 426|         vertical_links,
 427|         red_room_event,
 428|     }
 429| }

 502|     fn snapshot_5x5() -> String {
 503|         let noise = noise();
 504|         let mut out = String::new();
 505|         for cz in -2i64..=2 {
 506|             for cx in -2i64..=2 {
 507|                 out.push_str(&describe(&plan_macro_cell(
 508|                     SEED,
 509|                     MacroCellId::new(cx, cz),
 510|                     1.0,
 511|                     &noise,
 512|                 )));
 513|             }
 514|         }
 515|         out

 518|     fn digest(text: &str) -> u64 {
 519|         let mut h = 0xCBF2_9CE4_8422_2325u64;
 520|         for byte in text.bytes() {
 521|             h = mix64(h ^ byte as u64);
 522|         }
 523|         h
 524|     }
 525| 
 526|     /// The same seed, coordinates and scale must always produce the same
 527|     /// graph — byte for byte. If this digest changes, the world changed for
 528|     /// every player: update the constant only for an *intentional*
 529|     /// generation change, and say so in the commit message.
 530|     #[test]
 531|     fn five_by_five_topology_snapshot_is_stable() {
 532|         let text = snapshot_5x5();
 533|         assert_eq!(text, snapshot_5x5(), "topology is not replayable");
 534|         assert_eq!(
 535|             digest(&text),
 536|             SNAPSHOT_DIGEST,
 537|             "macro topology for seed {SEED} changed; snapshot follows:\n{text}"
 538|         );
 539|     }

 562|     /// Any two committed red-room events keep the cooldown distance: no two
 563|     /// events within the separation radius over a large scan.
 564|     #[test]
 565|     fn red_room_events_respect_their_separation_radius() {
 566|         let noise = noise();
 567|         let mut events = Vec::new();
 568|         for cz in -12i64..=12 {
 569|             for cx in -12i64..=12 {
 570|                 if let Some(event) =
 571|                     red_room_event_for_cell(SEED, &noise, MacroCellId::new(cx, cz), 1.0)
 572|                 {
 573|                     events.push(((cx, cz), event));
 574|                 }
 575|             }
 576|         }
 577|         assert!(
 578|             events.len() >= 5,
 579|             "red rooms too rare to test separation ({} events in 625 cells)",
 580|             events.len()
 581|         );
 582|         for (i, ((ax, az), _)) in events.iter().enumerate() {
 583|             for ((bx, bz), _) in events.iter().skip(i + 1) {
 584|                 let chebyshev = (ax - bx).abs().max((az - bz).abs());
 585|                 assert!(
 586|                     chebyshev > RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS,
 587|                     "events at ({ax},{az}) and ({bx},{bz}) violate the cooldown"
 588|                 );
 589|             }
 590|         }
 591|     }

 593|     /// The per-region query and the per-cell tournament are one system.
 594|     #[test]
 595|     fn region_query_matches_cell_tournament() {
 596|         let noise = noise();
 597|         for cz in -6i64..=6 {
 598|             for cx in -6i64..=6 {
 599|                 let cell = MacroCellId::new(cx, cz);
 600|                 let event = red_room_event_for_cell(SEED, &noise, cell, 1.0);
 601|                 for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 602|                     for dx in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
 603|                         let region = (
 604|                             cx * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + dx,
 605|                             cz * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + dz,
 606|                         );
 607|                         let hit = red_room_event_for_region(SEED, &noise, region.0, region.1, 1.0);
 608|                         match (&event, hit) {
 609|                             (Some(e), Some(h)) => {
 610|                                 assert_eq!(e.region, region);
 611|                                 assert_eq!(*e, h);
 612|                             }
 613|                             (Some(e), None) => assert_ne!(e.region, region),
 614|                             (None, Some(_)) => panic!("region fired without its cell"),
 615|                             (None, None) => {}
 616|                         }
 617|                     }
 618|                 }
 619|             }
 620|         }
 621|     }

 638|     fn fields_are_bounded_and_replayable() {
 639|         let noise = noise();
 640|         let mut spread = (f32::MAX, f32::MIN);
 641|         for z in (-2000..=2000).step_by(160) {
 642|             for x in (-2000..=2000).step_by(160) {
 643|                 let a = sample_fields(&noise, SEED, x as f32, z as f32);

 657|                 spread.1 = spread.1.max(a.openness);
 658|             }
 659|         }

 661|             spread.1 - spread.0 > 0.4,
 662|             "openness field is too flat to steer anything: {spread:?}"

 667|     #[test]
 668|     fn vertical_links_are_present_but_not_everywhere() {
 669|         let noise = noise();

 671|         let mut regions = 0usize;
 672|         for rz in -20i64..=20 {
 673|             for rx in -20i64..=20 {

 682|                     assert!(link.anchor.x > x0 + 8.0 && link.anchor.x < x0 + REGION_SIZE - 8.0);
 683|                     assert!(link.anchor.z > z0 + 8.0 && link.anchor.z < z0 + REGION_SIZE - 8.0);
 684|                 }
 685|             }
 686|         }
 687|         let ratio = links as f32 / regions as f32;
 688|         assert!(

world_topology.rs: 
- `red_room_event_for_cell` calls `red_room_candidate` for 8 neighbors, each calling `sample_fields` (6 fields × 3 octaves = 18 noise evaluations) → ~9 cells × 18 noise = 162 noise evals per macro cell. And `plan_macro_cell` calls `red_room_event_for_cell` + `sample_fields` again at cell center + `classify_region` per region (4 regions × 18 noise evals) + `vertical_link_for_region` per region (4 × 18 noise) + `red_room_candidate` itself samples fields at cell center... So per macro cell: ~ (1 + 8) × 18 (red room tournament: candidate + rivals) + 18 (center fields) + 4×18 (classify) + 4×18 (vertical links) ≈ 162+18+72+72 = 324 noise evaluations per macro cell. Each noise evaluation itself may be multi-octave in SimpleNoiseProvider. That's a constant factor — moderate redundancy: `classify_region` re-samples fields per region, and the red-room tournament re-samples rival cell fields — all pure, but recomputed every time a chunk is generated (see the level_zero finding). The redundancy is bounded (constant), so Medium at most. Worth noting: repeated `sample_fields` calls in one cell (center fields + classify per region + red room candidates) — 324 noise evals per macro cell, ~9-25 macro cells per chunk window → thousands of noise evals per chunk. But since each region plan is generated per region and window plans re-plan per chunk (level_zero issue), this multiplies.

Note: `plan_macro_cell` computes `sample_fields` at cell center (line 383), and `red_room_event_for_cell` → `red_room_candidate` also samples fields at the same center (line 220) — same point sampled twice. Then `classify_region` samples per region center. And `vertical_link_for_region` samples per region center. So for one macro cell: fields at center sampled twice (383 + 220), and per-region center sampled twice (classify 357 + vertical 301). Minor redundancy — Medium/Low. Could pass MacroFields around.

Now world_block.rs.
total: 452
   1| //! Loading a place instead of streaming a frontier.
   2| //!
   3| //! The level used to plan chunk-locally: every architectural decision had to
   4| //! be answerable from one coordinate with no cross-chunk reads, because a
   5| //! chunk arriving in front of the player had nobody to ask. That constraint
   6| //! bought infinite streaming and cost the architecture nearly everything
   7| //! that needs to see more than one room — connectivity you can *verify*
   8| //! rather than assume, integration over a circulation graph, composition
   9| //! staged across an area, a motif established before it is broken.
  10| //!
  11| //! A [`WorldBlock`] is the trade taken deliberately: behind one loading
  12| //! screen, plan a very large area at once. Only the *plans* are bulk-built —
  13| //! a region is a few kilobytes of assemblies, corridors and genomes, so a
  14| //! whole block is a few hundred kilobytes. Voxels keep streaming from those
  15| //! plans exactly as before, which is what keeps frame time flat on a small
  16| //! machine. Bulk-generating voxels instead would be hundreds of megabytes
  17| //! and would buy nothing: voxel sampling was never the part that was
  18| //! starved for context.
  19| //!
  20| //! Crossing a block is not a level transition. The player walks out of one
  21| //! and into the next with no seam and no pause, because the next was
  22| //! planned in the background the moment they crossed the [`PRELOAD_MARGIN`]
  23| //! — the loading screen is paid once, at the start, and never again.
  24| 
  25| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
  26| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
  27| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  28| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  29| use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
  30| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  31| use crate::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
  32| 
  33| /// Regions along one edge of a block.
  34| ///
  35| /// Sixteen 80 u regions is a 1280 u square — 1.6 km² of floor. Crossing it
  36| /// in a straight line takes minutes; nobody crosses a labyrinth in a
  37| /// straight line, and finding your way through one is hours. That is the
  38| /// unit the loading screen is buying.
  39| pub const REGIONS_PER_BLOCK: i64 = 16;
  40| 
  41| /// Side of a block, world units.
  42| pub const BLOCK_SIZE: f32 = REGIONS_PER_BLOCK as f32 * REGION_SIZE;
  43| 
  44| /// How close to the edge a player must come before the next block starts
  45| /// planning, world units.
  46| ///
  47| /// Three regions. Wide enough that even a sprint across the margin finishes
  48| /// planning before the player arrives, narrow enough that a wanderer who
  49| /// merely brushes a boundary and turns back does not trigger work for a
  50| /// place they never visit.
  51| pub const PRELOAD_MARGIN: f32 = 3.0 * REGION_SIZE;
  52| 
  53| /// Address of a block on the block lattice.
  54| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
  55| pub struct BlockCoord {
  56|     pub x: i64,
  57|     pub z: i64,
  58| }
  59| 
  60| impl BlockCoord {
  61|     /// The block containing a world position.
  62|     pub fn of(world: Position) -> Self {
  63|         Self {
  64|             x: (world.x / BLOCK_SIZE).floor() as i64,
  65|             z: (world.z / BLOCK_SIZE).floor() as i64,
  66|         }
  67|     }
  68| 
  69|     pub fn origin(self) -> Position {
  70|         Position::new(self.x as f32 * BLOCK_SIZE, self.z as f32 * BLOCK_SIZE)
  71|     }
  72| 
  73|     pub fn bounds(self) -> WorldBounds {
  74|         let origin = self.origin();
  75|         WorldBounds::new(
  76|             origin.x,
  77|             origin.z,
  78|             origin.x + BLOCK_SIZE,
  79|             origin.z + BLOCK_SIZE,
  80|         )
  81|     }
  82| }
  83| 
  84| /// A large, fully planned, walkable area.
  85| pub struct WorldBlock {
  86|     coord: BlockCoord,
  87|     window: InfiniteRegionWindow,
  88| }
  89| 
  90| impl WorldBlock {
  91|     /// Plans an entire block, reporting progress so a loading screen has
  92|     /// something honest to show.
  93|     ///
  94|     /// `progress` receives `(regions_done, regions_total)`. It is called per
  95|     /// region rather than per chunk because a region is the unit of work
  96|     /// that actually takes time, and a progress bar that advances in units
  97|     /// nobody is waiting on is a lie.
  98|     pub fn load(
  99|         seed: u32,
 100|         coord: BlockCoord,
 101|         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 102|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 103|         progress: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize),
 104|     ) -> Self {
 105|         // One halo region beyond the block, so a chunk sampled at the very
 106|         // edge still finds the plan of the region across the boundary and
 107|         // the two blocks agree about what is built there.
 108|         //
 109|         // The halo is why the reported total is larger than
 110|         // `REGIONS_PER_BLOCK^2`: the window really does plan the surrounding
 111|         // ring, and a bar that hid that work would stall at 100% while it
 112|         // finished.
 113|         let window = InfiniteRegionWindow::covering_with_progress(
 114|             coord.bounds(),
 115|             REGION_SIZE,
 116|             seed,
 117|             config,
 118|             noise,
 119|             progress,
 120|         );
 121|         Self { coord, window }
 122|     }
 123| 
 124|     /// The planned regions, for feeding straight into chunk generation.
 125|     ///
 126|     /// Handing the window over rather than copying plans out is the whole
 127|     /// economy of the block: one derivation serves every chunk inside it,
 128|     /// and any block-scale pass run over these plans is automatically seen
 129|     /// by all of them.
 130|     pub fn plans(&self) -> &InfiniteRegionWindow {
 131|         &self.window
 132|     }
 133| 
 134|     pub fn coord(&self) -> BlockCoord {
 135|         self.coord
 136|     }
 137| 
 138|     pub fn bounds(&self) -> WorldBounds {
 139|         self.coord.bounds()
 140|     }
 141| 
 142|     /// The plan for a world point, if this block covers it.
 143|     pub fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
 144|         self.window.plan_at(world)
 145|     }
 146| 
 147|     /// Is this position inside the block proper (not merely its halo)?
 148|     pub fn contains(&self, world: Position) -> bool {
 149|         self.bounds().contains(world.x, world.z)
 150|     }
 151| 
 152|     /// Blocks that should start planning now, given where the player is.
 153|     ///
 154|     /// Returns the neighbours whose edge the player has come within
 155|     /// [`PRELOAD_MARGIN`] of — up to three at a corner. Empty in the
 156|     /// interior, which is almost always, so the caller does no work for most
 157|     /// of a session.
 158|     ///
 159|     /// Deliberately returns *what to load* rather than loading it: this
 160|     /// module plans, and only the caller knows whether it has a thread to
 161|     /// plan on.
 162|     pub fn preload_targets(&self, world: Position) -> Vec<BlockCoord> {
 163|         let b = self.bounds();
 164|         let mut out = Vec::new();
 165|         let near_west = world.x - b.min_x < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
 166|         let near_east = b.max_x - world.x < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
 167|         let near_north = world.z - b.min_z < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
 168|         let near_south = b.max_z - world.z < PRELOAD_MARGIN;
 169| 
 170|         let mut push = |dx: i64, dz: i64| {
 171|             out.push(BlockCoord {
 172|                 x: self.coord.x + dx,
 173|                 z: self.coord.z + dz,
 174|             })
 175|         };
 176|         if near_west {
 177|             push(-1, 0);
 178|         }
 179|         if near_east {
 180|             push(1, 0);
 181|         }
 182|         if near_north {
 183|             push(0, -1);
 184|         }
 185|         if near_south {
 186|             push(0, 1);
 187|         }
 188|         // The diagonal too: a player heading for a corner arrives in the
 189|         // diagonal block without ever entering either edge neighbour, and
 190|         // finding it unplanned is exactly the stall this exists to avoid.
 191|         if near_west && near_north {
 192|             push(-1, -1);
 193|         }
 194|         if near_east && near_north {
 195|             push(1, -1);
 196|         }
 197|         if near_west && near_south {
 198|             push(-1, 1);
 199|         }
 200|         if near_east && near_south {
 201|             push(1, 1);
 202|         }
 203|         out
 204|     }
 205| }

 238|     fn progress_is_reported_in_units_someone_is_waiting_on() {
 239|         // A loading bar may only ever move forward, must finish exactly at
 240|         // its own total, and must count the work actually being done. The
 241|         // old implementation satisfied none of that: it announced 0 and then
 242|         // `total`, so the bar sat still through the entire wait — and the
 243|         // `total` it announced was the block's 256 interior regions while it
 244|         // went on to plan the surrounding halo ring too, so even an honest
 245|         // bar built on it would have stalled at 100%.
 246|         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 247|         let mut samples = Vec::new();
 248|         let mut progress = |done, total| samples.push((done, total));
 249|         WorldBlock::load(
 250|             42,
 251|             BlockCoord { x: 0, z: 0 },
 252|             &config(),
 253|             &noise,
 254|             &mut progress,
 255|         );
 256| 
 257|         let (_, total) = samples[0];
 258|         assert!(
 259|             samples.iter().all(|&(_, t)| t == total),
 260|             "the total moved under the bar"
 261|         );
 262|         assert!(
 263|             total >= (REGIONS_PER_BLOCK * REGIONS_PER_BLOCK) as usize,
 264|             "a block reported less work than it has regions: {total}"
 265|         );
 266|         assert_eq!(samples.first().map(|&(done, _)| done), Some(0));
 267|         assert_eq!(samples.last(), Some(&(total, total)));
 268|         assert_eq!(
 269|             samples.len(),
 270|             total + 1,
 271|             "progress should be reported once per region planned, plus the opening zero"
 272|         );

 359|     #[test]
 360|     fn neighbouring_blocks_agree_across_the_seam() {
 361|         // The whole point of planning per region on a world lattice: a block
 362|         // boundary must not be visible. Both blocks must describe the same
 363|         // building where they meet.
 364|         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 365|         let mut progress = |_, _| {};
 366|         let left = WorldBlock::load(
 367|             42,
 368|             BlockCoord { x: 0, z: 0 },
 369|             &config(),
 370|             &noise,
 371|             &mut progress,
 372|         );
 373|         let right = WorldBlock::load(
 374|             42,
 375|             BlockCoord { x: 1, z: 0 },
 376|             &config(),
 377|             &noise,
 378|             &mut progress,
 379|         );
 380| 
 381|         // A strip inside the right block, within the left block's halo.
 382|         let mut compared = 0;
 383|         for k in 0..12 {
 384|             let p = Position::new(BLOCK_SIZE + 4.0, k as f32 * 90.0 + 5.0);
 385|             if p.z >= BLOCK_SIZE {
 386|                 break;
 387|             }
 388|             let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (left.plan_at(p), right.plan_at(p)) else {
 389|                 continue;

 397|             );
 398|             assert_eq!(a.origin_world.x, b.origin_world.x);
 399|             assert_eq!(a.origin_world.z, b.origin_world.z);

 401|         }

   1| //! Region-scale architectural planning for Backrooms Level 0.
   2| //!
   3| //! The world is tiled by fixed 80 u square regions on a world-space lattice.
   4| //! [`generate_region_plan`] is a *pure* function of `(seed, region)`: it
   5| //! derives the region's designers ([`ArchitectGenome`]), routes a dominant
   6| //! circulation spine first (between edge portals shared with the neighboring
   7| //! regions), attaches incomplete program masses ([`AssemblyInstance`]) beside
   8| //! that circulation,
   9| //! gives them structure / ceilings / fixtures, and finally applies a
  10| //! Backrooms corruption pass (duplicated suites, abandoned expansions,
  11| //! renovation overlays).
  12| //!
  13| //! Cross-region continuity: a corridor leaves a region only at a *portal* on
  14| //! a shared edge, and the portal position is derived from the *edge's*
  15| //! lattice coordinate — both neighbors compute the identical portal, so
  16| //! corridors chain across regions forever (a main corridor that never ends
  17| //! is the first and cheapest corruption).
  18| //!
  19| //! Dimensions and split planes use a 0.4 u lattice. Hosted wall centerlines
  20| //! may use its 0.2 u half-step, which aligns them with coarse voxel centers
  21| //! without changing the physical plan at different LODs.
  22| 
  23| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  24| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  25| use crate::use_cases::anomaly_plan::plan_anomalies_for_region;
  26| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  27| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  28| 
  29| /// Side of a region, world units. A multiple of both chunk sizes (10/20).
  30| pub const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
  31| /// Plan wall thickness: an institutional double-wythe partition (two CAD
  32| /// interior walls back to back). The value must also stay >= one coarse
  33| /// voxel (0.4) or walls vanish at the LOD-1 proxy resolution.
  34| pub const PLAN_WALL_T: f32 = 2.0 * crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_WALL_THICKNESS;
  35| /// Doorways are cased rough openings around the referencable CAD single
  36| /// door: finished width plus 0.15 u of jamb clearance per side, so the
  37| /// coarsest supported voxel scale (0.4 u) still quantizes the opening
  38| /// wider than the player capsule.
  39| pub const DOOR_JAMB_CLEARANCE: f32 = 0.15;
  40| pub const DOOR_WIDTH: f32 =
  41|     crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_DOOR_WIDTH + 2.0 * DOOR_JAMB_CLEARANCE;
  42| /// Lintels sit at the standard CAD door-frame height.
  43| pub const DOOR_HEIGHT: f32 = crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_DOOR_HEIGHT;
  44| /// Snap lattice for all plan geometry (= coarsest voxel size).
  45| const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
  46| /// Keep-out margin from region edges for assembly footprints.
  47| const EDGE_MARGIN: f32 = 3.2;
  48| 
  49| /// Region lattice index of a world coordinate.
  50| pub fn region_index(w: f32) -> i64 {
  51|     (w / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64
  52| }
  53| 
  54| fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
  55|     (v / SNAP).round() * SNAP
  56| }
  57| 
  58| /// Corridor widths snap to 0.8 so *half*-widths stay on the 0.4 lattice and
  59| /// suite front walls land flush against corridor edges.
  60| fn snap_width(v: f32) -> f32 {
  61|     ((v / (2.0 * SNAP)).round() * 2.0 * SNAP).max(2.0 * SNAP)
  62| }
  63| 
  64| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  65| // Deterministic hashing and edge portals.
  66| //
  67| // All "randomness" flows through `world_topology::hash01`, and the portal a
  68| // corridor uses to cross a region border is the macro graph's portal — one
  69| // derivation shared by both neighbors of the edge and by the topology layer.
  70| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  71| 
  72| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::{hash01, primary_portal_z as v_edge_portal_z};
  73| 
  74| fn pick_index(h: f32, len: usize) -> usize {
  75|     ((h * len as f32) as usize).min(len - 1)
  76| }
  77| 
  78| /// World spawn: a point *on the main corridor centerline* of region (0, 0),
  79| /// a few units east of its west portal. The first thing the player sees is
  80| /// therefore the region's dominant circulation route — walls running away in
  81| /// both directions — rather than unplanned fabric. Both the generator core
  82| /// and the browser composition root derive spawn from this single function,
  83| /// so the player and the voxelizer can never disagree about where "here" is.
  84| pub fn spawn_point(seed: u32) -> Position {
  85|     // The main spine's west leg always runs from (0, west_z) to at least
  86|     // x = 0.35 * REGION_SIZE, so a few units in we are guaranteed to stand
  87|     // on a straight, readable stretch of corridor.
  88|     Position::new(6.0, v_edge_portal_z(seed, 0, 0))
  89| }

  91| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  92| // The planning stages, one intent per module.
  93| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  94| 
  95| mod circulation;
  96| mod corruption;
  97| mod debug;
  98| mod genome;
  99| mod suites;
 100| // Phase 2 steps 2-3: free-space decomposition and scored greedy placement.
 101| // These drive `generate_region_plan` -- see the placement pass below.
 102| mod layout;
 103| mod territories;
 104| #[cfg(test)]
 105| mod tests;

 107| pub use debug::debug_region_ascii;
