 113| /// Pure, deterministic plan for the region whose lower-left corner is
 114| /// `region_origin` (must lie on the region lattice).
 115| pub fn generate_region_plan(
 116|     seed: u32,
 117|     region_origin: Position,
 118|     region_size: f32,
 119|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 120|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 121| ) -> RegionPlan {
 122|     let rx = region_index(region_origin.x + 0.1);
 123|     let rz = region_index(region_origin.z + 0.1);
 124|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xA0 + k, rx, rz]);
 125| 
 126|     let dominant = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 0, noise);
 127|     let renovator = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 1, noise);
 128|     let mut architects = vec![dominant.clone(), renovator];
 129|     // A third designer intrudes where the style-blend field runs high: the
 130|     // macro fields decide *where* cultures leak into each other; the hash
 131|     // only decides whether this particular region exposes the seam.
 132|     let fields = crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields(
 133|         noise,
 134|         seed,
 135|         (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
 136|         (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
 137|     );
 138|     if h(0) < 0.10 + 0.55 * fields.style_blend {
 139|         architects.push(derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 2, noise));
 140|     }
 141| 
 142|     let corridors = build_corridors(seed, rx, rz, &dominant, region_origin, region_size);
 143| 
 144|     // --- incomplete masses beside circulation -------------------------------
 145|     // Scored greedy placement over the region's free space: decompose what
 146|     // circulation leaves, then let each program in the budget simulate every
 147|     // seat on every leg and commit the best. Every spine offers legs, not
 148|     // only the dominant one -- a secondary hall with nothing on it is a
 149|     // corridor to nowhere, which reads as liminal only when authored.
 150|     let mut assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
 151|     let mut taken: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = Vec::new();
 152|     let mut id = 0u32;
 153|     let placement_legs = layout::legs_of(&corridors, 14.0);
 154|     let territories = territories::free_territories(
 155|         region_origin.x,
 156|         region_origin.z,
 157|         region_size,
 158|         &corridors,
 159|         &taken,
 160|         EDGE_MARGIN,
 161|         PLAN_WALL_T,
 162|     );
 163|     assemblies.extend(layout::lay_out_suites(
 164|         &|k| hash01(seed, &[k, rx, rz]),
 165|         &dominant,
 166|         &placement_legs,
 167|         &territories,
 168|         region_origin,
 169|         region_size,
 170|         PLAN_WALL_T,
 171|         &corridors,
 172|         &mut taken,
 173|         &mut id,
 174|     ));
 175| 
 176|     // The stair placer wants raw leg spans, not placement candidates.
 177|     let legs: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = placement_legs
 178|         .iter()
 179|         .map(|l| (l.x0, l.x1, l.z, l.half_width * 2.0))
 180|         .collect();
 181| 
 182|     // --- corruption pass ----------------------------------------------------
 183|     corrupt(
 184|         seed,
 185|         rx,
 186|         rz,
 187|         &dominant,
 188|         config,
 189|         noise,
 190|         &mut assemblies,
 191|         &mut taken,
 192|         &corridors,
 193|     );
 194| 
 195|     // --- vertical circulation ------------------------------------------------
 196|     // The macro graph may have reserved a stairwell here. Upward links are
 197|     // realized as a Stair assembly beside the main spine; downward links
 198|     // stay graph reservations until the engine streams below elevation 0.
 199|     // Placed after corruption so no pass can duplicate, abandon, or redden
 200|     // a stair core.
 201|     if let Some(link) =
 202|         crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, rx, rz)
 203|         && crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry(&link)
 204|         && let Some(stair) = crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::place_stairwell(
 205|             id + 2000,
 206|             &link,
 207|             &legs,
 208|             region_origin,
 209|             region_size,
 210|             EDGE_MARGIN,
 211|             PLAN_WALL_T,
 212|             &taken,
 213|             |cx, cz, clearance| {
 214|                 corridors
 215|                     .iter()
 216|                     .all(|s| s.distance(cx, cz) >= s.width * 0.5 + clearance)
 217|             },
 218|         )
 219|     {
 220|         taken.push(stair.footprint.bounds());
 221|         assemblies.push(stair);
 222|     }
 223| 
 224|     // Macro anomalies are derived after ordinary architecture so compact red
 225|     // rooms can promote a real assembly, while region-spanning families keep
 226|     // stable world-lattice identities independent of this region query.
 227|     let anomalies = plan_anomalies_for_region(
 228|         seed,
 229|         region_origin,
 230|         region_size,
 231|         &assemblies,
 232|         spawn_point(seed),
 233|         config,
 234|         noise,
 235|     );
 236| 
 237|     RegionPlan {
 238|         origin_world: region_origin,
 239|         size_world: region_size,
 240|         architects,
 241|         assemblies,
 242|         corridors,
 243|         anomalies,
 244|     }
 245| }

total: 398
   1| //! Scored greedy room placement.
   2| //!
   3| //! The floor-plan literature's step 2 is: simulate placing each room at
   4| //! every free position, score the placements, commit the best, repeat, in
   5| //! order of program importance. This is that solver.
   6| //!
   7| //! What it replaces was a cursor walk: slide along the dominant corridor
   8| //! leg, roll a hash, and place a suite if the roll passed and the spot
   9| //! happened to be clear. Three consequences, all visible in a plan view --
  10| //! a failed spot was skipped rather than improved on, only the dominant leg
  11| //! was ever considered, and nothing compared two candidate spots against
  12| //! each other. An 80 u region resolved to two rooms and 90% unplanned
  13| //! fabric.
  14| //!
  15| //! Scoring, not solving: this is greedy best-first, not an optimizer. The
  16| //! literature is explicit that greedy placement with good scoring functions
  17| //! reproduces designer judgement well enough, and it stays fast and
  18| //! debuggable, which an annealer would not.
  19| 
  20| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  21|     ArchitectGenome, AssemblyInstance, CirculationSpine, SpaceProgram,
  22| };
  23| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  24| 
  25| use super::suites::{entrance_faces_route, place_suite};
  26| use super::territories::Territory;
  27| 
  28| /// Programs in descending importance, with how many of each a region wants
  29| /// at most. Importance order is load-bearing: the literature places the
  30| /// large public rooms first because they are the ones a bad leftover shape
  31| /// ruins, and lets small service rooms take what is left.
  32| /// Interleaved rather than grouped: importance still decides who chooses
  33| /// first, but taking all five open offices before any other program lets
  34| /// the first entry eat the floor and returns a region of nothing but open
  35| /// offices. One pass per round, largest programs earliest in the round.
  36| const PROGRAM_BUDGET: [(SpaceProgram, usize); 11] = [
  37|     // Public and large first: these are the rooms a bad leftover shape
  38|     // ruins, and the ones that give a floor its character.
  39|     (SpaceProgram::Atrium, 1),
  40|     (SpaceProgram::OpenOffice, 3),
  41|     (SpaceProgram::Reception, 1),
  42|     (SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom, 2),
  43|     (SpaceProgram::WaitingArea, 1),
  44|     (SpaceProgram::BreakRoom, 1),
  45|     (SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice, 3),
  46|     // Service last: small, tolerant of awkward remainders, and plausible
  47|     // wherever they end up. A floor plan that never shows its plumbing or
  48|     // its plant reads as a set rather than a building.
  49|     (SpaceProgram::RestroomCore, 2),
  50|     (SpaceProgram::Storage, 2),
  51|     (SpaceProgram::ServerRoom, 1),
  52|     (SpaceProgram::Mechanical, 1),
  53| ];
  54| 
  55| /// Rounds the solver makes over the budget. Each round places at most one
  56| /// of each program, so a floor gets a mix before it gets a repeat.
  57| /// Two, not three. The corruption pass that runs after this one needs
  58| /// somewhere to put duplicated suites, abandoned expansions and red rooms;
  59| /// a solver that takes every good seat leaves it nothing, and a Backrooms
  60| /// region without corruption is just an office. Density is traded against
  61| /// that headroom deliberately.
  62| const ROUNDS: usize = 2;
  63| 
  64| /// Candidate anchors are tried at this pitch along a leg. Finer than a
  65| /// room is wide, so no viable seat falls between two samples.
  66| const ANCHOR_PITCH: f32 = 2.0;
  67| 
  68| /// How much of a leg's ends stay clear of rooms, so corners and junctions
  69| /// remain legible as circulation.
  70| const LEG_END_MARGIN: f32 = 4.0;
  71| 
  72| /// Clear distance required between two placed rooms.
  73| ///
  74| /// The suite builder only rejects overlap by 0.8 u, which was ample when a
  75| /// region held two rooms far apart. Packed against each other, neighbours
  76| /// interfere: a doorway samples through the strip between two shells, and a
  77| /// ceiling fixture lands inside the next room's wall. Rooms in a real plan
  78| /// either share a wall or stand clear of one another, and sharing is the
  79| /// connectivity graph's job, not the packer's.
  80| pub(super) const ROOM_SEPARATION: f32 = 3.2;
  81| 
  82| /// A horizontal run of corridor that rooms can hang off.
  83| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
  84| pub(super) struct Leg {
  85|     pub x0: f32,
  86|     pub x1: f32,
  87|     pub z: f32,
  88|     pub half_width: f32,
  89| }
  90| 
  91| /// Extracts the corridor runs rooms may attach to.
  92| ///
  93| /// Every spine contributes, not only the dominant one: a secondary hall
  94| /// with nothing on it is a corridor to nowhere, which is a liminal
  95| /// *feature* only when it is authored as one rather than left over.
  96| pub(super) fn legs_of(spines: &[CirculationSpine], min_length: f32) -> Vec<Leg> {
  97|     let mut legs = Vec::new();
  98|     for spine in spines {
  99|         for segment in spine.path.windows(2) {
 100|             // Horizontal runs only. Vertical legs need the suite builder to
 101|             // work on the other axis, which it does not yet -- see the
 102|             // module note in `mod.rs`.
 103|             if (segment[0].z - segment[1].z).abs() > 1e-4 {
 104|                 continue;
 105|             }
 106|             let (x0, x1) = (
 107|                 segment[0].x.min(segment[1].x),
 108|                 segment[0].x.max(segment[1].x),
 109|             );
 110|             if x1 - x0 < min_length {
 111|                 continue;
 112|             }
 113|             legs.push(Leg {
 114|                 x0,
 115|                 x1,
 116|                 z: segment[0].z,
 117|                 half_width: spine.width * 0.5,
 118|             });
 119|         }
 120|     }
 121|     legs
 122| }
 123| 
 124| /// Places rooms by scored greedy selection, returning them in commit order.
 125| ///
 126| /// `taken` is extended with every committed footprint, so callers that run
 127| /// later passes (corruption, stairs) see the same occupancy this did.
 128| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 129| pub(super) fn lay_out_suites(
 130|     seed_hash: &dyn Fn(i64) -> f32,
 131|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 132|     legs: &[Leg],
 133|     territories: &[Territory],
 134|     origin: Position,
 135|     region_size: f32,
 136|     wall_thickness: f32,
 137|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 138|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
 139|     next_id: &mut u32,
 140| ) -> Vec<AssemblyInstance> {
 141|     let mut placed: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
 142|     if legs.is_empty() {
 143|         return placed;
 144|     }
 145| 
 146|     let mut used = [0usize; PROGRAM_BUDGET.len()];
 147|     for round in 0..ROUNDS {
 148|         for (slot, (program, budget)) in PROGRAM_BUDGET.iter().enumerate() {
 149|             if used[slot] >= *budget {
 150|                 continue;
 151|             }
 152|             let salt = (slot * 64 + round) as i64;
 153|             let aseed = seed_hash(0x5EA0 + salt);
 154|             let threshold_seed = seed_hash(0x7A110 + salt);
 155| 
 156|             // Simulate every anchor on every leg, both sides, and keep the
 157|             // best-scoring one that the builder actually accepts.
 158|             let mut best: Option<(f32, AssemblyInstance)> = None;
 159|             for leg in legs {
 160|                 let mut x = leg.x0 + LEG_END_MARGIN;
 161|                 let mut anchor = 0u32;
 162|                 while x <= leg.x1 - LEG_END_MARGIN {
 163|                     // Size is part of the placement, not a per-program
 164|                     // constant. Drawing one width for the whole round meant
 165|                     // every candidate for a program was the same room in a
 166|                     // different spot: a region whose legs are all short then
 167|                     // rejected that program everywhere (one region in 81 came
 168|                     // out with no assemblies at all), and the scorer's area
 169|                     // term could never prefer anything, because there was
 170|                     // nothing to prefer between. Advancing the draw per
 171|                     // anchor by the golden-ratio conjugate spreads sizes
 172|                     // low-discrepancy across the leg at no extra cost -- the
 173|                     // same number of candidates, now spanning the program's
 174|                     // size range.
 175|                     let aseed = (aseed + 0.618_034 * anchor as f32).fract();
 176|                     anchor += 1;
 177|                     for side in [1.0f32, -1.0] {
 178|                         let Some(candidate) = place_suite(
 179|                             *next_id,
 180|                             *program,
 181|                             genome,
 182|                             aseed,
 183|                             threshold_seed,
 184|                             x,
 185|                             leg.z,
 186|                             leg.half_width + wall_thickness * 0.5,
 187|                             side,
 188|                             origin,
 189|                             region_size,
 190|                             taken,
 191|                             spines,
 192|                         ) else {
 193|                             continue;
 194|                         };
 195|                         // The whole front wall must face corridor, not just
 196|                         // the anchor. A room hung off the last few units of
 197|                         // a leg overhangs its end, and the part that
 198|                         // overhangs faces fabric -- so its entrance opens
 199|                         // into solid wall.
 200|                         //
 201|                         // Against the leg's own span, not the anchor margin.
 202|                         // The margin keeps rooms from *starting* on a
 203|                         // junction; demanding the far wall clear it too
 204|                         // costs a room 8 u of leg it does not need, and a
 205|                         // genome whose rooms run wide then fits nowhere at
 206|                         // all -- one region in 81 came out empty that way,
 207|                         // every candidate rejected here rather than for any
 208|                         // architectural reason. A room flush to the end of a
 209|                         // leg still faces corridor along its whole front,
 210|                         // which is the only thing this guards.
 211|                         let b = candidate.footprint.bounds();
 212|                         if b.0 < leg.x0 || b.2 > leg.x1 {
 213|                             continue;
 214|                         }
 215|                         // Every entrance must read as a door onto a route.
 216|                         if !candidate.entrances().all(|e| {
 217|                             entrance_faces_route(spines, e.center.x, e.center.z, wall_thickness)
 218|                         }) {
 219|                             continue;
 220|                         }
 221|                         if taken.iter().any(|t| {
 222|                             b.0 < t.2 + ROOM_SEPARATION
 223|                                 && t.0 < b.2 + ROOM_SEPARATION
 224|                                 && b.1 < t.3 + ROOM_SEPARATION
 225|                                 && t.1 < b.3 + ROOM_SEPARATION
 226|                         }) {
 227|                             continue;
 228|                         }
 229|                         let score = score_placement(
 230|                             candidate.footprint.bounds(),
 231|                             *program,
 232|                             territories,
 233|                             &placed,
 234|                         );
 235|                         if best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(b, _)| score > *b) {
 236|                             best = Some((score, candidate));
 237|                         }
 238|                     }
 239|                     x += ANCHOR_PITCH;
 240|                 }
 241|             }
 242| 
 243|             let Some((_, chosen)) = best else {
 244|                 // Nothing viable for this program in this round. Smaller
 245|                 // programs later in the round may still fit, so move on
 246|                 // rather than abandoning the pass.
 247|                 continue;
 248|             };
 249|             taken.push(chosen.footprint.bounds());
 250|             placed.push(chosen);
 251|             used[slot] += 1;
 252|             *next_id += 1;
 253|         }
 254|     }
 255| 
 256|     placed
 257| }
 258| 
 259| /// How good a seat is for a room, higher is better.
 260| ///
 261| /// The terms are the ones the office-planning study derived from real
 262| /// layouts: usable area, a habitable proportion, and separation from rooms
 263| /// of the same kind. Corridor adjacency needs no term -- every candidate is
 264| /// corridor-hosted by construction, which is what keeps the plan reachable.
 265| fn score_placement(
 266|     bounds: (f32, f32, f32, f32),
 267|     program: SpaceProgram,
 268|     territories: &[Territory],
 269|     placed: &[AssemblyInstance],
 270| ) -> f32 {
 271|     let (width, depth) = (bounds.2 - bounds.0, bounds.3 - bounds.1);
 272|     let center = ((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
 273| 
 274|     // Area, against what this program wants. Both too small and too large
 275|     // are penalized: a 400 m^2 private office is as wrong as a 6 m^2 one.
 276|     let area = width * depth;
 277|     let ideal = ideal_area(program);
 278|     let area_score = 1.0 - ((area - ideal) / ideal).abs().min(1.0);
 279| 
 280|     // Proportion. Rooms read as rooms between about 1:1 and 1:1.8; beyond
 281|     // that they read as corridors that failed to become corridors.
 282|     let aspect = width.max(depth) / width.min(depth).max(0.01);
 283|     let aspect_score = 1.0 - ((aspect - 1.4) / 1.4).abs().min(1.0);
 284| 
 285|     // Space used well: a seat inside a large free territory leaves that
 286|     // territory still usable, while one that half-covers a small territory
 287|     // strands the remainder as a sliver.
 288|     let host = territories
 289|         .iter()
 290|         .filter(|t| {
 291|             let (cx, cz) = t.center();
 292|             (cx - center.0).abs() < t.width() * 0.5 + width * 0.5
 293|                 && (cz - center.1).abs() < t.depth() * 0.5 + depth * 0.5
 294|         })
 295|         .map(|t| t.area())
 296|         .fold(0.0f32, f32::max);
 297|     let fit_score = if host > 0.0 {
 298|         (area / host).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 299|     } else {
 300|         0.35
 301|     };
 302| 
 303|     // Separation from the same program: five open offices in a row is a
 304|     // tiled floorplan, which is the failure mode this whole pass exists to
 305|     // avoid. Distance to the nearest same-program room, saturating at 24 u.
 306|     let separation = placed
 307|         .iter()
 308|         .filter(|other| other.program == program)
 309|         .map(|other| {
 310|             let b = other.footprint.bounds();
 311|             let c = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
 312|             (c.0 - center.0).hypot(c.1 - center.1)
 313|         })
 314|         .fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
 315|     let separation_score = if separation.is_finite() {
 316|         (separation / 24.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 317|     } else {
 318|         1.0
 319|     };
 320| 
 321|     0.30 * area_score + 0.25 * aspect_score + 0.20 * fit_score + 0.25 * separation_score
 322| }
 323| 
 324| /// Floor area each program is planned around, m^2. Drawn from ordinary
 325| /// commercial space standards rather than tuned: the point of the term is
 326| /// to stop a server room from taking the biggest bay on the floor.
 327| fn ideal_area(program: SpaceProgram) -> f32 {
 328|     match program {
 329|         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 220.0,
 330|         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 90.0,
 331|         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 70.0,
 332|         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 80.0,
 333|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 45.0,
 334|         SpaceProgram::Storage => 55.0,
 335|         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 60.0,
 336|         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 300.0,
 337|         SpaceProgram::Reception => 110.0,
 338|         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 40.0,
 339|         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 50.0,
 340|         _ => 100.0,
 341|     }
 342| }

layout.rs analysis:
- `lay_out_suites`: rounds (2) × programs (11) × legs (L) × anchors per leg (~leg length / 2.0, up to 80/2=40) × 2 sides. Each candidate:
  - `place_suite(...)` — need to check its cost (in suites.rs).
  - `entrance_faces_route(spines, ...)` — checks all entrances against all spine segments? Need to check.
  - `taken.iter().any(...)` — O(|taken|), taken grows up to ~20+ rooms, fine but still O(T) per candidate. Total candidates: 2 rounds × 11 programs × L legs × ~40 anchors × 2 sides. With L ~ 3-6 legs: 2×11×4×40×2 = 7,040 candidates, each O(T + entrance checks + score). `score_placement` iterates territories and placed: O(|territories| + |placed|). Territories maybe ~5-20. Placed ~10. So per candidate ~O(40). Total ~280k ops per region. Not terrible, but the `taken.iter().any()` per candidate and score per candidate make it O(candidates × (taken+territories+placed)) = roughly O(R²) in rooms. Medium.

The key line: 221-228 `taken.iter().any(...)` — O(|taken|) per candidate — that's the head-start finding. Confirm: `lay_out_suites` lines 221-228.

`place_suite` — need to look at suites.rs to see its cost, especially any loops over spines for entrance checks.

   9| fn ceiling_height_for(program: SpaceProgram, aseed: f32) -> f32 {
  10|     match program {
  11|         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 4.8 + 0.6 * aseed,
  12|         // Compression is a deliberate contrast, never the default ceiling.
  13|         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom | SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 2.6 + 0.2 * aseed,
  14|         SpaceProgram::Storage | SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 3.0 + 0.3 * aseed,
  15|         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 3.5 + 0.7 * aseed,
  16|         _ => 3.2 + 0.5 * aseed,
  17|     }
  18| }
  19| 
  20| /// Splits a room's flat ceiling into authored bands.
  21| ///
  22| /// One height across a whole room is a specification, not a design. Level 0
  23| /// is described by its *contrast* -- compression against expanse -- and the
  24| /// canon reads that way at room scale too: carpet runs deep under arches and
  25| /// shallow between pillars, ceilings drop and lift as you cross a space.
  26| ///
  27| /// The band is a deliberate violation of the room's own baseline, which is
  28| /// what makes it read as authored rather than noisy: the room states a
  29| /// height, then contradicts it once, across a strip you walk through. Two
  30| /// contradictions in one room would just be a bumpy ceiling.
  31| ///
  32| /// Which contradiction depends on the designer. A mechanical-heavy hand
  33| /// (`ExposedSoffit`) drops a soffit; anyone else lifts the band instead,
  34| /// because a raised centre is what an architect does with a room they are
  35| /// proud of. Rooms too small to carry a band keep their single zone -- a
  36| /// strip needs room on both sides or it is just a lower ceiling.
  37| fn ceiling_bands_for(
  38|     footprint: &Polygon2,
  39|     base: CeilingZone,
  40|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  41|     aseed: f32,
  42| ) -> CeilingPlan {
  43|     /// Fraction of rooms that get a band at all. Most ceilings stay flat,
  44|     /// so the ones that do not are events.
  45|     const BAND_SHARE: f32 = 0.45;
  46|     /// Shortest room side that can carry a band across it.
  47|     const MIN_SIDE: f32 = 8.0;
  48| 
  49|     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
  50|     let (width, depth) = (x1 - x0, z1 - z0);
  51|     if width.min(depth) < MIN_SIDE || keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA4D) > BAND_SHARE {
  52|         return CeilingPlan::flat(base);
  53|     }
  54| 
  55|     // The band crosses the room's *long* axis, so it is something you pass
  56|     // under rather than a lower corner you never visit.
  57|     let long_x = width >= depth;
  58|     let span = if long_x { width } else { depth };
  59|     let band_width = snap((span * (0.22 + 0.16 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA5E))).clamp(2.4, 9.6));
  60|     // Kept off the room's ends, so the band never merges with a wall.
  61|     let free = span - band_width - 2.0 * PLAN_WALL_T;
  62|     if free <= 0.0 {
  63|         return CeilingPlan::flat(base);
  64|     }
  65|     let offset = snap(PLAN_WALL_T + free * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA60));
  66| 
  67|     let (band_area, drop) = if long_x {
  68|         (Polygon2::rect(x0 + offset, z0, band_width, depth), true)
  69|     } else {
  70|         (Polygon2::rect(x0, z0 + offset, width, band_width), true)
  71|     };
  72|     let _ = drop;
  73| 
  74|     let compress = genome.ceiling_language == CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit;
  75|     let height = if compress {
  76|         // Never below head height plus a margin; a soffit you cannot walk
  77|         // under is a wall.
  78|         (base.height_units - 0.8 - 0.4 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA61)).max(2.4)
  79|     } else {
  80|         base.height_units + 0.6 + 0.8 * keyed_unit(aseed, 0xBA61)
  81|     };
  82| 
  83|     CeilingPlan::banded(
  84|         base,
  85|         vec![CeilingZone {
  86|             area: band_area,
  87|             language: if compress {
  88|                 CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit
  89|             } else {
  90|                 CeilingLanguage::Coffered
  91|             },
  92|             height_units: height,
  93|         }],
  94|     )
  95| }

  97| fn structure_for(genome: &ArchitectGenome, aseed: f32) -> StructuralSystemInstance {
  98|     let bay = snap(4.4 + 1.6 * aseed);
  99|     let (bay_x, bay_z) = match genome.structural_system {
 100|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => (bay * 1.5, bay),
 101|         _ => (bay, bay),
 102|     };
 103|     // A designer with no tolerance for asymmetry (1) centers the column
 104|     // grid on the footprint instead of letting it fall wherever an offset
 105|     // phase lands; one with none of that tolerance (0) keeps today's
 106|     // freely offset grid.
 107|     let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 108|     let phase = (
 109|         snap(aseed * 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
 110|         snap(aseed * 8.0 % 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
 111|     );
 112|     StructuralSystemInstance {
 113|         system: genome.structural_system,
 114|         bay_x,
 115|         bay_z,
 116|         phase,
 117|         column_side: 0.4,
 118|     }
 119| }

 121| /// Fixtures for a rectangular footprint in the genome's lighting language.
 122| fn fixtures_for(
 123|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 124|     footprint: &Polygon2,
 125|     lit: bool,
 126|     aseed: f32,
 127| ) -> Vec<Fixture> {
 128|     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
 129|     let mut out = Vec::new();
 130|     match genome.lighting_language {
 131|         LightingLanguage::GridPanels => {
 132|             let step = 2.4;
 133|             let mut z = z0 + 1.2;
 134|             while z < z1 - 0.8 {
 135|                 let mut x = x0 + 1.2;
 136|                 while x < x1 - 0.8 {
 137|                     out.push(Fixture {
 138|                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(z)),
 139|                         half_x: 0.4,
 140|                         half_z: 0.4,
 141|                         lit,
 142|                     });
 143|                     x += step;
 144|                 }
 145|                 z += step;
 146|             }
 147|         }
 148|         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation => {
 149|             // Strips run down the room's long axis.
 150|             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
 151|             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
 152|             let step = 3.2;
 153|             if long_x {
 154|                 let mut x = x0 + 1.6;
 155|                 while x < x1 - 1.2 {
 156|                     out.push(Fixture {
 157|                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(cz)),
 158|                         half_x: 1.0,
 159|                         half_z: 0.25,
 160|                         lit,
 161|                     });
 162|                     x += step;
 163|                 }
 164|             } else {
 165|                 let mut z = z0 + 1.6;
 166|                 while z < z1 - 1.2 {
 167|                     out.push(Fixture {
 168|                         at: Position::new(snap(cx), snap(z)),
 169|                         half_x: 0.25,
 170|                         half_z: 1.0,
 171|                         lit,
 172|                     });
 173|                     z += step;
 174|                 }
 175|             }
 176|         }
 177|         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants => {
 178|             let n = 1 + (aseed * 2.0) as i32;
 179|             // A designer with high tolerance for symmetry mirrors and
 180|             // centers pendants along the room's long axis instead of
 181|             // scattering them by golden-ratio jitter; `tol` blends between
 182|             // the two rather than switching sharply between them.
 183|             let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 184|             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
 185|             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
 186|             for k in 0..n {
 187|                 let jx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.618 + aseed) % 1.0));
 188|                 let jz = z0 + (z1 - z0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.382 + aseed * 2.0) % 1.0));
 189|                 let centered = if n > 1 {
 190|                     k as f32 / (n - 1) as f32 - 0.5
 191|                 } else {
 192|                     0.0
 193|                 };
 194|                 let (sx, sz) = if long_x {
 195|                     (cx + centered * (x1 - x0) * 0.6, cz)
 196|                 } else {
 197|                     (cx, cz + centered * (z1 - z0) * 0.6)
 198|                 };
 199|                 let fx = jx + (sx - jx) * tol;
 200|                 let fz = jz + (sz - jz) * tol;
 201|                 out.push(Fixture {
 202|                     at: Position::new(snap(fx), snap(fz)),
 203|                     half_x: 0.3,
 204|                     half_z: 0.3,
 205|                     lit,
 206|                 });
 207|             }
 208|         }
 209|     }
 210|     out
 211| }

 213| /// Recursively divide a program envelope along its dominant axis. This is a
 214| /// small shape grammar, not a random room packer: every child remains inside
 215| /// its parent, split planes snap to the plan lattice, and stable path keys
 216| /// make the result independent of traversal, chunks, and voxel resolution.
 217| #[derive(Default)]
 218| struct SpaceLayout {
 219|     spaces: Vec<Space>,
 220|     partitions: Vec<(Position, Position)>,
 221| }
 222| 
 223| #[cfg(test)]
 224| fn spaces_for(
 225|     program: SpaceProgram,
 226|     footprint: &Polygon2,
 227|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 228|     aseed: f32,
 229| ) -> Vec<Space> {
 230|     space_layout_for(program, footprint, genome, aseed).spaces
 231| }
 232| 
 233| fn space_layout_for(
 234|     program: SpaceProgram,
 235|     footprint: &Polygon2,
 236|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 237|     aseed: f32,
 238| ) -> SpaceLayout {
 239|     if !matches!(
 240|         program,
 241|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice | SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom
 242|     ) {
 243|         return SpaceLayout::default();
 244|     }
 245|     let split_threshold = (1.0 - genome.partition_density).clamp(0.05, 0.95);
 246|     if aseed <= split_threshold {
 247|         return SpaceLayout::default();
 248|     }
 249| 
 250|     let rule = SubdivisionRule {
 251|         target_side: (genome.room_proportions.min_side * 0.42).clamp(4.0, 7.2),
 252|         max_depth: 1 + (genome.partition_density.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.5) as u8,
 253|         seed: aseed,
 254|     };
 255|     let mut leaves = Vec::new();
 256|     let mut partitions = Vec::new();
 257|     subdivide_space(
 258|         footprint.bounds(),
 259|         0,
 260|         1,
 261|         &rule,
 262|         &mut leaves,
 263|         &mut partitions,
 264|     );
 265|     if leaves.len() <= 1 {
 266|         return SpaceLayout::default();
 267|     }
 268|     SpaceLayout {
 269|         spaces: leaves
 270|             .into_iter()
 271|             .map(|(x0, z0, x1, z1)| Space {
 272|                 program,
 273|                 footprint: Polygon2::rect(x0, z0, x1 - x0, z1 - z0),
 274|             })
 275|             .collect(),
 276|         partitions,
 277|     }
 278| }
 279| 
 280| struct SubdivisionRule {
 281|     target_side: f32,
 282|     max_depth: u8,
 283|     seed: f32,
 284| }
 285| 
 286| fn subdivide_space(
 287|     bounds: (f32, f32, f32, f32),
 288|     depth: u8,
 289|     path: u32,
 290|     rule: &SubdivisionRule,
 291|     leaves: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
 292|     partitions: &mut Vec<(Position, Position)>,
 293| ) {
 294|     let width = bounds.2 - bounds.0;
 295|     let depth_units = bounds.3 - bounds.1;
 296|     let split_x = width >= depth_units;
 297|     let span = if split_x { width } else { depth_units };
 298|     if depth >= rule.max_depth || span < rule.target_side * 2.05 {
 299|         leaves.push(bounds);
 300|         return;
 301|     }
 302| 
 303|     let jitter = keyed_unit(rule.seed, path) - 0.5;
 304|     let split = (span * (0.5 + jitter * 0.16) / 0.4).round() * 0.4;
 305|     if split < rule.target_side || span - split < rule.target_side {
 306|         leaves.push(bounds);
 307|         return;
 308|     }
 309|     let (a, b) = if split_x {
 310|         let plane = bounds.0 + split;
 311|         partitions.push((
 312|             Position::new(plane, bounds.1),
 313|             Position::new(plane, bounds.3),
 314|         ));
 315|         (
 316|             (bounds.0, bounds.1, plane, bounds.3),
 317|             (plane, bounds.1, bounds.2, bounds.3),
 318|         )
 319|     } else {
 320|         let plane = bounds.1 + split;
 321|         partitions.push((
 322|             Position::new(bounds.0, plane),
 323|             Position::new(bounds.2, plane),
 324|         ));
 325|         (
 326|             (bounds.0, bounds.1, bounds.2, plane),
 327|             (bounds.0, plane, bounds.2, bounds.3),
 328|         )
 329|     };
 330|     subdivide_space(a, depth + 1, path << 1, rule, leaves, partitions);
 331|     subdivide_space(b, depth + 1, path << 1 | 1, rule, leaves, partitions);
 332| }
 333| 
 334| fn keyed_unit(seed: f32, key: u32) -> f32 {
 335|     let mut value = seed.to_bits() ^ key.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9);
 336|     value ^= value >> 16;
 337|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
 338|     value ^= value >> 13;
 339|     (value >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
 340| }
 341| 
 342| /// Whether an interior partition would run into an opening and seal it.
 343| ///
 344| /// Subdivision and the openings are derived independently, so nothing stops
 345| /// a partition plane from landing on a doorway: the opening is cut
 346| /// correctly and then a wall is built across it, perpendicular, from the
 347| /// inside. The room reads as walled shut and the plan's whole reachability
 348| /// argument fails at its first step. Observed as soon as rooms are placed
 349| /// densely: entrance on HostId(0) at x=11.20 with a Partition at x=11.20
 350| /// running through it.
 351| fn blocks_opening(start: Position, end: Position, opening: &Opening) -> bool {
 352|     let partition_is_horizontal = (start.z - end.z).abs() <= 1e-4;
 353|     // `through_x_wall` means you walk through it along Z, so the opening
 354|     // sits on a wall parallel to X and its clear span runs along X. A
 355|     // partition threatens it only when it runs the other way.
 356|     if partition_is_horizontal == opening.through_x_wall {
 357|         return false;
 358|     }
 359|     let (plane, along) = if partition_is_horizontal {
 360|         (start.z, opening.center.z)
 361|     } else {
 362|         (start.x, opening.center.x)
 363|     };
 364|     if (plane - along).abs() >= opening.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T {
 365|         return false;
 366|     }
 367|     // The plane alone is not enough: the partition must actually reach the
 368|     // opening's wall to seal it. One on the far side of the room merely
 369|     // sharing a coordinate with the doorway is not in its way.
 370|     let (near, far, wall) = if partition_is_horizontal {
 371|         (start.x.min(end.x), start.x.max(end.x), opening.center.x)
 372|     } else {
 373|         (start.z.min(end.z), start.z.max(end.z), opening.center.z)
 374|     };
 375|     near - PLAN_WALL_T <= wall && wall <= far + PLAN_WALL_T
 376| }
 377| 
 378| /// Lower a suite's room subdivision into explicit wall hosts and hosted
 379| /// openings. The recursive/automata layer can rewrite these elements later;
 380| /// voxel sampling no longer has to rediscover partitions from rectangles.
 381| fn hosts_and_openings_for(
 382|     footprint: &Polygon2,
 383|     partition_segments: &[(Position, Position)],
 384|     ceiling_units: f32,
 385|     entrance: Opening,
 386|     partition_density: f32,
 387|     grammar_seed: f32,
 388| ) -> (Vec<HostSegment>, Vec<Opening>) {
 389|     let mut hosts = HostSegment::rectangular_shell(footprint, PLAN_WALL_T, ceiling_units);
 390|     let mut openings = vec![entrance];
 391| 
 392|     // A short totalistic cellular automaton acts as a renovation/demolition
 393|     // pass over the partition graph. It can merge neighboring program cells,
 394|     // but never touches the shell and never creates an unpierced retained
 395|     // partition, so topology stays legible and walkable.
 396|     let retained = evolve_partitions(partition_segments, partition_density, grammar_seed);
 397|     for (&(start, end), retain) in partition_segments.iter().zip(retained) {
 398|         // Checked against every opening accepted so far, not just the
 399|         // entrance: two partitions can collide with each other's doorways
 400|         // exactly as one can collide with the shell's.

 401|         if retain && !openings.iter().any(|o| blocks_opening(start, end, o)) {
 402|             let host_id = HostId(hosts.len() as u32);
 403|             let horizontal = (start.z - end.z).abs() <= 1e-4;
 404|             let center = Position::new((start.x + end.x) * 0.5, (start.z + end.z) * 0.5);
 405|             hosts.push(HostSegment {
 406|                 id: host_id,
 407|                 start,
 408|                 end,
 409|                 thickness: PLAN_WALL_T,
 410|                 base_units: 0.0,
 411|                 top_units: ceiling_units,
 412|                 role: HostRole::Partition,
 413|             });
 414|             openings.push(Opening {
 415|                 id: OpeningId(openings.len() as u32),
 416|                 host: host_id,
 417|                 role: OpeningRole::Interior,
 418|                 center,
 419|                 width: super::DOOR_WIDTH,
 420|                 through_x_wall: horizontal,
 421|                 lintel_units: Some(super::DOOR_HEIGHT),
 422|             });
 423|         }
 424|     }
 425|     (hosts, openings)
 426| }
 427| 
 428| fn point_on_segment(point: Position, segment: (Position, Position)) -> bool {
 429|     const EPSILON: f32 = 1e-4;
 430|     if (segment.0.z - segment.1.z).abs() <= EPSILON {
 431|         (point.z - segment.0.z).abs() <= EPSILON
 432|             && point.x >= segment.0.x.min(segment.1.x) - EPSILON
 433|             && point.x <= segment.0.x.max(segment.1.x) + EPSILON
 434|     } else {
 435|         (point.x - segment.0.x).abs() <= EPSILON
 436|             && point.z >= segment.0.z.min(segment.1.z) - EPSILON
 437|             && point.z <= segment.0.z.max(segment.1.z) + EPSILON
 438|     }
 439| }
 440| 
 441| fn segments_touch(a: (Position, Position), b: (Position, Position)) -> bool {
 442|     point_on_segment(a.0, b)
 443|         || point_on_segment(a.1, b)
 444|         || point_on_segment(b.0, a)
 445|         || point_on_segment(b.1, a)
 446| }
 447| 
 448| fn evolve_partitions(segments: &[(Position, Position)], density: f32, seed: f32) -> Vec<bool> {
 449|     if segments.is_empty() {
 450|         return Vec::new();
 451|     }
 452|     let survival = (0.25 + density.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 0.75).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 453|     let mut state: Vec<bool> = segments
 454|         .iter()
 455|         .enumerate()
 456|         .map(|(index, _)| keyed_unit(seed, index as u32 ^ 0xA170) < survival)
 457|         .collect();
 458|     for _ in 0..2 {
 459|         state = segments
 460|             .iter()
 461|             .enumerate()
 462|             .map(|(index, segment)| {
 463|                 let neighbours = segments
 464|                     .iter()
 465|                     .enumerate()
 466|                     .filter(|(other_index, other)| {
 467|                         *other_index != index && segments_touch(*segment, **other)
 468|                     })
 469|                     .filter(|(other_index, _)| state[*other_index])
 470|                     .count();
 471|                 if state[index] {
 472|                     neighbours <= 3
 473|                 } else {
 474|                     neighbours == 2
 475|                 }
 476|             })
 477|             .collect();
 478|     }
 479|     if !state.iter().any(|retained| *retained) {
 480|         let fallback = (keyed_unit(seed, 0xFA11) * segments.len() as f32) as usize;
 481|         state[fallback.min(segments.len() - 1)] = true;
 482|     }
 483|     state
 484| }
 485| 
 486| pub(super) fn aabb_overlap(a: (f32, f32, f32, f32), b: (f32, f32, f32, f32), gap: f32) -> bool {
 487|     a.0 < b.2 + gap && b.0 < a.2 + gap && a.1 < b.3 + gap && b.1 < a.3 + gap
 488| }
 489| 
 490| /// Does an opening at `(x, z)` read as a door onto a route?
 491| ///
 492| /// Two conditions, and the second is the one that is easy to miss: the
 493| /// opening must sit in *some* corridor's wall band -- outside the clear
 494| /// width, inside the band beyond it -- and inside *no* corridor's clear
 495| /// width. Corridors cross, so an entrance correctly banded against the run
 496| /// its room hangs off can still sit squarely inside a perpendicular one.
 497| /// There, `compose_column` takes the circulation branch before it ever
 498| /// reaches the assembly: the column is carved full height and the doorway
 499| /// loses the lintel that makes it read as a door rather than a gap.
 500| ///
 501| /// Checking only "is banded against some corridor" is what let that
 502| /// through; both callers that place doors need the same answer, so they
 503| /// share this one.
 504| pub(super) fn entrance_faces_route(
 505|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 506|     x: f32,
 507|     z: f32,
 508|     wall_thickness: f32,
 509| ) -> bool {
 510|     let mut banded = false;
 511|     for spine in spines {
 512|         let d = spine.distance(x, z);
 513|         let half = spine.width * 0.5;
 514|         // Matches `compose_column`'s own test for "this column belongs to
 515|         // circulation", so the two can never disagree about a threshold.
 516|         if d <= half {
 517|             return false;
 518|         }
 519|         if d <= half + wall_thickness + 0.05 {
 520|             banded = true;
 521|         }
 522|     }
 523|     banded
 524| }
 525| 
 526| /// Places one suite beside a horizontal corridor segment. Returns `None` if
 527| /// the footprint would leave the region, collide with a prior assembly, or
 528| /// cross another corridor.
 529| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 530| pub(super) fn place_suite(
 531|     id: u32,
 532|     program: SpaceProgram,
 533|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 534|     aseed: f32,
 535|     threshold_seed: f32,
 536|     cursor_x: f32,
 537|     corridor_z: f32,
 538|     corridor_half: f32,
 539|     side: f32, // +1 = suite on +Z side of corridor, -1 = -Z side
 540|     origin: Position,
 541|     size: f32,
 542|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 543|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 544| ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
 545|     let p = &genome.room_proportions;
 546|     let w = snap((p.min_side + (p.max_side - p.min_side) * aseed).clamp(12.0, 24.0));
 547|     let d = snap((w * (0.72 - 0.28 * p.elongation)).clamp(8.0, 18.0));
 548| 
 549|     let x0 = snap(cursor_x);
 550|     // Wall centerlines may occupy the half-step of the 0.4-unit plan lattice:
 551|     // coarse voxel centers live there too. Snapping this midpoint back to a
 552|     // full step can move the shell outside the corridor wall it is hosting.
 553|     let z_front = if side > 0.0 {
 554|         corridor_z + corridor_half
 555|     } else {
 556|         corridor_z - corridor_half - d
 557|     };
 558|     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, w, d);
 559|     let b = footprint.bounds();
 560| 
 561|     // Stay inside the region with margin.
 562|     if b.0 < origin.x + EDGE_MARGIN
 563|         || b.1 < origin.z + EDGE_MARGIN
 564|         || b.2 > origin.x + size - EDGE_MARGIN
 565|         || b.3 > origin.z + size - EDGE_MARGIN
 566|     {
 567|         return None;
 568|     }
 569|     if taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.8)) {
 570|         return None;
 571|     }
 572|     // Don't let a suite swallow a *different* corridor (its front corridor
 573|     // touching the footprint edge is fine and expected).
 574|     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
 575|     for s in spines {
 576|         if s.distance(center.0, center.1) < s.width * 0.5 + d.min(w) * 0.25 {
 577|             return None;
 578|         }
 579|     }
 580| 
 581|     // Entrance on the corridor-facing wall. The genome biases the language,
 582|     // but a narrow framed door is only about 8--14% of thresholds globally.
 583|     // Most fronts dissolve into a room through an unframed or broad portal.
 584|     let threshold = match genome.threshold_language {
 585|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.14 => {
 586|             ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel
 587|         }
 588|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.08 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
 589|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
 590|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.62 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
 591|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
 592|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
 593|         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
 594|     };
 595|     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
 596|     let (width, lintel) = match threshold {
 597|         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel => (super::DOOR_WIDTH, Some(super::DOOR_HEIGHT)),
 598|         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal => (4.8, None),
 599|         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal => (3.6, Some(3.0)),
 600|     };
 601|     let edge = width * 0.5 + 0.8;
 602|     let door_x = snap((b.0 + w * (0.25 + 0.5 * threshold_seed)).clamp(b.0 + edge, b.2 - edge));
 603|     let ceiling = CeilingZone {
 604|         area: footprint.clone(),
 605|         language: genome.ceiling_language,
 606|         height_units: ceiling_height_for(program, aseed),
 607|     };
 608|     let layout = space_layout_for(program, &footprint, genome, aseed);
 609|     let entrance = Opening {
 610|         id: OpeningId(0),
 611|         host: if side > 0.0 { HostId(0) } else { HostId(2) },
 612|         role: OpeningRole::Entrance,
 613|         center: Position::new(door_x, front_z),
 614|         width,
 615|         through_x_wall: true,
 616|         lintel_units: lintel,
 617|     };
 618|     let door_leaves = if threshold == ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel {
 619|         vec![DoorLeaf {
 620|             opening: entrance.id,
 621|         }]
 622|     } else {
 623|         Vec::new()
 624|     };
 625|     let (hosts, openings) = hosts_and_openings_for(
 626|         &footprint,
 627|         &layout.partitions,
 628|         ceiling.height_units,
 629|         entrance,
 630|         genome.partition_density,
 631|         aseed,
 632|     );
 633|     Some(AssemblyInstance {
 634|         id,
 635|         program,
 636|         spaces: layout.spaces,
 637|         structure: structure_for(genome, aseed),
 638|         ceiling: ceiling_bands_for(&footprint, ceiling, genome, aseed),
 639|         fixtures: fixtures_for(genome, &footprint, true, aseed),
 640|         service_voids: Vec::new(),
 641|         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
 642|         hosts,
 643|         openings,
 644|         door_leaves,
 645|         footprint,
 646|     })
 647| }

 823|     /// A ceiling band is an authored contradiction of the room's own stated
 824|     /// height, and has to stay walkable and inside the room to be one.
 825|     #[test]
 826|     fn ceiling_bands_contradict_the_baseline_without_leaving_the_room() {
 827|         let footprint = Polygon2::rect(10.0, 20.0, 18.0, 14.0);
 828|         let base = CeilingZone {
 829|             area: footprint.clone(),
 830|             language: CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
 831|             height_units: 3.6,
 832|         };
 833|         let mut banded = 0;
 834|         for step in 0..64 {
 835|             let aseed = step as f32 / 64.0;
 836|             for language in [
 837|                 CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
 838|                 CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
 839|                 CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
 840|             ] {
 841|                 let mut genome = genome_with(0.5, 0.5);
 842|                 genome.ceiling_language = language;
 843|                 let plan = ceiling_bands_for(&footprint, base.clone(), &genome, aseed);
 844|                 let zones: Vec<&CeilingZone> = plan.zones().collect();
 845|                 assert!(zones.len() <= 2, "one contradiction per room, not several");
 846|                 assert_eq!(zones[0].height_units, base.height_units, "baseline kept");
 847|                 let Some(band) = zones.get(1) else { continue };
 848|                 banded += 1;
 849|                 assert_ne!(
 850|                     band.height_units, base.height_units,
 851|                     "a band at the baseline height contradicts nothing"
 852|                 );
 853|                 assert!(band.height_units >= 2.4, "a soffit must stay walkable");
 854|                 let (bx0, bz0, bx1, bz1) = band.area.bounds();
 855|                 let (fx0, fz0, fx1, fz1) = footprint.bounds();
 856|                 assert!(
 857|                     bx0 >= fx0 - 1e-3
 858|                         && bz0 >= fz0 - 1e-3
 859|                         && bx1 <= fx1 + 1e-3
 860|                         && bz1 <= fz1 + 1e-3,
 861|                     "band {:?} escapes the room",
 862|                     band.area.bounds()
 863|                 );
 864|                 // The soffit designer compresses; everyone else lifts.
 865|                 if language == CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit {
 866|                     assert!(band.height_units < base.height_units);
 867|                 } else {
 868|                     assert!(band.height_units > base.height_units);
 869|                 }
 870|             }
 871|         }
 872|         assert!(banded > 0, "sanity: some rooms must actually get a band");
 873|     }

suites.rs analysis:
- `place_suite` cost per candidate: 
  - `taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(...))` — O(|taken|)
  - `for s in spines { s.distance(center) }` — O(|spines|). What is `spine.distance` cost? It's in domain entities — likely O(segments). Need to check the domain entities for CirculationSpine::distance. Let me check that.
  - `space_layout_for` → `subdivide_space` — O(leaves) small.
  - `hosts_and_openings_for` → `evolve_partitions` — for each of the 2 automaton steps, iterates segments × segments for `segments_touch` — O(P²) where P = partitions (small, ~2-8). Fine.
  - `fixtures_for` — O(area/step²), e.g. room 24×18 → 10×7 = 70 fixtures. Fine.
- In `lay_out_suites`, per candidate: place_suite (O(T + S + small)), entrance_faces_route for each entrance (O(entrances × S)), taken.any (O(T)), score_placement (O(territories + placed)). Total candidates C ≈ ROUNDS × 11 × legs × anchors(≤ 40) × 2. So per region ~O(22 × L × 40 × 2 × (T + S + P)) — with small constants. It's quadratic-ish in L × T but with small numbers. The head-start finding says "rounds x program x legs x anchors x sides candidates, each checked vs taken.iter().any() O(|taken|)". That's confirmed at layout.rs:147-241, with the taken.iter().any at 221-228 and place_suite's own taken check at suites.rs:569.

Also `entrance_faces_route` at suites.rs:504-524 — called at layout.rs:216-218. It's O(spines) per entrance.

Note in `lay_out_suites`, the per-leg anchor loop starts at `leg.x0 + LEG_END_MARGIN` and increments by ANCHOR_PITCH (2.0) → up to ~36 anchors per leg. Each candidate calls `place_suite` which constructs a full AssemblyInstance (hosts, openings, fixtures...) — allocation-heavy for rejected candidates but that's constant factor.

An important note: `lay_out_suites` is called with `&mut taken` and `&mut id`, and `place_suite` receives `*next_id` — id not incremented for rejected candidates, fine.

Big-O: candidates = ROUNDS × 11 × Σ_legs (len/2 - margins) × 2 ≈ 22 × L × A × 2 where A ≈ 36, L ≈ 2-6 → ~3k-9k candidates; each O(T + S + E + P) with T up to ~25, S ~ 3-8 segments, E entrances ≤ 3. So ~O(10^5) per region plan — fine in absolute terms but it's O(C × T) which grows quadratically with rooms placed: T grows by 1 per placed room; total = Σ over candidates of T ≈ C × T_avg ≈ 7k × 12 ≈ 84k overlap checks per region. Per block: 324 regions × 84k ≈ 27M — hmm, that's meaningful but not crazy. It's a Medium finding: use a spatial grid or interval structure for `taken`.

   1| //! Free-space decomposition: what is left of a region once circulation and
   2| //! already-committed masses are removed.
   3| //!
   4| //! Room placement needs somewhere to place rooms. The old cursor walk did
   5| //! without this by sliding along a corridor leg and trying one spot at a
   6| //! time, which is why a region ended up with two suites and 90% unplanned
   7| //! fabric: a spot that failed was simply skipped, and space away from the
   8| //! dominant leg was never considered at all.
   9| //!
  10| //! This produces the candidate set the placement solver scores over:
  11| //! maximal free rectangles, biggest first, each carved out of the free area
  12| //! before the next is found. Rectangles rather than arbitrary polygons
  13| //! because rooms in this building are rectangular, and a candidate that
  14| //! cannot host a room is not a useful candidate.
  15| 
  16| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::CirculationSpine;
  17| 
  18| /// Free-space lattice pitch. Two coarse voxels: fine enough that a wall
  19| /// band cannot hide between samples, coarse enough that a region is a
  20| /// 100x100 grid rather than a 200x200 one.
  21| const CELL: f32 = 0.8;
  22| 
  23| /// Smallest side a territory may have and still be offered as a candidate.
  24| /// Below a corridor's width there is nothing a room could occupy.
  25| const MIN_SIDE: f32 = 3.2;
  26| 
  27| /// An axis-aligned patch of unoccupied region floor, in world units.
  28| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
  29| pub struct Territory {
  30|     pub min_x: f32,
  31|     pub min_z: f32,
  32|     pub max_x: f32,
  33|     pub max_z: f32,
  34| }
  35| 
  36| impl Territory {
  37|     pub fn width(&self) -> f32 {
  38|         self.max_x - self.min_x
  39|     }
  40| 
  41|     pub fn depth(&self) -> f32 {
  42|         self.max_z - self.min_z
  43|     }
  44| 
  45|     pub fn area(&self) -> f32 {
  46|         self.width() * self.depth()
  47|     }
  48| 
  49|     pub fn center(&self) -> (f32, f32) {
  50|         (
  51|             (self.min_x + self.max_x) * 0.5,
  52|             (self.min_z + self.max_z) * 0.5,
  53|         )
  54|     }
  55| 
  56|     /// Only the overlap assertions need a territory as a raw tuple; the
  57|     /// solver scores territories through `center`/`width`/`depth`.
  58|     #[cfg(test)]
  59|     pub fn bounds(&self) -> (f32, f32, f32, f32) {
  60|         (self.min_x, self.min_z, self.max_x, self.max_z)
  61|     }
  62| 
  63|     fn overlaps(&self, other: &(f32, f32, f32, f32)) -> bool {
  64|         self.min_x < other.2 && other.0 < self.max_x && self.min_z < other.3 && other.1 < self.max_z
  65|     }
  66| }
  67| 
  68| /// Decomposes the region's unoccupied floor into candidate territories,
  69| /// largest first.
  70| ///
  71| /// Pure in its inputs, so two chunks asking about the same region get the
  72| /// same answer without coordinating -- the same discipline the rest of the
  73| /// planner keeps.
  74| pub fn free_territories(
  75|     origin_x: f32,
  76|     origin_z: f32,
  77|     region_size: f32,
  78|     corridors: &[CirculationSpine],
  79|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
  80|     edge_margin: f32,
  81|     wall_thickness: f32,
  82| ) -> Vec<Territory> {
  83|     let usable = region_size - 2.0 * edge_margin;
  84|     if usable <= MIN_SIDE {
  85|         return Vec::new();
  86|     }
  87|     let n = (usable / CELL).floor() as usize;
  88|     if n == 0 {
  89|         return Vec::new();
  90|     }
  91|     let base_x = origin_x + edge_margin;
  92|     let base_z = origin_z + edge_margin;
  93| 
  94|     // A cell is free when its centre clears every corridor by half a width
  95|     // plus a wall, and falls in no committed footprint. Corridors are kept
  96|     // clear rather than merely un-overlapped: a room flush against a
  97|     // corridor edge has no wall between it and the route.
  98|     let mut free = vec![true; n * n];
  99|     for iz in 0..n {
 100|         for ix in 0..n {
 101|             let x = base_x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * CELL;
 102|             let z = base_z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * CELL;
 103|             let blocked = corridors
 104|                 .iter()
 105|                 .any(|s| s.distance(x, z) < s.width * 0.5 + wall_thickness)
 106|                 || taken
 107|                     .iter()
 108|                     .any(|b| x >= b.0 && x <= b.2 && z >= b.1 && z <= b.3);
 109|             free[iz * n + ix] = !blocked;
 110|         }
 111|     }
 112| 
 113|     let min_cells = (MIN_SIDE / CELL).ceil() as usize;
 114|     let mut out = Vec::new();
 115|     // Repeatedly take the largest all-free rectangle and remove it. Greedy
 116|     // maximal-rectangle carving, not an exact partition: the aim is a good
 117|     // candidate set for scoring, and the scorer is free to use only part of
 118|     // whatever it is offered.
 119|     while let Some(rect) = largest_free_rectangle(&free, n, min_cells) {
 120|         let (ix0, iz0, ix1, iz1) = rect;
 121|         for iz in iz0..=iz1 {
 122|             for ix in ix0..=ix1 {
 123|                 free[iz * n + ix] = false;
 124|             }
 125|         }
 126|         let territory = Territory {
 127|             min_x: base_x + ix0 as f32 * CELL,
 128|             min_z: base_z + iz0 as f32 * CELL,
 129|             max_x: base_x + (ix1 + 1) as f32 * CELL,
 130|             max_z: base_z + (iz1 + 1) as f32 * CELL,
 131|         };
 132|         if taken.iter().any(|b| territory.overlaps(b)) {
 133|             continue;
 134|         }
 135|         out.push(territory);
 136|         if out.len() >= 64 {
 137|             break;
 138|         }
 139|     }
 140|     out
 141| }
 142| 
 143| /// Largest all-free axis-aligned rectangle in the mask, as inclusive cell
 144| /// indices. Classic largest-rectangle-in-histogram swept down the rows:
 145| /// O(n^2) for the whole grid rather than the O(n^4) of testing every
 146| /// rectangle.
 147| fn largest_free_rectangle(
 148|     free: &[bool],
 149|     n: usize,
 150|     min_cells: usize,
 151| ) -> Option<(usize, usize, usize, usize)> {
 152|     let mut heights = vec![0usize; n];
 153|     let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, usize, usize, usize)> = None; // + area
 154| 
 155|     for iz in 0..n {
 156|         for ix in 0..n {
 157|             heights[ix] = if free[iz * n + ix] {
 158|                 heights[ix] + 1
 159|             } else {
 160|                 0
 161|             };
 162|         }
 163|         // Monotonic stack over this row's histogram.
 164|         let mut stack: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // (start index, height)
 165|         for ix in 0..=n {
 166|             let height = if ix == n { 0 } else { heights[ix] };
 167|             let mut start = ix;
 168|             while let Some(&(top_start, top_height)) = stack.last() {
 169|                 if top_height <= height {
 170|                     break;
 171|                 }
 172|                 stack.pop();
 173|                 let width = ix - top_start;
 174|                 let area = width * top_height;
 175|                 if width >= min_cells
 176|                     && top_height >= min_cells
 177|                     && best.is_none_or(|(_, _, _, _, b)| area > b)
 178|                 {
 179|                     best = Some((top_start, iz + 1 - top_height, ix - 1, iz, area));
 180|                 }
 181|                 start = top_start;
 182|             }
 183|             if ix < n {
 184|                 stack.push((start, height));
 185|             }
 186|         }
 187|     }
 188| 
 189|     best.map(|(x0, z0, x1, z1, _)| (x0, z0, x1, z1))
 190| }

territories.rs analysis:
- `free_territories`: builds n×n grid (n = (80-6.4)/0.8 ≈ 92). For each cell: `corridors.iter().any(|s| s.distance(x,z) < ...)` — O(n² × S × distance_cost). `spine.distance` — need to check its cost; if it's O(path segments), then total O(n² × S × segs). n=92 → 8464 cells × S(~3) × segs(~10-20) — ~500k ops. OK.
- `while let Some(rect) = largest_free_rectangle(...)` — each call is O(n²) with the histogram sweep (O(n²) — actually O(n²) per sweep: n rows × n columns with monotonic stack O(n) per row → O(n²) per call). The loop carves out the largest rectangle, and can iterate up to 64 times (cap at out.len() >= 64), each O(n²) → O(64 × n²) = O(64 × 8464) ≈ 542k. Fine. Worst case the loop runs many times but capped at 64 territories.
- Actually note: `largest_free_rectangle` is O(n²) per invocation, and each iteration zeroes out the found rect; the total iterations bounded by 64. So O(64·n²). Fine.

Note: `s.distance` cost needs checking in domain/entities/architecture.rs. Let me look at that. Also `CirculationSpine::distance` is used in several hot spots: territories (n²×S), layout candidates (C×S), stair placement.

   1| //! Circulation routing: one dominant cross-region spine plus rare branches.
   2| //!
   3| //! The main spine always runs west portal -> east portal, so circulation
   4| //! chains across regions forever; branches are optional and never form a
   5| //! competing street grid.
   6| 
   7| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
   8| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
   9| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
  10| 
  11| use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap, snap_width, v_edge_portal_z};
  12| 
  13| /// Z coordinate of the main spine where it passes world x (assumes the spine
  14| /// is a west-to-east Manhattan path).
  15| fn spine_z_at(path: &[Position], x: f32) -> f32 {
  16|     for seg in path.windows(2) {
  17|         let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
  18|         if a.z == b.z && (x >= a.x.min(b.x)) && (x <= a.x.max(b.x)) {
  19|             return a.z;
  20|         }
  21|     }
  22|     path[0].z
  23| }
  24| 
  25| pub(super) fn build_corridors(
  26|     seed: u32,
  27|     rx: i64,
  28|     rz: i64,
  29|     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
  30|     origin: Position,
  31|     size: f32,
  32| ) -> Vec<CirculationSpine> {
  33|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0 + k, rx, rz]);
  34|     let (x0, x1) = (origin.x, origin.x + size);
  35|     let (z0, z1) = (origin.z, origin.z + size);
  36|     let west_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx, rz);
  37|     let east_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx + 1, rz);
  38|     // The primary route is deliberately too broad for an ordinary office
  39|     // corridor. It carries the infinite cross-region continuity; anything
  40|     // else is an optional branch, never a competing street grid.
  41|     let main_w = snap_width(4.8 + 2.4 * h(1));
  42|     let sec_w = snap_width(3.6 + 1.4 * hash01(seed, &[0xC1, rx, rz]));
  43| 
  44|     let mut spines = Vec::new();
  45|     let mut id = 0u32;
  46|     let mut push = |kind: SpaceProgram, path: Vec<Position>, width: f32, id: &mut u32| {
  47|         spines_push(&mut spines, kind, path, width, id);
  48|     };
  49| 
  50|     // Main spine: west portal -> east portal, always. Its Manhattan bend
  51|     // position is the designer's one free choice.
  52|     let bend_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.35 + 0.30 * h(2)));
  53|     let main_path: Vec<Position> = match genome.circulation {
  54|         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine => {
  55|             let mid_z = snap(z0 + size * (0.30 + 0.40 * h(3)));
  56|             let bend2_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.60 + 0.25 * h(4)));
  57|             vec![
  58|                 Position::new(x0, west_z),
  59|                 Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
  60|                 Position::new(bend_x, mid_z),
  61|                 Position::new(bend2_x, mid_z),
  62|                 Position::new(bend2_x, east_z),
  63|                 Position::new(x1, east_z),
  64|             ]
  65|         }
  66|         _ => vec![
  67|             Position::new(x0, west_z),
  68|             Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
  69|             Position::new(bend_x, east_z),
  70|             Position::new(x1, east_z),
  71|         ],
  72|     };
  73|     let main_z_at = main_path.clone();
  74|     push(SpaceProgram::MainCorridor, main_path, main_w, &mut id);
  75| 
  76|     // Secondary routes are branches, not a second regional grid: roughly a
  77|     // quarter of regions have none, most have one, and a few have two. The
  78|     // former ring and north/south through-route are intentionally absent.
  79|     let branch_count = match genome.circulation {
  80|         CirculationStyle::StraightSpine if h(11) < 0.45 => 0,
  81|         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine if h(11) < 0.20 => 0,
  82|         _ if h(11) < 0.28 => 0,
  83|         _ if h(11) < 0.82 => 1,
  84|         _ => 2,
  85|     };
  86|     for k in 0..branch_count {
  87|         let sx = snap(x0 + size * (0.18 + 0.64 * h(12 + k)));
  88|         let sz = spine_z_at(&main_z_at, sx);
  89|         let len = snap(12.0 + 14.0 * h(22 + k));
  90|         let dir = if h(32 + k) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
  91|         let end = (sz + dir * len).clamp(z0 + EDGE_MARGIN, z1 - EDGE_MARGIN);
  92|         if (end - sz).abs() >= 8.0 {
  93|             push(
  94|                 SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall,
  95|                 vec![Position::new(sx, sz), Position::new(sx, snap(end))],
  96|                 sec_w,
  97|                 &mut id,
  98|             );
  99|         }
 100|     }
 101|     spines
 102| }
 103| 
 104| fn spines_push(
 105|     spines: &mut Vec<CirculationSpine>,
 106|     kind: SpaceProgram,
 107|     path: Vec<Position>,
 108|     width: f32,
 109|     id: &mut u32,
 110| ) {
 111|     spines.push(CirculationSpine {
 112|         id: *id,
 113|         spine_kind: kind,
 114|         path,
 115|         width,
 116|     });
 117|     *id += 1;
 118| }
