  16| /// Backrooms corruption: the plan was sane; the building is not. Pure
  17| /// sequencing over four independent rules, each its own named function so
  18| /// any one of them is testable without the other three — previously all
  19| /// four were inlined together sharing one hash-key closure, which made it
  20| /// impossible to exercise, say, just the abandonment rule in isolation.
  21| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  22| pub(super) fn corrupt(
  23|     seed: u32,
  24|     rx: i64,
  25|     rz: i64,
  26|     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
  27|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  28|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  29|     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
  30|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
  31|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
  32| ) {
  33|     if assemblies.is_empty() {
  34|         return;
  35|     }
  36|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0DE + k, rx, rz]);
  37| 
  38|     if h(1) < 0.6 {
  39|         let src = pick_index(h(2), assemblies.len());
  40|         let shift = snap(12.0 + 12.0 * h(3));
  41|         let dup = duplication_skews(&assemblies[src], spines)
  42|             .into_iter()
  43|             .find_map(|skew| {
  44|                 duplication_offsets(shift).into_iter().find_map(|offset| {
  45|                     duplicate_suite_candidate(
  46|                         assemblies,
  47|                         taken,
  48|                         spines,
  49|                         rx,
  50|                         rz,
  51|                         src,
  52|                         snap(offset),
  53|                         skew,
  54|                     )
  55|                 })
  56|             });
  57|         if let Some(dup) = dup {
  58|             taken.push(dup.footprint.bounds());
  59|             assemblies.push(dup);
  60|         }
  61|     }
  62| 
  63|     if h(6) < 0.6 {
  64|         let k = pick_index(h(7), assemblies.len());
  65|         abandon_assembly(&mut assemblies[k]);
  66|     }
  67| 
  68|     apply_renovation_history(dominant.renovation_history, assemblies, h(8), h(9));
  69| 
  70|     // Applied last so it respects whatever the earlier passes decided (an
  71|     // abandoned shell stays dark).
  72|     let sp = spawn_point(seed);
  73|     let forced_in_spawn_region = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom)
  74|         && rx == region_index(sp.x)
  75|         && rz == region_index(sp.z);
  76|     let red_room_realized = forced_in_spawn_region
  77|         && force_red_room_in_spawn_region(dominant, rx, rz, assemblies, taken, spines);
  78|     if !red_room_realized {
  79|         let red_room_scale = config.anomalies.frequency * config.anomalies.red_rooms;
  80|         realize_red_room_event(seed, noise, rx, rz, red_room_scale, assemblies);
  81|     }
  82| }
  83| 
  84| /// Longitudinal offsets a duplicate is tried at, in preference order.
  85| ///
  86| /// The authored distance first, then further down the corridor, then closer
  87| /// than authored. A fixed ladder of six offsets was enough when a region
  88| /// held two suites and the floor was mostly empty; against a floor the
  89| /// placement solver has actually laid out, every one of them lands on a
  90| /// neighbour, and duplication -- the most recognizably Backrooms corruption
  91| /// there is -- silently stopped happening in all 36 test regions. Sweeping
  92| /// finds whatever gap the solver left instead of guessing where one might
  93| /// be, and keeping the authored distance first means the seed still decides
  94| /// where the copy *wants* to sit; the sweep only decides where it can.
  95| fn duplication_offsets(shift: f32) -> Vec<f32> {
  96|     let authored = shift.abs().max(DUPLICATE_STEP);
  97|     let mut out = Vec::new();
  98|     let mut d = authored;
  99|     while d <= DUPLICATE_MAX_OFFSET {
 100|         out.push(d);
 101|         out.push(-d);
 102|         d += DUPLICATE_STEP;
 103|     }
 104|     let mut d = authored - DUPLICATE_STEP;
 105|     while d >= DUPLICATE_STEP {
 106|         out.push(d);
 107|         out.push(-d);
 108|         d -= DUPLICATE_STEP;
 109|     }
 110|     out
 111| }
 112| 
 113| /// Sweep pitch for duplicate offsets. Matches the placement solver's anchor
 114| /// pitch, so a gap the solver could seat a room in is one this can find.
 115| const DUPLICATE_STEP: f32 = 2.0;
 116| 
 117| /// Perpendicular offsets a duplicate is tried at: its own corridor first,
 118| /// then every other parallel run in the region.
 119| ///
 120| /// Staying on the source's own corridor run is the cleanest repetition, but
 121| /// it is also where there is least space -- the placement solver has
 122| /// already seated rooms along that leg, and a copy needs as much clearance
 123| /// as any other room. The free space is on the *other* runs. Moving the
 124| /// copy by the centerline distance between two parallel corridors lands it
 125| /// at the same offset from its new corridor as it had from its old, so the
 126| /// entrance stays in a wall band and faces a route; `duplicate_suite_candidate`
 127| /// re-checks that rather than trusting it.
 128| fn duplication_skews(source: &AssemblyInstance, spines: &[CirculationSpine]) -> Vec<f32> {
 129|     let mut out = vec![0.0];
 130|     let Some(entrance) = source.primary_entrance() else {
 131|         return out;
 132|     };
 133|     // The centerline the source's entrance actually sits against.
 134|     let Some(host_z) = spines
 135|         .iter()
 136|         .flat_map(|s| s.path.windows(2))
 137|         .filter(|seg| (seg[0].z - seg[1].z).abs() <= 1e-4)
 138|         .map(|seg| seg[0].z)
 139|         .min_by(|a, b| {
 140|             (a - entrance.center.z)
 141|                 .abs()
 142|                 .total_cmp(&(b - entrance.center.z).abs())
 143|         })
 144|     else {
 145|         return out;
 146|     };
 147|     let mut targets: Vec<f32> = spines
 148|         .iter()
 149|         .flat_map(|s| s.path.windows(2))
 150|         .filter(|seg| (seg[0].z - seg[1].z).abs() <= 1e-4)
 151|         .map(|seg| seg[0].z - host_z)
 152|         .filter(|skew| skew.abs() > 1e-4)
 153|         .collect();
 154|     // Nearest parallel run first, and deterministic: two queries of this
 155|     // region must order the candidates identically.
 156|     targets.sort_by(|a, b| a.abs().total_cmp(&b.abs()));
 157|     targets.dedup_by(|a, b| (*a - *b).abs() < 1e-4);
 158|     out.extend(targets);
 159|     out
 160| }
 161| 
 162| /// How far down the corridor a copy may sit from its source. Beyond a
 163| /// region there is no shared corridor to repeat along.
 164| const DUPLICATE_MAX_OFFSET: f32 = REGION_SIZE;
 165| 
 166| /// Rule 1: a suite repeats itself further down the corridor, slightly wrong.
 167| /// Pure — reads the existing plan, returns the candidate duplicate (already
 168| /// translated, with its misalignment recorded) or `None` if it would fall
 169| /// outside the region, overlap something already placed, or seal itself
 170| /// away from every corridor. The caller decides whether to keep it.
 171| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 172| fn duplicate_suite_candidate(
 173|     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
 174|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 175|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 176|     rx: i64,
 177|     rz: i64,
 178|     src: usize,
 179|     shift: f32,
 180|     skew: f32,
 181| ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
 182|     // `skew` moves the copy between parallel corridor runs, never off a
 183|     // corridor: the repetition is wrong in its position, not sealed away
 184|     // behind an accidental strip of wall. The `reachable` check below is
 185|     // what actually enforces that.
 186|     let mut dup = assemblies[src].clone();
 187|     dup.translate(shift, skew);
 188|     dup.id = assemblies.len() as u32 + 1000;
 189|     dup.corruption.misalignment = (shift, skew);
 190| 
 191|     let b = dup.footprint.bounds();
 192|     let inside = b.0 > rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
 193|         && b.2 < (rx + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN
 194|         && b.1 > rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
 195|         && b.3 < (rz + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN;
 196|     // The moved entrance must still read as a door onto a route, or the
 197|     // copy would be a sealed pocket.
 198|     let reachable = dup
 199|         .entrances()
 200|         .any(|e| entrance_faces_route(spines, e.center.x, e.center.z, PLAN_WALL_T));
 201|     // The same clearance the placement solver keeps between rooms, not a
 202|     // looser one. A copy squeezed into a 0.4 u gap is close enough that a
 203|     // neighbour's ceiling fixture samples inside this shell -- which reads
 204|     // as an abandoned expansion that is somehow still lit. Rooms in a real
 205|     // plan either share a wall or stand clear; a duplicate is no exception.
 206|     let clear = !taken
 207|         .iter()
 208|         .any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, super::layout::ROOM_SEPARATION));
 209|     (inside && reachable && clear).then_some(dup)
 210| }
 211| 
 212| /// Rule 2: one assembly was built and then never occupied — an empty shell,
 213| /// nothing lit.
 214| fn abandon_assembly(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
 215|     assembly.program = SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion;
 216|     assembly.corruption.abandoned = true;
 217|     assembly.spaces.clear();
 218|     assembly
 219|         .hosts
 220|         .retain(|host| host.role != HostRole::Partition);
 221|     assembly.openings.retain(|opening| {
 222|         opening.role != OpeningRole::Interior
 223|             && assembly.hosts.iter().any(|host| host.id == opening.host)
 224|     });
 225|     for f in &mut assembly.fixtures {
 226|         f.lit = false;
 227|     }
 228| }
 229| 
 230| /// Rule 3: renovation history overlays the original structural grid. A
 231| /// partial refit contradicts one assembly; a fuller history of layered
 232| /// refits leaves a second, distinct assembly contradicted too — otherwise
 233| /// the two `RenovationStyle` variants would be indistinguishable once
 234| /// generated, despite the type's own doc comment promising more.
 235| fn apply_renovation_history(
 236|     history: RenovationStyle,
 237|     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
 238|     pick1: f32,
 239|     pick2: f32,
 240| ) {
 241|     match history {
 242|         RenovationStyle::Untouched => {}
 243|         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit => {
 244|             let k = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
 245|             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k]);
 246|         }
 247|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => {
 248|             let k1 = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
 249|             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k1]);
 250|             if assemblies.len() > 1 {
 251|                 // Offset from k1 rather than re-rolling, so the second pick
 252|                 // is guaranteed distinct instead of merely likely to be.
 253|                 let k2 = (k1 + 1 + pick_index(pick2, assemblies.len() - 1)) % assemblies.len();
 254|                 overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k2]);
 255|             }
 256|         }
 257|     }
 258| }
 259| 
 260| /// A renovation overlays the original structural grid on one assembly.
 261| fn overlay_renovation(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
 262|     assembly.corruption.renovation_overlay = true;
 263| }
 264| 
 265| /// Rule 4a: the debug/authored path. `?force_anomaly=redroom` targets the
 266| /// region the player actually spawns in, so this must succeed there even
 267| /// when nothing qualifies yet — mark an existing occupied assembly if one
 268| /// exists, otherwise place a brand new one against the main corridor.
 269| /// Returns whether a red room was realized.
 270| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 271| fn force_red_room_in_spawn_region(
 272|     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
 273|     rx: i64,
 274|     rz: i64,
 275|     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
 276|     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
 277|     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 278| ) -> bool {
 279|     if let Some(a) = assemblies
 280|         .iter_mut()
 281|         .find(|a| a.primary_entrance().is_some() && !a.corruption.abandoned)
 282|     {
 283|         a.corruption.red_room = true;
 284|         return true;
 285|     }
 286|     let Some(spine) = spines
 287|         .iter()
 288|         .find(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
 289|     else {
 290|         return false;
 291|     };
 292|     let Some(seg) = spine.path.windows(2).find(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z) else {
 293|         return false;
 294|     };
 295|     let lx0 = seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x);
 296|     let lz = seg[0].z;
 297|     let origin = Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE);
 298|     let Some(mut a) = place_suite(
 299|         9999,
 300|         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,

 301|         dominant,
 302|         0.5,
 303|         0.5,
 304|         lx0 + 12.0,
 305|         lz,
 306|         spine.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5,
 307|         1.0,
 308|         origin,
 309|         REGION_SIZE,
 310|         taken,
 311|         spines,
 312|     ) else {
 313|         return false;
 314|     };
 315|     a.corruption.red_room = true;
 316|     taken.push(a.footprint.bounds());
 317|     assemblies.push(a);
 318|     true
 319| }
 320| 
 321| /// Rule 4b: the ordinary path. Where a red room happens is a *graph event*,
 322| /// not a per-region coin flip — the macro topology plans separated events on
 323| /// its lattice (`world_topology::red_room_event_for_region`), and this rule
 324| /// merely realizes an event that targets this region on one eligible
 325| /// assembly, rotating from a stable start so the choice replays identically
 326| /// for every query of this region. If no assembly qualifies the event stays
 327| /// unrealized — a planned encounter never overwrites navigable circulation.
 328| fn realize_red_room_event(
 329|     seed: u32,
 330|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 331|     rx: i64,
 332|     rz: i64,
 333|     red_room_scale: f32,
 334|     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
 335| ) {
 336|     let Some(event) = crate::use_cases::world_topology::red_room_event_for_region(
 337|         seed,
 338|         noise,
 339|         rx,
 340|         rz,
 341|         red_room_scale.clamp(0.0, 4.0),
 342|     ) else {
 343|         return;
 344|     };
 345|     let count = assemblies.len();
 346|     let start = (event.id % count as u64) as usize;
 347|     for offset in 0..count {
 348|         let a = &mut assemblies[(start + offset) % count];
 349|         if !a.corruption.abandoned && a.primary_entrance().is_some() {
 350|             a.corruption.red_room = true;
 351|             break;
 352|         }
 353|     }
 354| }

 422|     /// Runs through the region's own center so a suite fronting onto it
 423|     /// (a fixed 2.4u offset either side) never brushes `EDGE_MARGIN` at the
 424|     /// region boundary — a corridor at the very edge is not a shape any
 425|     /// real region plan produces, and would fail `place_suite`'s margin
 426|     /// check for reasons unrelated to whatever a test is actually checking.
 427|     /// Where `place_suite` actually seats a suite's front wall against
 428|     /// `corridor_spine`: half the clear width plus half a wall band past
 429|     /// the centerline. Fixtures that sit *on* the centerline describe a
 430|     /// room built in the middle of the corridor, which the planner never
 431|     /// produces and the sampler would carve full height.
 432|     const SUITE_FRONT_Z: f32 = REGION_SIZE * 0.5 + 2.0 + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5;
 433| 
 434|     fn corridor_spine() -> CirculationSpine {
 435|         CirculationSpine {
 436|             id: 0,
 437|             spine_kind: SpaceProgram::MainCorridor,
 438|             path: vec![
 439|                 Position::new(0.0, REGION_SIZE * 0.5),
 440|                 Position::new(REGION_SIZE, REGION_SIZE * 0.5),
 441|             ],
 442|             width: 4.0,
 443|         }
 444|     }

 447|     fn abandonment_clears_spaces_and_darkens_every_fixture() {
 448|         let mut a = minimal_assembly(0, 0.0, 20.0);
 449|         a.hosts.push(HostSegment {
 450|             id: HostId(4),
 451|             start: Position::new(7.0, 20.0),
 452|             end: Position::new(7.0, 30.0),
 453|             thickness: PLAN_WALL_T,
 454|             base_units: 0.0,
 455|             top_units: 3.4,
 456|             role: HostRole::Partition,

 459|             id: OpeningId(1),
 460|             host: HostId(4),
 461|             role: OpeningRole::Interior,

 622|     #[test]
 623|     fn forced_red_room_places_a_new_room_when_nothing_qualifies() {
 624|         let genome = test_genome();
 625|         let mut assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = vec![];
 626|         let mut taken = vec![];

corruption.rs analysis:
- `duplicate_suite_candidate`: clones the whole AssemblyInstance (including hosts, openings, fixtures) — O(assembly size). The find_map loops: skews (up to ~2-4) × offsets (up to ~20-40). So up to ~100 clones of an assembly per region. Each clone is small (few KB). Fine.
- `realize_red_room_event` → `red_room_event_for_region` → `red_room_event_for_cell` → `red_room_candidate` × 9 (itself + 8 rivals) each calling `sample_fields` (18 noise evals). So per region: ~9 × 18 = 162 noise evaluations + the classify_region in plan_macro_cell. This is in the region plan hot path, repeated per chunk when streaming without a WorldBlock. This confirms the redundancy finding.

Note that `realize_red_room_event` is called per region plan (via `corrupt`), and `red_room_event_for_region` is computed on the fly — this is the per-region cost. It's constant per region but re-derived for every region query. When `generate_from_plans` builds a window per chunk (level_zero finding), all this noise work repeats per chunk.

   1| //! Architect genomes: the designers a region inherits.
   2| //!
   3| //! `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator, 2 = intruder. The circulation style
   4| //! comes from low-frequency noise so neighboring regions tend to share a
   5| //! culture; every other property is hash-derived, but *not independently*:
   6| //! a real designer's decisions form a chain, not a set of parallel dice
   7| //! rolls. `structural_system` and `renovation_history` are decided first;
   8| //! everything downstream of them (room proportions, ceiling language,
   9| //! threshold language, furnishing density, tolerance for symmetry) biases
  10| //! toward what that earlier choice implies, with its own hash key still
  11| //! supplying the roll *within* the biased range. A `CoreAndShell` designer
  12| //! who chose that system to achieve big clear-span rooms should get big
  13| //! rooms and a ceiling that doesn't pretend to hide beams it doesn't have;
  14| //! a `DeepSpansWithBeams` designer's ceiling should show the beams that
  15| //! justify the system's name.
  16| 
  17| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  18| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  19| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  20| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
  21| 
  22| use super::{REGION_SIZE, pick_index};
  23| 
  24| /// Derive one designer for a region. `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator,
  25| /// 2 = intruder. The circulation style comes from low-frequency noise so
  26| /// neighboring regions tend to share a culture; everything else hashes.
  27| pub fn derive_genome(
  28|     seed: u32,
  29|     rx: i64,
  30|     rz: i64,
  31|     salt: i64,
  32|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  33| ) -> ArchitectGenome {
  34|     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0x6E0 + salt, rx, rz, k]);
  35|     // ~130 u wavelength: cultures span a few regions.
  36|     let culture = noise.evaluate_2d(
  37|         seed ^ 0xA11C_0DE ^ (salt as u32),
  38|         Position::new(
  39|             (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
  40|             (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
  41|         ),
  42|     );
  43|     let circulation = match ((culture * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999) * 4.0) as u32 {
  44|         0 => CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
  45|         1 => CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine,
  46|         2 => CirculationStyle::PairedBranches,
  47|         _ => CirculationStyle::TreeWithCulDeSacs,
  48|     };
  49|     // ---- site strategy: decided first, everything else answers to it ----
  50|     let structural_system = *[
  51|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
  52|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams,
  53|         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid,
  54|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
  55|     ]
  56|     .get(pick_index(h(1), 4))
  57|     .unwrap();
  58|     let renovation_history = *[
  59|         RenovationStyle::Untouched,
  60|         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit,
  61|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits,
  62|     ]
  63|     .get(pick_index(h(5), 3))
  64|     .unwrap();
  65| 
  66|     // ---- consequences of the structural system --------------------------
  67|     // CoreAndShell and DeepSpansWithBeams are chosen specifically to permit
  68|     // large clear-span rooms (see `suites::on_column`, which gives
  69|     // CoreAndShell zero interior columns); RegularGrid/OffsetGrid bound
  70|     // their rooms to a small structural module instead. Room size is a
  71|     // consequence of that choice, not a second independent roll.
  72|     let spans_wide = matches!(
  73|         structural_system,
  74|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell | StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams
  75|     );
  76|     let (min_lo, min_span, max_lo, max_span) = if spans_wide {
  77|         (16.0, 6.0, 24.0, 10.0)
  78|     } else {
  79|         (12.0, 4.0, 18.0, 6.0)
  80|     };
  81| 
  82|     // A coffered or exposed-soffit ceiling is a description of what a deep
  83|     // beam grid looks like from underneath, not an unrelated stylistic
  84|     // choice — so it should follow from having beams to show. CoreAndShell
  85|     // has no beam grid to express at all; flat tiles are the honest default
  86|     // for it. RegularGrid/OffsetGrid are unbiased: either reads as fine for
  87|     // an ordinary column grid.
  88|     let ceiling_language = match structural_system {
  89|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => match h(3) {
  90|             v if v < 0.55 => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
  91|             v if v < 0.85 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
  92|             _ => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
  93|         },
  94|         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => match h(3) {
  95|             v if v < 0.70 => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
  96|             v if v < 0.90 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
  97|             _ => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
  98|         },
  99|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => *[
 100|             CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
 101|             CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
 102|             CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
 103|         ]
 104|         .get(pick_index(h(3), 3))
 105|         .unwrap(),
 106|     };
 107| 
 108|     // A grid that never breaks its own module (Regular, CoreAndShell) reads
 109|     // as more deliberately symmetric than one that already contradicts
 110|     // itself every other row (OffsetGrid).
 111|     let symmetry_bias = match structural_system {
 112|         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => 0.25,
 113|         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => -0.20,
 114|         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => 0.0,
 115|     };
 116| 
 117|     // ---- consequences of the renovation history --------------------------
 118|     // A framed office door is now an anomaly. The chosen language is only a
 119|     // bias; each assembly still picks its own threshold so a whole region
 120|     // never turns into a row of identical openings. A designer who left
 121|     // layered refits behind also left wider, less consistent thresholds and
 122|     // denser leftover furnishing than a plan nobody ever touched.
 123|     let refit_bias = match renovation_history {
 124|         RenovationStyle::Untouched => 0.0,
 125|         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit => 0.12,
 126|         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => 0.25,
 127|     };
 128|     let threshold_language = match (h(2) + refit_bias).min(0.999) {
 129|         v if v < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
 130|         v if v < 0.55 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
 131|         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
 132|     };
 133| 
 134|     let lighting_language = *[
 135|         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
 136|         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
 137|         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation,
 138|         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants,
 139|     ]
 140|     .get(pick_index(h(4), 4))
 141|     .unwrap();
 142| 
 143|     ArchitectGenome {
 144|         circulation,
 145|         structural_system,
 146|         room_proportions: ProportionRules {
 147|             // Level 0 reads as broken retail-backroom masses, not a cubicle
 148|             // tiling. A suite frontage normally survives 12--24 u before a
 149|             // meaningful interruption, wider still where the structure
 150|             // permits it.
 151|             min_side: min_lo + min_span * h(6),
 152|             max_side: max_lo + max_span * h(7),
 153|             elongation: h(8),
 154|         },
 155|         threshold_language,
 156|         ceiling_language,
 157|         lighting_language,
 158|         partition_density: (0.3 + 0.7 * h(9) + refit_bias).min(1.0),
 159|         renovation_history,
 160|         tolerance_for_symmetry: (h(10) + symmetry_bias).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
 161|     }
 162| }

   6| /// ASCII plan view at `step` world units per character. Corridors `=`, macro
   7| /// anomalies `P/B/H` (pillar/blackout/pits), red loops `R`, assembly interiors
   8| /// by program initial, entrances `+`, empty fabric `.`.
   9| pub fn debug_region_ascii(plan: &RegionPlan, step: f32) -> String {
  10|     let n = (plan.size_world / step) as usize;
  11|     let mut out = String::with_capacity((n + 1) * n);
  12|     for iz in 0..n {
  13|         for ix in 0..n {
  14|             let x = plan.origin_world.x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * step;
  15|             let z = plan.origin_world.z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * step;
  16|             let mut ch = '.';
  17|             for a in &plan.assemblies {
  18|                 if a.footprint.contains(x, z) {
  19|                     ch = match a.program {
  20|                         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 'o',
  21|                         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 'p',
  22|                         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 'c',
  23|                         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 'b',
  24|                         SpaceProgram::Storage => 's',
  25|                         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 'v',
  26|                         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 'w',
  27|                         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => 'x',
  28|                         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 'A',
  29|                         SpaceProgram::Reception => 'R',
  30|                         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 't',
  31|                         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 'm',
  32|                         SpaceProgram::Stair => 'S',
  33|                         _ => 'r',
  34|                     };
  35|                 }
  36|             }
  37|             for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
  38|                 if anomaly.contains(x, z) {
  39|                     ch = match anomaly.kind {
  40|                         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => 'P',
  41|                         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => 'B',
  42|                         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => 'H',
  43|                         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => 'R',
  44|                         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => 'M',
  45|                     };
  46|                 }
  47|             }
  48|             for s in &plan.corridors {
  49|                 if s.distance(x, z) <= s.width * 0.5 {
  50|                     ch = '=';
  51|                 }
  52|             }
  53|             for a in &plan.assemblies {
  54|                 for e in a.entrances() {
  55|                     if (x - e.center.x).abs() < e.width * 0.5 && (z - e.center.z).abs() < step {
  56|                         ch = '+';
  57|                     }
  58|                 }
  59|             }
  60|             out.push(ch);
  61|         }
  62|         out.push('\n');
  63|     }
  64|     out
  65| }

   1| //! Assembly-derived Red Room encounter planning.
   2| //!
   3| //! A Red Room is not a macro-lattice shape. It inherits a real assembly's
   4| //! footprint and entrance, then adds stable semantic crossing planes.
   5| 
   6| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
   7|     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, AxisDirection, OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, QuarterTurn,
   8|     TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
   9| };
  10| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::AssemblyInstance;
  11| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  12| use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{SNAP, mix64, stable_id};
  13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  14| 
  15| const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
  16| const THRESHOLD_DEPTH: f32 = 2.8;
  17| const LOOP_GATE_DEPTH: f32 = 6.0;
  18| 
  19| fn clamp_inward(desired: f32, far_inner_plane: f32, direction: AxisDirection) -> f32 {
  20|     match direction {
  21|         AxisDirection::Positive => desired.min(far_inner_plane),
  22|         AxisDirection::Negative => desired.max(far_inner_plane),
  23|     }
  24| }
  25| 
  26| fn red_room_instance(
  27|     seed: u32,
  28|     region_origin: Position,
  29|     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
  30| ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
  31|     let entrance = *assembly.primary_entrance()?;
  32|     let bounds = assembly.footprint.bounds();
  33|     let center = Position::new((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
  34|     let region_x = (region_origin.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
  35|     let region_z = (region_origin.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
  36|     let id = mix64(
  37|         stable_id(seed, AnomalyKind::RedRoom, region_x, region_z)
  38|             ^ (assembly.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
  39|     );
  40|     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
  41|         center,
  42|         half_x: (bounds.2 - bounds.0) * 0.5,
  43|         half_z: (bounds.3 - bounds.1) * 0.5,
  44|         basis: OrthoBasis {
  45|             turn: QuarterTurn::Zero,
  46|         },
  47|     };
  48|     let axis = if entrance.through_x_wall {
  49|         Axis2::Z
  50|     } else {
  51|         Axis2::X
  52|     };
  53|     let (edge_coordinate, center_coordinate, half_depth) = match axis {
  54|         Axis2::X => (entrance.center.x, center.x, footprint.half_x),
  55|         Axis2::Z => (entrance.center.z, center.z, footprint.half_z),
  56|     };
  57|     let forward = if center_coordinate >= edge_coordinate {
  58|         AxisDirection::Positive
  59|     } else {
  60|         AxisDirection::Negative
  61|     };
  62| 
  63|     // Commitment happens inside the room, beyond the externally readable
  64|     // doorway. Entrance placement guarantees enough depth for this vestibule.
  65|     let threshold_plane = edge_coordinate + forward.sign() * THRESHOLD_DEPTH;
  66|     let (span_min, span_max) = if axis == Axis2::Z {
  67|         (
  68|             entrance.center.x - entrance.width * 0.5,
  69|             entrance.center.x + entrance.width * 0.5,
  70|         )
  71|     } else {
  72|         (
  73|             entrance.center.z - entrance.width * 0.5,
  74|             entrance.center.z + entrance.width * 0.5,
  75|         )
  76|     };
  77|     let affected_bounds = footprint.bounds();
  78|     let threshold_gate = TraversalGate {
  79|         id: mix64(id ^ 0x6A7E_0ED0),
  80|         instance_id: id,
  81|         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
  82|         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
  83|         axis,
  84|         plane: threshold_plane,
  85|         span_min,
  86|         span_max,
  87|         forward,
  88|         affected_bounds,
  89|     };
  90| 
  91|     // The loop checkpoint is six units beyond commitment when the room has
  92|     // that depth. Shallow rooms clamp it one plan voxel inside the far wall,
  93|     // keeping the semantic crossing on geometry owned by this encounter.
  94|     let far_inner_plane = center_coordinate + forward.sign() * (half_depth - SNAP).max(0.0);
  95|     let loop_plane = clamp_inward(
  96|         threshold_plane + forward.sign() * LOOP_GATE_DEPTH,
  97|         far_inner_plane,
  98|         forward,
  99|     );
 100|     let loop_gate = TraversalGate {
 101|         id: mix64(id ^ 0x9B4C_1A2F),
 102|         instance_id: id,
 103|         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
 104|         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
 105|         axis,
 106|         plane: loop_plane,
 107|         span_min,
 108|         span_max,
 109|         // `forward` records the authored inward direction. Runtime state owns
 110|         // the separate policy for which traversal directions advance a loop.
 111|         forward,
 112|         affected_bounds,
 113|     };
 114| 
 115|     Some(AnomalyInstance {
 116|         id,
 117|         kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
 118|         footprint,
 119|         basis: footprint.basis,
 120|         macro_anchor: (region_x, region_z),
 121|         pillar_lattice: None,
 122|         pit_lattice: None,
 123|         arch: None,
 124|         gates: vec![threshold_gate, loop_gate],
 125|         skeleton_half_width: 1.0,
 126|         entry_band: THRESHOLD_DEPTH,
 127|     })
 128| }

 134|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 135| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
 136|     let forced = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
 137|     let organic_enabled = config.anomalies.frequency > 0.0 && config.anomalies.red_rooms > 0.0;

  18|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  19|     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  20|     world_x: f32,
  21|     world_z: f32,
  22| ) -> ColumnPlan {
  23|     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
  24|     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
  25|     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
  26|     let loop_width = 2.0f32.min(half_x * 0.35).min(half_z * 0.35).max(1.2);
  27|     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
  28| 
  29|     // Warning cues intensify toward the shell but never replace masonry with
  30|     // a special red wall.  The anomaly is read through carpet, compression,
  31|     // and light; collision remains ordinary Level 0 architecture.
  32|     let contamination = (1.0 - boundary / (loop_width * 2.0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  33|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::red_room(contamination);
  34|     if boundary > PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
  35|         if contamination > 0.15 {
  36|             column.floor_material = profile.floor_voxel();
  37|         }
  38|         if contamination > 0.33 {
  39|             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.2).max(2.6);
  40|         }
  41|         if contamination > 0.66 {
  42|             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.4).max(2.4);
  43|         }
  44|     }
  45|     column.fixture = Some(crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureSample {
  46|         id: (instance.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
  47|         kind: crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
  48|         state: crate::use_cases::level_zero::FixtureState::Lit,
  49|         center_x: 0.0,
  50|         center_z: 0.0,
  51|         half_x: 0.3,
  52|         half_z: 0.3,
  53|         ceiling_units: column.ceiling_units,
  54|         red_room: true,
  55|     });
  56| 
  57|     let Some(state) = instance.state(reality) else {
  58|         return column;
  59|     };
  60|     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::Outside {
  61|         return column;
  62|     }
  63| 
  64|     // Commitment closes the remembered entrance and reduces the authored
  65|     // room to one walkable perimeter loop around an opaque core.
  66|     let in_core = local_x.abs() < half_x - loop_width && local_z.abs() < half_z - loop_width;
  67|     column.solid = boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T || in_core;
  68|     column.lintel_from_units = None;
  69|     column.floor_material = VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
  70|     column.ceiling_units = column.ceiling_units.min(2.8);
  71|     if column.solid {
  72|         column.fixture = None;
  73|     }
  74| 
  75|     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::EscapeOpen {
  76|         open_single_escape(
  77|             instance,
  78|             state.epoch,
  79|             config.anomalies.red_escape_bias,
  80|             local_x,
  81|             local_z,
  82|             &mut column,
  83|         );
  84|     }
  85|     column
  86| }
  87| 
  88| /// Opens one deterministic side of the loop.  The bias is an authored width
  89| /// control: zero keeps the encounter sealed; positive values widen a single
  90| /// breach without turning both symmetric walls into exits.
  91| fn open_single_escape(
  92|     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
  93|     epoch: u32,
  94|     bias: f32,
  95|     local_x: f32,
  96|     local_z: f32,
  97|     column: &mut ColumnPlan,
  98| ) {
  99|     let width = bias.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.4;
 100|     if width <= 0.0 {
 101|         return;
 102|     }
 103|     let Some(threshold) = instance.gates.first() else {
 104|         return;
 105|     };
 106|     let side_sign = if stable_bit(instance.id, epoch) {
 107|         1.0
 108|     } else {
 109|         -1.0
 110|     };
 111|     let (side_coordinate, side_extent, along) = match threshold.axis {
 112|         Axis2::Z => (local_x, instance.footprint.half_x, local_z),
 113|         Axis2::X => (local_z, instance.footprint.half_z, local_x),
 114|     };
 115|     let on_selected_wall = (side_coordinate - side_sign * side_extent).abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
 116|     if on_selected_wall && along.abs() < width {
 117|         column.solid = false;
 118|     }
 119| }
 120| 
 121| fn stable_bit(instance_id: u64, epoch: u32) -> bool {
 122|     let mut value = instance_id ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(29) ^ 0xE5CA_9E5C_A9E5_CA9E;
 123|     value ^= value >> 30;
 124|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
 125|     value ^= value >> 27;
 126|     value & 1 == 1
 127| }

   1| //! Addressing for the Level 0 world reached through a committed Red Room.
   2| //!
   3| //! A Red Room does not invent a second procedural grammar.  It addresses a
   4| //! distant, deterministic copy of Level 0 and changes its presentation.  The
   5| //! address must therefore be stable across chunk order and worker boundaries,

 156| impl RecursiveLevelAddress {
 157|     /// Derives an address using integer avalanche hashes only.  Both halves of
 158|     /// the 64-bit instance id participate in the seed and in each axis.
 159|     pub(crate) fn derive(world_seed: u32, instance_id: AnomalyId) -> Self {
 160|         let root = mix64(
 161|             ADDRESS_DOMAIN ^ instance_id ^ (world_seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15),
 162|         );
 163|         let seed_hash = mix64(root ^ 0x5EED_5EED_A11C_0DE5);
 164|         let derived_seed = (seed_hash as u32) ^ ((seed_hash >> 32) as u32);
 165|         let translation_regions = (
 166|             translation_component(root, 0x5841_5849_5300_0001),
 167|             translation_component(root, 0x5A41_5849_5300_0002),
 168|         );
 169| 
 170|         Self {
 171|             instance_id,
 172|             derived_seed,
 173|             translation_regions,
 174|         }
 175|     }
 176| 
 177|     /// Selects the committed Red Room represented by a canonical reality
 178|     /// snapshot, then derives its recursive address.

 181|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 182|     ) -> Option<(Self, &AnomalyStateStamp)> {
 183|         let state = active_red_room(reality)?;
 184|         Some((Self::derive(world_seed, state.instance_id), state))
 185|     }

 195|     /// Exact transform for region keys.  Planning should prefer this form so
 196|     /// large-world floating-point precision never participates in identity.
 197|     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_region(self, source_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
 198|         (
 199|             source_region.0.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.0),
 200|             source_region.1.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.1),
 201|         )
 202|     }
 203| 
 204|     pub(crate) fn to_source_region(self, recursive_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
 205|         (
 206|             recursive_region
 207|                 .0
 208|                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.0),
 209|             recursive_region
 210|                 .1
 211|                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.1),
 212|         )
 213|     }
 214| 
 215|     /// World-space form used by column sampling.  The translation is an exact
 216|     /// multiple of the 80u region lattice, preserving portals and 0.4u plan
 217|     /// geometry across every chunk and LOD.
 218|     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_world(self, source: Position) -> Position {
 219|         let (region, local) = split_world_position(source);
 220|         let recursive = self.to_recursive_region(region);
 221|         join_world_position(recursive, local)
 222|     }
 223| 
 224|     pub(crate) fn to_source_world(self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
 225|         let (region, local) = split_world_position(recursive);
 226|         let source = self.to_source_region(region);
 227|         join_world_position(source, local)
 228|     }
 229| 
 230|     pub(crate) fn translation_world(self) -> Position {
 231|         let translation = self.translation_regions();
 232|         Position::new(
 233|             translation.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 234|             translation.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 235|         )
 236|     }

 238|     /// Produces a Level 0 config for the addressed world.  Organic anomaly
 239|     /// tuning is preserved, allowing recursive Level 0 to remain the complete
 240|     /// generator; only the one-shot debug override is cleared so it cannot be
 241|     /// cloned into every recursive address.
 242|     pub(crate) fn recursive_config(self, mut base: GeneratorConfig) -> GeneratorConfig {
 243|         base.level = LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
 244|         base.anomalies.forced_kind = None;
 245|         base
 246|     }
 247| }
 248| 
 249| /// Chooses one committed Red Room without depending on snapshot insertion
 250| /// order.  Under the current state machine, only red thresholds can produce a
 251| /// non-`Outside` phase.  Progress is compared explicitly because `epoch` is
 252| /// the best available recency signal; stable identity is the final tie-break.
 253| pub(crate) fn active_red_room(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Option<&AnomalyStateStamp> {
 254|     reality
 255|         .stamps()
 256|         .iter()
 257|         .filter(|state| state.phase != RedRoomPhase::Outside)
 258|         .max_by_key(|state| {
 259|             (
 260|                 state.epoch,
 261|                 state.phase,
 262|                 state.loop_count,
 263|                 state.last_gate_id,
 264|                 state.instance_id,
 265|             )
 266|         })
 267| }
 268| 
 269| fn translation_component(root: u64, axis_domain: u64) -> i64 {
 270|     let hash = mix64(root ^ axis_domain);
 271|     let magnitude = MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS + (hash % TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN) as i64;
 272|     if hash & (1 << 63) == 0 {
 273|         magnitude
 274|     } else {
 275|         -magnitude
 276|     }
 277| }
 278| 
 279| fn split_world_position(position: Position) -> ((i64, i64), (f32, f32)) {
 280|     let region = (
 281|         (position.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 282|         (position.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 283|     );
 284|     let local = (
 285|         position.x - region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 286|         position.z - region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 287|     );
 288|     (region, local)
 289| }
 290| 
 291| fn join_world_position(region: (i64, i64), local: (f32, f32)) -> Position {
 292|     Position::new(
 293|         region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.0,
 294|         region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.1,
 295|     )
 296| }
 297| 
 298| fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
 299|     value ^= value >> 30;
 300|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
 301|     value ^= value >> 27;
 302|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
 303|     value ^ (value >> 31)
 304| }

red_rooms files:
- planning.rs: fine — plan_red_rooms iterates assemblies, O(A).
- geometry.rs: per-column sampling, O(1).
- recursive_level.rs: `around_chunk` builds an `InfiniteRegionWindow` per chunk — this is the mechanism the head-start finding references (level_zero/generate.rs:331 builds RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk per chunk generation). The recursive window plans a full window of regions (several region plans) for every chunk when a red room is committed. And then within `generate_from_plans` it does the same for the base world. This is O(regions × cost-per-region) per chunk, where cost-per-region includes all the noise sampling + layout solver. Since chunk generation is the hot path (per-frame in streaming), this is the MAJOR finding.

Note that recursive_level.rs's `around_chunk` is `pub(crate)` and used by level_zero (out of my scope but I can confirm the call site in level_zero/generate.rs).

  19| /// Returns every immutable anomaly instance whose footprint overlaps a region.
  20| ///

  22| /// adjacent regions or different voxel sizes and receive the same instance.
  23| /// The noise port feeds the macro `anomaly_pressure` field, which clusters
  24| /// candidates without ever placing one itself.
  25| pub fn plan_anomalies_for_region(
  26|     seed: u32,
  27|     region_origin: Position,
  28|     region_size: f32,
  29|     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
  30|     protected_point: Position,
  31|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  32|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  33| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
  34|     let query = WorldBounds::new(
  35|         region_origin.x,
  36|         region_origin.z,
  37|         region_origin.x + region_size,
  38|         region_origin.z + region_size,

   1| //! User-facing controls for Level 0 anomaly planning and mutation.
   2| 
   3| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
   4| 
   5| /// Anomaly controls are separate from ordinary office-fabric tuning: changing
   6| /// wall or light density must never silently change encounter frequency.
   7| /// Multipliers are centered on `1.0`; distances are world units.
   8| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
   9| pub struct AnomalyTuning {
  10|     /// Overall organic candidate frequency. Debug forcing remains independent.
  11|     pub frequency: f32,
  12|     /// Macro-footprint scale for region-spanning instances.
  13|     pub size: f32,
  14|     pub pillar_expanses: f32,
  15|     pub blackouts: f32,
  16|     pub red_rooms: f32,
  17|     pub pit_lattices: f32,
  18|     /// Strength/probability of epoch-dependent mutable infill.
  19|     pub remap_intensity: f32,
  20|     /// Minimum distance behind a crossed threshold before infill may differ.
  21|     pub remap_distance: f32,
  22|     /// Radius around the player protected from any resident transition.
  23|     pub safe_radius: f32,
  24|     /// Width of the deterministic single Red Room escape. Zero keeps the loop
  25|     /// sealed; one opens the widest authored breach.
  26|     pub red_escape_bias: f32,
  27|     /// Stable archway anchor-room frequency multiplier.
  28|     pub archways: f32,
  29|     /// Fraction of blackout glimmers placed off the recovery skeleton.
  30|     pub blackout_decoys: f32,
  31|     /// Debug-only forced family at the protected point.
  32|     pub forced_kind: Option<AnomalyKind>,
  33| }
  34| 
  35| impl Default for AnomalyTuning {
  36|     fn default() -> Self {
  37|         Self {
  38|             frequency: 1.0,
  39|             size: 1.0,
  40|             pillar_expanses: 1.0,
  41|             blackouts: 1.0,
  42|             red_rooms: 1.0,
  43|             pit_lattices: 1.0,
  44|             remap_intensity: 1.0,
  45|             remap_distance: 12.0,
  46|             safe_radius: 8.0,
  47|             red_escape_bias: 0.12,
  48|             archways: 1.0,
  49|             // Most glimmers lie: with the recovery skeleton buried under
  50|             // this many decoys, walking out of a blackout is a feat.
  51|             blackout_decoys: 0.85,
  52|             forced_kind: None,
  53|         }
  54|     }
  55| }

total: 43
   1| //! Shared deterministic primitives for anomaly planners.
   2| //!
   3| //! These helpers are intentionally integer-first. A candidate's identity must
   4| //! depend on the world seed and its stable lattice anchor, never on which
   5| //! region or voxel chunk happened to request it.
   6| 
   7| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
   8| 
   9| pub(crate) const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
  10| 
  11| pub(crate) fn snap(value: f32) -> f32 {
  12|     (value / SNAP).round() * SNAP
  13| }
  14| 
  15| pub(crate) fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
  16|     value ^= value >> 30;
  17|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  18|     value ^= value >> 27;
  19|     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  20|     value ^ (value >> 31)
  21| }
  22| 
  23| pub(crate) fn hash(seed: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> u64 {
  24|     mix64(
  25|         seed as u64
  26|             ^ salt
  27|             ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
  28|             ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(31),
  29|     )
  30| }
  31| 
  32| pub(crate) fn unit(hash: u64) -> f32 {
  33|     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
  34| }
  35| 
  36| pub(crate) fn stable_id(seed: u32, kind: AnomalyKind, anchor_x: i64, anchor_z: i64) -> u64 {
  37|     hash(
  38|         seed,
  39|         0xA110_4A1E_0000_0000 | kind as u64,
  40|         anchor_x,
  41|         anchor_z,
  42|     )
  43| }

   1| //! World-lattice planner for region-spanning Level 0 anomalies.
   2| //!
   3| //! Macro candidates live on a 160-unit lattice. Regions merely query that
   4| //! lattice, so overlapping region and chunk requests recover identical
   5| //! instance IDs, footprints, internal phases, and traversal gates.
   6| 
   7| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
   8|     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, ArchBehavior, ArchLayout, ArchProfile, Axis2, AxisDirection,
   9|     OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, PillarLattice, PitLattice, QuarterTurn, TraversalGate,
  10|     TraversalGateKind, WorldBounds,
  11| };
  12| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  13| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  14| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  15| use crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields;
  16| 
  17| use super::determinism::{hash, mix64, snap, stable_id, unit};
  18| 
  19| /// The anomaly lattice *is* the world-graph lattice, so anomaly anchors and
  20| /// macro-cell fields stay phase-aligned by construction.
  21| const MACRO_CELL: f32 = crate::domain::entities::world_topology::MACRO_CELL_SIZE;
  22| const MAX_QUERY_MARGIN: f32 = 400.0;
  23| 
  24| fn weighted_family(config: &GeneratorConfig, sample: f32) -> Option<AnomalyKind> {
  25|     let tuning = config.anomalies;
  26|     let weights = [
  27|         (AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse, tuning.pillar_expanses.max(0.0)),
  28|         (AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse, tuning.blackouts.max(0.0)),
  29|         (AnomalyKind::PitLattice, tuning.pit_lattices.max(0.0)),
  30|         (AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom, tuning.archways.max(0.0)),
  31|     ];
  32|     let total: f32 = weights.iter().map(|(_, weight)| weight).sum();
  33|     if total <= 0.0 {
  34|         return None;
  35|     }
  36| 
  37|     let mut cursor = sample * total;
  38|     for (kind, weight) in weights {
  39|         if cursor < weight {
  40|             return Some(kind);
  41|         }
  42|         cursor -= weight;
  43|     }
  44|     Some(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse)
  45| }
  46| 
  47| fn remap_gates(instance: &AnomalyInstance) -> Vec<TraversalGate> {
  48|     let (step, first, last) = match instance.kind {
  49|         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => {
  50|             let bay = instance.pillar_lattice.map_or(4.0, |lattice| lattice.bay_x);
  51|             (
  52|                 bay * 4.0,
  53|                 -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
  54|                 instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
  55|             )
  56|         }
  57|         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
  58|             22.0,
  59|             -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
  60|             instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
  61|         ),
  62|         _ => return Vec::new(),
  63|     };
  64| 
  65|     let mut gates = Vec::new();
  66|     let mut local_x = snap((first / step).ceil() * step);
  67|     let world_bounds = instance.footprint.bounds();
  68|     let axis = instance.basis.local_axis_in_world(Axis2::X);
  69|     while local_x <= last {
  70|         let at = instance.world_coords(local_x, 0.0);
  71|         let (plane, span_min, span_max) = match axis {
  72|             Axis2::X => (at.x, world_bounds.min_z, world_bounds.max_z),
  73|             Axis2::Z => (at.z, world_bounds.min_x, world_bounds.max_x),
  74|         };
  75|         let gate_index = (local_x / step).round() as i64;
  76|         gates.push(TraversalGate {
  77|             id: mix64(instance.id ^ (gate_index as u64).rotate_left(23) ^ 0x6A7E),
  78|             instance_id: instance.id,
  79|             anomaly_kind: instance.kind,
  80|             kind: TraversalGateKind::Remap,
  81|             axis,
  82|             plane,
  83|             span_min,
  84|             span_max,
  85|             forward: AxisDirection::Positive,
  86|             affected_bounds: world_bounds,
  87|         });
  88|         local_x += step;
  89|     }
  90|     gates
  91| }
  92| 
  93| fn macro_instance(
  94|     seed: u32,
  95|     anchor_x: i64,
  96|     anchor_z: i64,
  97|     kind: AnomalyKind,
  98|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  99| ) -> AnomalyInstance {
 100|     let id = stable_id(seed, kind, anchor_x, anchor_z);
 101|     let h = |salt| hash(seed, salt, anchor_x, anchor_z);
 102|     let size_scale = config.anomalies.size.clamp(0.5, 2.0);
 103|     let center_x = snap((anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC1)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
 104|     let center_z = snap((anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC2)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
 105|     let basis = OrthoBasis {
 106|         turn: if h(0xC3) & 1 == 0 {
 107|             QuarterTurn::Zero
 108|         } else {
 109|             QuarterTurn::Clockwise
 110|         },
 111|     };
 112|     let (half_x, half_z, entry_band, skeleton_half_width) = match kind {
 113|         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => (
 114|             snap((75.0 + 85.0 * unit(h(0xD1))) * size_scale),
 115|             snap((55.0 + 65.0 * unit(h(0xD2))) * size_scale),
 116|             16.0,
 117|             2.0,
 118|         ),
 119|         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
 120|             snap((65.0 + 70.0 * unit(h(0xD3))) * size_scale),
 121|             snap((50.0 + 55.0 * unit(h(0xD4))) * size_scale),
 122|             12.0,
 123|             2.0,
 124|         ),
 125|         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => (
 126|             snap((32.0 + 30.0 * unit(h(0xD5))) * size_scale),
 127|             snap((28.0 + 25.0 * unit(h(0xD6))) * size_scale),
 128|             6.0,
 129|             1.8,
 130|         ),
 131|         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => (
 132|             snap(4.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD7))),
 133|             snap(5.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD8))),
 134|             0.0,
 135|             0.0,
 136|         ),
 137|         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms are planned from assemblies"),
 138|     };
 139|     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
 140|         center: Position::new(center_x, center_z),
 141|         half_x,
 142|         half_z,
 143|         basis,
 144|     };
 145|     // "Occasionally, one will come across massive pillar rooms -- they can
 146|     // sometimes stretch for miles and will always appear in a lattice or
 147|     // grid pattern." The grid is the canon part and stays. The rest was
 148|     // not massive: a 1.2--1.6 u pillar every 3.6--4.8 u left barely two
 149|     // units of clearance, so the room played as a thicket you push through
 150|     // rather than a hall you are lost in -- and with only two possible
 151|     // sizes, every pillar in it was one of two objects.
 152|     //
 153|     // A bay you can see down, and pillars with the mass to block what is
 154|     // behind them. Each room draws its own bay and its own range of sizes,
 155|     // so one is a forest of squat piers and the next a colonnade of slabs.
 156|     let pillar_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse).then(|| {
 157|         let min_side = snap(1.2 + 0.8 * unit(h(0xE5)));
 158|         PillarLattice {
 159|             bay_x: snap(7.2 + 3.6 * unit(h(0xE1))),
 160|             bay_z: snap(7.2 + 3.6 * unit(h(0xE2))),
 161|             phase_x: snap((unit(h(0xE3)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
 162|             phase_z: snap((unit(h(0xE4)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
 163|             min_side,
 164|             max_side: snap(min_side + 1.2 + 1.6 * unit(h(0xE6))),
 165|             variation_seed: id ^ 0xA111_AA55_u64,
 166|         }
 167|     });
 168|     let pit_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PitLattice).then(|| PitLattice {
 169|         spacing_x: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF1))),
 170|         spacing_z: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF2))),
 171|         phase_x: snap(unit(h(0xF3)) * 1.2),
 172|         phase_z: snap(unit(h(0xF4)) * 1.2),
 173|         side: snap(0.8 + 0.2 * unit(h(0xF5))),
 174|         depth: 2.4,
 175|     });
 176|     let arch = (kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom).then(|| {
 177|         // Most arch rooms are walk-through connectors; the sheltered dead
 178|         // end is the rarer find. Both stay immutable anchors.
 179|         let layout = if unit(h(0xA0)) < 0.7 {
 180|             ArchLayout::Transition
 181|         } else {
 182|             ArchLayout::DeadEnd
 183|         };
 184|         // Transition rooms are graph connectors: most stay plain anchors,
 185|         // but some are seams into another culture or scale. A dead end
 186|         // connects nothing, so it never claims a seam behavior.
 187|         let behavior = if layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
 188|             ArchBehavior::Anchor
 189|         } else {
 190|             match unit(h(0xA4)) {
 191|                 v if v < 0.40 => ArchBehavior::Anchor,
 192|                 v if v < 0.75 => ArchBehavior::CultureSeam,
 193|                 _ => ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach,
 194|             }
 195|         };
 196|         // Every instance is its own arcade: rhythm, clear width, springing
 197|         // height, and blind cadence all vary, so no two arch rooms present
 198|         // the same silhouette — yet every non-blind opening stays walkable
 199|         // (the opening is capped so piers survive, and the head springs at
 200|         // standing height before rising toward the center).
 201|         let bay = snap(2.4 + 2.0 * unit(h(0xA1)));
 202|         ArchProfile {
 203|             layout,
 204|             behavior,
 205|             bay,
 206|             opening: snap((1.4 + 1.4 * unit(h(0xA2))).min(bay - 0.8)),
 207|             blind_every: 3 + (h(0xA3) % 4) as u8,
 208|             spring_units: ((2.0 + 0.8 * unit(h(0xA5))) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
 209|         }
 210|     });
 211|     let mut instance = AnomalyInstance {
 212|         id,
 213|         kind,
 214|         footprint,
 215|         basis,
 216|         macro_anchor: (anchor_x, anchor_z),
 217|         pillar_lattice,
 218|         pit_lattice,
 219|         arch,
 220|         gates: Vec::new(),
 221|         skeleton_half_width,
 222|         entry_band,
 223|     };
 224|     instance.gates = remap_gates(&instance);
 225|     instance
 226| }
 227| 
 228| fn forced_instance(
 229|     seed: u32,
 230|     query: WorldBounds,
 231|     protected_point: Position,
 232|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 233| ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
 234|     let kind = config.anomalies.forced_kind?;
 235|     if kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom {
 236|         return None;
 237|     }
 238| 
 239|     if kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom {
 240|         // A forced anchor is moved next to the protected point so it is both
 241|         // resident and visible; organic anchors keep their macro-cell center.
 242|         let center = Position::new(snap(protected_point.x + 10.0), snap(protected_point.z));
 243|         let anchor_x = (center.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 244|         let anchor_z = (center.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 245|         let mut instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
 246|         instance.footprint.center = center;
 247|         return instance
 248|             .footprint
 249|             .bounds()
 250|             .intersects(query)
 251|             .then_some(instance);
 252|     }
 253| 
 254|     let anchor_x = (protected_point.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 255|     let anchor_z = (protected_point.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 256|     let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
 257|     instance
 258|         .footprint
 259|         .bounds()
 260|         .intersects(query)
 261|         .then_some(instance)
 262| }
 263| 
 264| pub(crate) fn plan_macro_anomalies(
 265|     seed: u32,
 266|     query: WorldBounds,
 267|     protected_point: Position,
 268|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 269|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 270| ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
 271|     let mut instances: Vec<_> = forced_instance(seed, query, protected_point, config)
 272|         .into_iter()
 273|         .collect();
 274|     if config.anomalies.frequency <= 0.0 {
 275|         return instances;
 276|     }
 277| 
 278|     let expanded = query.expanded(MAX_QUERY_MARGIN);
 279|     let anchor_x_min = (expanded.min_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 280|     let anchor_x_max = (expanded.max_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 281|     let anchor_z_min = (expanded.min_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 282|     let anchor_z_max = (expanded.max_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
 283|     let base_chance = (0.20 * config.anomalies.frequency.clamp(0.0, 4.0)).min(0.75);
 284| 
 285|     for anchor_z in anchor_z_min..=anchor_z_max {
 286|         for anchor_x in anchor_x_min..=anchor_x_max {
 287|             // The macro anomaly-pressure field clusters candidates: quiet
 288|             // territory thins toward 0.4× the base chance and pressured
 289|             // territory rises toward 1.6×, so anomalies arrive in loose
 290|             // constellations instead of a uniform sprinkle. The field is a
 291|             // pure world function, so every query that can see this anchor
 292|             // computes the identical decision.
 293|             let pressure = sample_fields(
 294|                 noise,
 295|                 seed,
 296|                 (anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
 297|                 (anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
 298|             )
 299|             .anomaly_pressure;
 300|             let chance = base_chance * (0.40 + 1.20 * pressure);
 301|             let candidate = hash(seed, 0xCAAD_1DA7, anchor_x, anchor_z);
 302|             if unit(candidate) >= chance {
 303|                 continue;
 304|             }
 305|             let Some(kind) = weighted_family(config, unit(candidate.rotate_left(21))) else {
 306|                 continue;
 307|             };
 308|             let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
 309|             if !instance.footprint.bounds().intersects(query) {
 310|                 continue;
 311|             }
 312|             // Organic candidates honor the opening-region keep-out. Forced
 313|             // candidates intentionally bypass it for developer inspection.
 314|             if instance
 315|                 .footprint
 316|                 .bounds()
 317|                 .expanded(48.0)
 318|                 .contains(protected_point.x, protected_point.z)
 319|             {
 320|                 continue;
 321|             }
 322|             instances.push(instance);
 323|         }
 324|     }
 325|     instances
 326| }

macro_planner.rs analysis:
- `plan_macro_anomalies`: query expanded by MAX_QUERY_MARGIN 400 → region query 80u expands to 880u → anchors from -5..+5 → up to 11×11 = 121 anchors per region query. For each anchor: `sample_fields` (18 noise evals) + hash + possibly `macro_instance`. So ~121 × 18 = 2178 noise evals per region plan! And note this runs for EVERY region plan (in generate_region_plan → plan_anomalies_for_region). With a window of ~9-25 regions per chunk, that's ~20k-55k noise evals per chunk, all re-derived per chunk when not using WorldBlock plans... wait, no: region plans are only re-derived per chunk in the streaming path (level_zero finding). When using a WorldBlock, the plans are built once. But in the browser worker pipeline, is generate_from_plans used? Per the head-start: "RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk built on EVERY chunk generation inside generate_from_plans -> re-plans region window (incl red room commitment) per chunk". So the streaming path (and possibly the browser path) re-plans per chunk.

This is a significant constant factor: per region plan, plan_macro_anomalies costs 121 anchor samples × 18 noise = ~2178 noise calls. Per chunk window of 3×3 to 5×5 regions = 9-25 region plans = 20k-55k noise calls, most of them repeated across chunks (the same anchors get re-sampled since windows overlap). Plus region plan itself costs the layout solver etc.

Hmm wait — but is it really 121 anchors? MAX_QUERY_MARGIN = 400.0; the region query is 80×80, expanded by 400 on each side → 880×880. MACRO_CELL = 160. So anchors: 880/160 = 5.5 → ceil = 6 per axis → up to 7×7=49... floor of (min/160) to floor of (max/160): range 880u wide → 5 or 6 cells per axis → ~36-49 anchors. Still ~49 × 18 = ~880 noise evals per region. Per chunk window ~9-25 regions → 8k-22k noise evals per chunk. Each noise eval in SimpleNoiseProvider — let me check its cost (frameworks_drivers/simple_noise.rs). It's likely a few octaves of value noise. Anyway, this is the "redundant recomputation" theme: the same anomaly candidates are re-derived for every overlapping region query and every chunk. A per-anchor memo cache (keyed by (seed, anchor)) or caching in the window would eliminate this. This is Medium/High depending on noise cost. Also note `plan_anomalies_for_region` in anomalies/mod.rs is called once per region plan.

Also `remap_gates` — O(span/step) gates, small.

Now geometry.rs for anomalies (25KB — the biggest). Let me read it.

  22| /// Mutable anomaly infill uses a stable content tile for its seam guard. The

  27|     instance: &'a AnomalyInstance,
  28|     noise: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,

  42| /// Sample one immutable macro anomaly or stable archway anchor.
  43| ///
  44| /// Corridors have already won composition priority before this function is
  45| /// called, so every family may assume its protected bearing route is the only
  46| /// remaining cross-cutting circulation concern. Blackout expanses delegate
  47| /// their substrate to the ordinary Level 0 fabric sampler before applying the
  48| /// anomaly profile.
  49| pub(crate) fn sample_anomaly(
  50|     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
  51|     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  52|     seed: u32,
  53|     config: &GeneratorConfig,
  54|     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  55|     world_x: f32,
  56|     world_z: f32,
  57| ) -> ColumnPlan {
  58|     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
  59|     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
  60|     let seam_x = world_x.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
  61|     let seam_z = world_z.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
  62|     let context = SampleContext {
  63|         instance,
  64|         noise,
  65|         seed,
  66|         config,
  67|         reality,
  68|         world_x,
  69|         world_z,
  70|         local_x,
  71|         local_z,
  72|         boundary,
  73|         perimeter: boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T,
  74|         skeleton: local_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width,
  75|         away_from_seam: seam_x > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
  76|             && seam_x < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
  77|             && seam_z > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
  78|             && seam_z < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0,
  79|     };
  80| 
  81|     match instance.kind {
  82|         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => sample_pillar_expanse(&context),
  83|         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => sample_blackout_expanse(&context),
  84|         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => sample_pit_lattice(&context),
  85|         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => sample_archway_anchor(&context),
  86|         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms have a dedicated geometry sampler"),
  87|     }
  88| }

  90| /// Dehydration multiplies mutable-infill probability: tier 3 nearly
  91| /// doubles how much anomalous mass a re-dealt space grows.
  92| fn delirium_gain(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> f32 {
  93|     1.0 + 0.3 * reality.delirium() as f32
  94| }
  95| 
  96| fn anomaly_hash(instance: &AnomalyInstance, epoch: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> f32 {
  97|     let mut hash = instance.id
  98|         ^ salt
  99|         ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(19)
 100|         ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
 101|         ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(37);
 102|     hash ^= hash >> 30;
 103|     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
 104|     hash ^= hash >> 27;
 105|     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
 106|     hash ^= hash >> 31;
 107|     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
 108| }

 110| fn remap_epoch(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
 111|     let state = context.instance.state(context.reality)?;
 112|     (state.epoch > 0
 113|         && context.boundary > context.instance.entry_band
 114|         && state.point_is_in_wake(
 115|             context.world_x,
 116|             context.world_z,
 117|             context.config.anomalies.remap_distance,
 118|         ))
 119|     .then_some(state.epoch)
 120| }

 122| fn sample_pillar_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
 123|     let instance = context.instance;
 124|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
 125|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
 126|     let lattice = instance.pillar_lattice.expect("pillar instance lattice");
 127|     // A pillar stands *on* a lattice line, straddling it, so the column
 128|     // that owns it is the nearest line — `round`, not `floor`. Under
 129|     // `floor` the four quadrants of one pillar fell into four different
 130|     // bays and each looked up its own size, which is why pillars came out
 131|     // as stepped, L-shaped masses that read as two or three blocks fused.
 132|     // That was invisible while every pillar was the same size and became
 133|     // obvious the moment they were not: the bug was always there, the
 134|     // uniformity was hiding it.
 135|     let mut off_x = local_x - lattice.phase_x;
 136|     let off_z = local_z - lattice.phase_z;
 137|     let cell_z = (off_z / lattice.bay_z).round() as i64;
 138| 
 139|     // Distortion grows only after the entry has taught the player a regular
 140|     // grid. The route and entry band therefore remain a reliable baseline.
 141|     // Every decision here is about *this pillar* — drop it, fatten it,
 142|     // shift its row — so each is answered once, against the row's own
 143|     // budget rather than a budget that varies across the pillar's own
 144|     // footprint.
 145|     let row_centre = instance.world_coords(
 146|         lattice.phase_x + off_x,
 147|         lattice.phase_z + cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z,
 148|     );
 149|     let budget = ((instance.boundary_distance(row_centre.x, row_centre.z) - instance.entry_band)
 150|         / (instance.entry_band.max(8.0) * 2.5))
 151|         .clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 152|     let immutable_zone = context.skeleton || budget <= 0.0;
 153|     // A shifted row moves the whole line of pillars half a bay across.
 154|     // Decided before the column index is taken, so the shift moves which
 155|     // pillar this is rather than tearing the one it lands on.
 156|     if !immutable_zone && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D1, cell_z, 0) < 0.30 * budget {
 157|         off_x += lattice.bay_x * 0.5;
 158|     }
 159|     let cell_x = (off_x / lattice.bay_x).round() as i64;
 160|     let mut shape = instance
 161|         .pillar_shape(cell_x, cell_z)
 162|         .unwrap_or(PillarShape {
 163|             half_x: 0.6,
 164|             half_z: 0.6,
 165|             cross: None,
 166|         });
 167| 
 168|     // The protected bearing lane is a route the wanderer can trust, and it
 169|     // is cut before anything is built rather than after: a pillar the lane
 170|     // passes through is not built at all. Clipping it instead left a thin
 171|     // cap of masonry on each side of the route — debris, and precisely the
 172|     // kind of fragment that reads as a mistake rather than as a building.
 173|     let reach_z = shape
 174|         .cross
 175|         .map_or(shape.half_z, |(_, hz)| shape.half_z.max(hz));
 176|     let line_z = lattice.phase_z + cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z;
 177|     let mut dropped = line_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width + reach_z;
 178|     let mut nudge_x = 0.0f32;
 179|     if !immutable_zone {
 180|         dropped |= anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D0, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.10 * budget;
 181|         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D2, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.08 * budget {
 182|             shape = shape.grown(0.2);
 183|         }
 184|     }
 185| 
 186|     // A committed wake may change relationships between bays, but never at a
 187|     // stable content-tile seam where resident reality cohorts meet.
 188|     let wake_epoch = (!immutable_zone && context.away_from_seam)
 189|         .then(|| remap_epoch(context))
 190|         .flatten();
 191|     if let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
 192|         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F4, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.25 {
 193|             shape = shape.grown(0.2);
 194|         }
 195|         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F5, cell_z, cell_x) < 0.35 {
 196|             // Off its line, and off it as one piece: the pillar moves, it
 197|             // does not smear.
 198|             nudge_x = 0.4;
 199|         }
 200|     }
 201| 
 202|     let dx = (off_x - cell_x as f32 * lattice.bay_x - nudge_x).abs();
 203|     let dz = (off_z - cell_z as f32 * lattice.bay_z).abs();
 204|     let mut solid = context.perimeter || (!dropped && shape.covers(dx, dz));
 205|     if !solid && let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
 206|         let edge_x = dx < PLAN_WALL_T;
 207|         let edge_z = dz < PLAN_WALL_T;
 208|         let threshold =
 209|             (0.12 * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity * delirium_gain(context.reality))
 210|                 .clamp(0.0, 0.48);
 211|         solid = (edge_x && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F1, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold)
 212|             || (edge_z && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F2, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold);
 213|     }
 214|     if context.skeleton {
 215|         solid = false;
 216|     }
 217| 
 218|     let lane_light =
 219|         local_z.abs() < 0.45 && (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
 220|     let field_light = (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
 221|         && (local_z + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
 222|         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11A7, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.62 * tuning.lights;
 223|     let ceiling_units = if !immutable_zone
 224|         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D3, cell_x / 2, cell_z / 2) < 0.35 * budget
 225|     {
 226|         4.0
 227|     } else {
 228|         4.2
 229|     };
 230|     let fixture = (!solid && (lane_light || field_light)).then_some(FixtureSample {
 231|         id: (instance.id as u64) << 32 ^ ((cell_x as u64) << 16) ^ (cell_z as u64 & 0xFFFF),
 232|         kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
 233|         state: FixtureState::Lit,
 234|         center_x: context.world_x,
 235|         center_z: context.world_z,
 236|         half_x: 0.3,
 237|         half_z: 0.3,
 238|         ceiling_units,
 239|         red_room: false,
 240|     });
 241|     ColumnPlan {
 242|         fixture,
 243|         solid,
 244|         ceiling_units,
 245|         floor_material: EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel(),
 246|         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
 247|     }
 248| }
