 250| fn sample_blackout_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
 251|     let instance = context.instance;
 252|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
 253|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
 254|     // The blackout substrate is ordinary fabric under the profile — and it
 255|     // drifts under the same Peripheral Shift stamps as ordinary fabric. In
 256|     // here the engine also advances drift *behind the player in real time*
 257|     // (the darkness hides the swap), so a blackout rearranges more cruelly
 258|     // than the level outside it: turning around is never a way back.
 259|     let mut plan = BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
 260|         context.noise,
 261|         context.seed ^ instance.id as u32,
 262|         tuning,
 263|         context.reality,
 264|         context.world_x,
 265|         context.world_z,
 266|     );
 267|     let depth = instance.normalized_depth(context.world_x, context.world_z);
 268|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::blackout(depth);
 269|     plan.wall_material = profile.wall_voxel();
 270| 
 271|     // Ordinary fixtures thin through the approach instead of cutting directly
 272|     // to black, so the darkness is spatially earned.
 273|     if depth <= 0.22 {
 274|         let cell_x = (context.world_x / 2.8).floor() as i64;
 275|         let cell_z = (context.world_z / 2.8).floor() as i64;
 276|         let keep = 1.0 - depth / 0.22;
 277|         let has_fixture = anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xFADE, cell_x, cell_z) < keep;
 278|         plan.fixture = has_fixture.then_some(FixtureSample {
 279|             id: ((instance.id as u64) << 32)
 280|                 ^ ((cell_x as u64) << 16)
 281|                 ^ (cell_z as u64)
 282|                 ^ 0xFADE_C0DE_0000_0000,
 283|             kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
 284|             state: FixtureState::Lit,
 285|             center_x: context.world_x,
 286|             center_z: context.world_z,
 287|             half_x: 0.3,
 288|             half_z: 0.3,
 289|             ceiling_units: plan.ceiling_units,
 290|             red_room: false,
 291|         });
 292|     } else {
 293|         plan.fixture = None;
 294|     }
 295|     plan.ceiling_units = if depth > 0.68 {
 296|         2.6
 297|     } else if depth > 0.35 {
 298|         3.0
 299|     } else {
 300|         3.4
 301|     };
 302| 
 303|     if profile.floor == FloorState::RecessedFluid && !plan.solid && !context.skeleton {
 304|         let cell = 7.2;
 305|         let basin_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
 306|         let basin_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
 307|         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xF10D, basin_x, basin_z) < 0.22
 308|             && local_x.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
 309|             && local_z.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
 310|         {
 311|             plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
 312|         }
 313|     }
 314| 
 315|     plan.solid |= context.perimeter;
 316|     if context.skeleton {
 317|         plan.solid = false;
 318|         plan.fixture =
 319|             (local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45 && tuning.lights > 0.0).then_some(FixtureSample {
 320|                 id: (instance.id as u64) << 16 ^ 0xCA71_C001,
 321|                 kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentStrip,
 322|                 state: FixtureState::Lit,
 323|                 center_x: context.world_x,
 324|                 center_z: context.world_z,
 325|                 half_x: 0.3,
 326|                 half_z: 0.3,
 327|                 ceiling_units: plan.ceiling_units,
 328|                 red_room: false,
 329|             });
 330|         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
 331|         return plan;
 332|     }
 333| 
 334|     // Deception is nearly unbounded on purpose: blackouts are meant to be
 335|     // almost impossible to walk out of, so decoy glimmers may heavily
 336|     // outnumber the honest skeleton — and a delirious wanderer sees more
 337|     // liars still.
 338|     let decoys = (context.config.anomalies.blackout_decoys
 339|         + 0.03 * context.reality.delirium() as f32)
 340|         .clamp(0.0, 0.95);

 341|     let off_lane = (local_z.abs() - (instance.skeleton_half_width + 7.2)).abs() < 0.45;
 342|     if off_lane
 343|         && depth > 0.3
 344|         && local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45
 345|         && tuning.lights > 0.0
 346|         && anomaly_hash(
 347|             instance,
 348|             0,
 349|             0xDEC0,
 350|             (local_x / 28.0).floor() as i64,
 351|             local_z.is_sign_negative() as i64,
 352|         ) < decoys
 353|     {
 354|         plan.fixture = Some(FixtureSample {
 355|             id: (instance.id as u64) << 16 ^ 0xDEC0_0001,
 356|             kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
 357|             state: FixtureState::Lit,
 358|             center_x: context.world_x,
 359|             center_z: context.world_z,
 360|             half_x: 0.3,
 361|             half_z: 0.3,
 362|             ceiling_units: plan.ceiling_units,
 363|             red_room: false,
 364|         });
 365|         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
 366|     }
 367| 
 368|     if context.away_from_seam
 369|         && let Some(epoch) = remap_epoch(context)
 370|     {
 371|         let cell = 7.2;
 372|         let cell_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
 373|         let cell_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
 374|         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(cell);
 375|         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(cell);
 376|         let edge = within_x < PLAN_WALL_T || within_z < PLAN_WALL_T;
 377|         let threshold =
 378|             (0.20 * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity * delirium_gain(context.reality))
 379|                 .clamp(0.0, 0.65);
 380|         if edge && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0xB1AC, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold {
 381|             plan.solid = true;
 382|             plan.fixture = None;
 383|         }
 384|     }
 385| 
 386|     // The dark owns a structural layer the Peripheral Shift re-deals: past
 387|     // the approach band, room-scale partitions stand on the instance's own
 388|     // lattice. Their epoch comes from the fabric drift stamps, so the
 389|     // engine's rear shift does not merely nudge 0.4 u fabric bands — it
 390|     // rearranges *rooms* behind the player. Every drawn partition is
 391|     // pierced by its own doorway, so no shift can seal space it creates,
 392|     // and the recovery skeleton stays exempt below.
 393|     if depth > 0.25 && !context.skeleton && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
 394|         const PARTITION_CELL: f32 = 9.6;
 395|         let cell_x = (local_x / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
 396|         let cell_z = (local_z / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
 397|         let anchor = instance.world_coords(
 398|             (cell_x as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
 399|             (cell_z as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
 400|         );
 401|         let epoch = context.reality.fabric_drift_epoch(anchor.x, anchor.z);
 402|         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
 403|         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
 404|         for (in_band, along, wall_salt, door_salt) in [
 405|             (within_x < PLAN_WALL_T, within_z, 0xB1D0u64, 0xB1D1u64),
 406|             (within_z < PLAN_WALL_T, within_x, 0xB1D2u64, 0xB1D3u64),
 407|         ] {
 408|             if !in_band {
 409|                 continue;
 410|             }
 411|             if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, wall_salt, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.5 {
 412|                 let gap = anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, door_salt, cell_x, cell_z);
 413|                 let gap_pos = 0.8 + (PARTITION_CELL - 3.2) * gap;
 414|                 if along < gap_pos || along >= gap_pos + 1.6 {
 415|                     plan.solid = true;
 416|                     plan.fixture = None;
 417|                 }
 418|             }
 419|         }
 420|     }
 421|     plan
 422| }

 431|         && context.boundary > lattice.side
 432|         && dx < lattice.side * 0.5
 433|         && dz < lattice.side * 0.5;

 435|         && context.local_x.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
 436|         && context.local_z.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
 437|         && context.config.tuning.lights > 0.0;

 440|         solid: context.perimeter,

 442|             id: (context.instance.id as u64) ^ 0x0107_0000_0000,
 443|             kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
 444|             state: FixtureState::Lit,

 448|             half_z: 0.3,

 456| /// Stable pale arch rooms never inspect `RealitySnapshot`, which keeps them a
 457| /// fixed landmark against every mutable anomaly family.
 458| ///
 459| /// A `Transition` room is a *graph connector*: its `ArchBehavior` decides
 460| /// what its far half (local `z > 0`) belongs to. The seam is expressed only
 461| /// through legal architectural vocabulary — ceiling regime, floor finish,
 462| /// lintel height, fixture rhythm — never through impossible collision or a
 463| /// repainted wall, so the crossing is felt before it is understood.
 464| fn sample_archway_anchor(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
 465|     let instance = context.instance;
 466|     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
 467|     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
 468|     let arch = instance.arch.expect("arch instance profile");
 469|     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::archway_room();
 470|     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
 471|     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
 472| 
 473|     // The far half of a seam room disagrees with the near half.
 474|     let far_side = local_z > 0.0;
 475|     let (ceiling_units, floor_material) = match arch.behavior {
 476|         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => {
 477|             (3.0, EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel())
 478|         }
 479|         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => (4.4, profile.floor_voxel()),
 480|         _ => (3.6, profile.floor_voxel()),
 481|     };
 482|     let mut plan = ColumnPlan {
 483|         wall_material: profile.wall_voxel(),
 484|         floor_material,
 485|         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
 486|     };
 487| 
 488|     let bay_index = ((local_x + half_x) / arch.bay).floor() as i64;
 489|     let along = (local_x + half_x).rem_euclid(arch.bay);
 490|     // The far arcade of a scale breach broadens its openings; a culture
 491|     // seam presses its lintels lower. Both stay on the shared bay rhythm so
 492|     // the two walls visibly disagree about the same structure.
 493|     let effective_opening = match arch.behavior {
 494|         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => arch.opening * 1.5,
 495|         _ => arch.opening,
 496|     };
 497|     let head_drop = match arch.behavior {
 498|         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => 0.4,
 499|         _ => 0.0,
 500|     };
 501|     let across_opening = (along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() < effective_opening * 0.5;
 502|     let blind = bay_index.rem_euclid(arch.blind_every as i64) == arch.blind_every as i64 - 1;
 503|     let arch_head = {
 504|         let t = ((along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() / (effective_opening * 0.5)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 505|         (((arch.spring_units - head_drop) + 0.6 * (1.0 - t)) / 0.2).round() * 0.2
 506|     };
 507| 
 508|     if context.perimeter {
 509|         plan.solid = tuning.walls > 0.0;
 510|         let on_long_wall = half_z - local_z.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T;
 511|         match arch.layout {
 512|             ArchLayout::Transition => {
 513|                 if on_long_wall && across_opening && !blind {
 514|                     plan.solid = false;
 515|                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(arch_head);
 516|                 }
 517|             }
 518|             ArchLayout::DeadEnd => {
 519|                 let on_entrance_wall = half_x - local_x.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T && local_x < 0.0;
 520|                 if on_entrance_wall && local_z.abs() < 1.0 {
 521|                     plan.solid = false;
 522|                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(
 523|                         ((arch.spring_units + 0.6 * (1.0 - local_z.abs())) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
 524|                     );
 525|                 }
 526|             }
 527|         }
 528|         return plan;
 529|     }
 530| 
 531|     if arch.layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
 532|         let arcade_plane = half_z - 1.2 - PLAN_WALL_T;
 533|         let in_arcade = (local_z.abs() - arcade_plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5;
 534|         let in_alcove = local_z.abs() > arcade_plane;
 535|         if in_arcade && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
 536|             if across_opening && !blind {
 537|                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(arch_head);
 538|             } else {
 539|                 plan.solid = true;
 540|             }
 541|         } else if in_alcove {
 542|             plan.ceiling_units = 3.0;
 543|             if ((local_x * 2.5).sin() * (local_z * 1.7).cos()).abs() < 0.3 {
 544|                 plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
 545|             }
 546|         }
 547|     }
 548| 
 549|     let has_light = local_z.abs() < 0.45
 550|         && (local_x + half_x - arch.bay * 0.5).rem_euclid(arch.bay * 2.0) < 0.45
 551|         && tuning.lights > 0.0;
 552|     plan.fixture = has_light.then_some(FixtureSample {
 553|         id: (instance.id as u64) ^ 0xA0C1_0000_0000,
 554|         kind: FixtureKind::FluorescentPanel,
 555|         state: FixtureState::Lit,
 556|         center_x: context.world_x,
 557|         center_z: context.world_z,
 558|         half_x: 0.3,
 559|         half_z: 0.3,
 560|         ceiling_units,
 561|         red_room: false,
 562|     });
 563|     let _ = context.boundary;
 564|     plan
 565| }

   1| //! Inward-facing interfaces required by application use cases.

   3| //! Use cases define only the capability they need. Adapters and drivers own

   8| /// `NoiseProvider` is a pure interface for deterministic continuous noise.
   9| /// We use this to evaluate the Macro Field (Drift, Density, Motif Selection).
  10| pub trait NoiseProvider {
  11|     /// Returns a noise value, ideally in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
  12|     /// The function must be deterministic given the same seed and position.
  13|     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32;
  14| }

  16| /// Visual lookup required by use cases that prepare renderer-facing artifacts.
  17| /// The policy lives in an outer adapter; core material ids remain presentation
  18| /// agnostic and tests can inject a tiny deterministic palette.

  20|     fn color(&self, material: u8) -> u32;

  23| /// `TelemetryPort` abstracts wall-clock access and log emission so use cases
  24| /// never touch `std::time` or stdout directly. Both are frameworks concerns,
  25| /// and `SystemTime::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
  26| pub trait TelemetryPort {
  27|     /// Monotonic-ish timestamp in microseconds from an arbitrary epoch.
  28|     /// Only ever used to compute durations, never absolute dates.
  29|     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64;
  30|     /// Emits one log line to whatever sink the outer layer provides.
  31|     fn log(&self, message: &str);
  32| }

  39|         0
  40|     }
  41|     fn log(&self, _message: &str) {}
  42| }

   1| //! Stairwells: the first physical layer of the vertical world graph.
   2| //!
   3| //! The macro topology ([`crate::use_cases::world_topology`]) reserves
   4| //! [`VerticalLink`]s — stair and shaft obligations anchored inside regions.
   5| //! This module realizes the *upward* links as concrete architecture:
   6| //!
   7| //! * [`place_stairwell`] gives the region planner a `SpaceProgram::Stair`
   8| //!   assembly beside its primary corridor, near the link's anchor.
   9| //! * [`apply_stair_profile`] shapes the interior per voxel column: a flat
  10| //!   vestibule, a flight of 0.2 u treads, and a landing. An
  11| //!   [`VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent`] flight never lands — it keeps
  12| //!   rising under a raised, unlit shaft ceiling until the far wall
  13| //!   swallows it in the dark.
  14| //!
  15| //! What this deliberately does **not** do yet: move the player between
  16| //! elevations. The engine's collision world is a fixed-eye-height slider,
  17| //! so a stair is currently a readable, colliding landmark and a topology
  18| //! contract. Downward links (`EndlessDescent`, `ServiceShaft`) stay
  19| //! reservation-only until chunks can stream below elevation 0; realizing
  20| //! them as fake geometry would spend the mystery without paying it off.
  21| //!
  22| //! Geometry invariants (tested in `region_plan` / here):
  23| //! * treads rise monotonically from the entrance, 0.2 u per 0.4 u of run;
  24| //! * headroom above every tread stays >= 2.2 u;
  25| //! * the entrance column itself is always flat and walkable;
  26| //! * the profile is a pure function of world position and the assembly.
  27| 
  28| use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  29|     AssemblyInstance, CeilingPlan, CeilingZone, CorruptionProfile, Fixture, HostId, HostSegment,
  30|     Opening, OpeningId, OpeningRole, Polygon2, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystem,
  31|     StructuralSystemInstance,
  32| };
  33| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  34| use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind};
  35| use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
  36| 
  37| /// Stairwell frontage along its corridor, world units.
  38| const STAIR_WIDTH: f32 = 4.8;
  39| /// Stairwell depth away from the corridor.
  40| const STAIR_DEPTH: f32 = 8.8;
  41| /// Flat entry vestibule before the first riser.
  42| const VESTIBULE_DEPTH: f32 = 2.0;
  43| /// One tread: rise per run, both on the 0.4/0.2 plan lattices.
  44| const TREAD_RUN: f32 = 0.4;
  45| const TREAD_RISE: f32 = 0.2;
  46| /// An ordinary flight lands here (half a story on the macro lattice).
  47| const LANDING_UNITS: f32 = 1.6;
  48| /// An endless ascent keeps climbing to this height before the dark takes it.
  49| const ASCENT_MAX_UNITS: f32 = 3.2;
  50| /// Clear space kept above every tread.
  51| const MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS: f32 = 2.2;
  52| /// Stairwell ceiling: high enough that the top of an endless flight still
  53| /// has headroom, low enough to fit the level's 5.8 u grid.
  54| const STAIR_CEILING_UNITS: f32 = 5.4;
  55| 
  56| fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
  57|     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
  58| }
  59| 
  60| /// Should this link become a stair assembly this iteration? Upward links
  61| /// voxelize; downward links remain graph reservations (see module docs).
  62| pub(crate) fn link_wants_geometry(link: &VerticalLink) -> bool {
  63|     matches!(
  64|         link.kind,
  65|         VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair | VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent
  66|     )
  67| }
  68| 
  69| /// Builds the stairwell assembly for one vertical link, beside a horizontal
  70| /// main-corridor leg. Mirrors the suite-placement contract: returns `None`
  71| /// if the footprint would escape the region, collide with a prior assembly,
  72| /// or swallow another corridor — the reservation then stays unrealized
  73| /// rather than corrupting the plan.
  74| #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  75| pub(crate) fn place_stairwell(
  76|     id: u32,
  77|     link: &VerticalLink,
  78|     legs: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
  79|     origin: Position,
  80|     size: f32,
  81|     edge_margin: f32,
  82|     wall_t: f32,
  83|     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
  84|     corridor_clearance: impl Fn(f32, f32, f32) -> bool,
  85| ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
  86|     // The leg whose axis passes closest to the anchor hosts the stair.
  87|     let (lx0, lx1, lz, lw) = legs.iter().copied().min_by(|a, b| {
  88|         let da = (link.anchor.z - a.2).abs();
  89|         let db = (link.anchor.z - b.2).abs();
  90|         da.total_cmp(&db)
  91|     })?;
  92|     if lx1 - lx0 < STAIR_WIDTH + 8.0 {
  93|         return None;
  94|     }
  95| 
  96|     let side = if link.anchor.z >= lz { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
  97|     // Center the hosted shell on the corridor edge wall. The old placement
  98|     // put the shell beyond that wall, leaving a second independently sampled
  99|     // wall band between corridor and doorway.
 100|     let corridor_half = lw * 0.5 + wall_t * 0.5;
 101|     let x0 = snap((link.anchor.x - STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5).clamp(lx0 + 4.0, lx1 - STAIR_WIDTH - 4.0));
 102|     let z_front = if side > 0.0 {
 103|         lz + corridor_half
 104|     } else {
 105|         lz - corridor_half - STAIR_DEPTH
 106|     };
 107|     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, STAIR_WIDTH, STAIR_DEPTH);
 108|     let b = footprint.bounds();
 109| 
 110|     if b.0 < origin.x + edge_margin
 111|         || b.1 < origin.z + edge_margin
 112|         || b.2 > origin.x + size - edge_margin
 113|         || b.3 > origin.z + size - edge_margin
 114|     {
 115|         return None;
 116|     }
 117|     if taken
 118|         .iter()
 119|         .any(|t| t.0 < b.2 + 0.8 && b.0 < t.2 + 0.8 && t.1 < b.3 + 0.8 && b.1 < t.3 + 0.8)
 120|     {
 121|         return None;
 122|     }
 123|     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
 124|     if !corridor_clearance(center.0, center.1, STAIR_DEPTH.min(STAIR_WIDTH) * 0.25) {
 125|         return None;
 126|     }
 127| 
 128|     // A broad, framed threshold: the stair announces itself as circulation.
 129|     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
 130|     let hosts = HostSegment::rectangular_shell(&footprint, wall_t, STAIR_CEILING_UNITS);
 131|     let openings = vec![Opening {
 132|         id: OpeningId(0),
 133|         host: if side > 0.0 { HostId(0) } else { HostId(2) },
 134|         role: OpeningRole::Entrance,
 135|         center: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), front_z),
 136|         width: 2.4,
 137|         through_x_wall: true,
 138|         lintel_units: Some(2.6),
 139|     }];
 140| 
 141|     // One warm fixture over the vestibule; the flight above stays unlit so
 142|     // the climb visibly leaves the light.
 143|     let vestibule_z = if side > 0.0 {
 144|         b.1 + VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
 145|     } else {
 146|         b.3 - VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
 147|     };
 148|     let fixtures = vec![Fixture {
 149|         at: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), snap(vestibule_z)),
 150|         half_x: 0.4,
 151|         half_z: 0.4,
 152|         lit: true,
 153|     }];
 154| 
 155|     Some(AssemblyInstance {
 156|         id,
 157|         program: SpaceProgram::Stair,
 158|         spaces: Vec::new(),
 159|         // A stair core is circulation: nothing stands on a flight.
 160|         // Core-and-shell: the stair core carries itself; no interior columns
 161|         // may interrupt a flight.
 162|         structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
 163|             system: StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
 164|             bay_x: 4.8,
 165|             bay_z: 4.8,
 166|             phase: (0.0, 0.0),
 167|             column_side: 0.4,
 168|         },
 169|         ceiling: CeilingPlan::flat(CeilingZone {
 170|             area: footprint.clone(),
 171|             language: crate::domain::entities::architecture::CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
 172|             height_units: STAIR_CEILING_UNITS,
 173|         }),
 174|         fixtures,
 175|         service_voids: Vec::new(),
 176|         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
 177|         hosts,
 178|         openings,
 179|         door_leaves: Vec::new(),
 180|         footprint,
 181|     })
 182| }
 183| 
 184| /// Shapes one interior column of a stair assembly: vestibule, flight,
 185| /// landing (or an endless climb). Pure in `(assembly, kind, wx, wz)`.
 186| pub(crate) fn apply_stair_profile(
 187|     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
 188|     kind: VerticalLinkKind,
 189|     plan: &mut ColumnPlan,
 190|     _wx: f32,
 191|     wz: f32,
 192| ) {
 193|     let Some(entrance) = assembly.primary_entrance() else {
 194|         return;
 195|     };
 196|     let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 197|     // Walk axis runs perpendicular to the entrance wall; depth is measured
 198|     // from the entrance side inward.
 199|     let depth_in = if entrance.through_x_wall {
 200|         if (entrance.center.z - b.1).abs() < (entrance.center.z - b.3).abs() {
 201|             wz - b.1
 202|         } else {
 203|             b.3 - wz
 204|         }
 205|     } else {
 206|         // Stairwells are placed with X-wall entrances today; a Z-wall stair
 207|         // would measure along X the same way.
 208|         return;
 209|     };
 210| 
 211|     let target = match kind {
 212|         VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent => ASCENT_MAX_UNITS,
 213|         _ => LANDING_UNITS,
 214|     };
 215|     let treads = ((depth_in - VESTIBULE_DEPTH) / TREAD_RUN).floor().max(0.0);
 216|     let raw = treads * TREAD_RISE;
 217|     plan.floor_units = raw.min(target);
 218|     // Headroom is a hard invariant: the ceiling zone is planned high enough,
 219|     // but clamp anyway so no future ceiling tweak can pinch a flight.
 220|     plan.floor_units = plan
 221|         .floor_units
 222|         .min(plan.ceiling_units - MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS)
 223|         .max(0.0);
 224| 
 225|     // The climb leaves the light: no fixture survives above the first riser,
 226|     // and an endless flight rises into an unlit shaft.
 227|     if plan.floor_units > 0.0 {
 228|         plan.fixture = None;
 229|     }
 230| }

 232| #[cfg(test)]

total: 432
   1| //! Fold an SVO's lower levels into dense bricks.
   2| //!
   3| //! A pointer-chasing SVO stores one voxel per leaf node, so a ray pays a
   4| //! dependent memory fetch at every level of every step, and the bottom of
   5| //! the tree is where almost all the nodes are: a fully populated 4x4x4
   6| //! subtree costs 1 + 8 + 64 = 73 nodes to describe 64 voxels.
   7| //!
   8| //! Laine & Karras' answer is to stop subdividing early and store a dense
   9| //! *brick* at the leaves. Traversal descends to the brick, then indexes
  10| //! straight into contiguous memory -- no pointers, good locality, and a
  11| //! shape a 3D texture can hold. That is the representation the "infinite
  12| //! voxel" demos rely on, and it is the prerequisite for shrinking voxels
  13| //! without the node count exploding.
  14| //!
  15| //! This is derived from a finished [`SparseVoxelOctree`] rather than
  16| //! replacing it, exactly as `compress_svdag` is: the SVO stays the
  17| //! authority for collision, editing and the world-identity digest, and
  18| //! only the GPU upload path consumes bricks.
  19| 
  20| use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
  21| 
  22| /// Voxels along one brick edge.
  23| ///
  24| /// A brick is dense, so it stores air explicitly and the right edge length
  25| /// is decided by how sparse the world actually is. Measured on a real
  26| /// Level 0 chunk (seed 42, `low_spec`), against a 16209-node / 256 KiB SVO:
  27| ///
  28| /// | edge | nodes | GPU     | brick occupancy |
  29| /// |------|-------|---------|-----------------|
  30| /// | 8    |   297 | 440 KiB | 13.1% solid     |
  31| /// | 4    |  1169 | 227 KiB | 27.4% solid     |
  32| ///
  33| /// 8^3 buys a further 4x node cut for 1.9x the memory -- a bad trade in a
  34| /// corridor world that is mostly air. 4^3 still removes 93% of the nodes
  35| /// while coming in *under* the SVO it replaces, so it wins outright.
  36| /// Revisit if voxels shrink: finer voxels raise occupancy per brick and
  37| /// shift the balance back toward 8^3.
  38| pub const BRICK_EDGE: u32 = 4;
  39| /// Octree levels a brick replaces (`BRICK_EDGE == 1 << BRICK_DEPTH`).
  40| pub const BRICK_DEPTH: u32 = 2;
  41| /// Voxels held by one brick.
  42| pub const BRICK_VOXELS: usize = (BRICK_EDGE * BRICK_EDGE * BRICK_EDGE) as usize;
  43| /// `u32`s per voxel in the brick arena.
  44| pub const WORDS_PER_VOXEL: usize = 2;
  45| /// `u32`s occupied by one brick.
  46| pub const WORDS_PER_BRICK: usize = BRICK_VOXELS * WORDS_PER_VOXEL;
  47| 
  48| /// One node of the bricked hierarchy.
  49| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  50| pub enum BrickNode {
  51|     /// Eight children stored contiguously from `child_base`. `child_mask`
  52|     /// bit `i` is clear when child `i` is entirely air.
  53|     Internal { child_base: u32, child_mask: u8 },
  54|     /// A dense `BRICK_EDGE^3` block starting at `word_base` in the arena.
  55|     Brick { word_base: u32 },
  56|     /// A subtree that is one repeated voxel. Storing it as a node instead
  57|     /// of a brick is what keeps solid walls and open air nearly free.
  58|     Uniform {
  59|         voxel_type: u8,
  60|         color: u32,
  61|         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
  62|         face_occlusion: u8,
  63|     },
  64| }
  65| 
  66| /// A bricked view of an octree, ready for GPU upload.
  67| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  68| pub struct BrickPool {
  69|     pub root: u32,
  70|     pub nodes: Vec<BrickNode>,
  71|     /// Packed voxel payloads, `WORDS_PER_BRICK` per brick.
  72|     ///
  73|     /// word 0: `color` in bits 0..24, `voxel_type` in bits 24..32
  74|     /// word 1: `face_occlusion` in bits 0..8, then r/g/b light nibbles at
  75|     ///         bits 8, 12 and 16
  76|     pub voxels: Vec<u32>,
  77|     pub depth: u32,
  78|     pub world_size: f32,
  79| }
  80| 
  81| impl BrickPool {
  82|     pub fn brick_count(&self) -> usize {
  83|         self.voxels.len() / WORDS_PER_BRICK
  84|     }
  85| 
  86|     /// Bytes the GPU upload would occupy, for comparison against the
  87|     /// four-words-per-node encoding this replaces.
  88|     pub fn gpu_bytes(&self) -> usize {
  89|         self.nodes.len() * 4 * 4 + self.voxels.len() * 4
  90|     }
  91| 
  92|     /// Reads back a voxel, so the pool can be proven equivalent to the
  93|     /// octree it came from.
  94|     pub fn get(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
  95|         let extent = 1u32 << self.depth;
  96|         if x >= extent || y >= extent || z >= extent {
  97|             return None;
  98|         }
  99|         Some(self.get_from(self.root as usize, x, y, z, self.depth))
 100|     }
 101| 
 102|     fn get_from(&self, node: usize, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32, depth: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
 103|         match self.nodes[node] {
 104|             BrickNode::Uniform {
 105|                 voxel_type,
 106|                 color,
 107|                 light_rgb,
 108|                 face_occlusion,
 109|             } => (voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion),
 110|             BrickNode::Brick { word_base } => {
 111|                 let index = brick_offset(x, y, z);
 112|                 let base = word_base as usize + index * WORDS_PER_VOXEL;
 113|                 unpack_voxel(self.voxels[base], self.voxels[base + 1])
 114|             }
 115|             BrickNode::Internal {
 116|                 child_base,
 117|                 child_mask,
 118|             } => {
 119|                 let bit = depth - 1;
 120|                 let octant = octant_index(x, y, z, bit);
 121|                 if child_mask & (1 << octant) == 0 {
 122|                     return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
 123|                 }
 124|                 let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
 125|                 self.get_from(
 126|                     child_base as usize + octant as usize,
 127|                     x & mask,
 128|                     y & mask,
 129|                     z & mask,
 130|                     depth - 1,
 131|                 )
 132|             }
 133|         }
 134|     }
 135| }
 136| 
 137| fn octant_index(x: u32, y: u32, z: u32, bit: u32) -> u32 {
 138|     (((z >> bit) & 1) << 2) | (((y >> bit) & 1) << 1) | ((x >> bit) & 1)
 139| }
 140| 
 141| /// Brick-local linear offset. X varies fastest so a ray stepping along X
 142| /// walks contiguous words.
 143| fn brick_offset(x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> usize {
 144|     let edge = BRICK_EDGE;
 145|     ((z % edge) * edge * edge + (y % edge) * edge + (x % edge)) as usize
 146| }
 147| 
 148| fn pack_voxel(voxel_type: u8, color: u32, light_rgb: [u8; 3], face_occlusion: u8) -> (u32, u32) {
 149|     let word0 = (color & 0x00FF_FFFF) | ((voxel_type as u32) << 24);
 150|     let word1 = face_occlusion as u32
 151|         | ((light_rgb[0] as u32 & 0xF) << 8)
 152|         | ((light_rgb[1] as u32 & 0xF) << 12)
 153|         | ((light_rgb[2] as u32 & 0xF) << 16);
 154|     (word0, word1)
 155| }
 156| 
 157| fn unpack_voxel(word0: u32, word1: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
 158|     let voxel_type = (word0 >> 24) as u8;
 159|     let color = word0 & 0x00FF_FFFF;
 160|     let light_rgb = [
 161|         ((word1 >> 8) & 0xF) as u8,
 162|         ((word1 >> 12) & 0xF) as u8,
 163|         ((word1 >> 16) & 0xF) as u8,
 164|     ];
 165|     (voxel_type, color, light_rgb, (word1 & 0xFF) as u8)
 166| }
 167| 
 168| /// Builds a [`BrickPool`] from a finished octree.
 169| pub fn build_brick_pool(octree: &SparseVoxelOctree) -> BrickPool {
 170|     let mut pool = BrickPool {
 171|         root: 0,
 172|         nodes: Vec::new(),
 173|         voxels: Vec::new(),
 174|         depth: octree.depth,
 175|         world_size: octree.world_size,
 176|     };
 177|     // The root occupies slot 0 so `child_base` runs are contiguous and a
 178|     // subtree can be written into a slot its parent reserved in advance.
 179|     push(&mut pool, EMPTY);
 180|     emit_into(&mut pool, octree, octree.root, octree.depth, 0);
 181|     pool.root = 0;
 182|     pool
 183| }
 184| 
 185| const EMPTY: BrickNode = BrickNode::Uniform {
 186|     voxel_type: 0,
 187|     color: 0,
 188|     light_rgb: [0; 3],
 189|     face_occlusion: 0,
 190| };
 191| 
 192| /// Writes the subtree rooted at `node` into the already-reserved `slot`.
 193| ///
 194| /// Children are reserved as one contiguous run *before* they are filled,
 195| /// so `child_base + octant` stays a direct offset and no node is ever
 196| /// emitted twice.
 197| fn emit_into(
 198|     pool: &mut BrickPool,
 199|     octree: &SparseVoxelOctree,
 200|     node: usize,
 201|     depth: u32,
 202|     slot: usize,
 203| ) {
 204|     if let Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion)) = uniform_value(octree, node) {
 205|         pool.nodes[slot] = BrickNode::Uniform {
 206|             voxel_type,
 207|             color,
 208|             light_rgb,
 209|             face_occlusion,
 210|         };
 211|         return;
 212|     }
 213| 
 214|     if depth <= BRICK_DEPTH {
 215|         // Split the borrows: the brick is built against the voxel arena
 216|         // before the node slot is written.
 217|         let brick = emit_brick(&mut pool.voxels, octree, node, depth);
 218|         pool.nodes[slot] = brick;
 219|         return;
 220|     }
 221| 
 222|     let SvoNode::Internal {
 223|         child_base_index,
 224|         child_mask,
 225|     } = octree.nodes[node]
 226|     else {
 227|         unreachable!("uniform_value already handled every leaf");
 228|     };
 229| 
 230|     let child_base = pool.nodes.len() as u32;
 231|     // Eight slots are reserved even for absent children so the octant
 232|     // index stays a direct offset; absent ones remain air.
 233|     for _ in 0..8 {
 234|         push(pool, EMPTY);
 235|     }
 236|     pool.nodes[slot] = BrickNode::Internal {
 237|         child_base,
 238|         child_mask,
 239|     };
 240|     for octant in 0..8u32 {
 241|         if child_mask & (1 << octant) == 0 {
 242|             continue;
 243|         }
 244|         emit_into(
 245|             pool,
 246|             octree,
 247|             child_base_index as usize + octant as usize,
 248|             depth - 1,
 249|             child_base as usize + octant as usize,
 250|         );
 251|     }
 252| }
 253| 
 254| fn emit_brick(
 255|     voxels: &mut Vec<u32>,
 256|     octree: &SparseVoxelOctree,
 257|     node: usize,
 258|     depth: u32,
 259| ) -> BrickNode {
 260|     let word_base = voxels.len() as u32;
 261|     voxels.resize(voxels.len() + WORDS_PER_BRICK, 0);
 262|     // A subtree shallower than one brick only occupies the low corner;
 263|     // the rest of the brick stays air rather than tiling the subtree.
 264|     let extent = 1u32 << depth;
 265|     for z in 0..BRICK_EDGE.min(extent) {
 266|         for y in 0..BRICK_EDGE.min(extent) {
 267|             for x in 0..BRICK_EDGE.min(extent) {
 268|                 let voxel = sample(octree, node, x, y, z, depth);
 269|                 let (w0, w1) = pack_voxel(voxel.0, voxel.1, voxel.2, voxel.3);
 270|                 let slot = word_base as usize + brick_offset(x, y, z) * WORDS_PER_VOXEL;
 271|                 voxels[slot] = w0;
 272|                 voxels[slot + 1] = w1;
 273|             }
 274|         }
 275|     }
 276|     BrickNode::Brick { word_base }
 277| }
 278| 
 279| /// Reads a voxel out of an octree subtree in that subtree's local frame.
 280| fn sample(
 281|     octree: &SparseVoxelOctree,
 282|     node: usize,
 283|     x: u32,
 284|     y: u32,
 285|     z: u32,
 286|     depth: u32,
 287| ) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
 288|     match octree.nodes[node] {
 289|         SvoNode::Leaf {
 290|             voxel_type,
 291|             color,
 292|             light_rgb,
 293|             face_occlusion,
 294|         } => (voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion),
 295|         SvoNode::Internal {
 296|             child_base_index,
 297|             child_mask,
 298|         } => {
 299|             if depth == 0 {
 300|                 return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
 301|             }
 302|             let bit = depth - 1;
 303|             let octant = octant_index(x, y, z, bit);
 304|             if child_mask & (1 << octant) == 0 {
 305|                 return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
 306|             }
 307|             let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
 308|             sample(
 309|                 octree,
 310|                 child_base_index as usize + octant as usize,
 311|                 x & mask,
 312|                 y & mask,
 313|                 z & mask,
 314|                 depth - 1,
 315|             )
 316|         }
 317|     }
 318| }
 319| 
 320| /// `Some` when the subtree is a single repeated voxel.
 321| fn uniform_value(octree: &SparseVoxelOctree, node: usize) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
 322|     match octree.nodes[node] {
 323|         SvoNode::Leaf {
 324|             voxel_type,
 325|             color,
 326|             light_rgb,
 327|             face_occlusion,
 328|         } => Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion)),
 329|         SvoNode::Internal { child_mask, .. } if child_mask == 0 => Some((0, 0, [0; 3], 0)),
 330|         SvoNode::Internal { .. } => None,
 331|     }
 332| }
 333| 
 334| fn push(pool: &mut BrickPool, node: BrickNode) -> u32 {
 335|     pool.nodes.push(node);
 336|     (pool.nodes.len() - 1) as u32
 337| }

   1| //! Cellular-automata environmental decay: dampness creeps, wallpaper ages,
   2| //! aged walls crumble.
   3| //!
   4| //! One step is a pure, synchronous transition over the horizontal Moore
   5| //! neighborhood (the eight same-height neighbors): every decision reads the
   6| //! *previous* state only, so stepping is order-independent and
   7| //! deterministic. Decay is a post-pass an integrator applies a fixed number
   8| //! of times after voxelization — never during sampling, where neighbor
   9| //! reads would break the chunk-independence contract.
  10| 
  11| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  12|     VOXEL_AGED_WALLPAPER, VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLUID,
  13|     VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
  14| };
  15| 
  16| /// Thresholds for the three transition rules, in damp-neighbor counts out
  17| /// of the eight horizontal neighbors.
  18| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  19| pub struct DecayRules {
  20|     /// Dry carpet saturates into sticky carpet at this many damp neighbors.
  21|     pub carpet_saturates_at: u8,
  22|     /// Exposed wall (>=1 air neighbor) grows aged wallpaper at this many.
  23|     pub wall_ages_at: u8,
  24|     /// Aged wallpaper crumbles into damaged wall at this many.
  25|     pub wallpaper_crumbles_at: u8,
  26| }
  27| 
  28| impl Default for DecayRules {
  29|     fn default() -> Self {
  30|         Self {
  31|             carpet_saturates_at: 3,
  32|             wall_ages_at: 2,
  33|             wallpaper_crumbles_at: 4,
  34|         }
  35|     }
  36| }
  37| 
  38| /// Materials that radiate dampness onto their neighbors.
  39| const DAMP_SOURCES: [u8; 3] = [VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_WATER];
  40| 
  41| /// The horizontal Moore neighborhood: neighbor damp/air census at (x, y, z).
  42| fn census(grid: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> (u8, u8) {
  43|     let (mut damp, mut air) = (0u8, 0u8);
  44|     for dz in -1i64..=1 {
  45|         for dx in -1i64..=1 {
  46|             if dx == 0 && dz == 0 {
  47|                 continue;
  48|             }
  49|             let (nx, nz) = (x as i64 + dx, z as i64 + dz);
  50|             if nx < 0 || nz < 0 || nx >= grid.width() as i64 || nz >= grid.depth() as i64 {
  51|                 continue;
  52|             }
  53|             let material = grid.get(nx as usize, y, nz as usize);
  54|             if DAMP_SOURCES.contains(&material) {
  55|                 damp += 1;
  56|             } else if material == VOXEL_AIR {
  57|                 air += 1;
  58|             }
  59|         }
  60|     }
  61|     (damp, air)
  62| }
  63| 
  64| /// The next state of one cell, or `None` when it keeps its material.
  65| fn transition(rules: &DecayRules, current: u8, damp: u8, air: u8) -> Option<u8> {
  66|     match current {
  67|         VOXEL_DRY_CARPET if damp >= rules.carpet_saturates_at => Some(VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET),
  68|         VOXEL_WALL if air >= 1 && damp >= rules.wall_ages_at => Some(VOXEL_AGED_WALLPAPER),
  69|         VOXEL_AGED_WALLPAPER if damp >= rules.wallpaper_crumbles_at => Some(VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL),
  70|         _ => None,
  71|     }
  72| }
  73| 
  74| /// Advances the automaton one generation in place. Returns how many cells
  75| /// changed, so integrators can run to quiescence (`while step(..) > 0`).
  76| pub fn step_cellular_decay(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, rules: &DecayRules) -> usize {
  77|     // Read the whole previous generation before the first write.
  78|     let mut changes = Vec::new();
  79|     for y in 0..grid.height() {
  80|         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
  81|             for x in 0..grid.width() {
  82|                 let current = grid.get(x, y, z);
  83|                 let (damp, air) = census(grid, x, y, z);
  84|                 if let Some(next) = transition(rules, current, damp, air) {
  85|                     changes.push((x, y, z, next));
  86|                 }
  87|             }
  88|         }
  89|     }
  90|     for &(x, y, z, material) in &changes {
  91|         grid.set(x, y, z, material);
  92|     }
  93|     changes.len()
  94| }
  95|

   1| //! Menger-style recursive space partitioning for macro structure.
   2| //!
   3| //! A floor plate splits into a 3x3 lattice of cells; the center cell is
   4| //! carved out as primary circulation (the Menger "cutout"), and each ring
   5| //! cell either recurses — growing finer corridor loops — or stays a leaf
   6| //! room. Depth-limited and span-limited by human passage dimensions, so the
   7| //! recursion can never produce a hall too narrow to walk.
   8| //!
   9| //! Pure and deterministic: structure is a function of (bounds, seed) alone,
  10| //! so overlapping windows regenerate identical partitions — the same
  11| //! seam-freedom contract the level generators rely on.
  12| 
  13| use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
  14| use crate::domain::entities::cad::CAD_CORRIDOR_WIDTH;
  15| use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
  16| 
  17| /// One node of the partition tree. Leaves are rooms or corridor segments;
  18| /// internal nodes carry their nine children in row-major (x, z) order.
  19| #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  20| pub struct MengerNode {
  21|     pub bounds: WorldBounds,
  22|     pub depth: u32,
  23|     pub is_corridor: bool,
  24|     pub children: Vec<MengerNode>,
  25| }
  26| 
  27| impl MengerNode {
  28|     fn leaf(bounds: WorldBounds, depth: u32, is_corridor: bool) -> Self {
  29|         Self {
  30|             bounds,
  31|             depth,
  32|             is_corridor,
  33|             children: Vec::new(),
  34|         }
  35|     }
  36| 
  37|     /// Depth-first visit of every node in the partition.
  38|     pub fn visit(&self, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&MengerNode)) {
  39|         f(self);
  40|         for child in &self.children {
  41|             child.visit(f);
  42|         }
  43|     }
  44| }
  45| 
  46| /// Fraction of ring cells that subdivide instead of staying one room.
  47| const SUBDIVIDE_CHANCE: f32 = 0.65;
  48| 
  49| /// Splits `bounds` into the 3x3 child lattice, row-major in (x, z).
  50| fn subdivide_thirds(bounds: WorldBounds) -> [WorldBounds; 9] {
  51|     let dx = (bounds.max_x - bounds.min_x) / 3.0;
  52|     let dz = (bounds.max_z - bounds.min_z) / 3.0;
  53|     std::array::from_fn(|i| {
  54|         let (ix, iz) = ((i % 3) as f32, (i / 3) as f32);
  55|         WorldBounds::new(
  56|             bounds.min_x + ix * dx,
  57|             bounds.min_z + iz * dz,
  58|             bounds.min_x + (ix + 1.0) * dx,
  59|             bounds.min_z + (iz + 1.0) * dz,
  60|         )
  61|     })
  62| }
  63| 
  64| /// A cell may only subdivide while each of its nine children can still hold
  65| /// a walkable corridor.
  66| fn subdividable(bounds: WorldBounds) -> bool {
  67|     let child_x = (bounds.max_x - bounds.min_x) / 3.0;
  68|     let child_z = (bounds.max_z - bounds.min_z) / 3.0;
  69|     child_x.min(child_z) >= CAD_CORRIDOR_WIDTH
  70| }
  71| 
  72| /// Generates the partition for one floor plate. `max_depth` bounds the
  73| /// recursion; span limits stop it earlier wherever cells shrink to human
  74| /// scale first.
  75| pub fn generate_menger_bsp(bounds: WorldBounds, max_depth: u32, seed: u32) -> MengerNode {
  76|     generate_recursive(bounds, 0, max_depth, seed)
  77| }
  78| 
  79| fn generate_recursive(bounds: WorldBounds, depth: u32, max_depth: u32, seed: u32) -> MengerNode {
  80|     if depth >= max_depth || !subdividable(bounds) {
  81|         return MengerNode::leaf(bounds, depth, false);
  82|     }
  83| 
  84|     let children = subdivide_thirds(bounds)
  85|         .into_iter()
  86|         .enumerate()
  87|         .map(|(i, child_bounds)| {
  88|             if i == 4 {
  89|                 // The Menger cutout: center cell becomes circulation.
  90|                 return MengerNode::leaf(child_bounds, depth + 1, true);
  91|             }
  92|             // Ring cells decide from their own world position, never their
  93|             // parent's identity, so overlapping queries agree.
  94|             let roll = hash(
  95|                 seed,
  96|                 0x3E9C_E11A_0000_0000 ^ u64::from(depth),
  97|                 child_bounds.min_x.floor() as i64,
  98|                 child_bounds.min_z.floor() as i64,
  99|             );
 100|             if unit(roll) < SUBDIVIDE_CHANCE {
 101|                 generate_recursive(child_bounds, depth + 1, max_depth, seed)
 102|             } else {
 103|                 MengerNode::leaf(child_bounds, depth + 1, false)
 104|             }
 105|         })
 106|         .collect();
 107| 
 108|     MengerNode {
 109|         bounds,
 110|         depth,
 111|         is_corridor: false,
 112|         children,
 113|     }
 114| }

 124|     fn collect<'a>(root: &'a MengerNode) -> Vec<&'a MengerNode> {
 125|         let mut nodes = Vec::new();
 126|         let mut stack = vec![root];
 127|         while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
 128|             nodes.push(node);
 129|             stack.extend(node.children.iter());
 130|         }
 131|         nodes
 132|     }

cellular_decay.rs:
- `step_cellular_decay`: O(W×H×D × 8) per step — the census function does `DAMP_SOURCES.contains(&material)` — contains on a 3-element array — fine, constant. Each step is O(V). If run to quiescence, number of steps could be O(depth of decay) — each step spreads dampness 1 cell further, so up to O(max(W,D)) steps → O(V × max(W,D)) worst case. Typically few steps. Note the changes Vec allocation per step — fine. Also, this is a post-pass with potential O(steps × V). Mentioned as Low/Medium.

menger_bsp.rs:
- generate_recursive: 3×3 split, recursion depth bounded by max_depth and span. Node count up to 9^depth. For a plate 81u, depth 3 → up to 9³ = 729 nodes. `visit` recursion — depth ≤ max_depth fine. Note hash per child. Fine. One concern: `generate_recursive` recursion depth = max_depth which could be 10 in tests — fine.

   1| //! The CAD-voxel marriage: samples a finished CSG solid straight into the
   2| //! sparse octree through [`build_octree_direct`], with no dense grid in
   3| //! between.
   4| //!
   5| //! An authored structure (extruded, cut, combined) becomes a
   6| //! [`SolidSampler`] positioned in chunk-local space, and voxelizes through
   7| //! the same direct SVO path as generated architecture — so player-built
   8| //! geometry and the infinite level share one representation, one renderer
   9| //! upload, and one collision story.
  10| 
  11| use crate::domain::use_cases::csg::{BspNode, Solid, v3};
  12| use crate::use_cases::build_octree_direct::{SvoLeaf, VoxelSampler};
  13| use crate::use_cases::ports::MaterialPalette;
  14| 
  15| /// Adapts one CSG solid to the voxel sampler port. Coordinates map voxel
  16| /// indices to world positions at cell centers; everything inside the solid
  17| /// becomes `material`, everything else air.
  18| pub struct SolidSampler<'a> {
  19|     bsp: BspNode,
  20|     /// World AABB of the solid, for whole-cube air pruning.
  21|     bounds: Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])>,
  22|     /// World position of voxel (0, 0, 0)'s minimum corner.
  23|     origin: [f64; 3],
  24|     voxel_size: f64,
  25|     material: u8,
  26|     palette: &'a dyn MaterialPalette,
  27| }
  28| 
  29| impl<'a> SolidSampler<'a> {
  30|     pub fn new(
  31|         solid: &Solid,
  32|         origin: [f64; 3],
  33|         voxel_size: f64,
  34|         material: u8,
  35|         palette: &'a dyn MaterialPalette,
  36|     ) -> Self {
  37|         Self {
  38|             bsp: solid.bsp(),
  39|             bounds: solid
  40|                 .aabb()
  41|                 .map(|(lo, hi)| ([lo.x, lo.y, lo.z], [hi.x, hi.y, hi.z])),
  42|             origin,
  43|             voxel_size,
  44|             material,
  45|             palette,
  46|         }
  47|     }
  48| 
  49|     fn cell_center(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> [f64; 3] {
  50|         [
  51|             self.origin[0] + (f64::from(x) + 0.5) * self.voxel_size,
  52|             self.origin[1] + (f64::from(y) + 0.5) * self.voxel_size,
  53|             self.origin[2] + (f64::from(z) + 0.5) * self.voxel_size,
  54|         ]
  55|     }
  56| }
  57| 
  58| impl VoxelSampler for SolidSampler<'_> {
  59|     fn sample(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> SvoLeaf {
  60|         let [px, py, pz] = self.cell_center(x, y, z);
  61|         if !self.bsp.contains_point(v3(px, py, pz)) {
  62|             return SvoLeaf::AIR;
  63|         }
  64|         SvoLeaf {
  65|             voxel_type: self.material,
  66|             color: self.palette.color(self.material),
  67|             light_rgb: [0; 3],
  68|             face_occlusion: 0,
  69|         }
  70|     }
  71| 
  72|     fn uniform_hint(&self, cube_origin: [u32; 3], size: u32) -> Option<SvoLeaf> {
  73|         // A cube of cells wholly outside the solid's AABB is provably air.
  74|         let (lo, hi) = self.bounds?;
  75|         let cube_min = self
  76|             .cell_center(cube_origin[0], cube_origin[1], cube_origin[2])
  77|             .map(|c| c - 0.5 * self.voxel_size);
  78|         let extent = f64::from(size) * self.voxel_size;
  79|         let outside =
  80|             (0..3).any(|axis| cube_min[axis] >= hi[axis] || cube_min[axis] + extent <= lo[axis]);
  81|         outside.then_some(SvoLeaf::AIR)
  82|     }
  83| }

 100|         let voxel_size = 0.1;
 101|         let wall = Solid::cuboid(v3(0.0, 0.0, 2.0), v3(6.0, 3.0, 2.2));
 102|         // Cut the rough opening one voxel wider than the finished width:
 103|         // voxelization quantizes to cell centers, so an exact-width cut can
 104|         // lose up to a voxel of clearance to the jambs. Same practice as
 105|         // framing a real door.
 106|         let rough_half = (CAD_DOOR_WIDTH as f64 + voxel_size) / 2.0;
 107|         let door = Solid::cuboid(

 109|             v3(3.0 + rough_half, CAD_DOOR_HEIGHT as f64, 2.4),
 110|         );
 111|         let doored_wall = wall.subtract(&door);
 112|         let sampler = SolidSampler::new(
 113|             &doored_wall,
 114|             [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 115|             voxel_size,
 116|             VOXEL_WALL,
 117|             &DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PALETTE,
 118|         );

 120| 
 121|         let at = |wx: f64, wy: f64, wz: f64| {
 122|             svo.get(
 123|                 (wx / voxel_size) as u32,
 124|                 (wy / voxel_size) as u32,
 125|                 (wz / voxel_size) as u32,
 126|             )
 127|             .unwrap()
 128|             .0
 129|         };
 130|         assert_eq!(at(3.0, 1.0, 2.1), VOXEL_AIR, "doorway center is open");
 131|         assert_eq!(at(3.0, 1.9, 2.1), VOXEL_AIR, "head height is open");
 132|         assert_eq!(at(3.0, 2.5, 2.1), VOXEL_WALL, "lintel is solid");
 133|         assert_eq!(at(1.0, 1.0, 2.1), VOXEL_WALL, "jamb wall is solid");
 134| 
 135|         // Measure the clear opening in voxel space and hold it to code.
 136|         let z = (2.1 / voxel_size) as u32;
 137|         let y = (1.0 / voxel_size) as u32;

 139|             .filter(|&x| svo.get(x, y, z).unwrap().0 == VOXEL_AIR && x > 10 && x < 50)
 140|             .count();

 142|         assert!(

 144|             "clear width {clear_width} under ADA minimum"
 145|         );
 146|         assert!(fits_human_passage(clear_width, CAD_DOOR_HEIGHT));

 149|     /// The AABB hint prunes the empty world around a small structure: the
 150|     /// arena must stay far below the full-tree node count.
 151|     #[test]
 152|     fn empty_space_around_a_structure_collapses_without_sampling() {
 153|         let cabinet = Solid::cuboid(v3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0), v3(2.0, 2.0, 2.0));
 154|         let sampler = SolidSampler::new(
 155|             &cabinet,
 156|             [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 157|             0.1,
 158|             VOXEL_WALL,
 159|             &DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PALETTE,
 160|         );
 161|         let svo = build_octree_direct(&sampler, 6, 6.4);
 162|         assert_eq!(svo.get(15, 10, 15).unwrap().0, VOXEL_WALL);
 163|         assert_eq!(svo.get(50, 10, 50).unwrap().0, VOXEL_AIR);
 164|         assert!(
 165|             svo.nodes.len() < 20_000,
 166|             "AABB pruning failed: {} nodes",
 167|             svo.nodes.len()
 168|         );
 169|     }
 170| }

csg_voxelizer.rs: SolidSampler::sample calls `self.bsp.contains_point(...)` — the cost of BSP contains is O(depth of BSP tree), which for authored CSG is small but could be O(n_planes) worst. It's per sampled voxel in the direct SVO builder — the number of point samples is O(surface × depth) since uniform_hint prunes outside AABB. Per-voxel BSP walk is fine (authored solids are small). Note: `build_octree_direct` with `SolidSampler` — the octree cube is 2^depth, and sampling happens for cubes intersecting the AABB only. OK.

 182| /// Generates one legacy blueprint chunk. Pure in `(chunk_pos, seed, config)`
 183| /// given a deterministic noise provider; telemetry is observation only.
 184| pub(crate) fn generate_legacy_blueprint(
 185|     noise_provider: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 186|     telemetry: &dyn TelemetryPort,
 187|     chunk_pos: Position,
 188|     seed: u32,
 189|     config: GeneratorConfig,
 190| ) -> VoxelGrid {
 191|     let start_micros = telemetry.now_micros();
 192| 
 193|     let width = (config.chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
 194|     let depth = (config.chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
 195| 
 196|     // Cell voxel borders derive from world space (cells are 5.0 units) so
 197|     // every LOD of a chunk puts its walls on the same world planes.
 198|     // Truncating a fixed voxels-per-cell instead compresses the maze at
 199|     // scales where 5.0/voxel_scale is fractional.
 200|     let cell_border = |c: usize| (c as f32 * 5.0 / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
 201|     let cell_w = ((config.chunk_size / 5.0).round() as usize).max(1);
 202|     let cell_d = cell_w;
 203| 
 204|     let mut abstract_grid = Grid::new(cell_w, cell_d);
 205| 
 206|     // --- ZONE ASSIGNMENT PASS ---
 207|     let mut max_chunk_height_units = 3.0_f32;
 208|     for cz in 0..cell_d {
 209|         for cx in 0..cell_w {
 210|             let wx = chunk_pos.x * config.chunk_size + (cx as f32) * 5.0;
 211|             let wz = chunk_pos.z * config.chunk_size + (cz as f32) * 5.0;
 212| 
 213|             // Low frequency noise for zone clustering
 214|             let n = noise_provider.evaluate_2d(
 215|                 seed ^ 0x2b8f_a43c,
 216|                 crate::domain::entities::position::Position::new(wx * 0.05, wz * 0.05),
 217|             ); // n is in [-1, 1]
 218| 
 219|             use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
 220|             let mut zone = MicrobiomeZone::Standard;
 221| 
 222|             if n < -0.7 {
 223|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Blackout;
 224|             } else if n < -0.4 {
 225|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Holes;
 226|             } else if n > 0.85 - (config.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1) {
 227|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Atrium;
 228|             } else if n > 0.6 {
 229|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::PillarField;
 230|             } else if n > 0.4 {
 231|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Arch;
 232|             } else if n > 0.2 && n < 0.25 {
 233|                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom;
 234|             }
 235| 
 236|             if let Some(cell) = abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, cz) {
 237|                 cell.zone = zone;
 238|             }
 239| 
 240|             let cell_h = match zone {
 241|                 MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,  // 4.0 * 3.0x
 242|                 MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2, // 4.0 * 0.8x
 243|                 _ => 4.0,
 244|             };
 245|             if cell_h > max_chunk_height_units {
 246|                 max_chunk_height_units = cell_h;
 247|             }
 248|         }
 249|     }
 250| 
 251|     let height = (max_chunk_height_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize + 2; // +2 for floor and ceiling bounds
 252| 
 253|     telemetry.log(&format!(
 254|             "[INFO] Entering GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::execute. Args: chunk_pos={:?}, seed={}, chunk_size={} (Voxel dimensions: {}x{}x{})",
 255|             chunk_pos, seed, config.chunk_size, width, height, depth
 256|         ));
 257| 
 258|     let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
 259| 
 260|     // STARTING HUB OVERRIDE: Chunk (0,0) is a massive open plaza that feeds seamlessly into the maze
 261|     if chunk_pos.x.abs() < 1.0 && chunk_pos.z.abs() < 1.0 {
 262|         for z in 0..depth {
 263|             for x in 0..width {
 264|                 grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_FLOOR);
 265|                 grid.set(x, height - 1, z, VOXEL_CEILING);
 266| 
 267|                 // Scatter ceiling panels without replacing walkable floor material.
 268|                 if x > 0 && z > 0 && x % 20 == 0 && z % 20 == 0 {
 269|                     grid.set(x, height - 1, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 270|                 }
 271|             }
 272|         }
 273|         let lighting =
 274|             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
 275|                 config.voxel_scale,
 276|             )
 277|             .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
 278|         crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
 279|         return grid;
 280|     }
 281| 
 282|     // ==========================================
 283|     // DYNAMIC GENERATION (Growing Tree & BSP)
 284|     // ==========================================
 285|     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(
 286|         (seed as u64) ^ (chunk_pos.x.to_bits() as u64) ^ (chunk_pos.z.to_bits() as u64),
 287|     );
 288|     // Per-voxel cosmetic noise (floor holes, dotted pillars) draws from
 289|     // its own stream: the number of those draws depends on voxel
 290|     // resolution, and letting them share the structural RNG would
 291|     // desynchronize wall/door placement between LODs of the same chunk.
 292|     let mut detail_rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(
 293|         (seed as u64)
 294|             ^ (chunk_pos.x.to_bits() as u64)
 295|             ^ (chunk_pos.z.to_bits() as u64)
 296|             ^ 0xD57A_11ED,
 297|     );
 298| 
 299|     let maze_gen = GrowingTreeGenerator {
 300|         junction_density: config.tuning.junction_density,

 301|     };
 302|     maze_gen.generate(&mut abstract_grid, &mut rng);
 303| 
 304|     // Organic room segmentation
 305|     let mut rooms = Vec::new();
 306|     let mut room_grid = vec![None; cell_w * cell_d];
 307| 
 308|     // Tunable parameters
 309|     let num_room_attempts = 15;
 310|     for _ in 0..num_room_attempts {
 311|         let cx = rng.random_range(0..cell_w);
 312|         let cz = rng.random_range(0..cell_d);
 313|         let rw = rng.random_range(1..=3);
 314|         let rd = rng.random_range(1..=3);
 315| 
 316|         if cx + rw <= cell_w && cz + rd <= cell_d {
 317|             let mut overlap = false;
 318|             for i in 0..rw {
 319|                 for j in 0..rd {
 320|                     if room_grid[(cz + j) * cell_w + cx + i].is_some() {
 321|                         overlap = true;
 322|                     }
 323|                 }
 324|             }
 325|             if !overlap {
 326|                 let room_id = rooms.len();
 327|                 for i in 0..rw {
 328|                     for j in 0..rd {
 329|                         room_grid[(cz + j) * cell_w + cx + i] = Some(room_id);
 330|                         if let Some(cell) = abstract_grid.get_mut(cx + i, cz + j) {
 331|                             if j > 0 {
 332|                                 cell.walls[0] = false;
 333|                             }
 334|                             if i < rw - 1 {
 335|                                 cell.walls[1] = false;
 336|                             }
 337|                             if j < rd - 1 {
 338|                                 cell.walls[2] = false;
 339|                             }
 340|                             if i > 0 {
 341|                                 cell.walls[3] = false;
 342|                             }
 343|                         }
 344|                     }
 345|                 }
 346|                 rooms.push(Room {
 347|                     name: "Organic",
 348|                     x0: cell_border(cx),
 349|                     x1: cell_border(cx + rw) - 1,
 350|                     z0: cell_border(cz),
 351|                     z1: cell_border(cz + rd) - 1,
 352|                 });
 353|             }
 354|         }
 355|     }
 356| 
 357|     // Hallway reservation (Part 1)
 358|     let mut non_room_indices = Vec::new();
 359|     for i in 0..(cell_w * cell_d) {
 360|         if room_grid[i].is_none() {
 361|             non_room_indices.push(i);
 362|         }
 363|     }
 364| 
 365|     let target_corridors = (non_room_indices.len() as f32 * 0.20) as usize;
 366|     let mut corridor_count = 0;
 367| 
 368|     use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
 369|     non_room_indices.shuffle(&mut rng);
 370| 
 371|     for &idx in &non_room_indices {
 372|         if corridor_count >= target_corridors {
 373|             break;
 374|         }
 375|         let cx = idx % cell_w;
 376|         let cz = idx / cell_w;
 377|         if abstract_grid.get(cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor {
 378|             continue;
 379|         }
 380| 
 381|         abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
 382|         corridor_count += 1;
 383| 
 384|         // Extend North
 385|         let mut current_cz = cz;
 386|         while current_cz > 0 && !abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().walls[0] {
 387|             current_cz -= 1;
 388|             if room_grid[current_cz * cell_w + cx].is_some()
 389|                 || abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor
 390|             {
 391|                 break;
 392|             }
 393|             abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
 394|             corridor_count += 1;
 395|         }
 396|         // Extend South
 397|         let mut current_cz = cz;
 398|         while current_cz < cell_d - 1 && !abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().walls[2] {
 399|             current_cz += 1;
 400|             if room_grid[current_cz * cell_w + cx].is_some()
 401|                 || abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor
 402|             {
 403|                 break;
 404|             }
 405|             abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
 406|             corridor_count += 1;
 407|         }
 408|         // Extend West
 409|         let mut current_cx = cx;
 410|         while current_cx > 0 && !abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().walls[3] {
 411|             current_cx -= 1;
 412|             if room_grid[cz * cell_w + current_cx].is_some()
 413|                 || abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor
 414|             {
 415|                 break;
 416|             }
 417|             abstract_grid.get_mut(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
 418|             corridor_count += 1;
 419|         }
 420|         // Extend East
 421|         let mut current_cx = cx;
 422|         while current_cx < cell_w - 1 && !abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().walls[1] {
 423|             current_cx += 1;
 424|             if room_grid[cz * cell_w + current_cx].is_some()
 425|                 || abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor
 426|             {
 427|                 break;
 428|             }
 429|             abstract_grid.get_mut(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
 430|             corridor_count += 1;
 431|         }

 433| 
 434|     // Draw abstract grid to VoxelGrid
 435|     for cz in 0..cell_d {
 436|         for cx in 0..cell_w {
 437|             let cell = abstract_grid.get(cx, cz).unwrap();
 438|             let v_x0 = cell_border(cx);
 439|             let v_z0 = cell_border(cz);
 440|             let v_x1 = (cell_border(cx + 1) - 1).min(width - 1);
 441|             let v_z1 = (cell_border(cz + 1) - 1).min(depth - 1);
 442| 
 443|             use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
 444|             let cell_h_units = match cell.zone {
 445|                 MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,
 446|                 MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2,
 447|                 _ => 4.0,
 448|             };
 449|             let wall_max_y = (cell_h_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
 450|             let door_max_y = (2.5 / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize; // Doorways are 2.5 units tall
 451| 
 452|             let wall_type = VOXEL_WALL;
 453| 
 454|             // Floors and Ceilings
 455|             for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
 456|                 for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
 457|                     grid.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
 458| 
 459|                     if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Holes {
 460|                         if vx > v_x0 + 5 && vx < v_x1 - 5 && vz > v_z0 + 5 && vz < v_z1 - 5 {
 461|                             if detail_rng.random_bool(0.05) {
 462|                                 grid.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_AIR);
 463|                             }
 464|                         }
 465|                     }
 466| 
 467|                     if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Atrium {
 468|                         // Normal ceilings with hanging light
 469|                         grid.set(vx, wall_max_y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING); // Always close the ceiling
 470|                         if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Blackout && (vx % 10 == 0 && vz % 10 == 0) {
 471|                             if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
 472|                                 grid.set(
 473|                                     vx,
 474|                                     wall_max_y - 1,
 475|                                     vz,
 476|                                     crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
 477|                                 );
 478|                             } else {
 479|                                 grid.set(vx, wall_max_y - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 480|                             }
 481|                         }
 482|                         for y in (wall_max_y + 1)..height {
 483|                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
 484|                         }
 485|                     } else {
 486|                         // Atrium ceiling and bright hanging light
 487|                         grid.set(vx, wall_max_y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
 488|                         if vx % 10 == 0 && vz % 10 == 0 {
 489|                             grid.set(vx, wall_max_y - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 490|                         }
 491|                     }
 492|                 }
 493|             }
 494| 
 495|             if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::PillarField {
 496|                 for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
 497|                     grid.set(v_x0, y, v_z0, wall_type);
 498|                     grid.set(v_x1, y, v_z0, wall_type);
 499|                     grid.set(v_x0, y, v_z1, wall_type);
 500|                     grid.set(v_x1, y, v_z1, wall_type);
 501|                     if detail_rng.random_bool(0.3) {
 502|                         grid.set((v_x0 + v_x1 + 1) / 2, y, (v_z0 + v_z1 + 1) / 2, wall_type);
 503|                     }
 504|                 }
 505|                 continue;
 506|             }
 507| 
 508|             // South Wall (z1)
 509|             if cz < cell_d - 1 {
 510|                 let same_room = room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx] == room_grid[(cz + 1) * cell_w + cx]
 511|                     && room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx].is_some();
 512| 
 513|                 if !same_room {
 514|                     let width_choice = rng.random_range(0..100);
 515|                     let hole_units = if width_choice < 15 {
 516|                         1.2
 517|                     } else if width_choice < 85 {
 518|                         2.0
 519|                     } else {
 520|                         3.5
 521|                     };
 522|                     let hole_w = (hole_units / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
 523|                     // Drawn in centimetres of the 5.0-unit cell span, not
 524|                     // voxels, so every LOD picks the same door position.
 525|                     let hole_cm = (hole_units * 100.0) as u32;
 526|                     let max_offset_cm = 500u32.saturating_sub(hole_cm + 50);
 527|                     let offset_cm = if max_offset_cm > 50 {
 528|                         rng.random_range(50..max_offset_cm)
 529|                     } else {
 530|                         50
 531|                     };
 532|                     let offset = (offset_cm as f32 / 100.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
 533|                     let hole_x0 = v_x0 + offset;
 534|                     let hole_x1 = hole_x0 + hole_w;

 936| fn validate_stamp_placement(
 937|     grid: &VoxelGrid,
 938|     room: &Room,
 939|     stamp: &RoomStamp,
 940|     start_x: usize,
 941|     start_z: usize,
 942| ) -> bool {
 943|     if start_x < room.x0
 944|         || start_x + stamp.width > room.x1
 945|         || start_z < room.z0
 946|         || start_z + stamp.depth > room.z1
 947|     {
 948|         return false;
 949|     }
 950| 
 951|     for lz in 0..stamp.depth {
 952|         for lx in 0..stamp.width {
 953|             let vx = start_x + lx;
 954|             let vz = start_z + lz;
 955|             if stamp.data[lz * stamp.width + lx] > 0 {
 956|                 if grid.get(vx, 1, vz) != VOXEL_AIR && grid.get(vx, 1, vz) != VOXEL_FLOOR {
 957|                     return false;
 958|                 }
 959|             }
 960|         }
 961|     }
 962| 
 963|     true
 964| }
 965| 
 966| fn place_stamp(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, stamp: &RoomStamp, start_x: usize, start_z: usize) {
 967|     let max_y = grid.height() - 2;
 968|     for sz in 0..stamp.depth {
 969|         for sx in 0..stamp.width {
 970|             let val = stamp.data[sz * stamp.width + sx];
 971|             let vx = start_x + sx;
 972|             let vz = start_z + sz;
 973|             if val == 1 {
 974|                 for y in 1..=3 {
 975|                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
 976|                 }
 977|             } else if val == 2 {
 978|                 for y in 1..=max_y {
 979|                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
 980|                 }
 981|             } else if val == 3 {
 982|                 for y in 1..=1 {
 983|                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
 984|                 }
 985|             } else if val == 4 {
 986|                 // Raised floor
 987|                 grid.set(vx, 1, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
 988|                 grid.set(vx, 2, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
 989|             } else if val == 5 {
 990|                 // Step 1
 991|                 grid.set(vx, 1, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
 992|             } else if val == 6 { // Step 2
 993|                 // Just floor, already set
 994|             }
 995|         }
 996|     }
 997| }

legacy_blueprint.rs analysis:
- Maze generation via GrowingTreeGenerator (domain, out of scope).
- Room attempts: 15 attempts × 9 cells — fine.
- Corridor extension: O(cells).
- Draw pass: for each cell, iterate over voxel ranges — total O(width × depth × height) = O(V). But note: for the "PillarField" case, the `continue` at line 505 skips the walls, OK.
- Room stamps: for each room, possible_stamps loop; then stamp placement loops with validate_stamp_placement O(stamp area) — small.
- One noteworthy point: floor/ceiling loops at lines 455-493 fill every voxel in each cell including setting `for y in (wall_max_y + 1)..height { grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING) }` — O(V) total, fine.
- The whole function is O(V) with V = 200×42×200 ≈ 1.68M for high spec. Fine.
- Room lighting loop 886-903 — z from room.z0+8 step 12 — O(room size) fine.

Now frame_quality_controller.rs and authoring.rs.
total: 288
   1| //! # Frame Quality & Budget Controller Use Case
   2| //!
   3| //! ## Business Intent & Rationale
   4| //! In low-spec rendering environments (WebGL, low-end integrated GPUs, mobile devices),
   5| //! hardware rendering capacity is strictly constrained. Running out of frame budget causes
   6| //! stuttering, thermal throttling, and missed v-sync intervals.
   7| //!
   8| //! The `FrameQualityController` orchestrates runtime quality profiles (`SurfaceQualityProfile`)
   9| //! and enforces hard frame work budgets (maximum visible surface chunks, triangle limits, light limits).
  10| //!
  11| //! ## Design Patterns Used
  12| //! - **Strategy Pattern**: `FrameQualityHysteresisStrategy` decouples performance measurement
  13| //!   and tier transition logic from chunk submission algorithms. Hysteresis ensures the system
  14| //!   degrades rapidly upon detecting performance degradation (1 slow frame triggers downgrade)
  15| //!   while upgrading conservatively (requiring 30 consecutive fast frames to upgrade).
  16| //! - **Observer Pattern / Telemetry**: `SurfaceRenderingTelemetry` records per-frame performance metrics,
  17| //!   ISO 8601 timestamps, input arguments, and return values for observability.
  18| 
  19| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  20| use crate::domain::entities::surface_quality_profile::{SurfaceQualityProfile, SurfaceQualityTier};
  21| use std::time::Duration;
  22| 
  23| /// Telemetry metric payload for observability & performance tracking.
  24| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  25| pub struct SurfaceRenderingTelemetry {
  26|     /// ISO 8601 formatted timestamp of the frame render event.
  27|     pub timestamp_iso8601: String,
  28|     /// Total candidate chunks evaluated for rendering.
  29|     pub candidate_chunks: usize,
  30|     /// Chunks culled by frustum/distance culling.
  31|     pub distance_culled_chunks: usize,
  32|     /// Chunks culled due to work budget limits.

  34|     /// Chunks accepted and submitted for surface rendering.

  38|     /// Total surface triangles submitted (2 per quad).

  40|     /// Total draw call submissions.

  45|     pub active_tier: SurfaceQualityTier,

  73| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  74| pub struct ChunkSurfaceCandidate {
