  81| /// Use case controller governing real-time frame quality and budget culling.
  82| #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  83| pub struct FrameQualityController {
  84|     pub profile: SurfaceQualityProfile,
  85|     target_frame_duration: Duration,
  86|     fast_frame_counter: usize,
  87|     upgrade_threshold_frames: usize,
  88| }
  89| 
  90| impl FrameQualityController {
  91|     pub fn new(initial_tier: SurfaceQualityTier) -> Self {
  92|         let profile = match initial_tier {
  93|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => SurfaceQualityProfile::ultra_low(),
  94|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => SurfaceQualityProfile::low(),
  95|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced(),
  96|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => SurfaceQualityProfile::high(),
  97|         };
  98|         Self {
  99|             profile,
 100|             target_frame_duration: Duration::from_millis(16), // ~60 FPS target
 101|             fast_frame_counter: 0,
 102|             upgrade_threshold_frames: 30, // Require 30 consecutive fast frames to upgrade
 103|         }
 104|     }
 105| 
 106|     /// Reports a completed frame's execution time and applies hysteresis rules.
 107|     ///
 108|     /// # Inputs
 109|     /// - `frame_duration`: Execution time of the previous frame.
 110|     ///
 111|     /// # Returns
 112|     /// - `bool`: True if the quality tier was changed.
 113|     pub fn report_frame_time(&mut self, frame_duration: Duration) -> bool {
 114|         let slow_threshold = self
 115|             .target_frame_duration
 116|             .saturating_add(Duration::from_millis(4)); // > 20ms is slow
 117|         let fast_threshold = Duration::from_millis(11); // < 11ms is fast
 118| 
 119|         if frame_duration > slow_threshold {
 120|             // Immediate downgrade on sustained slow frame to protect frame rate stability
 121|             self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
 122|             self.downgrade_tier()
 123|         } else if frame_duration < fast_threshold {
 124|             self.fast_frame_counter += 1;
 125|             if self.fast_frame_counter >= self.upgrade_threshold_frames {
 126|                 self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
 127|                 self.upgrade_tier()
 128|             } else {
 129|                 false
 130|             }
 131|         } else {
 132|             self.fast_frame_counter = 0;
 133|             false
 134|         }
 135|     }
 136| 
 137|     fn downgrade_tier(&mut self) -> bool {
 138|         match self.profile.tier {
 139|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => {
 140|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced();
 141|                 true
 142|             }
 143|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => {
 144|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::low();
 145|                 true
 146|             }
 147|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => {
 148|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::ultra_low();
 149|                 true
 150|             }
 151|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => false,
 152|         }
 153|     }
 154| 
 155|     fn upgrade_tier(&mut self) -> bool {
 156|         match self.profile.tier {
 157|             SurfaceQualityTier::UltraLow => {
 158|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::low();
 159|                 true
 160|             }
 161|             SurfaceQualityTier::Low => {
 162|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::balanced();
 163|                 true
 164|             }
 165|             SurfaceQualityTier::Balanced => {
 166|                 self.profile = SurfaceQualityProfile::high();
 167|                 true
 168|             }
 169|             SurfaceQualityTier::High => false,
 170|         }
 171|     }
 172| 
 173|     /// Filters and sorts surface chunk candidates by distance from player, enforcing hard work budgets.
 174|     ///
 175|     /// # Rules
 176|     /// 1. Chunks farther than max distance or max_visible_chunks budget are culled.
 177|     /// 2. Triangle budget (`max_triangles_per_frame`) is strictly enforced.
 178|     /// 3. Closest chunks to player are prioritized deterministically.
 179|     pub fn evaluate_and_cull_chunks(
 180|         &self,
 181|         player_pos: Position,
 182|         candidates: &[ChunkSurfaceCandidate],
 183|         iso8601_timestamp: &str,
 184|     ) -> (Vec<ChunkSurfaceCandidate>, SurfaceRenderingTelemetry) {
 185|         let mut telemetry = SurfaceRenderingTelemetry::new(
 186|             iso8601_timestamp,
 187|             self.profile.tier,
 188|             self.profile.render_scale,
 189|         );
 190|         telemetry.candidate_chunks = candidates.len();
 191| 
 192|         // Distance calculate and sort candidates closest to player first
 193|         let mut scored: Vec<(f32, &ChunkSurfaceCandidate)> = candidates
 194|             .iter()
 195|             .map(|c| {
 196|                 let dx = c.origin.x - player_pos.x;
 197|                 let dz = c.origin.z - player_pos.z;
 198|                 let dist_sq = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 199|                 (dist_sq, c)
 200|             })
 201|             .collect();
 202| 
 203|         scored.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.partial_cmp(&b.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 204| 
 205|         let mut accepted = Vec::new();
 206|         let mut accumulated_triangles = 0;
 207| 
 208|         for (_dist_sq, candidate) in scored {
 209|             if accepted.len() >= self.profile.max_visible_chunks {
 210|                 telemetry.budget_culled_chunks += 1;
 211|                 continue;
 212|             }
 213| 
 214|             let cand_triangles = candidate.quad_count * 2;
 215|             if accumulated_triangles + cand_triangles > self.profile.max_triangles_per_frame
 216|                 && !accepted.is_empty()
 217|             {
 218|                 telemetry.budget_culled_chunks += 1;
 219|                 continue;
 220|             }
 221| 
 222|             accumulated_triangles += cand_triangles;
 223|             telemetry.submitted_quads += candidate.quad_count;
 224|             accepted.push(candidate.clone());
 225|         }
 226| 
 227|         telemetry.visible_surface_chunks = accepted.len();
 228|         telemetry.submitted_triangles = accumulated_triangles;
 229|         telemetry.draw_calls = accepted.len(); // 1 draw call per chunk baseline
 230|         telemetry.active_lights = self.profile.max_dynamic_lights;
 231| 
 232|         (accepted, telemetry)
 233|     }
 234| }

total: 447
   1| //! User-authored construction: the CAD sandbox's edit model.
   2| //!
   3| //! The generator answers "what is here"; this answers "what did someone
   4| //! build here". An [`AuthoringSession`] is an ordered list of CAD operations
   5| //! — add this wall, cut that doorway, drop a desk — held as CSG solids and
   6| //! baked into generated chunks. Order is the edit history: a doorway cut
   7| //! after a wall is a hole in it, the same cut before it is nothing.
   8| //!
   9| //! Why solids rather than painted voxels: an authored wall has to survive
  10| //! being re-voxelized at a different LOD, and a doorway has to stay a
  11| //! doorway when it is. Storing the *operation* keeps that true at any voxel
  12| //! size, which painting individual voxels cannot.
  13| //!
  14| //! The rule this module exists to enforce is [`rough_opening`]. Voxelization
  15| //! samples cell centers, so a cut made at exactly the finished width loses
  16| //! up to a voxel of clearance to the jambs and the door comes out too narrow
  17| //! to walk through. Real framing has the same problem and the same answer:
  18| //! frame the rough opening oversize, then finish it. Every cut this module
  19| //! makes goes through that rule, so an authored door is passable by
  20| //! construction rather than by the author having remembered.
  21| 
  22| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  23| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
  24| use crate::domain::use_cases::csg::{Solid, Vec3, v3};
  25| 
  26| /// What an operation does to the world.
  27| #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  28| pub enum EditOp {
  29|     /// Add solid matter in a material.
  30|     Add,
  31|     /// Remove matter, leaving air. Doorways, windows, demolition.
  32|     Cut,
  33| }
  34| 
  35| /// One authored construction operation.
  36| #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  37| pub struct AuthoredElement {
  38|     pub solid: Solid,
  39|     pub op: EditOp,
  40|     /// Material for [`EditOp::Add`]; ignored for a cut.
  41|     pub material: u8,
  42| }
  43| 
  44| /// Enlarges a finished opening dimension to the rough opening that will
  45| /// actually voxelize to it.
  46| ///
  47| /// Voxelization asks whether each cell *center* is inside the solid, so an
  48| /// opening cut at exactly its finished width can lose up to a whole voxel of
  49| /// clear width to the jambs — the cut passes between two cell centers and
  50| /// neither is removed. A 0.9 m door quantized down to 0.8 m at a 0.2 m voxel
  51| /// is no longer a door anyone fits through.
  52| ///
  53| /// Oversizing by one voxel guarantees the finished width survives
  54| /// quantization at any grid phase. This is exactly what framing a rough
  55| /// opening does in a real building, for a related reason.
  56| pub fn rough_opening(finished: f32, voxel_size: f32) -> f32 {
  57|     finished + voxel_size
  58| }
  59| 
  60| /// An ordered edit history over the generated world.
  61| #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
  62| pub struct AuthoringSession {
  63|     elements: Vec<AuthoredElement>,
  64| }
  65| 
  66| impl AuthoringSession {
  67|     pub fn new() -> Self {
  68|         Self::default()
  69|     }
  70| 
  71|     pub fn elements(&self) -> &[AuthoredElement] {
  72|         &self.elements
  73|     }
  74| 
  75|     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  76|         self.elements.is_empty()
  77|     }
  78| 
  79|     /// Undo: drops the most recent operation.
  80|     pub fn undo(&mut self) -> Option<AuthoredElement> {
  81|         self.elements.pop()
  82|     }
  83| 
  84|     pub fn push(&mut self, element: AuthoredElement) -> &mut Self {
  85|         self.elements.push(element);
  86|         self
  87|     }
  88| 
  89|     /// Builds a straight wall between two plan points.
  90|     ///
  91|     /// Centered on the line the author drew, like every CAD wall tool: an
  92|     /// author drawing a room's outline means the wall's centerline, and a
  93|     /// wall grown to one side of it puts the room off by half a thickness.
  94|     pub fn wall(
  95|         &mut self,
  96|         from: Position,
  97|         to: Position,
  98|         thickness: f32,
  99|         height: f32,
 100|         material: u8,
 101|     ) -> &mut Self {
 102|         let half = (thickness * 0.5) as f64;
 103|         let (x0, x1) = ordered(from.x as f64, to.x as f64);
 104|         let (z0, z1) = ordered(from.z as f64, to.z as f64);
 105|         // Axis-aligned walls only, matching the rest of the plan vocabulary.
 106|         // The thin axis takes the thickness; a diagonal request degrades to
 107|         // its bounding run rather than silently building nothing.
 108|         let (min, max) = if (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0) {
 109|             let mid = (z0 + z1) * 0.5;
 110|             (v3(x0, 0.0, mid - half), v3(x1, height as f64, mid + half))
 111|         } else {
 112|             let mid = (x0 + x1) * 0.5;
 113|             (v3(mid - half, 0.0, z0), v3(mid + half, height as f64, z1))
 114|         };
 115|         self.push(AuthoredElement {
 116|             solid: Solid::cuboid(min, max),
 117|             op: EditOp::Add,
 118|             material,
 119|         })
 120|     }
 121| 
 122|     /// Cuts a doorway through whatever stands at `center`.
 123|     ///
 124|     /// `finished_width`/`finished_height` are the dimensions the author
 125|     /// wants to walk through; the cut itself is made at the rough opening,
 126|     /// so that is what they get. `depth` must exceed the wall's thickness or
 127|     /// the cut stops inside it.
 128|     pub fn doorway(
 129|         &mut self,
 130|         center: Position,
 131|         finished_width: f32,
 132|         finished_height: f32,
 133|         depth: f32,
 134|         voxel_size: f32,
 135|         along_x: bool,
 136|     ) -> &mut Self {
 137|         let half_w = (rough_opening(finished_width, voxel_size) * 0.5) as f64;
 138|         // Height is oversized at the head only: the floor already bounds the
 139|         // opening below, and lifting the sill would leave a step to trip on.
 140|         let top = rough_opening(finished_height, voxel_size) as f64;
 141|         let half_d = (depth * 0.5) as f64;
 142|         let (cx, cz) = (center.x as f64, center.z as f64);
 143|         let (min, max) = if along_x {
 144|             (
 145|                 v3(cx - half_w, 0.0, cz - half_d),
 146|                 v3(cx + half_w, top, cz + half_d),
 147|             )
 148|         } else {
 149|             (
 150|                 v3(cx - half_d, 0.0, cz - half_w),
 151|                 v3(cx + half_d, top, cz + half_w),
 152|             )
 153|         };
 154|         self.push(AuthoredElement {
 155|             solid: Solid::cuboid(min, max),
 156|             op: EditOp::Cut,
 157|             material: VOXEL_AIR,
 158|         })
 159|     }
 160| 
 161|     /// A horizontal slab: floor, ceiling plane, or a desk top.
 162|     pub fn slab(
 163|         &mut self,
 164|         from: Position,
 165|         to: Position,
 166|         base_units: f32,
 167|         top_units: f32,
 168|         material: u8,
 169|     ) -> &mut Self {
 170|         let (x0, x1) = ordered(from.x as f64, to.x as f64);
 171|         let (z0, z1) = ordered(from.z as f64, to.z as f64);
 172|         self.push(AuthoredElement {
 173|             solid: Solid::cuboid(v3(x0, base_units as f64, z0), v3(x1, top_units as f64, z1)),
 174|             op: EditOp::Add,
 175|             material,
 176|         })
 177|     }
 178| 
 179|     /// Bakes the edit history into an already-generated chunk.
 180|     ///
 181|     /// `origin` is the chunk's world corner and `voxel_size` its scale, so
 182|     /// authored geometry lands in world space regardless of which chunk is
 183|     /// being written — an authored wall crossing a chunk seam is written
 184|     /// correctly into both, because both ask the same solids the same
 185|     /// world-space question.
 186|     pub fn apply_to_grid(&self, grid: &mut VoxelGrid, origin: Position, voxel_size: f32) {
 187|         for element in &self.elements {
 188|             let Some((lo, hi)) = element.solid.aabb() else {
 189|                 continue;
 190|             };
 191|             // Only walk the cells the element could possibly touch.
 192|             let (ix0, ix1) = cell_range(lo.x, hi.x, origin.x as f64, voxel_size, grid.width());
 193|             let (iy0, iy1) = cell_range(lo.y, hi.y, 0.0, voxel_size, grid.height());
 194|             let (iz0, iz1) = cell_range(lo.z, hi.z, origin.z as f64, voxel_size, grid.depth());
 195|             let bsp = element.solid.bsp();
 196|             for y in iy0..iy1 {
 197|                 for z in iz0..iz1 {
 198|                     for x in ix0..ix1 {
 199|                         let point = v3(
 200|                             origin.x as f64 + (x as f64 + 0.5) * voxel_size as f64,
 201|                             (y as f64 + 0.5) * voxel_size as f64,
 202|                             origin.z as f64 + (z as f64 + 0.5) * voxel_size as f64,
 203|                         );
 204|                         if !bsp.contains_point(point) {
 205|                             continue;
 206|                         }
 207|                         match element.op {
 208|                             EditOp::Add => grid.set(x, y, z, element.material),
 209|                             EditOp::Cut => grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_AIR),
 210|                         }
 211|                     }
 212|                 }
 213|             }
 214|         }
 215|     }
 216| }
 217| 
 218| fn ordered(a: f64, b: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
 219|     (a.min(b), a.max(b))
 220| }
 221| 
 222| /// Half-open cell index range covering a world span, clamped to the grid.
 223| fn cell_range(lo: f64, hi: f64, origin: f64, voxel_size: f32, count: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
 224|     let v = voxel_size as f64;
 225|     let start = ((lo - origin) / v).floor().max(0.0) as usize;
 226|     let end = (((hi - origin) / v).ceil().max(0.0) as usize + 1).min(count);
 227|     (start.min(count), end)
 228| }
 229| 
 230| /// Convenience for callers that only have a `Vec3`.
 231| pub fn plan_point(point: Vec3) -> Position {
 232|     Position::new(point.x as f32, point.z as f32)
 233| }

authoring.rs:
- `apply_to_grid`: for each element, walk cells in its AABB range, test `bsp.contains_point` — O(elements × aabb_volume × bsp_depth). For authored solids with small AABBs, fine. Note it re-computes `element.solid.bsp()` per element per chunk — fine. Each apply is O(edit volume) — the number of elements grows unbounded with user edits (no cap) but that's a user-space concern; each bake re-walks the whole history: O(E × V_e) per bake. If a session has thousands of edits, each chunk bake re-applies all — worth a Low note (no incremental/dirty-region tracking).

   1| //! Bake finite-range voxel irradiance from the scene's emissive geometry.
   2| //!
   3| //! This use case deliberately separates four physically meaningful stages:
   4| //!
   5| //! 1. erase the previous bake;
   6| //! 2. inject emission through exposed downward faces of ceiling fixtures;
   7| //! 3. find shortest unobstructed paths through air in world-space units;
   8| //! 4. project that air irradiance onto the first solid surface it reaches.
   9| //!
  10| //! Solids are receivers, never propagation nodes. A wall can therefore be lit
  11| //! on its near side without becoming a light source for the room behind it.
  12| //! The working calculation is floating point; quantization happens only when
  13| //! the result is written back to the grid's established RGB 0--15 contract.
  14| //! This field is deliberately an approximate, finite-range diffuse fill. The
  15| //! renderer's analytic area lights remain authoritative for direct lighting;
  16| //! this bake neither invents omnidirectional emitters nor requires unbounded
  17| //! cross-chunk propagation halos.
  18| 
  19| mod clear_previous_bake;
  20| mod exposed_emissive_faces;
  21| mod project_onto_solid_receivers;
  22| mod propagate_through_air;
  23| mod settings;
  24| mod voxel_neighborhood;
  25| mod world_space_attenuation;
  26| mod write_air_irradiance;
  27| 
  28| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
  29| 
  30| pub use settings::{
  31|     DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings, VoxelLightingSettings,
  32| };
  33| 
  34| /// Replaces every prior light sample in `grid` with a deterministic bake.
  35| ///
  36| /// Once light has entered the air below a fixture, approximate diffuse fill
  37| /// attenuates symmetrically along face-connected paths. Its independent
  38| /// variable is shortest unobstructed path length in world units, so changing
  39| /// voxel resolution does not silently change a fixture's physical reach.
  40| pub fn bake_voxel_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, settings: VoxelLightingSettings) {
  41|     clear_previous_bake::clear_previous_bake(grid);
  42| 
  43|     let propagated = propagate_through_air::propagate_through_air(grid, settings);
  44|     write_air_irradiance::write_air_irradiance(grid, &propagated, settings);
  45|     project_onto_solid_receivers::project_onto_solid_receivers(grid, &propagated, settings);
  46| }
  47| 
  48| #[cfg(test)]
  49| mod tests;

   1| use std::error::Error;

   4| /// Default finite reach of baked fixture light, measured in world units.
   5| ///
   6| /// Six units keeps ordinary 3.2--5.4 unit rooms illuminated while still
   7| /// reaching zero before distant fixtures can flatten a whole streamed scene.
   8| pub const DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS: f32 = 6.0;
   9| 
  10| /// Physical sampling settings for one voxel-light bake.
  11| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  12| pub struct VoxelLightingSettings {
  13|     voxel_size_world_units: f32,
  14|     max_range_world_units: f32,
  15| }
  16| 
  17| impl VoxelLightingSettings {
  18|     /// Creates validated settings. Both values are lengths in the same world
  19|     /// coordinate system used by generated architecture and runtime lights.
  20|     pub fn new(
  21|         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
  22|         max_range_world_units: f32,
  23|     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
  24|         if !voxel_size_world_units.is_finite() || voxel_size_world_units <= 0.0 {
  25|             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::VoxelSize);
  26|         }
  27|         if !max_range_world_units.is_finite() || max_range_world_units <= 0.0 {
  28|             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::MaxRange);
  29|         }
  30|         Ok(Self {
  31|             voxel_size_world_units,
  32|             max_range_world_units,
  33|         })
  34|     }
  35| 
  36|     /// Uses the engine's ordinary finite fixture range with an exact scene
  37|     /// voxel size supplied by the generation configuration.
  38|     pub fn with_default_range(
  39|         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
  40|     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
  41|         Self::new(voxel_size_world_units, DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS)
  42|     }
  43| 
  44|     pub fn voxel_size_world_units(self) -> f32 {
  45|         self.voxel_size_world_units
  46|     }
  47| 
  48|     pub fn max_range_world_units(self) -> f32 {
  49|         self.max_range_world_units
  50|     }
  51| }
  52| 
  53| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  54| pub enum InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
  55|     VoxelSize,
  56|     MaxRange,
  57| }
  58| 
  59| impl Display for InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
  60|     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  61|         match self {
  62|             Self::VoxelSize => {
  63|                 formatter.write_str("voxel size must be finite and greater than zero")
  64|             }
  65|             Self::MaxRange => {
  66|                 formatter.write_str("maximum light range must be finite and greater than zero")
  67|             }
  68|         }
  69|     }
  70| }
  71| 
  72| impl Error for InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {}

   1| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{

   7| /// One spectral emission class in the compact 0--15 bake domain.
   8| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
   9| pub(crate) struct EmissionProfile {
  10|     pub(crate) voxel_type: u8,
  11|     pub(crate) rgb: [f32; 3],
  12| }
  13| 
  14| pub(crate) const EMISSION_PROFILES: [EmissionProfile; 3] = [
  15|     EmissionProfile {
  16|         voxel_type: VOXEL_LIGHT,
  17|         rgb: [15.0, 14.0, 11.0],
  18|     },
  19|     EmissionProfile {
  20|         voxel_type: VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
  21|         rgb: [15.0, 3.0, 2.0],
  22|     },
  23|     EmissionProfile {
  24|         voxel_type: VOXEL_GLIMMER,
  25|         rgb: [3.0, 5.0, 7.0],
  26|     },
  27| ];
  28| 
  29| pub(crate) fn emission_rgb(voxel_type: u8) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
  30|     EMISSION_PROFILES
  31|         .iter()
  32|         .find(|profile| profile.voxel_type == voxel_type)
  33|         .map(|profile| profile.rgb)
  34| }
  35| 
  36| /// Returns the air-cell centers immediately below exposed fixture undersides.
  37| ///
  38| /// The voxel materials in [`EMISSION_PROFILES`] describe ceiling-style
  39| /// fixtures: ordinary fluorescent panels, red panels, and dim emergency
  40| /// glimmers. They all emit through their downward face. A material placed on
  41| /// the floor (`y == 0`), buried below a solid, or exposed only on a side is
  42| /// still visible geometry, but it does not seed the diffuse-fill field. This
  43| /// is the same one-sided source contract used by analytic scene lights.
  44| pub(crate) fn exposed_downward_air_cells(
  45|     grid: &VoxelGrid,
  46|     dimensions: GridDimensions,
  47|     profile: EmissionProfile,
  48| ) -> Vec<VoxelCoord> {
  49|     let mut exposed = Vec::new();
  50|     for_each_voxel(dimensions, |coord| {
  51|         if let Some(air_cell) = exposed_air_cell_below(grid, coord, profile.voxel_type) {
  52|             exposed.push(air_cell);
  53|         }
  54|     });
  55|     exposed
  56| }
  57| 
  58| /// Identifies the single face through which a ceiling fixture may seed the
  59| /// approximate diffuse-fill field. Keeping this predicate separate makes the
  60| /// orientation and boundary behavior explicit and independently testable.
  61| fn exposed_air_cell_below(
  62|     grid: &VoxelGrid,
  63|     emitter: VoxelCoord,
  64|     expected_material: u8,
  65| ) -> Option<VoxelCoord> {
  66|     if emitter.y == 0 || grid.get(emitter.x, emitter.y, emitter.z) != expected_material {
  67|         return None;
  68|     }
  69| 
  70|     let air_cell = VoxelCoord {
  71|         y: emitter.y - 1,
  72|         ..emitter
  73|     };
  74|     (grid.get(air_cell.x, air_cell.y, air_cell.z) == VOXEL_AIR).then_some(air_cell)
  75| }

   1| use std::collections::VecDeque;
   2| 
   3| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
   4| 
   5| use super::exposed_emissive_faces::{
   6|     EMISSION_PROFILES, EmissionProfile, exposed_downward_air_cells,
   7| };
   8| use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
   9| use super::voxel_neighborhood::{GridDimensions, for_each_face_neighbor};
  10| 
  11| pub(crate) const UNREACHABLE: u32 = u32::MAX;
  12| 
  13| pub(crate) struct PropagatedEmission {
  14|     pub(crate) profile: EmissionProfile,
  15|     /// Shortest count of air-cell center transitions from an exposed seed.
  16|     pub(crate) distance_steps: Vec<u32>,
  17| }
  18| 
  19| pub(crate) struct AirPropagation {
  20|     pub(crate) dimensions: GridDimensions,
  21|     pub(crate) emissions: Vec<PropagatedEmission>,
  22| }
  23| 
  24| /// Finds shortest face-connected paths through air for every emission class.
  25| ///
  26| /// A class uses one multi-source breadth-first search. This means equally
  27| /// colored panels form a nearest-emitter envelope instead of multiplying
  28| /// energy merely because a large panel occupies several source voxels.
  29| pub(crate) fn propagate_through_air(
  30|     grid: &VoxelGrid,
  31|     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
  32| ) -> AirPropagation {
  33|     let dimensions = GridDimensions::of(grid);
  34|     let mut emissions = Vec::with_capacity(EMISSION_PROFILES.len());
  35| 
  36|     for profile in EMISSION_PROFILES {
  37|         let mut distance_steps = vec![UNREACHABLE; dimensions.volume()];
  38|         let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
  39| 
  40|         // An exposed air center is half a voxel from the emitting face. Do
  41|         // not inject a sample that is already beyond the requested range.
  42|         if settings.voxel_size_world_units() * 0.5 < settings.max_range_world_units() {
  43|             for seed in exposed_downward_air_cells(grid, dimensions, profile) {
  44|                 let index = dimensions.index(seed);
  45|                 if distance_steps[index] == UNREACHABLE {
  46|                     distance_steps[index] = 0;
  47|                     queue.push_back(seed);
  48|                 }
  49|             }
  50|         }
  51| 
  52|         while let Some(coord) = queue.pop_front() {
  53|             let current_steps = distance_steps[dimensions.index(coord)];
  54|             let next_steps = current_steps + 1;
  55|             let next_center_distance =
  56|                 (next_steps as f32 + 0.5) * settings.voxel_size_world_units();
  57|             if next_center_distance >= settings.max_range_world_units() {
  58|                 continue;
  59|             }
  60| 
  61|             for_each_face_neighbor(coord, dimensions, |neighbor| {
  62|                 if grid.get(neighbor.x, neighbor.y, neighbor.z) != VOXEL_AIR {
  63|                     return;
  64|                 }
  65|                 let neighbor_index = dimensions.index(neighbor);
  66|                 if next_steps < distance_steps[neighbor_index] {
  67|                     distance_steps[neighbor_index] = next_steps;
  68|                     queue.push_back(neighbor);
  69|                 }
  70|             });
  71|         }
  72| 
  73|         emissions.push(PropagatedEmission {
  74|             profile,
  75|             distance_steps,
  76|         });
  77|     }
  78| 
  79|     AirPropagation {
  80|         dimensions,
  81|         emissions,
  82|     }
  83| }

   1| use super::exposed_emissive_faces::EmissionProfile;
   2| use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
   3| 
   4| /// Adds one emission class after finite-range linear attenuation.
   5| ///
   6| /// `cell_offsets` accounts for the half-cell from an emitting face to its
   7| /// first air center. Air samples use 0.5. A solid receiver adds the second
   8| /// half-cell from its neighboring air center to the receiving face and uses
   9| /// 1.0. Those two halves make equal physical gaps agree at 0.1 and 0.2 unit
  10| /// voxel sizes instead of differing by one resolution-dependent cell center.
  11| pub(crate) fn accumulate_attenuated(
  12|     accumulated: &mut [f32; 3],
  13|     profile: EmissionProfile,
  14|     distance_steps: u32,
  15|     cell_offsets: f32,
  16|     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
  17| ) {
  18|     let distance_world = (distance_steps as f32 + cell_offsets) * settings.voxel_size_world_units();
  19|     let remaining = (1.0 - distance_world / settings.max_range_world_units()).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  20|     for channel in 0..3 {
  21|         accumulated[channel] += profile.rgb[channel] * remaining;
  22|     }
  23| }
  24| 
  25| pub(crate) fn pack_rgb(accumulated: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
  26|     accumulated.map(|channel| channel.round().clamp(0.0, 15.0) as u8)
  27| }
  28| 
  29| pub(crate) fn pack_emission(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
  30|     pack_rgb(rgb)
  31| }

   4| use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
   5| use super::voxel_neighborhood::for_each_voxel;
   6| use super::world_space_attenuation::{accumulate_attenuated, pack_rgb};
   7| 
   8| pub(crate) fn write_air_irradiance(
   9|     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
  10|     propagated: &AirPropagation,
  11|     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
  12| ) {
  13|     for_each_voxel(propagated.dimensions, |coord| {
  14|         if grid.get(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z) != VOXEL_AIR {
  15|             return;
  16|         }
  17|         let index = propagated.dimensions.index(coord);
  18|         let mut irradiance = [0.0; 3];
  19|         for emission in &propagated.emissions {
  20|             let distance_steps = emission.distance_steps[index];
  21|             if distance_steps != UNREACHABLE {
  22|                 accumulate_attenuated(
  23|                     &mut irradiance,
  24|                     emission.profile,
  25|                     distance_steps,
  26|                     0.5,
  27|                     settings,
  28|                 );
  29|             }
  30|         }
  31|         grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_rgb(irradiance));
  32|     });
  33| }

   9| /// Copies incident air irradiance onto the first occupied voxel at a surface.
  10| /// Receivers are never fed back into propagation, which is the invariant that
  11| /// prevents a lit wall from leaking energy into the room behind it.
  12| pub(crate) fn project_onto_solid_receivers(
  13|     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
  14|     propagated: &AirPropagation,
  15|     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
  16| ) {
  17|     for_each_voxel(propagated.dimensions, |coord| {
  18|         let voxel_type = grid.get(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z);
  19|         if voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
  20|             return;
  21|         }
  22| 
  23|         if let Some(rgb) = emission_rgb(voxel_type) {
  24|             grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_emission(rgb));
  25|             return;
  26|         }

  28|         let mut irradiance = [0.0; 3];

  30|             let mut nearest_air_steps = UNREACHABLE;
  31|             for_each_face_neighbor(coord, propagated.dimensions, |neighbor| {
  32|                 if grid.get(neighbor.x, neighbor.y, neighbor.z) != VOXEL_AIR {
  33|                     return;
  34|                 }
  35|                 nearest_air_steps = nearest_air_steps
  36|                     .min(emission.distance_steps[propagated.dimensions.index(neighbor)]);
  37|             });
  38|             if nearest_air_steps != UNREACHABLE {
  39|                 accumulate_attenuated(
  40|                     &mut irradiance,
  41|                     emission.profile,
  42|                     nearest_air_steps,
  43|                     1.0,
  44|                     settings,
  45|                 );
  46|             }
  47|         }
  48|         grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_rgb(irradiance));
  49|     });
  50| }

  48| /// implementation reproducible, while shortest integer distances make the
  49| /// result independent of which equally short route was visited first.

  51|     coord: VoxelCoord,

  63|             x: coord.x - 1,

  65|         });

  69|             y: coord.y + 1,

bake_voxel_lighting analysis:
- `clear_previous_bake`: O(V) writes.
- `propagate_through_air`: For each of 3 emission profiles, multi-source BFS over air cells — each air cell can be updated at most once per profile (distances monotonically decrease; standard BFS with deque ensures each cell's distance is set at most... actually with the `next_steps < distance_steps[neighbor_index]` check and BFS order, each cell is pushed at most once per profile... In BFS with uniform edge weight, the first time a cell is discovered gives the shortest distance, so it's pushed once; the `next_steps <` check prevents re-pushes. So BFS is O(V) per profile → O(3V) total. Memory: 3 × V × 4 bytes = 12 × V bytes + queue. For a 202×242×202 grid ≈ 9.87M voxels → 3 × 9.87M × 4B = 118MB of distance arrays! Plus the grid itself. Hmm — MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS is 9,874,568 → distance_steps for 3 profiles = 3 × 9.87M × 4B = 118MB. That's a significant memory spike per chunk bake (temporary). Actually it's per bake and freed after; but on a low-memory target (the docstrings mention "low-memory targets" for direct SVO), a 118MB transient is huge. Worth a Medium finding: the distance arrays could be u16 (range ≤ 6.0/0.1=60 steps... actually max_range 6.0 / voxel 0.1 → 60 steps; u8 would suffice for ≤255 steps) — pack to u8/u16, or process per-profile and free each array before the next (only the final projected results need cross-profile accumulation, which is done per-voxel at write time). Actually write_air_irradiance and project_onto_solid_receivers need ALL profiles at once. But they could accumulate incrementally: propagate profile 1, write its contribution into a per-voxel [f32;3] accumulation buffer... The current design holds 3×V u32 arrays = 12B/voxel. Could hold 3×V u8 = 3B/voxel or accumulate. This is a real memory finding for the 202³ chunk: 9.87M voxels → 118MB vs grid 10MB.
- BFS bounded by max_range: the `next_center_distance >= max_range` cutoff — good.
- `write_air_irradiance`: O(V × 3).
- `project_onto_solid_receivers`: O(V × 3 × 6).

Total bake: O(V) time with constant ~3×BFS + passes, and 12 bytes/voxel of transient memory. This runs per chunk (generate_chunk.rs:409 and legacy_blueprint.rs:922).

   1| //! Level 34-B — "The Grassland".
   2| //!
   3| //! A safe, flat, endless grass plane you can noclip into from Level 0:
   4| //! * grass ground everywhere, with smooth-noise **lakes** of shallow water,
   5| //! * scattered **trees** (solid trunk, leaf canopy) on a hashed world grid,
   6| //! * a glowing **sky layer** at the top of the grid plus dim ground glow
   7| //!   sources hidden inside the turf, so the plane reads as daylight even
   8| //!   though lighting is the same BFS flood used indoors.
   9| //!
  10| //! Like every [`LevelGenerator`], all placement is a pure function of
  11| //! world-space coordinates so chunks tile seamlessly.
  12| 
  13| use crate::domain::entities::position::Position;
  14| use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  15|     VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
  16| };
  17| use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  18| use crate::use_cases::generated_chunk::GeneratedChunk;
  19| use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
  20| use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  21| 
  22| /// Grid height in world units; the sky glow layer sits at the top.
  23| const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
  24| /// Trees sit on a world grid of this period (units); most cells are empty.
  25| const TREE_PERIOD: f32 = 9.0;
  26| /// Ground glow sources ("sun-lit turf") every N units.
  27| const GLOW_PERIOD: f32 = 3.2;
  28| 
  29| pub struct GrasslandLevel;
  30| 
  31| impl GrasslandLevel {
  32|     /// Uniform per-cell hash in [0, 1): samples the value noise exactly on
  33|     /// its lattice (provider frequency 0.05 → inputs that are multiples of
  34|     /// 20 hit lattice points, where the noise is a raw uniform hash).
  35|     fn hash(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, salt: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64) -> f32 {
  36|         let v = noise.evaluate_2d(
  37|             seed ^ salt,
  38|             Position::new(cx as f32 * 20.0, cz as f32 * 20.0),
  39|         );
  40|         (v * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999)
  41|     }
  42| }
  43| 
  44| impl LevelGenerator for GrasslandLevel {
  45|     fn generate_with_reality(
  46|         &self,
  47|         chunk_pos: Position,
  48|         seed: u32,
  49|         config: GeneratorConfig,
  50|         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
  51|         _reality: &crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot,
  52|     ) -> GeneratedChunk {
  53|         let s = config.voxel_scale;
  54|         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
  55|         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
  56|         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
  57|         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
  58|         let sky_y = height - 1;
  59| 
  60|         for z in 0..depth {
  61|             for x in 0..width {
  62|                 let wx = chunk_pos.x + (x as f32 + 0.5) * s;
  63|                 let wz = chunk_pos.z + (z as f32 + 0.5) * s;
  64| 
  65|                 // Lakes: smooth blobs of the world-space noise field.
  66|                 let lake = noise.evaluate_2d(seed ^ 0x1A5E, Position::new(wx * 0.7, wz * 0.7));
  67|                 let ground = if lake > 0.62 {
  68|                     VOXEL_WATER
  69|                 } else {
  70|                     VOXEL_GRASS
  71|                 };
  72|                 grid.set(x, 0, z, ground);
  73| 
  74|                 // Sky glow: an unbroken luminous layer overhead.
  75|                 grid.set(x, sky_y, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
  76| 
  77|                 // Ground glow grid keeps the turf bright at eye level (the
  78|                 // BFS light from the sky layer alone fades before the floor).
  79|                 let gx = wx.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
  80|                 let gz = wz.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
  81|                 if ground == VOXEL_GRASS && gx < s && gz < s {
  82|                     grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
  83|                 }
  84| 
  85|                 // Trees: hashed world cells, never in water.
  86|                 let cell_x = (wx / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
  87|                 let cell_z = (wz / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
  88|                 if Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE5, cell_x, cell_z) > 0.6 && ground == VOXEL_GRASS {
  89|                     // Trunk position jittered inside the cell.
  90|                     let jx =
  91|                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE6, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
  92|                     let jz =
  93|                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE7, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
  94|                     let tx = cell_x as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jx;
  95|                     let tz = cell_z as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jz;
  96|                     let dx = wx - tx;
  97|                     let dz = wz - tz;
  98|                     let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
  99| 
 100|                     let trunk_top = (2.2 / s) as usize;
 101|                     let canopy_top = (3.6 / s) as usize;
 102|                     if d2 < (0.25f32).powi(2) {
 103|                         for y in 1..trunk_top.min(height - 2) {
 104|                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_TREE);
 105|                         }
 106|                     }
 107|                     if d2 < (1.6f32).powi(2) {
 108|                         for y in trunk_top..canopy_top.min(height - 2) {
 109|                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_GRASS);
 110|                         }
 111|                     }
 112|                 }
 113|             }
 114|         }
 115| 
 116|         GeneratedChunk::new(grid)
 117|     }
 118| }

 753| impl CirculationSpine {
 754|     /// Distance from (x, z) to the spine centerline (axis-aligned segments).
 755|     pub fn distance(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> f32 {
 756|         self.nearest(x, z).0
 757|     }
 758| 
 759|     /// Nearest point on the centerline: `(distance, along, is_horizontal)`.
 760|     /// `along` is the world coordinate *along* the nearest segment's axis, so
 761|     /// modules (light strips, wall gaps) repeat in world space and stay
 762|     /// continuous across chunk and region borders.
 763|     pub fn nearest(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> (f32, f32, bool) {
 764|         let mut best = (f32::MAX, 0.0, true);
 765|         for seg in self.path.windows(2) {
 766|             let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 767|             let (dx, dz) = (b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z);
 768|             let len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 769|             let t = if len2 > 0.0 {
 770|                 (((x - a.x) * dx + (z - a.z) * dz) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 771|             } else {
 772|                 0.0
 773|             };
 774|             let (px, pz) = (a.x + t * dx, a.z + t * dz);
 775|             let d2 = (x - px) * (x - px) + (z - pz) * (z - pz);
 776|             if d2 < best.0 {
 777|                 let horizontal = dx.abs() >= dz.abs();
 778|                 best = (d2, if horizontal { px } else { pz }, horizontal);
 779|             }
 780|         }
 781|         (best.0.sqrt(), best.1, best.2)
 782|     }
 783| }

 303|         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;

Confirmed: level_zero/generate.rs:331 — `RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk` is built on EVERY chunk generation inside `generate_from_plans`, and at line 321-328, when no plans are provided, `region_plans_for` (an `InfiniteRegionWindow::around_chunk`) is also derived per chunk. So the streaming path derives a full window of region plans per chunk (chunk 10u + halo 1u → regions 80u: window covering 10+2 = 12u → up to 2×2 = 4 regions; plus halo → maybe 2×2 or 3×3), plus a recursive window when a red room is committed (also ~2×2-3×3 regions, each with the full plan cost including macro anomaly scan of ~36-49 anchors × 18 noise evals).

Cost per region plan (my estimate):
- derive_genome ×2-3: 2-3 noise evals
- build_corridors: ~15 hash01
- free_territories: n=92 → 8464 cells × corridors(~3) × distance (O(segs)) ≈ 8464×3×4 ≈ 100k ops + largest_free_rectangle up to 64 × O(n²) ≈ 64 × 8464 ≈ 540k ops. Hmm wait — largest_free_rectangle is O(n²) = O(8464)? No: it sweeps n rows × n columns = n² cells = 8464 iterations per call. 64 calls → 542k. OK.
- lay_out_suites: ~22 rounds × legs(~3-5) × anchors(~36) × 2 sides ≈ 22×4×36×2 ≈ 6,336 candidates × O(T+S+E+P) ≈ 6,336 × ~30 ≈ 190k ops.
- corrupt: dup sweep ~2-4 skews × ~20-40 offsets × clone+checks ≈ small.
- plan_anomalies_for_region → plan_macro_anomalies: ~36-49 anchors × 18 noise evals ≈ 650-880 noise evals (this dominates!). Plus red room tournament per corrupt: red_room_event_for_region → 9 candidates × 18 noise = 162 noise evals.
- Also vertical_link_for_region: 18 noise evals.

So per region plan ≈ 800-1100 noise evaluations, each of which in SimpleNoiseProvider is maybe 3-5 octaves of value noise ≈ hundreds of ops. So per region plan ≈ 300k-500k ops from noise alone. Per chunk with 2×2-3×3 = 4-9 regions → 2-5M ops of planning per chunk. Per WorldBlock (324 regions) → ~100-160M ops for planning once. Then per chunk the streaming path (browser) re-derives windows per chunk: that's the MAJOR finding (level_zero/generate.rs:321 + 331).
